TCS Registration – 2027 Batch

Greetings from Tata Consultancy Services!!!

We are pleased to invite eligible students from your institute to

participate in the TCS Priority Institution National Qualifier Test (NQT)

for the 2027 graduating batch. As TCS accelerates the enterprise adoption

of AI and Generative AI, students joining us will have opportunities to

work on AI-led transformation programs at scale, supported by enterprise AI

platforms, deep industry context, and global technology partnerships.

Kindly ensure that all eligibility criteria and validation checks are

completed before sharing the final student list with us on or before May

15, 2026 9.00 am. Please note, no changes will be permitted after the

closure date.

TCS Eligibility Criteria:

Courses & Disciplines

Batch of 2027 Only.

Listed highest qualifications—B.Tech., M.Tech. (2yr & 5yr), M.C.A., M.Sc,

(2yr & 5yr),. from any discipline/department.

Course Type

Only Full-Time courses will be considered

(Part Time / Correspondence Courses will not be considered)

Percentage

Candidates must have a minimum aggregate of 60%

OR

6 CGPA in all semesters up to the latest declared results.

AND

Offer is valid only if the final degree or provisional certificate confirms

'FIRST CLASS' in the highest qualification, completed within the stipulated

time.

Backlogs / Arrears / ATKT:

Application & Test Process: The student should not have more than 1 (one)

pending or active backlog / arrear / ATKT at the time of appearing for

the TCS Selection process.

Onboarding Process: At the time of onboarding, no pending backlogs /

arrears / ATKT will be permitted.

Please note: All pending backlogs / arrears / ATKT should be cleared

within the course duration stipulated by the University.

Gap / Break in Education

Ensure any academic gaps during your education are declared and supported

with valid proof; breaks should not exceed 24 months.

Work Experience

Students with prior work experience of up to two years are eligible to

apply for this hiring process (Applicable only for postgraduate students).

Age

A student should be 18 to 28 years of age to participate in

the TCS Hiring Process.

Sl.No

Important Notes

1

Only students graduating in the year 2027 are eligible to apply, and this

must be clearly indicated in their TCS Application Form

2

All students must ensure that they use their Personal Email ID Only.

Please note: Email ID CANNOT be changed once submitted.

3

Reference ID series starting DT/CT 2023 onwards to be used, as older IDs

will not be accepted; if students have a reference ID prior to 2023, they

should contact us for profile deletion and re-registration should be

completed before the registration date.

4

Please do eligibility check for the candidate data at your end too and

eliminate any ineligible profiles.

All the students are asked to go through the entire mail before

registering.

TCS Registration Process:

1) Visit https://nextstep.tcsapps.com/indiacampus/#/

2) Click “Register Now”

3) Select category as “IT”

4) Fill in details to generate a Reference ID

5) Click “Apply for Drive”

If a candidate already has a Reference ID, please ensure “Apply for Drive”

is clicked.

The registration window for the assessment process will be open from 11

May to 15 May 2026 9.00 am.

https://forms.gle/QmYM3mtDNMxW5J3h8

asked to register without fail (if they are eligible), Students who are not

registering will be blacklisted on 16th May 2026.

AI-focused Career Opportunities for Students

Students hired through this drive may be aligned to future-ready work

across areas such as AI and data engineering, machine learning, deep

learning and GenAI, cloud data platforms, intelligent automation, and

AI-enabled software engineering.

Career pathways may include AI and Data tracks, including roles such as ML

Engineer and GenAI-focused engineering roles, along with broader digital

roles where AI is embedded into delivery.

As the industry landscape undergoes significant shifts in required skills

and expertise, TCS offers students a strong opportunity to remain relevant,

continuously upskill, and build careers for the new era.

Additional 15% Student Nomination from Group Institutes

The Placement Officer of a TCS Priority Institute may share an additional

list of students who are interested in taking the TCS NQT for Priority

Institutes. This additional list will be limited to 15% of the eligible

students who have applied for the TCS NQT for Priority Institutes from the

parent institute. The eligibility criteria will remain the same as

mentioned above.

Disclaimer

 - Any ineligible candidature or misrepresentation of information will

Greetings from Dell Technologies.

We are pleased to invite your esteemed institution to participate in the

Dell Futureminds AI Hackathon, an inter-college AI-focused hackathon aimed

at identifying and nurturing future-ready technical talent. The hackathon is

planned to run during the mid- May to June/July 2026 timeframe.

Overview of the Hackathon

Dell Futureminds AI Hackathon is a multi-stage, inter-collegiate

competition where interested students will work on real-world problem

statements curated by Dell Technologies. The event is designed to assess

technical depth, problem-solving skills, collaboration, and innovation.

Participation Flow & Structure

The hackathon will be conducted in the following stages:

 1. Student Interest Registration

 Interested students from your college will register to participate.

 2. Eligibility Criteria: 2nd year students from CS, IT and relevant

 branches with 60% in 10th , 12th , and Graduation.

 3. Screening & Assessment

 - Dell will screen registrations based on defined eligibility

 criteria.

 - Eligible students will undergo a HackerRank assessment.

 4. Team Formation & Round 1 (College-Level)

 - Shortlisted students will form teams of 5 members each.

 - Dell will provide problem statements for the hackathon.

 - Colleges will be responsible for forming teams and conducting the

 first round of evaluation.

 - The top 4 teams from each college will qualify for Round 2.

 5. Round 2 (Dell Evaluation)

 - Qualified teams will be evaluated by Dell technical panels.

 - Based on performance, one team from each of the top 5 colleges will

 be selected for the final round.

 - All Round 2 qualifiers will receive digital participation

 certificates from Dell.

 6. Final Round – Onsite at Dell Bangalore Office

 - The final round will be conducted in person at the Dell Bangalore

 office.

 - Stay and accommodation will be arranged by Dell.

 - Travel arrangements will need to be managed by the qualifying

 teams.

 7. Rewards & Recognition

 - Exciting prizes will be awarded to the winning teams.

 - Finalists will gain invaluable exposure through interaction with

Dell leaders

 and experts.

 - Round 2 qualifiers will receive official digital certificates,

 enhancing their academic and professional profiles.

We believe this initiative will provide your students with a strong

Subject: Congratulations to Team NAVega for Securing 3rd Place at Aakaar 2026 – IIT Bombay
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Team NAVega, representing ASCE-VIT,

secured 3rd Place in the Industrial Design Project (IDP) at Aakaar 2026,

the 18th Annual Civil Engineering Technical Festival conducted by IIT

Bombay, held on 15th March 2026.

The competition brought together top engineering teams from across the

country, where participants were evaluated on technical design, modelling,

and practical application of civil engineering concepts. The team submitted

a comprehensive design package including horizontal and vertical alignment

reports, component quantity estimation, and a 10 km highway plan-profile

design, along with 3D corridor modelling and visualization.

Following a rigorous evaluation process, the team was shortlisted among the

top 13 teams nationally and advanced to the final round. Through their

innovative approach and technical expertise, Team NAVega secured a podium

position in this prestigious competition.

This experience enabled the team to gain hands-on exposure to highway

design, optimization techniques, and real-world engineering challenges,

along with valuable interaction with industry experts.

Team Members:

 3. Varoon R – 23BCL0013

We sincerely acknowledge the invaluable guidance and continuous support of

the Faculty Coordinator, Dr. Sofi A (Emp. ID: 11162), whose mentorship

significantly contributed to this achievement.

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to Team NAVega on this

commendable achievement and wish them continued success in their future

endeavors.

Subject: Congratulations to Angiras Shounak Nazar for Securing 1st Place at Nagpur Got Talent - MSRLM, Nagpur
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Angiras Shounak Nazar (22BEI0029) of SPIC

MACAY-VIT has brought laurels to VIT by securing 1st Place at Nagpur Got

Talent 2026, a government-organized talent competition held in Nagpur,

Maharashtra in the month of March 2026.

The event was conducted as part of Mahalaxmi Saras, an exhibition organized

by the Government of Maharashtra, and witnessed participation from over

1000 performers across Maharashtra and neighboring states. The competition

consisted of two rounds, including an online elimination round followed by

the finals, where the top 54 participants competed.

Showcasing exceptional musical talent, he performed solo singing in front

of a large audience and emerged as the winner of the competition.

We acknowledge the invaluable guidance and continuous support of the

Faculty Coordinator, Dr. Sudheer C V (Emp. ID: 13573), whose mentorship

significantly contributed to this achievement.

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to Angiras Shounak Nazar on this

commendable achievement and wish him continued success in his future

endeavors.

Subject: Apply Now: HDSE Leadership Intensive (July 2026)
Body:
Dear Students,

On behalf of Lehigh University, IUCEE, and the Agastya International

Foundation, the Office of International Relations at VIT is happy to share

an exciting opportunity:

Applications are now open for the Leadership Intensive (HDSE) Leadership

Intensive

https://www.google.com/url?q=https://creativeinquiry.lehigh.edu/outreach/hdse-leadership-intensive-india&source=gmail-imap&ust=1777387527000000&usg=AOvVaw1xKWLO3wzQ5rGkE0B1aSme,

a highly selective, week-long experience at the Agastya International

Foundation offered in two cohorts.

Program Dates:

• Cohort 1: July 12–16, 2026

• Cohort 2: July 19–23, 2026

This is not a traditional lecture-based program. Participants will explore

complex societal challenges and design solutions using skills developed

through the HDSE Virtual Academy

https://www.google.com/url?q=https://creativeinquiry.lehigh.edu/outreach/hdse-virtual-academy&source=gmail-imap&ust=1777387527000000&usg=AOvVaw1D2UeoTpDU-lFbSM39IUnh,

a self-guided course completed prior to the intensive focused on the

fundamentals of social entrepreneurship and humanitarian design.

During the intensive, students will:

 -

 Collaborate in interdisciplinary teams to address real-world challenges

 -

 Engage with stakeholders to better understand needs and context

 -

 Co-develop scalable, impact-driven solutions

 -

 Translate ideas into actionable venture blueprints

 -

 Present their ventures at the end of the program, with top teams

 receiving awards.

Guided by mentors and social innovators, students will gain hands-on

experience in social entrepreneurship and humanitarian design while

building practical leadership, teamwork, and communication skills.

Program Cost:

The program fee is 13,000 INR, payable directly to the Agastya

International Foundation. For selected students from IUCEE-affiliated

colleges and universities, program costs will be covered, while students

are personally responsible for travel to and from Agastya’s campus in

Kuppam.

Details and applications for highly motivated undergraduate and graduate

students from all disciplines are available on the HDSE Leadership

Intensive - India

https://www.google.com/url?q=https://creativeinquiry.lehigh.edu/outreach/hdse-leadership-intensive-india&source=gmail-imap&ust=1777387527000000&usg=AOvVaw1xKWLO3wzQ5rGkE0B1aSme

 website.

Please feel free to contact email id - vid623@lehigh.edu or Whatsapp number

- +91 9820544659 for any clarification.

Dear Students,

The Office of International Relations is pleased to announce that University

of Tours 1st summer school is now open to all its partners!

The "Loire Valley Summer School" will take place from June 22 to July 10,

2026, in Tours (France). 

Students will have the opportunity to take part in an ambitious summer

program in France combining

1 core curriculum + 1 academic track up to choice.

------------------------------

Core curriculum = French language & culture (45h) 

+

 Track 1 : French cinema and/in the world (36h) 

 OR 

Track 2: Sustainable & Eco-responsible management (36h)

------------------------------

This innovative 3-weeks program is designed for students with a B1 or B2

level in French (in accordance with the CEFR

https://europass.europa.eu/en/what-common-european-framework-languages-cefr

).

It includes:

 - 81 hours of classes (45h French Language&Culture + 36h disciplinary

 track)

 - Practical workshops and field visits

 - Cultural excursions to discover Touraine and the Loire Valley

Participants will receive a certificate of participation at the end of the

program and a recognition of 3 ECTS credits is possible.

The application deadline has been extended until May 11th !

Find all about practical information and registration on this webpage

https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/short-programs/loire-valley-summer-school-2026.

Dear VITians,

 We are pleased to invite bright and motivated students to apply for the

VIT– IITB National Geospatial Internship through the School of Computer

Science Engineering and Information Systems (SCORE) at VIT, Vellore.

Duration :

Two Months (15/05/2026 to 15/07/2026)

Satellite Image Processing, AI powered Geospatial technologies and

open-source tools

shortlisted candidates will have to carry out their work offline in G19A

Subject: Application for Student Council - 2026-27.
Body:
Dear Students,

The Student Council is a diverse group of students from across all

departments, working together to represent the needs and aspirations of the

entire student body. It coordinates with various other departments along

with the Office of Students' Welfare to execute various university level

events and put continuous efforts to make such events grand and

successful. If you're passionate about making VIT an even better place and

you are the leader who wants to make change, we encourage you to nominate

yourself!

The Office of Students' Welfare is inviting nominations for the

Student Council 2026-27. This is your opportunity to represent your

peers, contribute to student initiatives, and play a vital role in shaping

student life at VIT.

For submitting your nomination and more information on the nomination

process and the role of the Student Council, please visit the following

link.

Form Link: https://forms.gle/LWRneEJdv8cdNx8s6

https://forms.gle/LWRneEJdv8cdNx8s6

The link will be available only till 10th May . The applications

received will be scrutinized and called for an interview.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA:

 1. Students who have been involved in any form of disciplinary action,

 either currently or in the past, are not eligible to hold any position.

 2. As of the Winter Semester 2025–26, only students in their pre-final

 year are eligible to apply for the post of Executive Member.

 3. As of the Winter Semester 2025–26, students in the 6th semester of a

 5-year degree programme (B.Arch. and Integrated Programmes) are also

 eligible to apply for the post of Executive Member.

 4. Students from all other years are eligible to apply for the post of

 Member Secretary.

 5. The position of Member Secretary is categorized into three

 specialized divisions: Technical, Cultural, and Digital.

 6. A minimum CGPA of 9.0 is required to be eligible for the posts of

 Executive Member and Member Secretary.

 7. A minimum CGPA of 8.5 is required to be eligible for the posts of

 Member Secretary – Cultural and Member Secretary – Technical.

 8. A minimum CGPA of 7.5 is required to be eligible for the post of

 Member Secretary – Digital.

 9. CGPA eligibility will be assessed based on the grades announced after

 the Winter Semester 2025–26.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF STUDENT COUNCIL MEMBERS:

 - To officially represent all the students in the school / institute.

 - To identify and help solve problems encountered by students in the

 school / institute.

 - To communicate its opinion to the school / institute administration on

 any subject that concerns students.

 - To promote and encourage the involvement of students in organizing

 school / institute level activities.

 - To inform students about any subject that concerns them.

 - To consult students on any issue of importance and bring it to the

 notice of the Students' Welfare office.

 - To support and contribute to achieve better / higher accreditation for

 the institute.

 - To participate in the development of the school activities.

 - To propose activities to the school/institute administration that

 would improve the quality of student life in the school/institute.

We look forward to receiving your nominations!

In this regard, we are sharing the "List of courses under the program" and

"Key Takeaways" on pursuing this Minor program by the B. Tech students, which

is exclusively designed for them.

Importance and key Takeaways - 

Combining engineering with a Minor in Accounting And Finance will

essentially position oneself for roles where technical decisions meet

money and strategy. Here are the careers where that combo really pays

off—and why.

1. The business side of engineering –

a. Engineering projects aren’t just about design and

performance—they’re constrained by budgets, costs, and expected returns.

Basic knowledge of concepts like Accounting and Finance allows you to

interpret financial statements, evaluate project feasibility, and

communicate better with managers or clients.

2. Decision-making –

a. Example: when choosing between two designs, an engineer with

finance knowledge can analyse cost-benefit trade-offs, return on

investment, and long-term financial impact—not just technical efficiency.

This is closely tied to concepts like Cost–Benefit Analysis and Return on

Investment.

3. Roles –

a. especially in management, consulting, startups, or product

development—value people who can bridge technical and financial domains. If

you aim for roles like project manager, product manager, or even

entrepreneur, this combination is powerful. It’s particularly useful in

fields like Project Management, where budgeting and financial tracking are

essential. pairing engineering with accounting and finance makes you more

versatile, improves your problem-solving in real-world contexts, and

expands your career opportunities beyond strictly technical roles.

b. This combination is most valuable in roles where:

 i. Decisions

involve money + engineering trade-offs

 ii. You

interact with business stakeholders

 iii. You

influence strategy, not just execution

c. Anything involving leadership, business, or decision-making, it’s

an advantage.

4. Flexibility –

a. If you ever want to transition into business-oriented roles like

operations, consulting, or even pursue an M.Com/MBA/CA/ICWA, your

background in finance and accounting will make that shift much smoother.

5. Exclusive Software –

a. NSmart: MoU with NSE Academy Ltd (NAL)

b. ZOHO Books: As VAC

c. ArthaVidhya - accredited by the National Skill Development

Corporation (NSDC): As VAC

d. Tally - will be taught with Principles of Accounting as a LAB

Subject: INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS - WINTER SEMESTER 2025-26 THEORY FAT
Body:
INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS APPEARING FOR WINTER SEMESTER 

 2025-26 THEORY FAT

General Instructions

· Students must enter the examination hall 15-30 Minutes before

the commencement of examination (between 9.00 - 9.15 AM for FN Session)

· You need to WEAR Student IDENTITY CARD during the ENTIRE

EXAMINATION PERIOD. If you don’t have a Proper ID Card contact the

Registrar Office and apply for a new one and get it before coming to the

Exam. The ID card should be scratched free with a proper tag. Exchange of

ID cards or Tags will be considered as Malpractice. If you have misplaced

your ID card or forgot to bring it to the Examination Hall, Report to the

Control Room (PRP 115/SJT G01/TT 104) of your test venue to get One Time

Permit Slips. You need to pay Rs. 100 through V-TOP online payment only.

· You will NOT be permitted to use the toilet/washroom during the

examination, so be prepared for it.

· Exchange of Calculators, Stationeries, Code Books, pen, pencil

etc., are not permitted. The code Books or standard tables should have been

signed by either the faculty or School office. No markings of any kind

should be found in such booklets.

· As per VIT rules, even if you keep your mobile phone/smart watch

in a switched off position inside the examination hall, it will be treated

as examination malpractice. Such malpractices will lead to confiscation of

the devices (including SIM card) for one semester and ’N’ grade (ALL PAPER

ZERO) in all the registered courses including lab & project components in

that semester. Hence, before entering the examination hall, students should

check their pockets thoroughly to avoid carrying mobile phones/smart

watches by mistake.

· Possession of any Electronic Gadget (Mobile Phone, Smart Watch,

Bluetooth device, any device embedded with scanner /camera, etc.), holding

chit papers/ suspicious content in the examination hall is considered as

malpractice.

· Chewing gums or any other eatable items like Chocolates etc. are

strictly prohibited inside the examination hall 

A. Pre-Exam Activities

1.

Note down your seating arrangement (Building, Room Number and Seat Number)

from the V-TOP students login. Seating arrangement will not be displayed

for courses in which a student has been debarred. Please report yourself

half an hour prior to the exam. No student would be permitted to enter the

hall after 9.15 AM.

2.

Possession of unauthorised material, even if you do not intend to use it

will be considered as malpractice. Before starting the exam, check any

materials written on desks or walls, or found papers nearby/ around you on

the floor and inform the invigilators the same.

B. During the exam

1.

Candidate has to sit in the allotted seat only. Listen to the invigilator

and follow their instructions at all times. Strict Silence should be

maintained in the examination hall. Discussions/ communications of any kind

inside the exam hall are treated as examination malpractices.

2.

Check the class number in the Question paper with the Attendance sheet

Class Number. If you have not received the right question paper or

incomplete or badly printed, please contact the invigilator immediately. If

you have any doubt on class number, course name, course code, slot, and any

other details related to your question paper, please check while signing in

the attendance sheet.

3.

Read carefully and follow the instructions printed in the question paper

and in the answer booklet.

4.

Fill required details (Register No., course code, course title etc.) in the

answer booklet before you start writing the exam. After signing in the

attendance sheet, check the barcode sticker pasted on your answer booklet

for its correctness as your answer booklets will be scanned for valuation

using this barcode only.

5.

First clearly write the Question number in the space provided and then

start writing your answers. USE BLUE / BLACK PEN ONLY for writing the

Answers. Writings on any thin pens, pencil / light colours may not be

visible on the scanned images used for evaluation. Remember to write the

answers within the space provided in the answer booklet. If you write

anything outside the margin, it will be cut during the scanning process. If

you are using extra sheets like graph sheets / templates given by faculty,

write your answer booklet number alone on the top left edge outside the

margin and keep it immediately after the first sheet. Do not fold it as it

needs to be scanned for valuation. Do your rough work in the last page of

the main answer booklet itself. Before finishing the exam, strike out all

the rough works.

6.

Don’t write anything in the question paper or in your hand or leg or on a

desk or on walls nearby you.

7.

Correcting pens, fluid or tape and erasable pens are not to be used for

corrections in the answer booklet.

8.

Do not discuss / borrow anything with other candidates during the

examination.

9.

Do not get involved in any unfair or dishonest practice during the exam. If

you try to cheat or break the rules in any way, it will invite appropriate

sanctions under malpractice.

10.

Students are not allowed to ask questions of any kind during the

examination. Invigilators have been instructed not to answer any enquiry

whatsoever relating to the question papers, whether an explanation or

meaning or correction or typographical error

11.

On the day of the exam, if you feel that you are affected by ill health,

please contact the Chief Superintendent or Invigilator. You can write the

examination at the Health Centre.

12.

Do not leave the examination hall until told to do so by the invigilator.

You cannot leave the examination hall until 30 min from the start of the

examination. If any student leaves the exam hall before 12.00 noon, he/she

has to submit the question paper along with the answer sheet.

13.

Do not take your answer booklets or unused ones, from the examination hall.

It is a serious Malpractice.

14.

Answer booklet contains 42 pages and no additional sheets, no threads,

will be provided. 

C. If booked under Malpractice

1.

Be calm and give a written response to the allegation and follow the

instructions from the exam squad / Invigilator / Asst. CS / CS.

2.

Do not indulge in any disrespectful activities such as shouting / creating

/ diverting attention of all other students, a scene in the examination

hall.

3.

Hand over the materials and get a receipt for electronic devices.

NON-COOPERATION WILL BE VIEWED AS AN ACT OF INDISCIPLINE WHICH MAY INVITE

SEPARATE DISCIPLINARY ACTION.

4.

Examination malpractice actions/punishments are very serious, may lead to

All paper ZERO or suspension of one semester. All malpractice actions are

informed to the students / published in VTOP student Login. Please go

through it follow the examination rules appropriately

5.

OBEY ALL THE EXAMINATION RULES SERIOUSLY

Controller of Examinations

With Regards

Prof.S.Sivabalan Ph.D

Controller of Examinations

Vellore Institute of Technology ( VIT)

Vellore 632014, TN, India

Subject: Congratulations to Team Foresight for their Achievement at RedShield National Hackathon - MSAJCE, Chennai
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Team Foresight delivered an outstanding

performance at the RedShield National Hackathon, conducted at Mohamed

Sathak A. J. College of Engineering, Chennai, held on 6–7 April 2026.

The hackathon witnessed participation from over 60 teams and was conducted

through three rigorous evaluation rounds, where participants were assessed

based on innovation, technical implementation, and real-world applicability

of their solutions.

Representing VIT, Team Foresight developed a project titled “Foresight

Crime Detection Platform”. The solution aims to transform traditional

policing into a proactive, intelligence-driven ecosystem using predictive

analytics, spatial intelligence, and real-time decision support systems.

The project demonstrated features such as predictive crime analysis, patrol

optimization, real-time SOS handling, dynamic risk evaluation, and smart

resource allocation, showcasing a strong industry-oriented solution.

Through their innovative approach and technical execution, the team was

recognized among the top teams in the competition and was awarded a 90-day

paid internship opportunity with Cytnexus, along with a stipend of

₹10,000 per month.

Team Members:

Subject: Congratulations to Suhani Mohapatra for Securing 1st Place at Classique – Vibrance 2026, VIT Chennai
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Suhani Mohapatra (24BCE2844) from SPIC

MACAY secured 1st Place in Classique, the solo classical dance

competition held during Vibrance 2026 at VIT Chennai.

The event celebrated India’s rich cultural heritage through classical dance

performances and consisted of two rounds of evaluation. In the first round,

participants performed a pre-choreographed classical dance and were judged

on technique, expressions, and adherence to traditional style. The second

round required dancers to pick an emotion and create an impromptu routine

based on it. Participants were evaluated on beat sense, expressions, stage

presence, and costume presentation.

Competing against 14 participants and progressing through two rounds of

elimination (one online round and the final round), Suhani demonstrated

exceptional grace and artistic excellence to secure the top position in the

competition.

We sincerely acknowledge the invaluable guidance and continuous support of

the Faculty Coordinator, Mr. Sudheer C V (Emp. ID: 13573), whose mentorship

significantly contributed to this achievement.

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to Suhani Mohapatra on this

commendable achievement and wish her continued success in her future

endeavors.

Subject: Université de Tours, France - Semester Exchange students - Nominations 2026/27
Body:
Kind Attention: Pre-Final year students

University of Tours, France is opening the nomination period for

mobilities starting during the first semester of the 2026/27 academic

year.

In order for you to have a holistic overview upon the aspects connected to

this matter, please find a list of useful information enumerated below.

Academic calendar for nominations and online applications - incoming

exchange students

Term dates

First semester (autumn / winter semester): 4 months (September to December)

Second semester (spring / summer semester): 5 months (January to May)

Nota bene: should you have different term dates, please think about

prioritising mobilities that fit within our framework, in order to avoid

any unpleasant situation for the selected students (example: if your second

semester starts in February / March, you should prioritise mobilities

starting in September; we would be delighted to welcome your students for a

complete academic year)

Nominations calendar

Autumn / winter semester (or full academic year): starting in September 2025

Nomination period: 23.03.2026 – 10.05.2026

Application period: 30.03.2026 – 05.06.2026

Nota bene: a second nomination period will be opened in October – November

2026 for international mobilities of studies taking place during the second

semester of the 2026/27 academic year (starting in January 2027)

Nomination process for incoming exchange students

The International Relations Office has to officially nominate the outgoing

students for international mobility at the University of Tours.

The official nomination consists in completing an online form

https://forms.office.com/e/TaWdzFXZ6g:

 - Following nominations, the students will be contacted with all the

 instructions to follow as to pre-register at UT. The nominating person

 at the International Relations Office or the concerned service will also

 receive that e-mail, for efficient monitoring.

Why choose the University of Tours to study abroad in France?

 - Course offer

 - Online course catalogue (-> course name, credits, content, hours,

 coordinator, level) – disciplinary courses

Students can use our online catalogue, that lists the most popular courses

(French/English) for exchange students: Course Catalogue for Exchange

Students. https://cces.univ-tours.fr/Accueil.php?language=EN

Beyond disciplinary courses taught in French, UT also provides students

with more than 150 courses in English in different fields (Humanities,

Science and Technology). Only a beginner-intermediate level of French is

required if students choose disciplinary courses taught in English.

They have the right to choose courses in any discipline (from all faculties

apart from medicine), provided the conditions of our interinstitutional

agreement are fulfilled (the majority of their classes must be taken within

a specific field of studies, for example), that both their academic

coordinators approve it, and that their home university will recognize the

credits obtained in a different discipline than the student’s major at the

end of the mobility, these credits being relevant to the student’s academic

project.

 - French language and culture classes

Exchange students can complete their learning agreement with French courses

https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/admission-process-for-exchange-students/6-learn-french-cuefee-crl

 provided by our University Center of French as a Foreign Language

(CUEFEE). They can select up to 3 courses (up to 72 hours), that are

completely free of charge for exchange students. Each course will give

students 4 ECTS, as follows:

§ Written language (24h/semester), 4 ECTS credits

§ Oral language (24h/semester), 4 ECTS credits

§ Cultural options (20h/semester), 4 ECTS credits (from B1 level)

Classes are taught beginning with the A1 CEFR level in French to C1. This

is the main scheme for international exchange students.

 - Individual support

The University of Tours assists international exchange students prior to

their mobility with every administrative aspect related to their arrival in

France, from the online pre-registration, to the visa procedure (if

applicable), and facilitates their accommodation request in a public

student residency.

 - Visa – Campus France procedure for exchange students that are not

 European citizens (not a citizen of one of the 27 EU member states), or

 citizens of a Schengen / EEA country

 - Accommodation – housing request for public student residencies

 - Learning Agreement and online course catalogue

 - French language and culture classes

 - Academic calendar and timetable

 - Integration – we value the integration of exchange students, and

 different resources exist in order to facilitate it

 - Buddy System: a French student to support them soon after their

 arrival in Tours

 - Erasmus Student Network

 https://www.instagram.com/esntoursofficiel/: the association

 organizes cooking activities, international dinners, theme

evenings. The

 membership gives access to preferential rates for the cultural events

 organized by the international relations office of the UT and

gives them

 the right to have discounts with the partners of the

association (Ryanair,

 local stores…).

 - Cultural programme

 - International Relations Service organizes a great cultural

 program

 https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/welcome-to-ut/cultural-programme

 me for the students with visits to the chateaux of the Loire

 Valley and many other unmissable spots of the region and France.

 - In addition, the cultural service of the university organizes

 many cultural events and offers discounts to the students who have the

 cultural pass (opera, cinema, shows…).

 - Sports

§ Students have access to a wide variety of sports at the UT. They can

subscribe to the Pack’Sport and take up to 3 different sport classes a

week, absolutely free of charge! They can also do sports trainings during

week-ends on different themes (hiking at the Mont-Saint-Michel, canyoning,

skiing…) and attend sport events or wellness activities (badminton, fitness

night, rugby…).

o Orientation maps

§ A map of UT’s campuses, faculties, and student services

https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?mid=1Oe2Q_yuy9VbAkhtfCiHYJhzh8K8iYXA&usp=sharing

§ A map allowing students to discover the city

https://www.google.com/maps/d/viewer?mid=1KeCNJLFEccVbzUZTNfD3VfNAz-ktLv0&ll=47.38009226217868%2C0.688595800000007&z=13

from

an extracurricular point of view

· Our warm welcome

As a token of hospitality and deep interest in student welfare, UT welcomes

students individually upon their arrival to help them finalize their

registration, and give them all the practical information they need for

their settling in (presentation of the different useful university

services, organized events, information about the ESN, public

transportation, etc.). UT is available before, all along and after the

mobility to answer students’ questions.

Moreover, every September, the UT gathers many actors and welcome services

of international students in a single event, the International Students

Welcome Desk.

https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/admission-process-for-exchange-students

UT’s Welcome Desk team is here to direct and give students advice to ensure

a coordinated and efficient setup in Tours.

Useful information - Admission process for Exchange students

You will find detailed information on the admission process for exchange

students (registration, accommodation, visa, learning agreement) on: UT -

Admission process for Exchange students (univ-tours.fr)

https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/admission-process-for-exchange-students

Useful resources for partners and students - UT Promotional Materials

Please consult our official web page intended for partner institutions and

exchange students, where you will find our communication toolkits (PPT,

Fact sheet), a link to our online course catalogue for exchange students, a

list of supervised projects, as well as some information on French studies:

https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/about-ut/useful-documents-aimed-at-international-partners

 Interested students may contact Dr. Sainu Franco, International Relations

Officer, Vellore Institute of Technology, MB 105 and register your interest

on or before 10th May, 2026.

GOOD REASONS TO STUDY AT UT:

 - A multidisciplinary and dynamic university in the very heart of the

 city

 - An international city close to Paris, located in the Loire Valley

regulated sectors (government, BFSI). Identify technical friction points in

their current setups that make them prime targets for a CrowdStrike

sovereign cloud migration.

Competitive Intelligence (CI) team to develop technical battlecards, data

flow diagrams, and architectural comparisons specifically for the India

market. Equip our sales and solutions engineering teams with the technical

data needed to effectively challenge competitor claims.

and government solicitations. Analyze their technical prerequisites and

draft highly accurate, engineering-focused responses that align

CrowdStrike’s architecture with the buyer's strict sovereign computing

mandates.

microservices, and containerization. Note: Hands-on deployment experience

insights, model development, ML Engineering and Insights Activation. This

team is situated within the larger Data Platform group, which serves as one

of the core pillars of our company. We process data at a truly immense

scale. Our processing is composed of various facets including threat events

collected via telemetry data, associated metadata, along with IT asset

information, contextual information about threat exposure based on

additional processing, etc. These facets comprise the overall data

platform, which is currently over 200 PB and maintained in a hyper scale

Data Lakehouse, built and owned by the Data Platform team. The ingestion

mechanisms include both batch and near real-time streams that form the core

Threat Analytics Platform used for insights, threat hunting, incident

investigations and more.

 As an engineer in this team, you will play an integral role as we build

out our ML Experimentation Platform from the ground up. You will

collaborate closely with Data Platform Software Engineers, Data Scientists

& Threat Analysts to design, implement, and maintain scalable ML pipelines

that will be used for Data Preparation, Cataloging, Feature Engineering,

Model Training, and Model Serving that influence critical business

decisions. You'll be a key contributor in a production-focused culture that

bridges the gap between model development and operational success. Future

plans include generative AI investments for use cases such as modeling

attack paths for IT assets.

 supervised / unsupervised approaches: how, why, and when labeled data is

 created and used

 - Exposure to ML Platform tools like Jupyter Notebooks, NVidia

 Workbench, MLFlow, Ray, or Vertex AI through coursework, personal projects,

 or internships

 - Familiarity with data processing frameworks such as Apache Spark,

 Flink, or comparable tools through academic or personal projects. Exposure

 to Iceberg or similar table formats is a plus.

 - Foundational understanding of distributed computing and orchestration

 concepts (Kubernetes, Airflow, etc.) through coursework or self-directed

 learning

 - Awareness of infrastructure-as-code concepts such as Terraform, FluxCD

 through coursework, labs, or personal exploration

 - Strong proficiency in Python; exposure to Java/Scala is recommended.

 Ability to write clean, well-structured Python code and a willingness to

 learn how to provide standardized and simplified interfaces for data

Dear Student,

As per the curriculum requirements, students are expected to earn their

internship credits by completing a minimum of 28 days of training in a

domain-specific industry.

However, it is recognized that some students may not have the opportunity

to undertake the internship in an industry. In such cases, an alternative

pathway has been provided, allowing students to earn the required credits

by registering and successfully completing an approved certification course.

The following guidelines pertain to the certification courses offered and

the Internship Credit eligibility criteria. Please note that pursuing a

certification is entirely optional.

Credit Eligibility:

Only the professional proctored certification examination will be

considered for summer internship credit.

Course completion certificates will not be accepted under any circumstances.

Course Selection & Preference:

Students may take up to two courses; however, only one proctored

certification examination will be considered for internship credit. The

second course, if chosen, may be pursued for skilling or personal

development purposes.

Any course failing to meet the minimum threshold of 50 selections will be

discontinued.

Training and Payment:

Upon commencement of the course, students will have one week to complete

the payment. Within this period, students may switch to another course or

certification. Once the payment is made, the student is required to

continue with that particular certification. Students may attend the

one-week training session and proceed with payment upon satisfaction.

Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that the VIT Debate Society achieved notable

recognition at Manzar 2026, the annual flagship British Parliamentary (BP)

debating tournament hosted by the English Debating Society of Miranda

House, University of Delhi, held from 21–23 February 2026.

Manzar is one of the prominent debating tournaments on the Indian debating

circuit, bringing together leading debaters and adjudicators from various

institutions across the country. Representing VIT with distinction, our

participants engaged in rigorous rounds of parliamentary debate and

adjudication.

Achievement Secured:

 1. Shivansh Choukse (24MIS0266) – Adjudicator Break: Novice Semifinals,

 Open Pre-Quarterfinals, and Open Semifinals (Adjudicated 3 out of 4

 outrounds in the tournament)

This accomplishment highlights the analytical ability, debating expertise,

and adjudication excellence demonstrated by the members of the VIT Debate

Society on a prominent national debating platform.

We sincerely acknowledge the invaluable guidance and continuous support of

the Faculty Coordinator, Prof. Anil Premraj (Emp. ID: 12531), whose

mentorship significantly contributed to this achievement.

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to the VIT Debate Society on this

commendable achievement and wish them continued success in their future

endeavors.

Subject: Congratulations to Sriraam A V on Being Selected for the Amgen Scholars Program 2026 at Kyoto University, Japan
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Sriraam A V (23BCE0929) has been selected

for the Amgen Scholars Program 2026, where he will undertake a research

internship at Kyoto University, Japan.

The Amgen Scholars Program is a prestigious and fully funded

international research initiative sponsored by the Amgen Foundation,

offering outstanding undergraduate students the opportunity to conduct

advanced research at leading global universities. Notably, Sriraam is among

only 15 students selected globally for this program.

This achievement is particularly significant as Sriraam becomes the first

student from VIT to be selected for this distinguished program, marking an

important milestone for the university.

Kyoto University, one of Japan’s premier research institutions, is

currently ranked #2 in Japan and #57 globally (QS Rankings) and is widely

recognized for its academic excellence and contributions to groundbreaking

research.

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to Sriraam A V on this remarkable

achievement and wish him continued success in his research journey and

future endeavors.

Subject: Congratulations to Team Ojas Racing for their Achievement at Formula Student Concept Class (FSCC) 2025 - Formula Bharat
Body:

Student Concept Class (FSCC) 2025, an online competition organized by Formula

Bharat, held from 18th of October to the 22nd of November 2025.

technical and strategic assessments, including the Engineering Design

Subject: Outstanding Achievements of Biotechnology Students in Franco-Indian Twinning Program
Body:
Dear all,

Greetings!

We are pleased and delighted to share that three students from the M.Sc.

Biotechnology Franco-Indian Twinning Program have been selected to pursue

their Ph.D. studies in France. Two of these students are from the 2023

batch, and one is from the 2024 batch. All three have been awarded

prestigious fellowships (approximately €2000 per month) for a duration of

three years through highly competitive international grants funded by

the Government

of France.

Ms. Anisha Judith (2023–25 Phyto Batch) has been awarded the Eiffel

International Scholarship by Campus France. She will pursue her Ph.D. at

Claude Bernard University Lyon 1 under the guidance of Prof. Léa Payen and

Prof. Francesca Angileri, specializing in Cancer Biology and Toxicology

Ms. Ganga Girish (2023–25 Phyto Batch) has been awarded the INTERREG

Réunion Fellowship and has already commenced her Ph.D. at the University of

La Réunion. She began her doctoral research at CBST under my supervision as

part of an ongoing collaboration between VIT and the University of La

Réunion, in association with Prof. Christian Lefebvre d’Hellencourt and

Prof. Olivier Meilhac. Her research focuses on developing novel

therapeutics for cardiovascular diseases and stroke.

Ms. Varsha Gowri (2024–26 AI Batch) has also been awarded the Eiffel

International Scholarship by Campus France. She will pursue her Ph.D. at

the University of Poitiers under the supervision of Prof. Brigitte Vannier,

working in the area of disease biomarkers and bioinformatics.

I am also very happy to inform you that a total of 13 second-year M.Sc.

Biotechnology (Twinning Program) students and 4 second-year M.Tech.

Biotechnology Dual Degree students are currently undertaking their capstone

research projects in France. These students have secured fellowships and

travel grants through prestigious initiatives such as the Franco-Indian

Campus ILIADE Project, Erasmus+ mobilities, and the InnovoInOnco Graduate

Initiative

 We are thrilled to celebrate the remarkable achievement of our three

students, whose dedication, enthusiasm, and discipline have led to

outstanding success. This milestone fills us all with immense pride and

inspires confidence that many more students will continue to secure

opportunities at prestigious French institutions, bringing further laurels

to our institution.

Let’s continue to strive for excellence and make every moment count!

 I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to Our Beloved and

Honourable Chancellor, the top management, the core group, the Dean of

Academics, COE, Admissions, Director IR, Prof. Vijayalakshmi, Dr. V.

Krishnan, and all others who have been instrumental in the successful

execution of this twinning program. Their unwavering support, guidance, and

dedication have been pivotal in achieving these milestones and in

strengthening our international academic collaborations.

Subject: Congratulations to Team Deeps for Securing 1st Place at Chakravyuha 1.0
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Team Deeps secured 1st Prize in the

domain of Blockchain at Chakravyuha 1.0, conducted at Sri Sairam

Engineering College, Chennai, held on 24–25 March 2026, and received a cash

prize of ₹5,000.

Representing VIT, Team Deeps developed a project titled “CreatorChain –

Decentralized Creator Economy Platform”. The solution addresses challenges

related to digital content ownership, plagiarism, and transparent royalty

distribution. The platform enables creators to upload digital assets,

verify originality using hashing techniques, mint NFTs for ownership, and

receive automated royalty payments through smart contracts.

The team successfully implemented a fully functional blockchain-based

system integrating NFT minting, smart contract-based royalty distribution,

IPFS-based decentralized storage, and duplicate detection mechanisms, which

was highly appreciated by the judging panel.

Team Members:

Subject: Congratulations to Team Neuromotive for Securing 3rd Place at EV Battery Intelligence Challenge - Christ University, Bangalore
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Team Neuromotive secured 3rd Place at

the EV Battery Intelligence Challenge, a national-level hardware

innovation competition organized by VLSI System Design in collaboration

with the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC),

Thiruvananthapuram, and Christ University (Kengeri Campus), Bangalore.

The competition witnessed participation from over 300 teams across various

institutions in India and was conducted through three rigorous technical

rounds spanning more than one month, with multiple stages of evaluation and

elimination. Unlike conventional hackathons, the event required

participants to design and demonstrate a working embedded hardware system

using the VSDSquadron Ultra RISC-V development platform powered by the

indigenous THEJAS32 processor. The challenge focused on developing

innovative solutions to address real-world EV battery safety and monitoring

problems.

Representing VIT, Team Neuromotive developed an intelligent EV battery

monitoring system incorporating real-time diagnostics and embedded

intelligence. Through their innovative design and technical implementation,

the team secured 3rd Place in the competition and received a cash prize

of ₹25,000, along with a VSDSquadron Ultra development board and an

internship

opportunity.

Team Members:

 1. Dhakshana Bala S – 23BEC0212

 2. Abisek S – 23BEC0266

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to Team Neuromotive on this

commendable achievement and wish them continued success in their future

endeavors.

Dear Students,

We are pleased to invite all students of VIT to participate in the IANC

Design-Thon, organized in collaboration with Honeywell.

The competition features 10 problem statements across diverse domains in

the aerospace and defence sectors. For each problem statement, a dedicated

faculty advisor is assigned, who will serve as the single point of contact

for both administrative and technical queries.

Students are encouraged to form teams with interdisciplinary expertise,

wherever applicable. Each team can have a maximum of four members. Teams

may also choose to work on multiple problem statements.

Students are requested to visit the IANC website and navigate to Events →

Design-A-Thon – Honeywell. The problem statements are available within the

registration link.

Link: https://vit.ac.in/ianc/

Kindly complete your registration on or before 30 March 2026.

Registration Guidelines:

 -

 Registration must be completed as a team.

 -

 The team leader should register on behalf of all members.

 -

 Details of all team members must be included in the registration form.

 -

 All team members are required to make the payment individually.

 -

 The team leader must compile and upload all payment receipts as a single

 PDF file on the registration page.

 -

 Students who have already registered through the Google Form may edit

 their submission to upload the payment receipts.

Following registration, faculty advisors may conduct detailed briefing

sessions on their respective problem statements on 31 March 2026.

 -

In addition, 10 selected ideas (shortlisted by the Honeywell panel) will be

offered an 8-week student project opportunity at the college under

Shortlisting at the first level will be conducted at the institute level,

where the top 2–3 ideas from each category will be forwarded for final

evaluation.

This is a gentle reminder that the registration deadline is today. We

encourage all interested students to complete the registration at the

earliest.

Body:
Dear VITians,

Greetings from the Centre for VIT Happiness and Well Being!!!

Our heartfelt thanks to the VIT Management and Core group members for their

support and encouragement on taking our first initiative from the Centre to

promote positivity and well-being around the campus.

We express our sincere gratitude to our Founder & Honourable Chancellor,

Respected Vice Presidents, Executive Director, Assistant Vice President,

Vice Chancellor, Pro Vice Chancellor, and Registrar for their constant

support, guidance, and encouragement in organizing ‘International Happiness

Week’ on the theme of ‘Caring and Sharing’ from 20th to 26th March, 2026.

We had participants from the faculty, staff, research scholars and students

in our campus from various Schools and Centres who have not only enjoyed

the five days enriching experiential moments of music therapy, rejuvenate

and regenerate yoga wellness, dance therapy, art therapy and finally with

laughter therapy but also have requested to conduct many more such events

in future. We would like to thank all our participants whole heartedly who

have given time for themselves and enjoyed every moment with joy and

wellness.

Our heartfelt thanks to the Director -Event Management, Director, Assistant

Directors and Staff of Student Welfare along with the Students (Club

members) who are associated with the Student Welfare office, Assistant

Director-PRO & Outreach and Event Manager for their valuable support and

guidance in terms of their friendly coordination and helping in organizing

the weekly events.

We also thank Estates, CTS, Transport, Finance, Purchase, Central Stores,

Electricians present in different venues, Darling Canteen, and the Guest

House for their continuous assistance and coordination.

The success of the Happiness Week is a result of the collective effort,

commitment, dedication and enthusiasm of the Counselling team.

Finally, we would like to thank each and every VITians whose involvement

and cooperation made this event a grand success.

Happiness is not just a moment, but a practice. Our Centre thanks all of

you for participating whole heartedly by enjoying every moment in all our

events.

Subject: Student Innovation Project Contest 2026 - Registration Regarding
Body:
Dear Students,

 Greetings.

 The School of Computer Science and Engineering (SCOPE) is pleased to

announce the Student Innovation Project Contest 2026, an initiative aimed

at promoting innovation, creativity, and project-based learning among

students. The contest provides a platform for students to showcase their

technical ideas, prototypes, and interdisciplinary solutions that address

real-world problems using computing technologies.

Eligibility and Participation: The following criteria define who can

participate and the expectations for team composition and project nature:

• Students from B.Tech and Integrated M.Tech programmes are eligible to

participate

• Students from all years of SCOPE - currently working on real-time

projects, including those involving hardware integration, can apply.

• Faculty members guiding such projects are encouraged to motivate and

nominate eligible student teams for participation.

• Projects carried out as part of final year projects or any project-based

academic courses will not be considered. Only independent, innovative, and

real-time projects developed beyond regular curriculum requirements are

encouraged

• Each team can have a maximum of three members, and each team must have at

least one student from SCOPE.

Project Verticals: Projects should be aligned with one of the following

thematic areas reflecting core and interdisciplinary computing domains:

• Vertical 1: Artificial Intelligence, Data Science and Intelligent Systems

• Vertical 2: Secure, Scalable and Distributed Computing Systems

• Vertical 3: Interdisciplinary Computing and Human-Centered Innovations

Registration and Selection Process: The registration and evaluation

process is designed to ensure fair selection of high-quality and impactful

projects:

• Interested teams must register through the Google Form link:

https://forms.gle/WwTxd82T59wi2r6C9 https://forms.gle/WwTxd82T59wi2r6C9

• Deadline for submission of entries: 30.03.2026

• Projects will be evaluated by a faculty review committee based on:

Innovation and novelty, technical depth, Societal relevance, Implementation

quality

• Completeness of the solution, including the development of an end-to-end

system with components such as a functional user interface, hardware

integration where applicable, and practical deployment considerations

• Technology Readiness Level (TRL), with an expected minimum level of TRL 4

(technology validated in a lab environment) and preference for higher

levels such as TRL 5 to TRL 7 demonstrating validation and prototyping in

relevant or operational environments

• Approximately 20 projects will be shortlisted and shortlisted teams will

present and demonstrate their projects during the final event

Event Details: The final presentation and evaluation of shortlisted

projects will be conducted as per the following schedule:

• Date: 9th April 2026

• Time: 10:00 AM to 1:30 PM

• Venue: Main Foodys, VIT

Final presentations will be evaluated by a jury panel comprising an

industry expert and faculty members

Awards and Recognition: Outstanding projects will be recognized and

rewarded with cash prizes and certificates to encourage innovation and

excellence:

• First Prize: ₹12,000 • Second Prize: ₹8,000 • Third Prize: ₹5,000

Note: Awards will be provided as Amazon gift vouchers, and certificates

will be issued to all shortlisted participants.

Faculty guides of the final-level participants will be presented with a

memento

Students are strongly encouraged to take part in this contest and showcase

their innovative capabilities.

This is an excellent opportunity to gain recognition, enhance practical

exposure, and contribute to impactful technological solutions.

For any queries, please contact the event coordinators from SCOPE: Prof. N.

Yuvaraj & Prof. A K P Kovendan.

Best regards,

Organizing Team—Student Innovation Project Contest 2026.

With Regards,

Dr. N. Jaisankar, B.E., M.E., Ph.D

Subject: QS World University Rankings: by Subject 2026

Dear VITians,

Greetings

QS has released the World University Rankings by Subject 2026. VIT has made

a significant improvement again. In “Engineering and Technology” category,

VIT rank moved up to 119th this year from 142nd in 2025. Seventeen subjects

ranked this year as compared to fifteen in the last year. Two subjects

entered within the TOP 100 in the World: Computer Science & Information

Systems (86th, 6th in India, 24 positions up this year) and Electrical &

Electronics Engineering (87th, 6th in India, 88 positions up this year).

Four subjects are within the top 200 in the world - Mathematics (104th,

5th in India, 121 positions up this year), Material Science (137th, 7th in

India, 38 positions up this year), Mechanical, Aeronautical & Manufacturing

(148th, 8th in India, 77 positions up this year) and Data

Science & Artificial Intelligence (101-200, 7-8th in India). This is the

first time VIT subjects Civil & Structural Engineering and Arts &

Design entered into QS subject rank list.

QS ranks the subjects based on the reputation among academic leaders and

employers, citation per paper, H index and IRN (International Research

Network). The total weightage of academic reputation and employer

reputation is 70% (40% + 30%) in the “Engineering and Technology” category,

where our score has improved.

Let us thank the RAAC team for their tireless efforts. Thanks to our CDC

team, VITAA team, IR team and the faculty members for the significant

through their strong network worldwide.

Subject: International Happiness Day 2026 – Join the Celebration with Cultural Performances at Greenos!
Body:
Dear VITians,

The Office of Students' Welfare warmly invites you to a vibrant celebration

of the International Happiness Day 2026, brought to life through an

evening of spectacular cultural programs!

In celebration of the International Happiness Day 2026, established by the

UN to recognize happiness as a fundamental human goal, this year’s

theme, “Caring

and Sharing”, highlights kindness, connection, and the impact of social

media on well-being.

This special occasion is dedicated to spreading joy, positivity, and

togetherness across our campus. Experience an exciting showcase of talent,

diversity, and creativity as students come together to celebrate happiness

through music, dance, and artistic expression.

Get ready for an evening filled with energy, colors, and unforgettable

moments that reflect the true spirit of unity and joy at VIT.

Venue: Greenos

Time: 5:00 PM onwards

Date: 25th March, 2026

Let’s celebrate happiness together—through culture, connection, and

collective joy. Your presence will make the celebration even more

meaningful!

Today's Events by Clubs and Chapters:

 - Inithu Inithu

 - Happiness Through Nostalgia

 - Cultural Performances

 - International Happiness Day 2026 - Stalls

Tamil Literary Association

Event Name: Inithu Inithu

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 1:00 PM

Event Description: Inithu Inithu is a lively and engaging event designed to

spread joy, laughter, and positivity among students. The session includes a

variety of fun activities such as creative games like Green Screen,

interactive conversations about the stories behind students' smiles, and

sharing memorable moments connected to meaningful places. Participants will

also have the opportunity to write special notes to the world, expressing

thoughts that inspire happiness and strength.

Venue: PRP Annexe 302

Anokha NGOEvent Name: Happiness Through Nostalgia

Event Time: 10:30 AM - 1:00 PM

Event Description: The Happiness Through Nostalgia event celebrates the

International Day of Happiness through interactive activities like

dialogue-guessing games and a Kahoot quiz. By revisiting nostalgic movie

moments and shared memories, it promotes laughter, connection, and friendly

competition, creating a joyful and refreshing experience for students.

Venue: CBMR 203

SIGMA.XIEvent Name: Compliments & Mini Talent Showcase – Spread

Kindness, Share Your Spark

Event Time: 5:00 PM onwards

Event Description: This interactive event combines a Compliment Booth and a

Mini Talent Showcase to spread positivity and celebrate student creativity.

Participants can write and share kind compliments with others while also

enjoying short performances where students showcase their hidden talents

such as singing, dancing, poetry, comedy, or other unique skills. The event

aims to create a joyful and supportive environment that encourages

confidence, appreciation, and community bonding.

Venue: Greenos

SESI VIT

Event Name: International Happiness Day 2026 Celebrations - Stalls

Event Time: 5:00 PM onwards

Event Description: As part of Happiness Week, interactive stalls are set up

to spread joy and positivity. Participants can visit anytime to enjoy quick

fun activities, relax, and share cheerful moments. The stalls create a

lively space for connection, laughter, and refreshing breaks from routine,

leaving everyone with a happy and positive vibe.

Venue: Greenos

Enajori (ALA VIT)Event Name: International Happiness Day 2026

Celebrations - Stalls

Event Time: 5:00 PM onwards

Event Description: Celebrate joy at our Enajori (ALA VIT) Happiness Day

stall! Enjoy fun mini games like “Throw the Ball & Take a Dare,” the “Make

Us Laugh Challenge,” and classic marble games. Bring your friends, share

laughter, and create cheerful memories. Exciting surprises and smiles

await, along with small takeaways to brighten your day—because happiness

grows when shared. Join us at greenos from 5pm onwards and spread

positivity, one game at a time!

Venue: Greenos

Anokha NGOEvent Name: International Happiness Day 2026 Celebrations -

Stalls

Event Time: 5:00 PM onwards

Event Description: The Happiness Day Stall is an interactive space designed

to promote positivity and stress relief through fun activities.

Participants can engage in games like Burst Your Anger, Blindfold

Placement, Tissue Pop Dare, and Stack Your Mood, while also expressing

themselves through the Happiness Chart and Self-Care Chits. The stall aims

to create a cheerful atmosphere, encourage interaction, and spread smiles

among everyone.

Venue: Greenos

start date
.

Body:
Dear VITians

Greetings from the Centre for VIT Happiness and Well Being!

The Centre for VIT Happiness and Well Being proudly brings you this week of

joy and happiness based on the theme, “Caring, Sharing and Well Being." Art

therapy provides a safe and creative outlet for students to express their

thoughts and feelings, especially when verbal communication may be

challenging. We are pleased to introduce Individual Art Therapy Sessions as

part of our ongoing efforts to support your mental health and emotional

well-being.

Art therapy is a guided, one-on-one process that uses creative

expression—such as drawing, painting, and visual exploration—to help you

understand and manage your thoughts and emotions. It is especially helpful

if you are experiencing stress, anxiety, academic pressure, or simply wish

to explore yourself in a safe and confidential space. No prior artistic

skill or experience is required.

The International Office of the University of Applied Sciences

Zwickau, Saxony,

program.

The University of Applied Sciences Zwickau (WHZ) offers more than 60 degree

programs in the fields of Technology, Economics, Language, Healthcare and

Saxony and is one of the smaller cities. Because of its size, Zwickau has

affordable rents. But come and see for yourself!

Dear VITians,

In celebration of International Happiness Day 2026, initiated by the UN

to recognize happiness as a fundamental human goal, the 2026 observance

focuses on the theme of "Caring and Sharing" promoting kindness,

connection, and social media’s impact on well-being.

course.

Dear VITians,

Greetings from the Office of Students' Welfare!

We are delighted to invite you to join us in celebrating International

Women’s Day, a day dedicated to recognizing the strength, resilience, and

achievements of women across all walks of life, with this year’s theme

being “Give to Gain”.

The idea behind Give to Gain is simple yet powerful. When we give—whether

it is support, opportunities, mentorship, appreciation, or kindness—we

create a culture where everyone grows together while strengthening our

community. This Women’s Day, let us celebrate the spirit of generosity,

collaboration, and empowerment that helps individuals and organizations

thrive.

We are honoured to have Ms Linda. C. Sorto, Director of Boeing Engineering

Germany & Boeing Engineering Turkiye, as our Chief Guest and Ms. Divya

Amarnath, Vice President & HR Head, RedBus as our Guest of Honour, who will

grace the International Women's Day Celebration with their presence on 9th

March 2026 at 10:30 a.m. in Dr. Channa Reddy Auditorium and inspire us with

their thoughts and experiences.

Join us for an engaging and vibrant celebration filled with inspiring

conversations, meaningful reflections, and a shared commitment to building

a more inclusive and supportive environment.

Let’s come together to celebrate, uplift, and embody the true spirit of

Give to Gain.

We look forward to your presence and participation in making this

celebration truly special.

Dear Students,

The nominations and admissions for Fall 2026 at Fontys International

Business Studies are now open.

Fontys cluster Economics

Fontys schools are organised by their fields of study. This email focuses

on the cluster Economics and includes the following Fontys Schools:

 - Fontys International Business Studies (Venlo)

 - Fontys Economics (Tilburg)

 - Fontys Business and Communication (Eindhoven)

Please meet Dr Sainu Franco, O/o International Relations on or before 31st

March and fill in the nomination Excel file so that they can determine

which programme the student(s) would like to participate in.

If you would like to choose a school other than Fontys International

Business Studies, they need to check with the relevant programme

coordinator to see if they can accept you.

Programme offer for Fall 2026 

Find attached the Fontys International Business Studies programme. The

website

https://www.fontys.nl/en/Fontys-Study-Abroad/Fontys-Clusters/Cluster-Economics.htm

 provides additional information regarding the programmes of the schools

within the cluster Economics.

Please note that the schools are divided across three campuses in Venlo,

Eindhoven, and Tilburg. A combination of programmes and/or locations is not

possible.

Also included is the factsheet in the attachment.

In Venlo, they have launched an exciting new programme this semester.

Students looking for a 1st or 2nd semester programme are welcome to join

“Unlocking Global Business”.

A mix of International Business, International Finance & Control, and

Marketing Management related topics is now combined into a single

first-year programme. You can find more information in the attached

overview or on their website.

Non-fee-paying students can start the application process through the

link we will send them once their nomination has been accepted.

 Fee-paying students (free movers) will receive the application forms to

fill out and return to us once their nomination has been accepted.

Nomination deadline: 1 May 2026

Application deadline: 15 May 2026. Students must register in the online

application programme by this date. Documents can still be uploaded after

this date.

The exchange team is ready to answer any questions, so please do not

hesitate to contact exchangevenlo@fontys.nl

Dear Students,

Greetings from the VIT Model United Nations Society.

The Office of Students’ Welfare is pleased to invite you to participate in

the VIT Model United Nations Conference (VITMUN’26), which will be held

on the 27th, 28th, and 29th of March 2026 at Vellore Institute of

Technology.

VITMUN is one of the leading Model United Nations conferences in the South

Indian circuit. The conference provides a platform for students to step

into the role of global diplomats, deliberate on pressing international

issues, and work together to develop practical and sustainable solutions.

It also offers participants an opportunity to strengthen their public

speaking, negotiation, and research skills while engaging with students

from diverse institutions.

is available in the attached brochure and on the VITMUNSoc Instagram page

https://www.instagram.com/vitmunsoc/.

Body:
Dear All,

Greetings !

We are pleased and happy to inform you that our SBST student team from the

Integrated M.Sc. Biotechnology (2nd Year) participated in the 7th

International Conference on Genome Biology (ICGB-7) and the 57th Annual

Aqua-Terr Day held on 27th and 28th February 2026 at the School of

Biological Sciences, Madurai Kamaraj University, Madurai.

Health” and was awarded First Place in the poster competition.

We congratulate the students for their outstanding achievement and for

bringing pride to our department.

 hardest opening question without rambling.

Subject: Reminder: Navigating Your Career in Management
Body:
Dear Students,

When people hear "management," they often think of boardrooms and power

suits. But in reality, management is the engine behind every tech startup,

global NGO, and creative agency. It’s about solving complex problems,

leading teams, and turning ideas into scalable reality.

Whether you are an aspiring entrepreneur or simply curious about how

organizations actually work, we invite you to our upcoming session: "Careers

in Management: Paths, Skills, and Strategies."

Why Attend?

The world of management is vast, and it can be hard to know where you fit.

We’re breaking down the jargon to help you understand:

 -

 1) Detailed overview of the MBA curriculum and academic structure.

 2) Career opportunities across major management streams—finance,

 marketing, sales, operations, and HR.

 3) Understanding management degree options such as MBA, MIM, and

 deferred MBA programs.

 4) Key components of a strong academic and professional profile for MBA

 aspirants.

 5) Important considerations for MBA/MiM applications in India and abroad.
