PeintDigital – Digital Painting invites students into the world of

digital artistry, offering a creative space to illustrate ideas using

digital tools and modern design techniques. This event encourages

participants to experiment with colour palettes, lighting, textures, and

digital brushes to craft expressive and visually rich artworks. It aims to

nurture creativity in the digital medium, allowing emerging artists to

showcase their imagination, technical skill, and storytelling through

digital illustration.

Danse Éclatante – Solo Dance (Western) brings the energy and dynamism of

Western dance styles to PRIMA VERA’25, welcoming participants to perform

with confidence, creativity, and technical flair. Whether it’s

contemporary, hip-hop, jazz, ballet, or freestyle fusion, dancers are

encouraged to express individuality and innovation through their movements.

The event aims to provide a stage where performers can explore versatility,

push their artistic boundaries, and celebrate their unique style.

Taal Tarang – Solo Dance (Eastern) is a vibrant celebration of India’s

classical and traditional dance forms, inviting students to express rhythm,

grace, and cultural depth through movement. This event gives performers a

platform to bring their chosen style—be it classical, semi-classical, or

folk—to life with expressive storytelling and refined technique. It aims to

encourage dancers to embrace their heritage, explore fluidity and emotion,

and showcase their passion in an inspiring and artistic atmosphere.

Get ready to shine at the 6th edition of Prima Vera — our annual cultural

extravaganza packed with creativity, energy, and endless fun. This year’s

edition brings together a vibrant lineup of competitions, performances, and

showcases designed to highlight the incredible talents of our students.

Whether you’re stepping onto the stage, behind the lens, or into the

spotlight, Prima Vera’25 is your moment to express, explore, and excel.

Come be a part of the excitement, the artistry, and the unforgettable

memories waiting to be made!

Join us for an unforgettable celebration!

Body:
Dear VITians,

Greetings!

The Office of Students' Welfare invites you to spring into action on Day-2

as we dive into an exciting week filled with cultural vibrance. After long

schedules and academic fatigue, this is the perfect moment to unwind,

recharge, and rediscover the joy of campus life.

We proudly present the 6th edition of Prima Vera - a week-long cultural

festival celebrating the creativity, passion, and spirit of VIT’s dynamic

student community. Get ready for a series of thrilling competitions, each

designed to bring out your best and help you showcase your unique talents.

Expect energetic performances, artistic showdowns, and engaging events, all

culminating in an unforgettable cultural experience.

And yes — there are exciting cash prizes waiting for the winners, along

with the pride of taking center stage in one of VIT’s most anticipated

festivals.

Gear up, participate, cheer, and make Prima Vera’25 a celebration to

remember!

Day-2 Schedule

Imaginem MosaicAnime – Collage is a creative showcase in PRIMA VERA’25,

inviting students to assemble expressive artworks using mixed media

elements. This event encourages participants to blend textures, colours,

and imagery to craft meaningful visual stories. It celebrates imaginative

thinking while giving students a platform to explore artistic composition,

experiment with layering techniques, and present unique perspectives

through collage art.

Peinture – Painting is designed to inspire artists to bring their visions

to life through the vibrant medium of paint. This event welcomes

participants to explore diverse styles, techniques, and themes, offering

complete freedom to express emotions, ideas, and personal artistic

identity. It aims to nurture creativity among students by providing a

supportive space to experiment, innovate, and celebrate the beauty of

visual expression.

Mehfil-e-Mendhī – Mehndi Design celebrates the grace and intricacy of

traditional henna art, inviting participants to create detailed and

culturally inspired designs. This event encourages students to explore the

elegance of Mehndi patterns while showcasing precision, creativity, and

storytelling through motifs. It aims to promote artistic flair and cultural

appreciation, giving budding designers a platform to shine.

Maticraft – Clay Modelling invites students to step into the world of

three-dimensional creativity by sculpting unique forms using clay. This

event encourages participants to transform imagination into tangible

artistic pieces through shape, texture, and structure. It aims to inspire

hands-on experimentation and celebrate the craftsmanship and originality of

emerging student artists.

Visage d’Art – Face Painting transforms artistic imagination into live,

expressive canvases. This event invites participants to design striking

face-art concepts ranging from fantasy themes to vibrant abstract patterns.

It encourages creativity, colour exploration, and bold artistic expression

while providing a fun and supportive space for students to showcase their

talent.

Slice & Style – Vegetable Carving transforms everyday vegetables into

exquisite works of art. This event invites participants to demonstrate

creativity and precision through intricate carvings and decorative designs.

It encourages patience, fine craftsmanship, and artistic expression while

giving students a platform to explore a unique and skill-based art form.

Rhythmus Vivo – Beatboxing celebrates the dynamic art of vocal

percussion, inviting participants to create rhythmic beats, sound effects,

and musical patterns using only their voice. This event promotes

creativity, originality, and performance confidence, offering a stage for

students to push the boundaries of vocal skill. It aims to inspire young

performers to explore beatboxing as a powerful form of modern musical

expression.

Swar Sangam – Music Band (Eastern) highlights the richness of Eastern

musical traditions, inviting student bands to perform soulful and dynamic

compositions. This event encourages participants to explore classical,

semi-classical, and folk influences while blending melody and rhythm with

creativity. It aims to provide a stage for young musicians to express their

passion, connect with audiences, and celebrate the depth of Indian music.

Sonitas Unitas – Music Band (Western) brings the energy and vibrance of

Western music to PRIMA VERA’25, inviting bands to perform genres ranging

from rock and pop to jazz and indie. This event encourages participants to

showcase musical innovation, stage presence, and teamwork. It serves as a

platform for budding performers to express their individuality and

celebrate the global language of music.

Get ready to shine at the 6th edition of Prima Vera — our annual cultural

extravaganza packed with creativity, energy, and endless fun. This year’s

edition brings together a vibrant lineup of competitions, performances, and

showcases designed to highlight the incredible talents of our students.

Whether you’re stepping onto the stage, behind the lens, or into the

spotlight, Prima Vera’25 is your moment to express, explore, and excel.

Come be a part of the excitement, the artistry, and the unforgettable

memories waiting to be made!

Join us for an unforgettable celebration!

Body:
Dear VITians,

Greetings!

The Office of Students' Welfare invites you to spring into action on Day-1

as we dive into an exciting week filled with cultural vibrance. After long

schedules and academic fatigue, this is the perfect moment to unwind,

recharge, and rediscover the joy of campus life.

We proudly present the 6th edition of Prima Vera - a week-long cultural

festival celebrating the creativity, passion, and spirit of VIT’s dynamic

student community. Get ready for a series of thrilling competitions, each

designed to bring out your best and help you showcase your unique talents.

Expect energetic performances, artistic showdowns, and engaging events, all

culminating in an unforgettable cultural experience.

And yes — there are exciting cash prizes waiting for the winners, along

with the pride of taking center stage in one of VIT’s most anticipated

festivals.

Gear up, participate, cheer, and make Prima Vera’25 a celebration to

remember!

Day-1 Schedule

Eshi no Sekai – Anime Drawing Competition is a highlight of PRIMA

VERA’25, inviting freshers to showcase their creativity and passion for

anime art. This competition provides a platform for new students to express

their imagination, experiment with styles, and demonstrate their drawing

skills in a supportive and inspiring environment. It aims to encourage

budding artists to step forward, celebrate their talent.

Kalligraphia – Calligraphy Competition (Solo Event) is one of the

signature contests of PRIMA VERA’25, designed to encourage freshers to

explore the elegance and discipline of artistic lettering. The competition

invites new students to express creativity through strokes, curves, and

handcrafted scripts, giving them a platform to showcase their precision,

style, and imagination. It aims to nurture emerging talent and help

freshers discover the beauty of calligraphy.

Rekha Kalā – Pencil Sketching Competition is an engaging contest under

PRIMA VERA’25, created to inspire freshers to explore the art of sketching

through lines, shades, and imagination. This competition encourages new

students to express their creativity using the simplicity of a pencil,

showcasing their ability to capture ideas, emotions, and forms with

precision. It serves as a platform for budding artists to discover their

potential, refine their skills.

Lux et Imago – DSLR Photography Competition is an exciting feature of

PRIMA VERA’25, inviting freshers to step behind the lens and capture the

world through their unique perspective. This competition encourages new

students to explore light, composition, and storytelling through

photography, allowing them to express creativity and emotion in every

frame. It serves as a platform for budding photographers to showcase their

talent, experiment with techniques, and become part of VIT’s dynamic and

artistic community.

 Pixel Tales – Mobile Photography Competition is a vibrant and inclusive

contest under PRIMA VERA’25, encouraging freshers to capture creative

stories using nothing more than their mobile phones. This event empowers

new students to explore framing, lighting, and spontaneous moments, proving

that great photography doesn’t require professional gear—just vision and

imagination. It serves as an inviting platform for budding photographers to

showcase their perspective, experiment with mobile techniques.

 Swar Saaz – Solo Vocal (Eastern) Competition is a distinguished musical

event under PRIMA VERA’25, inviting freshers to showcase their talent in

classical and semi-classical Eastern vocal music. This competition

encourages new students to express their voice, emotion, and artistry

through traditional melodies, offering them a stage to perform with

confidence and grace. It aims to nurture budding singers, celebrate the

richness of Eastern music, and welcome freshers into VIT’s vibrant cultural

and performing arts community.

 Vocal Virtuoso – Solo Vocal (Western) Competition is an electrifying

musical highlight of PRIMA VERA’25, inviting freshers to showcase their

talent in Western singing styles. This event encourages new students to

explore genres such as pop, rock, jazz, soul, and contemporary music,

giving them the space to express individuality, stage presence, and vocal

range. It provides a platform for budding performers to shine, build

confidence, and become part of VIT’s dynamic and diverse performing arts

community.

Get ready to shine at the 6th edition of Prima Vera — our annual cultural

extravaganza packed with creativity, energy, and endless fun. This year’s

edition brings together a vibrant lineup of competitions, performances, and

showcases designed to highlight the incredible talents of our students.

Whether you’re stepping onto the stage, behind the lens, or into the

spotlight, Prima Vera’25 is your moment to express, explore, and excel.

Come be a part of the excitement, the artistry, and the unforgettable

memories waiting to be made!

Join us for an unforgettable celebration!

Subject: Student Nominations are Open - Fields-Mitacs Undergraduate Summer Research Program @ Toronto, Canada
Body:
Dear Students,

The Fields-Mitacs-Undergraduate Summer Research Program nominations are now

open. As this is a new initiative, MScAC @ Dept. CompSci will facilitate

FUSRP nominations getting to Fields. As such, students do not need to use

the regular application link on the FUSRP website. Interested students may

meet Dr Sainu Franco in person in the IR Office (Main Building 105) on or

before the 15th of December.

Program Overview

The Fields Undergraduate Summer Research Program (FUSRP) is an annual

program that provides competitive funding supporting undergraduate research

at the Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences. The

program welcomes carefully selected undergraduate students from around the

world for a rich mathematical research experience, matching groups of up to

four or five excellent students with faculty from Fields Principal

Sponsoring or Affiliate Universities, visiting scientists, or researchers

in industry.

The Fields-Mitacs-India FURSP program is a component of the FURSP program

which partners with Mitacs, the Department of Computer Science at the

University of Toronto, and several universities in India.

Program Duration: 9 weeks, 1 June - 31 July

Program Location: Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences,

Toronto, Ontario

Program Goal: To provide a high-quality and enriching mathematics

research experience for undergraduates, fostering enthusiasm for continued

research through project experience, quality mentorship, and collaborative

teamwork.

Application Timeline:

Student application/institution nomination period: December 2 - January 4

(5pm ET) - all application materials, including references should be

submitted to the MScAC team. Institutions should choose two male and two

female students to put forward.

First round offers: January 28 - February 11 (selected candidates receive

offers and have two weeks to decide)

Second round offers: February 12 onward (rolling offers continue until the

program is filled)

Student evaluation rubric:

 - Transcript - academic performance (minimum GPA is usually 85%),

 relevant coursework and grade trends

 - References - quality of 2 best letters from a maximum of 3 submitted;

 assessment of research potential, work ethic, and interpersonal skills

 - CV/Resume - quality, relevance of experience, research exposure,

 extracurricular involvement

 - Cover letter: clear interest in the project, fit with the project,

 communication skills, motivation.

Student funding and support:

Mitacs Globalink provides funding to selected students, up to a maximum of

$8,000. This funding includes:

 - Roundtrip airfare of up to $1800, as well as associated ground travel

 - Housing and meal cost of $550/week

 - Health insurance costs

The Fields Institute hosts and provides support to the research projects,

including:

 - Coordinating research projects contributed by researchers at DCS and

 across the network, as well as associated professional development and

 We are pleased to be able to announce that the dates of the King’s College

London Summer School 2026, as well as the pricing and the modules we have

curated for the coming year are now confirmed.

Session 1 (6-17 July 2026)

Data Analysis for Business & Finance

Subject: India–UK Workshop on Developing Future Researchers (DFR 2025) – VIT, 15 December 2025 – Reg.
Body:
Dear Research Scholars and students,

We are pleased to inform you that the India–UK Workshop on Developing

Future Researchers: Designing and Demonstrating Research Impact (DFR 2025)

will be held as per the details below:

Date: 15 December 2025

Time: 10:00 AM – 05:00 PM

Venue: Rajaji Hall, Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT), Vellore

This one-day international workshop is jointly organised by the School of

Mechanical Engineering (SMEC), in collaboration with Sponsored Research and

Industrial Consultancy (SpoRIC) and the Teaching Learning Centre of

Excellence (TLCE). The event is supported by SPARC (India), the EPSRC

IAA/UKIERI Programme, the British Council, the Royal Society of Edinburgh,

and the Erasmus Mundus Programme.

About the Workshop

The workshop aims to equip Master’s students and early-stage Ph.D.

researchers with essential skills to:

 -

 Design research projects with measurable impact

 -

 Structure competitive research proposals

 -

 Visualise and communicate research outcomes effectively

 -

 Understand pathways for successful doctoral progress

Sessions will be led by eminent experts from VIT, Heriot-Watt University

(UK), IIT Kanpur, ARCI, CSIR-CSIO, CeNS, and other leading institutions.

Eligibility

 -

 Final-year Master’s students aspiring for Ph.D. admission

 -

 Early-stage Ph.D. scholars

 -

 Faculty members

Note: Participation is restricted to 50 internal candidates to ensure

high-quality interaction and engagement.

Application Process

Interested candidates must submit a 100-word Statement of Interest

describing:

 -

 Why they wish to attend, and

 -

 How the workshop will benefit their research career.

Registration Link:

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc_E8klYLvItwH9qp7Wl9M3F_YieDCpQNxHSq-ClSzobzWuHA/viewform

Submission Deadline: 5 December 2025, 5:00 PM (IST)

Selected participants will be notified by 8 December 2025, along with the

detailed programme schedule.

Please find the attached brochure for more information.

Subject: Congratulations to Team iGEM - VIT Vellore for Winning Silver Medal at iGEM 2025 | Paris, France
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Team iGEM - VIT Vellore has brought great

pride to our institution by securing the Silver Medal at the International

Genetically Engineered Machine (iGEM) Competition 2025, held at the Paris

Convention Centre, France, from October 28–31, 2025.

The iGEM Grand Jamboree is the world’s largest synthetic biology event,

bringing together students and researchers from over 50 countries to

design innovative biological systems addressing real-world challenges. The

competition, organized by the iGEM Foundation, promotes global

collaboration and innovation in synthetic biology toward a more sustainable

and resilient future.

This year, Team iGEM - VIT Vellore’s project focused on developing

a sustainable and cruelty-free alternative to ambergris through microbial

biosynthesis of ambrein, showcasing an outstanding combination

of scientific innovation and environmental responsibility. Among 400+

international teams, the team’s excellence was recognized with the Silver

Medal, celebrating their technical rigor, creativity, and commitment to

sustainability.

Subject: University of Queensland (UQ), Australia and the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi) Research Academy Call for applications / Expression of Interest for Joint PhD programme July 2026
Body:
Dear Students,

The University of Queensland (UQ), Australia and the Indian Institute of

Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi) have announced the opening of Expressions of

Interest (EOI) for their prestigious Joint Doctor of Philosophy (PhD)

Programme, commencing in July 2026.

The collaborative programme offers candidates the opportunity to undertake

cutting-edge research under the supervision of leading academics from both

institutions, while experiencing the academic environments of India and

Australia. Graduates will be awarded a joint PhD degree from UQ and IIT

Delhi upon successful completion.

Applications are invited from exceptional candidates across diverse

disciplines including Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics,

Humanities, and Social Sciences. EOIs can be submitted online until 7:00

PM (IST) on Wednesday, 7 January 2026, via the official website:

https://uqiitd.org/study.

Prospective students are encouraged to participate in the upcoming online

information session on 10 December 2025 (registration link) to learn more

about the programme structure, eligibility, and application process.

The UQ–IIT Delhi Joint PhD Programme exemplifies the growing commitment

between Australia and India to promote high-impact research collaborations,

foster innovation, and strengthen academic ties.

Landing (eVTOL) vehicles—future “flying taxis.” This field is rapidly

evolving in Europe, the US, and China, offering exceptional academic and

career opportunities.

 Former Indian students from the lab will help with task-specific

Subject: FALL SEMESTER 2025-26 THEORY FAT INSTRUCTIONS
Body:
Dear Students,

INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS APPEARING FOR FALL SEMESTER 

 2025-26 THEORY FAT

General Instructions

· Students must enter the examination hall 15-30 Minutes before

the commencement of examination (between 9.00 - 9.15 AM )

· You need to WEAR Student IDENTITY CARD during the ENTIRE

EXAMINATION PERIOD. If you don’t have a Proper ID Card contact the

Registrar Office and apply for a new one and get it before coming to the

Exam. The ID card should be scratches free with a proper tag. Exchange of

ID cards or Tags will be considered as Malpractice. If you have misplaced

your ID card or forgot to bring it to the Examination Hall, Report to the

Control Room (PRP 115/SJT G01/TT 104) of your test venue to get One Time

Permit Slips. You need to pay Rs. 100 through V-TOP online payment only.

· You will NOT be permitted to use the toilet/washroom during the

examination, so be prepared for it.

· Exchange of Calculators, Stationeries, Code Books, pen, pencil

etc., are not permitted. The code Books or standard tables should have been

signed by either the faculty or School office. No markings of any kind

should be found in such booklets.

· As per VIT rules, even if you keep your mobile phone/smart watch

in a switched off position inside the examination hall, it will be treated

as examination malpractice. Such malpractices will lead to confiscation of

the devices (including SIM card) for one semester and ’N’ grade (ALL PAPER

ZERO) in all the registered courses including lab & project components in

that semester. Hence, before entering the examination hall, students should

check their pockets thoroughly to avoid carrying mobile phones/smart

watches by mistake.

· Possession of any Electronic Gadget (Mobile Phone, Smart Watch,

Bluetooth device, any device embedded with scanner /camera, etc.), holding

chit papers/ suspicious content in the examination hall is considered as

malpractice.

 A. Pre-Exam Activities

1.

Note down your seating arrangement (Building, Room Number and Seat Number)

from the V-TOP students login. Seating arrangement will not be displayed

for courses in which a student has been debarred. Please report yourself

half an hour prior to the exam. No student would be permitted to enter the

hall after 9.15 AM.

2.

Possession of unauthorised material, even if you do not intend to use it

will be considered as malpractice. Before starting the exam, check any

materials written on desks or walls, or found papers nearby/ around you in

the floor and inform the same to the invigilators.

B. During the exam

1.

Candidate has to sit in the allotted seat only. Listen to the invigilator

and follow their instructions at all times. Strict Silence should be

maintained in the examination hall. Discussions/ communications of any kind

inside the exam hall are treated as examination malpractices.

2.

Check the class number in the Question paper with the Attendance sheet

Class Number. If you have not received the right question paper or

incomplete or badly printed, please contact the invigilator immediately. If

you have any doubt on class number, course name, course code, slot, and any

other details related to your question paper, please check while signing in

the attendance sheet.

3.

Read carefully and follow the instructions printed in the question paper

and in the answer booklet.

4.

Fill required details (Register No., course code, course title etc.) in the

answer booklet before you start writing the exam. After signing in the

attendance sheet, check the barcode sticker pasted on your answer booklet

for its correctness as your answer booklets will be scanned for valuation

using this barcode only.

5.

First clearly write the Question number in the space provided and then

start writing your answers. USE BLUE / BLACK PEN ONLY for writing the

Answers. Writings on any thin pens, / light colours may not be visible on

the scanned images used for evaluation. Remember to write the answers

within the space provided in the answer booklet. If you write anything

outside the margin, it will be cut during the scanning process. If you are

using extra sheets like graph sheets / templates given by faculty, write

your answer booklet number alone on the top left edge outside the margin

and keep it immediately after the first sheet. Do not fold it as it needs

to be scanned for valuation. Do your rough work in the last page of the

main answer booklet itself. Before finishing the exam, strike out all the

rough works.

6.

Don’t write anything in the question paper or in your hand or leg or on a

desk or on walls nearby you.

7.

Correcting pens, fluid or tape and erasable pens are not to be used for

corrections in the answer booklet.

8.

Do not discuss / borrow anything with other candidates during the

examination.

9.

Do not get involved in any unfair or dishonest practice during the exam. If

you try to cheat or break the rules in any way, it will invite appropriate

sanctions under malpractice.

10.

Students are not allowed to ask questions of any kind during the

examination. Invigilators have been instructed not to answer any enquiry

whatsoever relating to the question papers, whether an explanation or

meaning or correction or typographical error

11.

On the day of the exam, if you feel that you are affected by ill health,

please contact the Chief Superintendent or Invigilator. You can write the

examination at the Health Centre.

12.

Do not leave the examination hall until told to do so by the invigilator.

You cannot leave the examination hall until 30 min from the start of the

examination. If any student leaves the exam hall before 12.00 noon, he/she

has to submit the question paper along with answer sheet.

13.

Do not take your answer booklets or unused ones, from the examination hall.

It is a serious Malpractice.

14.

Answer booklet contains 42 pages and no additional sheets, no threads,

will be provided. 

C. If booked under Malpractice

1.

Be calm and give a written response to the allegation and follow the

instructions from the exam squad / Invigilator / Asst. CS / CS.

2.

Do not indulge in any disrespectful activities such as shouting / creating

/ diverting attention of all other students, a scene in the examination

hall.

3.

Hand over the materials and get a receipt for electronic devices.

NON-COOPERATION WILL BE VIEWED AS AN ACT OF INDISCIPLINE WHICH MAY INVITE

SEPARATE DISCIPLINARY ACTION.

4.

Examination malpractice actions/punishments are very serious, may lead to

All paper ZERO or suspension of one semester. All malpractice actions are

informed to the students / published in VTOP student Login. Please go

through it follow the examination rules appropriately

5.

OBEY ALL THE EXAMINATION RULES SERIOUSLY

With Regards

Prof.S.Sivabalan Ph.D

Controller of Examinations

Vellore Institute of Technology ( VIT)

Vellore 632014, TN, India

Subject: Congratulations to Rohit N for Achievement under PRISM Scheme - DSIR
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Rohit N (21MID0138), a final-year student

of M.Tech. (Integrated) – Computer Science and Engineering with

Specialization in Data Science, has achieved a remarkable milestone under

the PRISM Scheme (Promoting Innovations in Individuals, Start-ups, and

MSMEs) of the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR),

Ministry of Science & Technology, Government of India.

His project titled “Autonomous Bee Hives” has been selected under

the Student

Innovator category with a total approved budget of Rs. 5,00,000.

Rohit.N has officially received the Grant Sanction Order for his first

installment from Dr. Sarika Madan, Scientist ‘E’, DSIR, at the Ministry

of Science & Technology, Technology Bhawan, New Delhi on 25th August 2025.

We also acknowledge the invaluable guidance and mentorship of Dr.

Kannadasan R [Emp ID: 12378], Associate Professor (Grade 1), School of

Computer Science and Engineering (SCOPE), under whose supervision the

project was developed and submitted for the PRISM grant.

This outstanding achievement reflects the spirit of innovation and

technological excellence nurtured at VIT and brings immense pride to the

institution.

Heartiest congratulations to Rohit N for this prestigious recognition from

the Government of India.

Standards Club VIT

Event Name: CASA: Standards for Healthier

Event Time: 10:00 AM - 11:00 AM

Event Description: The Standards Club of VIT, under the Office of Students'

Welfare, presents CASA - Standards for Healthier Tomorrow, an awareness

event focusing on the importance of standards in promoting health, safety,

and well-being. CASA (Campaign Against Substance Abuse) aims to educate

session will emphasize the role of standardization in ensuring product

event brings together brilliant minds to share stories, laughter, and

cosmic energy! Get ready for an inspiring alumni talk, an engaging

discussion, and a lively "Then & Now" segment packed with surprises and

interactive moments. It's a celebration of memories, connections, and the

shared passion that keeps us all orbiting the same stars.

connects numbers with nature and shows how math can truly make a difference.

https://www.instagram.com/mathverse_vit?igsh=a3o5NTFqaHZncGQw

define a nation’s progress. InfraQuest is an Instagram quiz event by

construction timelines. From record-breaking bridges to world-class transit

systems, test your knowledge of the projects that are transforming the

infrastructure landscape of India.

Venue: Instagram Stories

discover how performance changes with stress and learn to identify their

students can use to find their ideal concentration level—just in time for

exam season.

Venue: TT204

pathways to recovery and support.

Subject: Congratulations to Asmita Pal for setting World Records at the Global Mental Math Olympiad 2025 held in Dubai!
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Ms. Asmita Pal (Reg. No. 23BCE2200) has

brought immense pride to VIT Vellore by achieving remarkable success and

setting multiple world records at the Global Mental Math Olympiad (GMMO)

2025 and the Live Math World Record Events held in Dubai on 1st and

2nd November 2025.

Competing among participants from over 15 countries including Malaysia,

Japan, India, Romania, Bangladesh, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, the USA,

Spain, South Africa, Zimbabwe, Mauritius, Nigeria, and Seychelles, Asmita

demonstrated exceptional mental agility and mathematical precision.

World Record Performances (3-minute time limit):

· Perfect Square Root of 6-digit Numbers – 88 correct answers

· 3-Digit ± 2-Digit Mixed Operations – 130 correct answers

· 2-Digit + 2-Digit Addition – 137 correct answers

Asmita also secured top ranks in multiple Olympiad categories:

· 1st Rank – Standard Mandatory Challenge (Perfect score: 1000/1000 in

4.40 minutes)

· 1st Rank – Addition–Subtraction (5-minute event)

· 2nd Rank – Multiplication event

Her exceptional performances highlight precision, consistency, and

determination on the global stage.

We congratulate Ms. Asmita Pal on this extraordinary accomplishment and

appreciate her for proudly representing VIT Vellore at an international

platform.

Body:
VIT faculty and Students,

We invite you all to the Faculty and Student Interactive Session "Learning

by Doing" , by Dr Manish Jain , Professor,IIT Gandhinagar.

Topic: Learning by Doing - Transistor to Transformation

Date: 07/11/2025( FRIDAY)

Time: 10.00AM to 01.00PM

Venue : Gallery I

OD will be given to all the students who attended.

These are the highlights of the talk.

Inspiring NextGen Hardware Innovators: Project Madhava: From Transistor to

Transformation

Along with cutting-edge semiconductor chips, the most significant strategic

vulnerability and possibly a largest market opportunity in India —lies in

the high-volume, low-margin (HVLM) chips that power 99% of everyday

electronics. True self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) will be achieved by

winning this foundational market, but we face a critical bottleneck: a

systemic failure in our educational pipeline. We are producing graduates

who are rich in theory but poor in the practical, hands-on skills required

to design, test, and build the hardware that startups need to innovate.

This talk outlines a scalable, "learning by doing" framework designed to

solve this talent gap at its root, building an 'army of creators' for the

HVLM ecosystem.

Having implemented a 8 Bit RISC processor (with 23 7400 IC's), multipliers,

Tetris with Indigenous VEGA processor, Center for Creative Learning

IITGandhinagar, is designing Hands-on Hardware program at scale (1L

students) for High Schools and Colleges called Project Madhava. Using CCL

designed Courses, Kits, Video, Workshops, students will get their hands

dirty making their own clocks, calculators, displays,

microprocessors/controllers and products they see in daily life.

In the talk professor will share learnings from running one of India's

largest STEM lab and program India, sending its STEM content to 200,000

schools , working with over 6L subscribers and 11CR views, via hugely

popular online programs 3030 EKLAVYA and Curiosity.

Dr. M.R. Murali, PhD

Dr. Murali has more than 17 years of professional experience in both

industry and academia. He is a regulatory toxicologist at MDR Laboratories

with extensive experience in preparing biological evaluation plans,

biological evaluation reports, addressing regulatory queries, and

performing toxicological risk assessments for all classes of devices for

submission to several notified bodies and regulatory agencies. He is

technically proficient in the ISO 10993 series of standards, ISO 18562

(2024), ISO 7405, implementation of FDA guidance on ISO 10993 (2023), and

Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (EU MDR). Dr. Murali obtained his PhD from the

University of Madras. He has worked with Kemin Industries and Laila

Pharmaceuticals, where he was involved in the design and execution of

preclinical studies and in preparing documents for regulatory submissions.

He also has post-doctoral research and academic experience at the

University of Malaya, Malaysia, enhancing his knowledge and skills in the

field of biomaterials which have the potential for further advancement as

medical devices. He has published over 40 articles in reputed international

journals and has also authored a patent and a book chapter.

Body:
Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s 5th November 

events.

Today's Events:

 - Deep Dive: The legacy of Rolls Royce

 - Aviation Cyber Resilience

 - Alumni Talk: The Champions Way

 - SDG-Sustain-a- Soil

 - Alumni talk: Beyond Borders: A biotech journey

 - MLOps Mastery

 - MLOps Decode

 - SDG: Zero Waste Cooking

 - Flutter Beats

 - CASA: Empower, Educate, Eradicate

 - CASA - Stronger Without Substance

 - Creativity meets curiosity

 - Inside PCB Design

 - SDG: Innovate for Impact

 - CASA: Mind Over Matter

 - Outreach: Electrofest 2.1

 - CASA: Addiction - Awareness and Recovery

 - SDG:Greenovate

Scroll down for more details

Society of Automotive engineers

Event Name: Deep Dive: The legacy of Rolls Royce

Event Time: 07:30 PM - 08:30 PM

Event Description:Join SAE VIT on 5th November from 7:30 PM to 8:30 PM for

Deep Dive: The Legacy of Rolls Royce. Explore the brand journey from its

historic beginnings to its modern innovations in luxury and engineering.

Discover how Rolls Royce became a global symbol of excellence,

craftsmanship, and timeless design. Tune in live on Google Meet for an

insightful session celebrating the spirit of automotive perfection.

Venue: Google Meet

Registration: VTOP

Instagram: http://goog_1306337256

https://www.instagram.com/sae_vit?igsh=dnJ2eG5pNWt4YnMz

Society of Automotive engineers

Event Name: Aviation Cyber Resilience

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 01:00 PM

Event Description:Experience the world of aviation security like never

before at Aviation Cyber Resilience, live on 5th November from 11:00 AM to

1:00 PM. Dive into the critical challenges of protecting Air Traffic

Management, onboard avionics, and ground operations from evolving cyber

threats. Engage with insights that reveal how the skies are kept safe in

the digital age and why cyber resilience is now a pillar of modern aviation.

Venue: Google Meet

Registration: VTOP

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/sae_vit?igsh=dnJ2eG5pNWt4YnMz

Yoga Club

Event Name: Alumni Talk: The Champions Way

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 01:00 PM

Event Description: Alumni Talk: The Champion’s Way is an inspiring session

where distinguished alumni share their journeys of perseverance, growth,

and success. Through personal stories and valuable insights, they motivate

students to embrace challenges, stay focused, and pursue excellence in

every endeavor.

The Champion’s Way encourages learners to adopt a winning mindset,

combining hard work, resilience, and self-belief. The session serves as a

bridge between experience and aspiration, guiding students to carve their

own paths toward achievement and fulfillment.

Venue: TT620

Registration: VTOP

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/vit_yoga_club/?next=%2F

AIChE-VIT

Event Name: SDG-Sustain-a- Soil

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 02:00 PM

Event Description:Sustain-A-Soil is a research-driven event where

participants design an eco-friendly fertiliser blend that enhances plant

growth while minimising environmental harm. Using agricultural data and

scientific references, teams must justify their sustainable formulation and

present it through a concise PowerPoint pitch, aligning with SDG 2 (Zero

Hunger) and SDG 15 (Life on Land).

Venue: SMV 110

Registration: VTOP

Instagram link :

https://www.instagram.com/aiche_vit/?hl=en

Facebook link:

https://www.facebook.com/aichevit/

LinkedIn link:

https://www.linkedin.com/in/aiche-vit-student-chapter/

The Biotech Research Society India

Event Name: Alumni talk: Beyond Borders: A biotech journey

Event Time: 19:00 AM - 11:30 PM

Event Description: Join us for an engaging session with Mr. Kumar Aavula,

VIT alumnus (M.Tech Biotechnology, 2011–2013) and Postdoctoral Researcher

at Harvard Medical School. In this interactive talk, he will share his

academic journey from VIT to Harvard and offer valuable insights into

pursuing higher education abroad. Learn how to choose the right country,

university, and research field amid changing visa regulations and global

trends. This session will guide aspiring biotechnology students toward

making informed decisions about their international career paths.

Venue: SMV121

Registration: VTOP

Instagram link: https://www.instagram.com/brsivitvellore/?hl=en

Facebook link: https://www.facebook.com/brsivitvellore/

The institution of Engineering and Technology

Event Name: MLOps Mastery

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 01:00 PM

Event Description: In today's AI driven world, building a machine learning

model is just the beginning - deploying, managing, and maintaining it at

scale is where the real challenge begins. MLOps Mastery bridges the gap

between data science and production engineering through hands-on

experience. Discover how to take models from research to real-world

deployment while ensuring stability, performance and continuous

improvement. Join us for a workshop that blends theory and practical

insights.

Venue: SJT 101

Registration: VTOP

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ietvit

The institution of Engineering and Technology

Event Name: MLOps Decode

Event Time: 02:00 PM - 08:00 PM

Event Description: Think you’ve mastered MLOps? Time to put your skills to

the test! MLOps Decode is an exciting, fast-paced quiz that dives into the

world of Machine Learning Operations from pipeline automation and CI/CD to

model monitoring and drift detection. Based on concepts from the MLOps

Mastery workshop, this interactive quiz will challenge your understanding

and help you uncover new insights into real-world AI workflows. Get ready

to decode, compete and learn!

Venue: Google Forms

Registration:VTOP

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ietvit

Culinary Club

Event Name: SDG: Zero Waste Cooking

Event Time: 10:30 AM - 01:00 PM

Event Description: A cooking event where participants would be challenged

to make a salad out of the ingredients provided to them with minimal waste.

This event is to promote Responsible Consumption and Production.

Venue: SJT Foodys

Registration: VTOP

Instagram: http://goog_1306337282

https://www.instagram.com/culinaryclubvit?igsh=bWY5dDVmbWNtaGlw

Computer Society of India VIT

Event Name: Flutter Beats

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 01:00 PM

Event Description: Join us for 'Flutter Beats', A hands-on workshop

designed to introduce students to Flutter app development by building a

simple, fully functional music player. Guided by our speaker, participants

will explore Flutter widgets, audio playback, file selection, and basic UI

design. By the end of the session, participants will understand Flutters

architecture, state management, and how to integrate third-party packages

effectively. Combine theory, coding, and creativity to begin your Flutter

journey.

Venue: SJT 502

Registration:VTOp

Instagram:

https://www.instagram.com/csivitu?igsh=MXI2cnRreG5ibGJ1dw%3D%3D&utm_source=qr

CodeChef-VIT

Event Name: CASA: Empower, Educate, Eradicate

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 01:00 PM

Event Description:CodeChef-VIT is on a mission to transform how our nation

addresses addiction by raising awareness amongst young individuals. We'll

dig deep into the physical and mental wreckage caused by drug abuse and

equip you with vital information on available treatment services. Whether

you're passionate about prevention or lending support to your loved ones,

let's stand together to build a healthier, more secure world. We extend our

hand to you, inviting you to unite, inviting you to CASA.

Venue: SJT-522

Registration: VTOP

Instagram: http://goog_1306337287https://www.instagram.com/codechefvit

Gujarati Literary Association (GLA)

Event Name: CASA - Stronger Without Substance

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 01:00 PM

Event Description:CASA - Stronger Without Substances is an initiative that

brings students together to reflect, share, and learn about making

healthier choices. Guided by Ms. Beulah Valarmathi Chandran, Student

Counsellor at VIT, the session will open up honest conversations on the

effects of substance use, the importance of awareness, and the power of

supporting one another.

Venue: MB210

Registration:VTOP

Instagram:

https://www.instagram.com/p/DQhDpBJEudS/?igsh=MWZ3MTgxdzM2NzFyZA==

Creative Club

Event Name: Creativity meets curiosity

Event Time: 10:00 AM - 1:00 PM

Event Description: Creativity Meets Curiosity is an outreach event by the

Creativity Club that inspires students to explore the power of imagination

through curiosity-driven activities. It aims to spark innovation, foster

creative expression and promote critical thinking, encouraging participants

to transform their curiosity into impactful ideas and creative outcomes.

Venue: Takshila School,Ambur

Registration: VTOP

Instagram: https://instagram.com/creativityclub_vit/

Robovitics

Event Name: Inside PCB Design

Event Time: 9:00 PM - 11:30 PM

Event Description: This session will provide a comprehensive understanding

of the world of circuit design. Participants will be exposed to the

important concepts such as schematic design, PCB layout and its designing

rules and DRC for layouts. They will also get an overview of PCB

fabrication, learning substrates, etching, layers, making footprints,

lamination and other key concepts. The session will end with the need for

PCBs with optimal designs in the field of robotics.

Venue: Microsoft Teams

Registration:VTOP

Instagram:

IEEE-Robotics & Automation Society

Event Name: SDG: Innovate for Impact

Event Time: 12:00 AM - 1:00 PM

Event Description: Bridging technology and purpose, this session highlights

how sustainable thinking fuels innovation. Participants will explore real

examples where engineering solutions have advanced SDG targets such as

clean energy, sustainable infrastructure, and quality education.

Venue: TT-201

Registration:VTOP

Instagram:

IEEE-Robotics & Automation

Event Name: CASA: Mind Over Matter

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 12:00 PM

Event Description: An awareness session focused on mental health, stress

management, and emotional regulation for students and professionals. This

session empowers participants to recognize early signs of burnout, develop

healthy coping strategies, and build resilience, essential skills for

future innovators and leaders.

Venue: TT 201

Registration:VTOP

Instagram:

IEEE Circuits and Systems (CAS)

Event Name: Outreach: Electrofest 2.1

Event Time: 10:00 AM - 1:00 PM

Event Description: IEEE-CAS is going to organize an outreach event at

Takshila Global School(ambur) for Grade 9 students on the topic of basics

and interesting concepts of electrical circuits. The session will include

interactive demonstrations and simple circuit-building activities designed

to spark students curiosity and inspire them to explore the world of

electronics and innovation

Venue: Takshilah Global School, Ambur.

Registration: VTOP

Instagram link :

https://www.instagram.com/ieee_cas_vit?igsh=eWMwYjA1OXUxanN5

LinkedIn link :

https://www.linkedin.com/company/ieee-circuits-and-systems-vit/

Whatsapp channel : https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaosmJC8PgsGrZIEts08

Astronomy Club-VIT Stellar

Event Name: CASA: Addiction - Awareness and Recovery

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 1:00 PM

Event Description: Join us for an insightful session led by our esteemed

guest speaker as we explore the journey from awareness to recovery in the

context of substance abuse. The talk aims to deepen understanding, promote

empathy, and encourage meaningful discussions on prevention,

rehabilitation, and building a more conscious and supportive community.

Venue: SJT 204

Registration:VTOP

Instagram:

https://www.instagram.com/vit_stellar?utm_source=ig_web_button_share_sheet&igsh=ZDNlZDc0MzIxNw==

Ayuda NGO CLub

Event Name: SDG:Greenovate

Event Time: 11:00 AM - 1:30 PM

Event Description:SDG: Greenovate is an inspiring ideathon that invites

students and young innovators to take on real-world sustainability

challenges. Organized by Ayuda NGO Club, the event encourages creative and

practical thinking aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development

Goals (SDGs). Participants will collaborate, innovate, and present ideas

that promote a cleaner, greener, and more sustainable future. Join us to be

a part of this movement that transforms ideas into impactful actions for

our planet and society.

Venue: SJT 107

Registration:VTOP

Dear VITians,

Greetings!

We are delighted to announce that the 5th Indian International Conference

on Industrial Engineering and Operations Management (IEOM 2025) will be

held from 6th to 8th November 2025 at VIT, Vellore. The conference is

jointly organized by the School of Mechanical Engineering, VIT Business

School, School of Electronics Engineering, and the IEOM Society

International, USA.

The event will feature an inspiring lineup of plenary talks, keynote

addresses, invited expert lectures, and oral presentations, providing an

excellent platform for knowledge exchange, collaboration, and innovation.

On behalf of the Organizing Committee, we cordially invite you to the

Inaugural

Ceremony of the conference, scheduled for 6th November 2025 (Thursday) at

10:00 AM, at the Dr. M. Channa Reddy Auditorium, Dr. M.G.R. Block, VIT,

Vellore.

We are also pleased to share that our Honourable Chancellor will be

conferred

with the "Transformative Education Leadership Award" by the IEOM Society

International, USA, during the inaugural session.

Please find attached the formal invitation and the detailed programme

schedule for the three-day conference.

We sincerely look forward to your gracious presence and active

participation in making this international event a grand success.

Subject: SPIC-MACAY: Carnatic Flute Concert by Vid. J.A. Jayant & Team– November 4, 2025
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to invite you to a Special Cultural Event organized

by SPIC MACAY VIT Vellore.

Immerse yourself in the soulful melodies of the Carnatic Flute

performed by Vid.

J.A. Jayant (AIR A-Top Grade Artist), accompanied by Vid. Kishore Ramesh on

Mridangam and Vid. S. Sunil Kumar on Kanjira.

Date: November 4, 2025

Time: 1:30 PM – 3:30 PM

Venue: Era Sezhiyan Auditorium, MGB

About the Artist: J. A. Jayant

Young Flute exponent J.A.Jayant is a Flautist, Collaborator, Educator, and

Composer performing across the globe and popularizing the art of flute

playing. A prodigy - having started performing at the age of 7, Flute

J.A.Jayant is a young musician of national and international repute with

over 45 international tours in over 25 countries and close to 2000 solo

concerts and jugalbandi/ collaborative performances to his credit. His

grandfather Flute Maestro Late T.S.Sankaran was his guru. Jayant is

recognized as the torch bearer of the Flute Mali style of Carnatic flute

playing. He was awarded the prestigious “A-TOP Grade “ by All India

Radio at a very young age. A global ambassador of Indian Music, Jayant has

performed and enthralled audiences at various prestigious organizations and

festivals in India and around the world. He is regarded as one of the most

popular and widely respected Instrumentalists from India performing and

collaborating with globally renowned musicians. He has the rare honor of

performing for the Honourable President of India and for the Indian Navy in

Port Blair.

About SPIC MACAY

SPIC MACAY (Society for the Promotion of Indian Classical Music And Culture

Amongst Youth) is a non-political, nationwide, voluntary movement founded

in 1977 by Dr. Kiran Seth, Professor-Emeritus at IIT-Delhi who was awarded

the 'Padma Shri' for his contribution to the arts in 2009. SPICMACAY’s

intention is to enrich the quality of formal education by increasing

awareness about different aspects of Indian heritage and inspiring the

young mind to imbibe the values embedded in it. For this, the most

accomplished artists of the country render programs of Indian classical

music and dance, folk, poetry, theatre, traditional paintings, crafts &

yoga primarily in schools and colleges. SPIC MACAY celebrates Nishkaam Seva

- the spirit of volunteerism – of giving selflessly without expectation, a

value that is intrinsic to our culture and important to nurture in today's

world.

We look forward to your presence and participation in celebrating the

richness of Indian classical music.

All are invited!

Dear Sir/Madam,

Warm Greetings from the Centre for Nanotechnology Research, VIT, India.

We are pleased to inform you that the Centre for Nanotechnology Research,

VIT, is organising one of the premier events, the “3rd International

Conference on Nanoscience and Nanotechnology – ICNAN 2025,” from December

16 to 19, 2025. (https://icnan.vit.ac.in/)

Based on various requests from VITians, we have extended the dates for

registration and glad to announce a discounted registration fee for

advances in the field. The conference covers a broad theme in this area to

Fellowship and YUKTI Innovation Challenge 2025 ( Ministry of Education).

social impact, and entrepreneurial excellence.

This remarkable accomplishment highlights the innovation-driven mindset

and commitment to solving real-world challenges demonstrated by our

students.

------------------------------

💰 Financial Support under the AICTE Productization Fellowship

The AICTE Productization Fellowship provides significant financial and

project development support:

 -

 ₹37,000 per month per student for up to one year in Stage 1

 -

 ₹37,000 per month per student for another one year in Stage 2,

 upon successful prototype completion

 -

 A contingency grant of ₹50,000 per year per team to cover tools,

 materials, and other project-related expenses

------------------------------

🚀 YUKTI Innovation Challenge 2025 – Key Benefits

 1.

 Funding & Incubation: Financial support of up to ₹10 lakh from

 AICTE–MoE, along with incubation access and startup acceleration

 within 12–15 months.

Subject: Guidelines – Course Registration (Winter Semester 2025 - 26)
Body:
Dear Student,

Guidelines – Course Registration (Winter Semester 2025 - 26)

 1. Current Students and timed-out students of all the programmes except

 BSc (Agri), BSc Catering & Hotel Management, B. Des., B. Arc., BSc

 Multimedia, BSc Visual Communication, M. Des., M. Arc., MSW, B. Tech

 Computer Science and Business Systems (2022, 2023 & 2024 Batches) are

 permitted to take part in the course registration.

 2. Course Registration is scheduled to be conducted on 01.11. 2025.

 3. Information on courses offered for the Winter Semester 2025 - 26 is

 available on VTOP and the VITian Mobile App.

 4. Information on the course registration schedule for the Winter

 Semester 2025 - 26 (time and duration for various groups of students) is

 available on VTOP and the VITian Mobile App.

5. During the course registration process, the system will prompt to

register for the applicable compulsory courses as per the curriculum of the

respective programmes. Subsequently, UC: University Core, PC: Programme

Core, FC: Foundation Core, Concentration. DLESC: Discipline linked

Engineering Sciences, DC: Discipline Core, PE: Programme Elective, UE:

University Elective, DE: Discipline Elective, SPE: Specialization Elective,

OE: Open Elective and compulsory courses with the following options will be

permitted:

 Regular / Re-register / Substitution (UE / OE / DE / PE and also in

HSM / Language Basket)

 Regular (UC as UE, PE as UE, DE as OE, SPE as OE)

 Minor Programmes (Except first year Students)

Multidisciplinary Elective (applicable to the B. Tech Core Programmes only

except BBS): An option is provided to earn the required credits under the

Discipline Elective / Open Elective category by registering courses listed

under multidisciplinary electives. The eligibility criteria to register

course(s) under the multidisciplinary elective are to have completed a

minimum of 9 credits from the courses listed under the Discipline

Electives. The remaining credits can be earned from the courses listed

under either Discipline Electives or Multidisciplinary Electives to

complete credit requirements as per the curriculum.

 6. The add / Drop option will be enabled for all the students from

 05.12.2025 to 07.12.2025. During the Add / Drop period, students can

 register for courses under Audit / Grade Improvement / Additional Course /

 Minor / Honour options.

 7. Removal of courses registered under the regular mode is not possible

 unless the course registered under ‘Additional’ is removed first.

 8. The student should generate an invoice on VTOP (in the timetable

 menu) and proceed for payment (under the menu – Online Payments) for the

 courses that demand course fees. The courses of fee defaulters will be

 deregistered after the deadline.

 9. Courses cannot be deleted or withdrawn if the fee payment is made.

 10. Students are required to go through the Academic Regulations for

 further clarification on the terminologies.

 11. Queries related to course offering should be addressed to the

 respective Head of the Department.

Project Registration Rules:

All eligible M. Tech./ MCA /MSc students who were admitted in 2024 -25 will

be permitted to register for Internship II / Dissertation II with a duration of

6 months.

Integrated students of MIC/MID/MIY who are admitted in 2021-22 will be

permitted to register Capstone project/ Master thesis with a duration of 6

months.

BXXX498J - Project II is compulsory for 2022-23 BTech batch students.

During the time of registration, students should select a guide and a

tentative title of the project.

Kindly note that there will be two options to register for Internship II /

Dissertation II / Capstone Project / Master Thesis:

a) ACAD - ACADEMICS

b) PAT - PLACEMENT AND TRAINING

Students who have already received an Internship offer through CDC have to

register the course under “PAT - PLACEMENT AND TRAINING”. The remaining

students have to register under ACAD – Academics, for which a “Faculty

Guide” is to be selected. (Guide change option will be enabled during Add /

Drop period)

Students can change the option from ACAD to PAT whenever an internship

offer is received in future by submitting proof (received from the CDC) and

a consent letter (from the Guide) to the Academics Office.

with regards

M. Anthony Xavior PhD

Body:
Reminder 

Ref:VIT/Regr./2025/106

 28 July 2025

CIRCULAR

Sub: All foreign inbound and outbound academic activities

All faculty members and students are hereby informed that, with effect

from 1 August 2025 (Friday), the following procedures will be mandatory on

the VTOP portal for all foreign inbound and outbound academic activities:

1. Inbound foreign students and faculty (Entering VIT)

All international students and faculty planning to join VIT for academic,

research, internship, exchange, or any other official purposes must

complete the following steps:

· VIT faculty members should submit a request on behalf of foreign

faculty members (all categories) /foreign students enrolled for an

internship/summer school programme for entry via

the “International Relations (IR)” section on VTOP.

Faculty Inbound Request Form (Incoming)

 - Upload required documents, including (1. Appointment Letter, 2.

 Invitation letter,

 3. Passport copy, 4. Visa copy )

 - Obtain mandatory approvals from:

 - Respective School Dean/Director

 - Director -International Relations Office

 - Registrar

 - Approval must be obtained at least two weeks before arrival at the VIT

 campus.

2. Outbound students and faculty (Travelling Abroad)

All students and faculty planning to travel abroad under institutional

agreements, exchange programs, internships, official trips, or research

collaborations must:

 - Initiate the “International Relations (IR)” section in VTOP

 -Faculty Outbound Request Form (Outgoing)

 - Submit supporting documents, including 1. Official invitation 2.

 Passport copy

 3. Visa copy 4. Funding by VIT/External funding, if yes, please attach

 the funding sanction letter 5. Any other support documents (1-5 documents).

 - Obtain mandatory approvals from:

 - Respective School Dean/Director

 - Director -International Relations Office

 - Registrar

 - Approval must be obtained at least 2 weeks before the departure date.

 - This measure is implemented to ensure institutional compliance,

 accurate data management for IQAC and RAAC, timely processing of

 reimbursements by the Finance Office, necessary HR approvals, Guest House

 booking, transport booking and effective coordination of international

 academic engagements abroad.

For further queries, please get in touch with the International Relations

Office (IRO) or email at international@vit.ac.in.

from international

The application deadline for

 - 1st Semester 2026 (February–June): Deadline October 31, 2025

 - 2nd Semester 2026 (August–December): Deadline May 30, 2026

Nomination & Application Procedures 

1. Partner institutions should nominate students by email to

intercambio@unaerp.br, including:

 - Full name

 - Email address

 - Current program of study at the home institution

2. Nominated students must:

 - Read the Application Guide

 https://unaerp.br/doclink/unaerp-application-guide-2026-2027/eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJ1bmFlcnAtYXBwbGljYXRpb24tZ3VpZGUtMjAyNi0yMDI3IiwiaWF0IjoxNzU2NDc5MDc5LCJleHAiOjE3NTY1NjU0Nzl9.D95mn_BSK4iHqGQ3cPKnw6ImSu7XEzYUNFzFFa-eIE4

 - Complete the Online Application Form

 https://forms.gle/xcHJC9YreagCQVKq7

 - Submit to intercambio@unaerp.br their Updated Academic Transcript by

 the deadlines above

Academic Programs 

International students may apply for:

 - Undergraduate Programs: Human Sciences, Health Sciences, Engineering

 https://unaerp.br/cursos/graduacao-presencial

 - Graduate Research Programs: Master’s and Doctorate

 https://unaerp.br/como-ingressar/veja-como-ingressar-em/mestrados-e-doutorados

 - Internship and Research Opportunities (contact us for more info)

Courses in Foreign Languages

For the 1st semester of 2026 (Feb-June), the following courses will be

offered:

· International Politics

· Democracy between consolidations and crisis

· International Management

· Portuguese for Foreigners - Basic Level

Additionally, selected Architecture & Urbanism and Business Administration

courses are “language-friendly,” with content taught in Portuguese but

support materials and assessments available in English/Spanish. Please,

write to intercambio@unaerp.br for more info.

A minimum number of students is required for the courses in foreign

languages to be offered. Classes will be confirmed in February 2026 when

the enrollment period for national students opens. If the minimum number of

registered students is not reached, international students will need to

choose only courses taught in Portuguese. Therefore, students should be

aware that it may be necessary to proceed only with courses in Portuguese

or a mix of courses in Portuguese and the English classes that have been

opened.

Campus Life & Student Integration

UNAERP offers several programs to support international students, including:

· Buddy Program

· Housing Program (assistance finding accommodation)

· Free Portuguese Language Classes

Body:
Dear Students,

We are delighted to share details about Bharat Innovates 2026, a

flagship deep-tech

venture support program by the Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of

India, under the guidance of the Office of the Principal Scientific

Adviser.

This initiative aims to showcase research-driven innovations from India’s

higher education institutions on a global platform. Selected ventures

will receive mentorship, access to labs and IP support, and an opportunity

to present their innovations at the Global Demo Day in Nice, France (17–19

June 2026).

Key Highlights

 -

 9-month program with bootcamps, national showcase, and mentoring

 -

 Open to teams from MoE-associated HEIs/CFTIs or incubated ventures

 -

 Focus areas include Biotechnology and Healthcare & MedTech

 -

 Covers 13 different technology themes: View Themes

 https://bharatinnovates.in/themes/

 -

 Application Deadline (Extended): 26 October 2025

For more information and registration, visit: Bharat Innovates 2026

https://bharatinnovates.in/

bharatinnovates@iitb.ac.in.

represent VIT on the global stage.

Subject: SBST-VIT Team Wins Grand Prize in 2025 Vivli AMR Surveillance Data Challenge - Reg.
Body:
Dear VITians,

Greetings !

We are pleased and delighted to inform you all that Dr. George Priya

Doss C and his scholar from the School of Biosciences and Technology

(SBST), VIT Vellore, has been awarded the Grand Prize – AMR Global

Leadership Award in the prestigious 2025 Vivli AMR Surveillance Data

Challenge, an initiative supported by Johnson & Johnson, Paratek, Pfizer,

and the U.S. National Institutes of Health.

SBST winning submission, titled “Causal Inference of Antimicrobial

Resistance Trends: Evaluating the Impact of Climate and Pollution Using

Global AMR Data,” was adjudged the top global entry. The study employed

advanced causal inference methodologies to elucidate the influence of

environmental pollutants on antifungal resistance dynamics in Candida

glabrata. Notably, they uncovered a novel time-lagged correlation between

ambient air pollution levels and rising fluconazole resistance, offering

new insights into the environmental determinants of AMR evolution.

Dr. GEORGE PRIYA DOSS C

their Student Exchange Program for the Even Semester 2025/2026 (Spring

log in to their online application, iMobilio

https://imobilio.apps.binus.ac.id/, which will be open from 16 – 30

October 2025.

Spring 2026

- Undergraduate program: 2 February – 4 July 2026

 - Graduate program: 2 March – 8 June 2026 (Period 1) & 13

 Mandatory orientation days will be 1 week before the study

period starts.

Should you have any questions or require further assistance, please do not

hesitate to contact

binusexchange@groups.binusnews.info

Body:
Dear VITians,

The Prem Jain Memorial Trust, in collaboration with the Indian Green

Building Council (IGBC), YLAC, Daikin India, NIUA, Association of

Designers of India – Bangalore, and the Council of Architecture,

is launching the National Green Earth Challenge 2026.

This nationwide competition invites young minds from architecture,

engineering, design, and allied fields to pioneer sustainable solutions

for a greener tomorrow.

Competition Categories

 -

 Sustainable Product Design – creating innovative, eco-friendly products

 -

 Sustainable Habitat – reimagining how we live and build for a

 sustainable future

Key Details:

 -

 Eligibility: Undergraduate students (Architecture, Engineering, Design

 & Allied Fields)

 -

 Prize Pool: Prizes worth Rs. 10 lakhs | National Winners: Rs. 1,50,000

 each

 -

 Timeline:

 -

 Submissions Open: 1st Sept 2025

 -

 Submissions Close: 10th Oct 2025

 -

 Preliminary Jury: Nov 2025

 -

 Zonal Jury: Jan 2026

 -

 National Grand Finale: Feb 2026, New Delhi

Apply Here: https://pjmtngec.premjainmemorialtrust.com/index.php

Website: https://pjmtngec.premjainmemorialtrust.com/index.php

We encourage students to make the best use of this opportunity to showcase

their creativity and contribute towards a sustainable, greener future.

Dear All,

Rice University USA- MECE Computer Vision Online Workshop

site for the schedule)

The MECE is a non-thesis professional master’s program that can be

completed in three to four semesters (most students complete it in 3

semesters). Our program prepares students to succeed and advance rapidly in

today’s technical marketplace. The degree emphasizes practical aspects of

engineering, combined with management and communication coursework,

allowing graduates to advance in their careers. The program has a year-long

capstone project, which allows students to develop expertise in one of

seven key focus areas. Our admission is open for both Fall and Spring

starts. The application deadline for the Fall 2026 term is December 15,

2025. Please refer to our website at www.ece.rice.edu

https://mx.technolutions.net/ss/c/u001.mv75SfSNMmSvduEMaqEjkHhbObrQC9fk6NqfmDy9Tb0/4k3/w63LEyNnRnC2zl_-f6ia1A/h3/h001.f9U1cp3JwwKR3jFxMHUns7KrL8Rv2KAuI_h8uxHV6hE

for

more information.

Please do not hesitate to contact us at ecemece@rice.edu if you have any

questions regarding the Computer Vision Online Workshop or the MECE program

in general.

The goal of the workshop is to introduce both fundamental and applied

aspects of computer vision through a combination of theoretical background

and hands-on coding exercises that students can run themselves.

This online workshop will feature six themed sessions taught by faculty

members in our ECE department. During the closing session, we will

introduce some of the courses taught at Rice University that are related to

the workshop content. We hope to provide participants with a glimpse of

what they can learn at Rice University's MECE program

Dear NAYAN SHARMA,

Financial Markets

Investment Banking

1. Assess investment proposals and identify companies with high growth potential and understand various stages of private equity investing.

2. Engage in setting up a Private Equity Fund, emphasizing investor onboarding, investing cycles & sectoral orientation.

3. Author case-based projects on successful exits in the private equity space, by analyzing mergers & acquisitions.

Subject: Université de Tours -France- International exchange students - Nominations S2 2025/26
Body:
Kind Attention: Pre-Final Year Students

The University of Tours will be opening the nomination period for

mobilities taking place during the second semester of the 2025/26 academic

year (January – May) next month, on the 6th of October 2025.

In order for you to have a holistic overview upon the aspects connected to

this topic, please find a list of useful information enumerated below.

Why choose the University of Tours for your semester abroad in France?

 - Course on offer

 - Online course catalogue (-> course name, credits, content, hours,

 coordinator, level) – disciplinary courses

Students can use our online catalogue, that lists the most popular courses

(French/English) for exchange students: Course Catalogue for Exchange

Students. https://cces.univ-tours.fr/Accueil.php?language=EN

Beyond disciplinary courses taught in French, UT provides also students

with more than 150 courses in English in different fields (Humanities,

Science and Technology). Only a beginner-intermediate level of French is

required if your students choose disciplinary courses taught in English.

They have the right to choose courses in any discipline (from all faculties

apart from medicine), provided the conditions of our interinstitutional

agreement are fulfilled (the majority of their classes must be taken within

a specific field of studies, for example), that both their academic

coordinators approve it, and that their home university will recognize the

credits obtained in a different discipline than the student’s major at the

end of the mobility, these credits being relevant to the student’s academic

project.

 - French language and culture classes

Exchange students can complete their learning agreement with French courses

https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/admission-process-for-exchange-students/6-learn-french-cuefee-crl

 provided by our University Center of Teaching French to International

Students (CUEFEE), labeled with a maximum three stars

https://www.univ-tours.fr/international/le-cuefee-renouvelle-son-label-qualite-fle-avec-3-etoiles

by

the French Government for the quality of its teaching and services

Students can select up to 3 courses (up to 72 hours), that are

completely free of charge for exchange students. Each course will give

students 4 ECTS, as follows:

§ Written language (24h/semester), 4 ECTS credits

§ Oral language (24h/semester), 4 ECTS credits

§ Cultural options (20h/semester), 4 ECTS credits (from B1 level on)

Classes are taught beginning with the A1 CEFR level in French to C1. This

is the main scheme for international exchange students.

 - Individual support

The University of Tours assists international exchange students prior to

their mobility with every administrative aspect related to their arrival in

France, from the online pre-registration to the visa procedure (if

applicable), and facilitates their accommodation request in a public

student residency.

 - Visa – Campus France procedure for exchange students that are not

 European citizens (not a citizen of one of the 27 EU member states), or

 citizens of a Schengen / EEA country

 - Accommodation – housing request for public student residencies

 - Learning Agreement and online course catalogue

 - French language and culture classes

 - Academic calendar and timetable

 - Integration – For the integration of exchange students different

 resources exist in order to facilitate it

 - Orientation period: organised at the beginning of each semester,

 it allows students to discover the city, the university, and

to meet other

 students, both local and internationals

 - Buddy System: a French student to support them soon after their

 arrival in Tours

 - Erasmus Student Network https://www.facebook.com/ESNTours/: the

 association organizes cooking activities, international dinners, theme

 evenings. The membership gives access to preferential rates for the

 cultural events organized by the international relations

office of the UT

 and gives them the right to have discounts with the partners of the

 association (Ryanair, local stores…).

 - Cultural programme

 - International Relations Service organizes a great cultural

 programme

 https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/admission-process-for-exchange-students/10-culture-sports

for

 the students with visits to the chateaux of the Loire Valley and

 many other unmissable spots of the region and France.

 - In addition, the cultural service of the university organizes

 many cultural events and offers discounts to the students who have the

 cultural pass (opera, cinema, shows…).

 - Sports

§ Students have access to a wide variety of sports at the UT

https://www.univ-tours.fr/campus/accueil-sport-1. They can subscribe to

the Pack’Sport and take up to 3 different sport classes a week, absolutely

free of charge! They can also do sports trainings during week-ends on

different themes (hiking at the Mont-Saint-Michel, canyoning, skiing…) and

attend sport events or wellness activities (badminton, fitness night,

rugby…).

o Orientation maps

§ A map of UT’s campuses, faculties, and student services

https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?mid=1Oe2Q_yuy9VbAkhtfCiHYJhzh8K8iYXA&usp=sharing

§ A map allowing students to discover the city

https://www.google.com/maps/d/viewer?mid=1KeCNJLFEccVbzUZTNfD3VfNAz-ktLv0&ll=47.38009226217868%2C0.688595800000007&z=13

from

an extracurricular point of view

· Warm welcome

As a token of hospitality and deep interest in student welfare, students

are welcomed individually upon their arrival to help them finalize their

administrative registration, and give them all the practical information

they need for their settling in (presentation of the different useful

university services, organized events, information about the ESN, public

transportation, etc.). Moreover, every September, the UT gathers many

actors and welcome services of international students in a single

event, the International

Students Welcome Desk.

https://www.univ-tours.fr/international/welcome-desk-1

UT’s Welcome Desk team is here to direct and give students advice to ensure

a coordinated and efficient setup in Tours.

Academic calendar for nominations and online applications - incoming

exchange students

Term dates

First semester (autumn / winter semester): 4 months (September to December)

Second semester (spring / summer semester): 5 months (January to May)

Nota bene: should you have different term dates, please think about

prioritising mobilities that fit within our framework, in order to avoid

any unpleasant situation for the selected students (example: if your second

semester starts in February / March, you can prioritize mobilities starting

in September; we would be delighted to welcome your students for a complete

academic year)

Nominations calendar

Spring / Summer semester: starting in January 2026

Nomination period: 06.10.2025 – 14.11.2025

Application period: 06.10.2025 – 21.11.2025

Nomination process for incoming exchange students

The International Relations Office will officially nominate the outgoing

students for an international mobility at the University of Tours.

Students interested in this programme may contact Dr. Sainu Franco,

International Relations Officer in- person, in the IR Office (MB 105)

between 9.00 AM and 5.00 PM, Monday through Friday, latest by 06/10/2025.

Following your nominations, students will be contacted with all the

instructions to follow as to pre-register at UT.

Useful information - Admission process for Exchange students

You will find detailed information on the admission process for exchange

students (registration, accommodation, visa, learning agreement) on: UT -

Admission process for Exchange students (univ-tours.fr)

https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/admission-process-for-exchange-students

Useful resources for partners and students - UT Promotional Materials

Please consult the official web page intended for partner institutions and

exchange students, where you will find communication toolkits (PPT, Fact

sheet), a link to the online course catalogue for exchange students, a list

of supervised projects, as well as some information on French studies:

https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/about-ut/useful-documents-aimed-at-international-partners

GOOD REASONS TO STUDY AT UT:

 - A multidisciplinary and dynamic university in the very heart of the

 city

 - An international city close to Paris, located in the Loire Valley

 - The historical birthplace of the French language

 - A lifestyle to enjoy, French heritage to discover

 - Over 3200 international students

Watch this video showing how it is nice to live in Tours: Tours, a

lively and dynamic city

https://protect-au.mimecast.com/s/NBq4CgZ0N1iAP8BJRUGwByM?domain=youtube.com

 & Tours’ 2024 retrospective

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vUlzJQfgCrk 

Should you have any subsequent questions, please do not hesitate to contact

Dr. Sainu Franco

International Relations Officer

O/o International Relations
