Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [24th January] 

 events.

NATIONAL GIRL CHILD DAY

National Girl Child Day was first initiated in 2008 by the Ministry of

Women and Child Development. The purpose of this day is to spread awareness

about the gender-based discrimination that girls face in our society and to

bring change in the attitude towards girls. The objective behind

celebrating the National Girl Child Day is to provide support and

opportunities to the girls of India. It also aims towards promoting

awareness about the rights of the girl child and to increase awareness on

the importance of girl education, and their health and nutrition.

The Indian government has taken several steps over the years to change this

and improve the conditions of girls. Several campaigns and programs such as

Save the Girl Child, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, free or subsidized education

for the girl children, reservations for women in colleges and universities

have been initiated to reduce this discrimination. Starting from female

infanticide to gender inequality to sexual abuse, there is no dearth of

issues. The main objective behind this is to highlight the inequalities

faced by girls, to promote awareness including the rights of a girl child,

the importance of education, health, and nutrition. Nowadays also gender

discrimination is a major problem that girls or women face

throughout their life.

Special Event: Cellphone Photography!

National Girl Child Day Photography Competition

Calling all VITians! Here's your chance to showcase your creativity and

support an important cause. Participate in our Cell Phone Photography

Competition as part of National Girl Child Day and stand a chance to win

exciting prizes in each category!

Topics to Capture

Choose from any of these themes to highlight the strength, beauty, and

potential of girls:

 - Empowered and Inspiring Girls – Capturing moments that reflect the

 strength, confidence, and resilience of girls.

 - Dreams in Focus – Showcasing the dreams and aspirations of young girls

 through creative visuals.

 - Education for Every Girl – Highlighting the importance of education

 and its transformative impact on girls.

 - Breaking Barriers – Photos of girls challenging stereotypes and

 excelling in unconventional roles or activities.

 - Her Smile, Her World – A focus on the happiness and positivity of

 girlhood, celebrating their unique stories.

Here's how to participate:

Guidelines:

 - Your submission must be original – no downloaded or stolen images.

 - Images must be taken using a cell phone camera.

 - Images should be captured inside the campus.

 - Each entry should reflect one of the listed topics and include a short

 caption or description.

 - Upload the photo on your Instagram page.

 - Tag SW page in the post @sw_vit (Make sure your post & profile are

 public).

 - Upload your photos before 06:00 PM today.

So, start clicking and share your best shots!

Vellore Institute of Technology shared a post: The School of Social Sciences and Languages at VIT organized a one-day international workshop on "Emerging Dimensions of Intellectual Property: European and Indian Perspectives," funded by SPARC, Ministry of Education, Government of India.

The workshop featured Dr. Razvan Dinca, Dean, School of Law, University of Bucharest, Romania, as the Chief Guest; Dr. Alexandre, Director, Master of Digital Law, University of Poitiers, France, as the Guest of Honour; and Dr. GB Reddy, Senior Professor, Osmania University, India, who joined virtually. The workshop brought together 105 participants from 57 institutions across India, 48 from VIT, and many others virtually via MS Teams. Focused on Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) and patent filings, the event fostered collaborations between technology and law, tradition and innovation, and India and Europe, promoting global knowledge exchange.

Dear Students,

This is to inform you that we will be orgainsing an orientation session on

the 2+2 and 4+1 transfer programs at the University of Edinburgh, UK, on

January 24 and 25 at 2:30 PM.

The session is open to interested students.

Date: 24th Jan'25

Time: 2:30 PM

Venue: Online Platform

https://ed-ac-uk.zoom.us/j/86187963067

Passcode: M6U3r8CZ

Timelines and requirements for applying to 2+2 and 4+1 are as follows.

Kindly note that the application deadline is 29th January and you will

need to apply through a system called UCAS

Following the submission of your application, the University of Edinburgh

will contact you to request these additional documents:

 - Official transcript

 - English language qualification (such as IELTS or TOEFL or Class XII

 English if you already have these – if not you will need to submit by 30

 th April)

 - List of courses you are currently studying but have not yet completed

 in Semester 4

You should aim to submit your supporting documents by 31st March 2025 but

you can submit your English language qualification later by 30th April 2025

if you do not have this yet.

You should be on track for an 80% or above GPA to be considered as well as

good grades in engineering-specific subjects.

Minimum English language requirements are 6.0 overall and 5.5 in each

component in IELTS (or equivalent). We are also pleased to offer a

scholarship of £3,500.00 per year for new students starting in 2025/26.

For details and interaction kindly login on above link and join the

session on 24th Jan'25 at 2:30 PM

Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [22nd January]

 events.

 Today's Events:

· Flight with Flutter

· Machine Learning 101

· A SDG Event- Neural Ethos

· Trailblazer's Talk

· Chess 960 Extravaganza

Scroll down for more details

CodeChef-VIT

Event Name: Flight with Flutter

Time: 02:00 PM - 04:00 PM

Event Description: Unlock the power of Flutter, the revolutionary framework

for cross-platform app development! In this hands-on workshop, learn to

build beautiful, high-performance apps, design seamless UIs, and use API

calls to fetch dynamic data. Perfect for beginners and developers alike,

boost your skills and creativity to become a Flutter pro!

Venue: Kamaraj Auditorium

Registration on: VTOP

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/codechefvit

CodeChef-VIT

Event Name: Machine Learning 101

Time: 04:00 PM - 06:00 PM

Event Description: Step into the exciting realm of Machine Learning with

our interactive session! Learn the fundamentals of supervised,

unsupervised, and reinforcement learning, dive into the math behind these

algorithms, and code them from scratch. This session is designed to make

you ready to implement ML in your projects and prepare you for the upcoming

hackathon. Perfect for beginners and tech enthusiasts—join us to turn

concepts into impactful applications and gear up for the future of

innovation!

Venue: Kamaraj Auditorium

Registration on: VTOP

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/codechefvit

The AI & ML Club - TAM

Event Name: A SDG Event- Neural Ethos

Time: 11:00 AM - 01:00 PM

Event Description: Neural Ethos explores how AI is transforming the global

economy by predicting and mitigating crises, improving decision-making, and

driving sustainable growth. Participants will learn how AI enhances

economic forecasting, boosts productivity, and enables data-driven

decisions for businesses and policymakers. This event highlights AI's role

in reshaping traditional economic models, promoting efficiency, and

aligning with sustainable development goals for a resilient economic future.

Venue: Shakespeare gallery

Registration: VTOP Registration

Instagram Link:

https://www.instagram.com/p/DFE3KnhyE9K/?igsh=Nm16NzhtbXN0eGIw

CSED

Event Name: Trailblazer's Talk

Time: 10:00 PM - 11:30 PM

Event Description: Trailblazer's Talk is an inspiring session featuring

accomplished entrepreneurs sharing their journey, challenges, and insights

into building successful ventures. Designed to ignite the entrepreneurial

spirit, this talk offers valuable guidance and motivation for aspiring

innovators to pursue their dreams and make an impact in the world of

business and beyond.

Venue: Google Meet (Online)

Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link:

https://www.instagram.com/p/DFE4kdxSArH/?igsh=N3N2N3BieDQxenU5

Google Meet Link: https://meet.google.com/kgz-tonf-jxe

Board Gamers Club

Event Name: Chess 960 Extravaganza

Time: 08:30 AM - 06:30 PM

Event Description: Chess 960 Extravaganza is an exhilarating day-long chess

tournament where strategy meets creativity. Designed to challenge players'

adaptability and skills, this event showcases the unique Chess 960 format,

offering an unpredictable and exciting twist to the classic game. The

tournament features a variety of time controls, starting with fast-paced

Blitz rounds, followed by thoughtful Rapid rounds, and culminating in an

intense Classical final. Join us on January 22, 2025, at the CS Hall for a

day filled with dynamic gameplay, strategic brilliance, and camaraderie

among chess enthusiasts.

Venue: CS Hall

Next.js. Learn the basics of setting up and writing code, then explore how

to make your website interactive using props and events. Use hooks like

useState and useEffect, and design stunning pages with Tailwind CSS.

Finally, connect everything using routing. This session is perfect for

anyone ready to take their first step into web development!

Registration on: VTOP

Subject: National Science Yatra – 2025-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

We are pleased to invite you to the National Science Yatra – 2025,

jointly organized by the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR)

and CSRD and Office of Students' Welfare.

This event aims to highlight the pivotal role of atomic energy in

nation-building, providing an engaging platform to explore advancements in

science and technology. Attendees will also gain valuable insights into

career and research opportunities in the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE).

The program includes inspiring talks, engaging competitions, and an

exhibition showcasing the remarkable contributions of DAE. Participants

will have the opportunity to interact with experts, learn about innovations

in the field, and explore how atoms contribute to the nation's progress.

Topic: Atoms in the Service of Nation

Programme Highlights

 - 09:00 - 09:05 hrs – Inauguration of exhibition showcasing DAE

 activities

 - 09:05 - 10:00 hrs – Exhibition open for students

 - 10:15 - 11:00 hrs – Technical talk on “Atoms in the service of

 nation”

 - 11:00 - 11:45 hrs – Talk on “Career and research opportunities in

 DAE”

 - 11:45 - 13:00 hrs – Competitions (Drawing, Quiz, Slogan)

 - 13:30 - 16:00 hrs – Exhibition visit

We look forward to your enthusiastic participation in this exciting journey

of discovery and learning.

Note: Programme Schedule is attached.

Subject: Entrepreneur Awards by Team MyPerro -reg
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are thrilled to share the remarkable success story of Team MyPerro,

the proud innovators behind Perro Technocare Private Limited a Startup

Under TBI, VIT Vellore, who have brought great honor to our institution by

excelling in two prestigious competitions:

 - The Global Student Entrepreneur Awards (GSEA) Kerala by

 Entrepreneurs' Organization

 - Disrupt 2025 by IIT Guwahati

Saiprasad Pandilwar represented Team MyPerro at the GSEA Regionals held in

Kochi, Kerala. Competing against 150 participants, he advanced through

multiple rounds, showcasing exceptional entrepreneurial skills and a

visionary idea. Saiprasad secured the runner-up position, a cash prize of

₹50,000, and a coveted spot in the GSEA India Finals scheduled for March.

Simultaneously, Team MyPerro participated in Disrupt 2025, facing over 450

participants across four rigorous rounds: business plan submission, market

study, pitch deck creation, and finals. Led by Manan Vyas, the team

delivered an outstanding pitch at the IIT Guwahati campus, securing the

runner-up position and winning a cash prize of ₹40,000.

In addition to their success, the team impressed investors, who expressed

interest in their product. On 19th January, Team MyPerro will showcase

their innovation at a dedicated stall at IIT Guwahati, engaging with

students, investors, and participants.

Team MyPerro Members

Saiprasad Pandilwar (22BDS0306): Founder

Manan Vyas (22BCB0201): Co-Founder

Meda Varshith Kumar Reddy (23BCE0614): DevOps Lead

Aarya Agarwal (24MIS0145): Public Relations

Dhanesh Baheti (24BEE0037): IoT Lead

Website: www.myperro.in

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to Team MyPerro for their

outstanding achievements and wish them continued success as they move

forward to the GSEA India Finals and other future endeavors.

Let’s celebrate their remarkable journey and cheer them on for greater

milestones ahead!

Dear Students,

The Institution’s Innovation Council is excited to invite you to a hands-on

workshop on Artificial Intelligence (AI) during Innovation Week. This

workshop is a fantastic opportunity to delve into the world of AI, guided

by an industry expert, Dr. Sateesh Kumar.

About the Speaker: Dr. Sateesh Kumar is the Founder & CEO of AgileTribers

and Karka Software Academy. He has previously served as the Head of Product

Engineering at Flow Global, bringing a wealth of knowledge and experience

Dear VITians,

This is regarding the initiatives by India Space Lab (भारत अंतरिक्ष

प्रयोगशाला) to advance space science and technology. We are delighted to

invite you to the Advanced Drone Workshop, The primary goal of this

workshop is to enhance space education and explore opportunities for

technological advancement.

The Government of India, under the visionary leadership of Honorable PM

Shri Narendra Modi, has initiated groundbreaking reforms in the space

sector. These initiatives are designed to enhance and promote space

education, research, and development across the nation. A key highlight of

these efforts is the celebration of India Space Week, scheduled from August

12 to August 18, along with National Space Day on August 23. This event is

organized by the Bharat Antriksh Saptah/India Space Lab with the Department

of Science and Technology. Following the successful India Space Week event

held from August 12 to 18, and National Space Day, India Space Lab is

conducting an Advanced Drone (Air Taxi) workshop.

We are honored to share that the AICTE Chairman Prof. T. G. Sitharam and

Former Governor of Chhattisgarh Shekhar Dutt graced the Advanced Drone

Technology Workshop. Their presence highlighted the importance of such

initiatives in shaping the future of space technology and education in

India.

Who can participate?

Anyone with a background in science and technology, including students and

faculty, is welcome to join the Advanced Drone Technology workshop.

Subject: Invitation from Rivera'25 team - Design & Media, Campus Decoration committees reg
Body:
Dear students

Greetings from the team Riviera'25

We at Vellore Institute of Technology-VIT Vellore believe that education is

not limited to the classroom but goes beyond. To facilitate this, VIT

conducts an Annual International Sports and Cultural Carnival Riviera that

strives to break every barrier, breach every limit, and

exceed every expectation year after year. With a footfall of more than

60,000 students from 70 different countries, it is with immense pleasure

and pride that we announce our next edition, RIVIERA 2025!

As we gear up for the next edition of RIVIERA, scheduled from 20th

February to 23rd February 2025, we are seeking enthusiastic individuals

who are eager to contribute their skills, creativity, and energy to create

an unforgettable experience for all participants.

We would like to invite applications from students for the post

of Student Organisers, Managers, Coordinators, and Volunteers for Riviera

‘25 in Design & Media, Campus Decoration committees.

https://shorturl.at/hc035

Deadline: 19th January 2025, Sunday 12:00 PM

The eligibility criteria are mentioned below:

1. Vellore Institute of Technology hosts two international

fests every year; those who have worked as Student Organizers in any one

fest, should not take part to give a fair chance to other students.

 2. Students’ Council members will not be considered for organizing

 positions. However, their services will be used appropriately.

 3. Academics requirements:

 Organizers should have at least 8.0 CGPA

 Managers should have at least 7.5 CGPA

 Coordinators should have at least 7.0 CGPA

 Volunteers should have at least 7.0 CGPA

 4. Physical attendance below 70% is not eligible for any of the posts.

 5. Students with standing arrears are not considered for any of the

 posts.

 6. Students who are involved in any disciplinary actions are not

 eligible. Even if he or she paid the fine, it is considered a disciplinary

 action.

 7. A student can be an Organizer/Manager if he/she has worked within

 the organizing committee of previous fests in the past year and has done

 considerable work. This needs to be acknowledged by the faculty coordinator

 of the concerned committee.

 Coordinators must have prominent contributions in clubs/chapters or in

 organizing any other event.

 Volunteers need not have prior experience.

 8. Students planning to do their project outside VIT are not eligible.

 9. If selected for the organizing team, the student should abide by the

 rules and regulations of the Riviera team.

 10. Only final-year students are eligible for the post

 of Student Organizer.

 Both final-year and pre-final-year students can apply for the post of

 Manager.

 Only pre-final year students can apply for the post of coordinator.

 Second-year students, the joining batch of 2023, are eligible only for

 the post of Volunteers.

Join us in creating memories that will last a lifetime and fostering an

international community that celebrates diversity and unity. We look

forward to welcoming you to the RIVIERA family!

Thank you

With warm regards

Dr K Gokul kumar

Professor-SMEC-VIT

Convenor-Riviera 25

Subject: Call for Applications for the Australian National University (ANU) - Future Research Talent (FRT) program - 2025 - Reg
Body:
Attention : All Pre-final UG/Pre-final year M.Tech (Integrated) / First

year PG Students

Pleased to share with you details of the 2025 round of The Australian

National University (ANU) Future Research Talent (FRT)

https://science.anu.edu.au/study/scholarships/future-research-talent-awards-india

 program.

The Future Research Talent (FRT) awards are jointly offered by ANU College

of Science and Medicine, ANU College of Systems and Society and ANU College

of Law, Governance and Policy to exceptional students from India.

The FRT is a competitive and prestigious program that attracts the very

best international students from high-quality Indian institutions and

provides them exposure to ANU research in the Sciences, Technology,

Engineering, Mathematics, and Medical research disciplines. The program

offers a valuable opportunity for India’s emerging research talent to form

international linkages and develop research skills at one of the world's

leading universities (ANU is ranked #30 in the world in QS World

University Rankings 2025).

The program will provide an opportunity to travel to ANU in 2025 to pursue

collaborative research projects. Each FRT scholar will receive AUD$8,500 to

support their travel to Canberra, Australia and cover living costs.

Interested students are requested to fill out the form

https://tinyurl.com/a77t5tku on or before 17.01.2025. 

Important Note: 

Pre-approval from academic staff at ANU is not necessary for this

program and that ANU academic staff should not be contacted during the

application process.

The process to be followed by VIT Students:

Eligibility 

:

Pre-final year student and having more than 8.5 CGPA till previous

semester

Application form filling : by 17.01.2025

Announcement of shortlisted students

for the 1st round via Email : on or before 20.01.2025

Apply through the ANU online portal (for shortlisted students only) : on or

before 22.01.2025

Subject: Wishing you all a happy Lohri, Pongal, Makar Sankranti, and Magh Bihu!
Body:
Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare wishes you all a Happy Lohri, Pongal, Makar

Sankranti, and Magh Bihu!

Lohri, Pongal, Makar Sankranti and Bihu are festivals that represent

different cultures but unite under one country – India. All the festivals

are loosely related to one single premise – crops, but vary depending on

the part of the country it is celebrated in. Let’s look at each of these

four festivals that people celebrate together.

Pongal, the four-day harvest festival celebrated in South India, especially

Tamil Nadu, will be celebrated with great enthusiasm from January 15-18

this year. Celebrated in mid-January every year, it also marks the

beginning of Uttarayan- the sun's journey towards the north and the end of

the winter season.

A large bonfire with people dancing, singing, and having a good time is

what contains the essence of this festival. Lohri is celebrated a day

before Makar Sankranti and is primarily celebrated in North India,

especially in the agricultural state of Punjab. It marks the end of the

sowing season. Delicacies and snacks, for example, Rewri, Peanuts, Sarson

Ka Saag, Makke Ki Roti, etc., are enjoyed with full vigor.

Makar Sankranti follows Lohri by a day and is a popular festival in most

parts of the country, but the festivity is at its prime, mainly in North

India. The festival marks the advent of the harvest season and also

signifies the end of Winter as the days start getting longer. Many people

dip in the sacred waters of the Ganga and offer their prayers to the Sun.

In many parts of North India, kites take over the skies, and delicious

sweets such as Til Ke Laddoo are enjoyed.

The same spirit and the same premise, when it travels all the way to North

East India, takes the shape of Magh Bihu. The end of the harvest season is

what the festival represents. Traditional dance, traditional games, and

activities such as Cooking in Meji (Bamboo Huts) define the festival in the

state of Assam.

Subject: Invitation to Apply for Smt. Rajeswari Viswanathan Memorial Scholarship Scheme 2024-25 - Reg
Body:
Dear Students,

We are pleased to inform you that applications for the Smt. Rajeswari

Viswanathan Memorial Scholarship (Financial Assistance to Deserving

Students) Scheme for the academic year 2024-25 are now open. This

scholarship aims to support students who demonstrate financial need and

merit.

To apply for the scholarship, please follow the steps below:

 - Log in to your VTOP account.

 - Navigate to the Services section.

 - Select Financial Assistance Scholarship.

 - Complete the application form and submit it online.

Instructions

Financial Assistance will be awarded to the eligible students subject to

the following conditions:-

 - The annual income of the parent shall not exceed Rs.1,00,000/-.

 - Student should not have any standing arrears in semester Exams.

 - Student should not be in receipt of any other scholarship(s).

 - Attendance of more than 75% in each subject in the fall semester.

 - Not have been involved in any act(s) of indiscipline etc.

 - Interviews will be conducted for short-listed students

 - The original income certificate will be verified during the Interview

Last date for application on VTOP: 31.01.2025

Body:
Dear Students of VIT,

Greetings!

We are excited to announce a collaboration with IIT Bombay for a 2-month

Training and Internship Program. This program offers certifications from

top global companies like CISCO, META (Facebook), IBM, and several

other multinational corporations in both technical and non-technical

 domains.

Eligibility:

This opportunity is available only to shortlisted students from VIT.

Note: If any of your batchmates missed this notification, feel free to

forward this email to them.

Registration Deadline:

To apply, please fill out the Application Form

https://forms.gle/hquuD27paudh24GP7. Shortlisted candidates will receive

further instructions from our HR team.

LINK:https://forms.gle/hquuD27paudh24GP7

https://forms.gle/hquuD27paudh24GP7

Additionally, you can Join the WhatsApp Group for updates and details.

Program Details:First Month:

 - Live training from IIT Bombay, including interactive sessions and

 mentorship from industry experts. (Login credentials will be shared after

 registration).

Second Month:

 - Internship with Real-World Projects:

 - Individual Projects: 10 projects, each intern will complete tasks

 with guidance from a mentor.

 - Capstone Project: A group project involving 4-5 interns.

Program Format:

 - Blended Program/Recorded Classes: Access recorded lectures and

 attend live sessions on weekends for doubt clearing.

 - Mentor-Led/Live Classes: Live Zoom sessions 3-4 times a week at 6:30

 PM. Recordings will also be available.

 - Learning Management System (LMS): 6 months of access to the LMS

 portal.

Benefits Upon Completion:

 - IIT Bombay Certification.

 - Verified certificates through Wipro Dice ID.

 - Co-branded Internship Certificate from leading MNCs.

 - 100% Placement Assistance.

 - Access to a growing professional community.

 - Curriculum covering Generative AI and Prompt Engineering.

 - Exclusive Masterclasses with top global company founders and CXOs.

 - Personalized Mentorship for career guidance.

Who Should Apply:

This notification is for students who missed the scholarship opportunity in

previous batches (Oct-Nov, Nov-Dec, Dec-Jan).

Take the first step toward an exciting career and Submit Your Application

Now https://forms.gle/hquuD27paudh24GP7.

We look forward to your participation!

Subject: Innovation week Call for Volunteers: Join Us for Innovation Week 2025!
Body:
Dear Students,

We are thrilled to announce Innovation Week 2025, a celebration of

creativity, technology, and ground-breaking ideas, scheduled to take place

from 21st January to 25th January 2025. To ensure the success of this

landmark event, we are inviting enthusiastic and dedicated students to join

as volunteers and play a vital role in its smooth execution.

This event is a platform to celebrate innovation, creativity, and the

spirit of entrepreneurship among our students.

To make this event a resounding success, we seek dedicated volunteers like

you to join our team. By volunteering, you will gain valuable experience in

event management, networking, and teamwork. You will also have the

opportunity to interact with successful entrepreneurs and industry leaders.

If you are interested in being part of this exciting initiative, please

fill out this form:

https://forms.gle/P7gbeQDZABe64fvj7

If you have any queries, contact:

Harshini M(+91 70947 88897)

Apurv (+91 87881 93190)

Let's make this event extraordinary together. Looking to get you there!

Subject: Today's Special Event: NRI Day Celebrations-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

We are delighted to invite you to join the celebration of Pravasi Bharatiya

Divas (NRI Day) on 9th January 2025. This special day honors the

contributions of NRIs and foreign students while celebrating the diverse

cultures that enrich our VIT community.

Event Highlights:

 1.

 Interactive Cultural Map: Pin your country and share unique cultural

 stories.

 2.

 Face Painting & Tattoo Making: Creative designs inspired by Indian

 culture.

 3.

 Live Photo Printing Booth: Capture memories with Indian-themed props.

 4.

 Pictionary with Indian Themes: Fun drawing games with Indian cultural

 prompts.

 5.

 Story Wall: Share your experiences as an NRI or foreign student.

 6.

 Guess the State: Identify Indian states through images, attire, and

 cuisines.

 7.

 Turban & Mehndi: Experience India’s vibrant traditions with turban

 tying and mehndi art.

Evening Session: (Open for All Students)

 -

 Time: 4:00 P.M. onwards

 -

 Venue: Greenos Pathway

 -

 Highlights:

 1.

 Interactive Cultural Events: Enjoy engaging cultural performances and

 activities.

 2.

 Cultural Stalls: Visit stalls set up by NRI and foreign students and

 indulge in interactive and fun activities.

 3.

 Cake Cutting: A special cake cutting ceremony in the presence of

 our esteemed guests.

Body:
The office of Students Welfare invites you for an enlightening session on

"Safe Roads, Safe Lives: Road Safety Awareness Week." organised by the

National Service Scheme (NSS). This event will focus on enhancing your

knowledge about traffic rules, safe driving practices, and pedestrian

safety. Gain valuable insights from, Traffic Inspector - Mr. R Govinda

Samy and SI - Mr. R Mithilesh Kumar, as they lead the session with talks,

demonstrations, and practical tips to ensure safer roads for everyone.

Event Details:

📍 Venue: Sarojini Naidu Gallery (Offline)

🗓 Date: 9th January 2025

⏰ Time: 11:00 AM to 12:30 PM

VTOP registration is mandatory to participate.

Let’s take this opportunity to learn, engage, and contribute to promoting

road safety. We look forward to seeing you all there!

Subject: Celebration of Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (NRI Day)-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

We are delighted to invite you to join the celebration of Pravasi Bharatiya

Divas (NRI Day) on 9th January 2025. This special day honors the

contributions of NRIs and foreign students while celebrating the diverse

cultures that enrich our VIT community.

Event Details:

Morning Session:

 -

 Time: 9:30 am - 12:30 am

 -

 Venue: Rajaji Hall

 -

 Highlights:

 1.

 Interactive Cultural Map: Pin your country and share unique cultural

 stories.

 2.

 Face Painting & Tattoo Making: Creative designs inspired by Indian

 culture.

 3.

 Live Photo Printing Booth: Capture memories with Indian-themed props.

 4.

 Pictionary with Indian Themes: Fun drawing games with Indian cultural

 prompts.

 5.

 Story Wall: Share your experiences as an NRI or foreign student.

 6.

 Guess the State: Identify Indian states through images, attire, and

 cuisines.

 7.

 Turban & Mehndi: Experience India’s vibrant traditions with turban

 tying and mehndi art.

Evening Session: (Open for All Students)

 -

 Time: 4:00 P.M. onwards

 -

 Venue: Greenos Pathway

 -

 Highlights:

 1.

 Interactive Cultural Events: Enjoy engaging cultural performances and

 activities.

 2.

 Cultural Stalls: Visit stalls set up by NRI and foreign students and

 indulge in interactive and fun activities.

 3.

 Cake Cutting: A special cake cutting ceremony in the presence of

 our esteemed guests.

Subject: Announcement: YANTRA Central Hackathon-reg
Body:
Dear VITians,

Greetings from Team Yantra 2025!

We are delighted to announce the Yantra Central Hackathon, an exciting

opportunity for all VIT Vellore students to collaborate and innovate. This

year’s theme is “AI for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)”, and the

hackathon is open to students from all branches and disciplines.

We’ve launched a dedicated website where you can find all the necessary

details about the hackathon and register: https://yantrahack.swvit.in/

📌 Registration Deadline: 17th January 2025

Attached to this email, you will find the Rule Book, which contains

comprehensive guidelines and other important information about the event.

We look forward to your participation and are excited to see your creative

ideas in action!

For any queries, feel free to reach out to Student Coordinator:

Ishan Jain - +918438162183

Subject: Clubs & Chapters enrollment is LIVE!
Body:
Dear Students,

Greetings!

The wait is over and it's time to enroll for the VIT Clubs and Chapters!

Hope you all attended Quanta 2024 and got to know more about the activities

of our various Clubs and Chapters functioning under the Office of Students'

Welfare.

Students can now register for their preferred Clubs & Chapters for the year

2025.

NO maximum limit for enrolling in clubs/chapters.

Clubs & Chapters enrollment is valid only for ONE year.

Registration can be done through VTOP- SW Events- Club/Chapter Enrollments.

Select the check box against your preferred Club & Chapter and submit.

A Green Tick against your selected CC means that you have been enrolled.

Please ensure that the registration process is completed before logging out.

For any queries, please mail to events.sw@vit.ac.in

Last Date for Enrollment: 31.01.2025 (Friday)

Body:
Dear VITians,

The Office of Students' Welfare, Tamil Literary Association, Department of

Physical Education, VAIAL School & HOT School invite you for the PONGAL

 CELEBRATION 2025.

We have a lot of traditional events and games lined up to help you

experience the traditional festival of Tamil Nadu!

Here are some of the exciting features that we have got for you:

 - Special traditional cultural events like Tanjavur Melam, Karagattam,

 Bharathanatyam, Jikkaattam, Silambattam, Devarattam, Parayattam,

 thudumbattam, and Periya Melam performed by invited professional artists

 and VIT students.

 - Pongal Making Competition for Faculty, Staff Members and Research

 Scholars

 - Distribution of Sweet Pongal and Sugarcane for all the attendees.

 - Food stalls (40+ traditional food items)

 - Pottery Making Stall.

 - Palm Leaf Craft Stall.

 - Mulai pari procession by VAIAL School students.

 - VAIAL School Students Exhibition Stall.

 - Release of Agriculture-related booklets authored by faculty.

 - Fun events stall by SW Office: Bambaram, Pallankuzhi & Karumbudaithal.

VAIAL School has also arranged a Model Village with the concept "One Day

in Village" for everyone to visit:

 - Paddy Farming

 - Fish Pond

 - Poultry

 - Cattle Shed (Goat and Cow)

 - Bullock Cart

 - Well

 - Traditional HUT with household utilities

 - Rabbit House

 - Gaming Zone

 - Jallikattu Kaalai

 - Pongal Making

 - Poonthottam

 - Azolla Cultivation

All are invited!

Body:
Dear Students,

Reminder: Last date for participant online registration: (Today) 7th

January 2025

ISRO has announced START 2025 programme. The third edition of Space science

and Technology Awareness Training (START) 2025 programme will be conducted

during January - February 2025. Since our university is nodal center for

this programme, kindly circulate the registration details to our students

and faculties.

ISRO START is an introductory level online training in space science

and technology for the under-graduate and post-graduate students of science

and technology. The programme is conducted online mode during Jan - Feb

2025. The theme of the current edition is "Future of India's Space

Exploration". . VIT, Vellore is nodal center for this programme . The

registration for this program can be done using Jigyasa portal by choosing

category 1. Category-1: Students from approved START host

institutes/nodal centres Post-graduate students and preferably the final

year under graduate students of physical sciences (Physics and Chemistry)

and technology (e.g. Electronics, Computer Science, Mechanical, Applied

Physics, Radiophysics, Optics & Opto-electronics, Instrumentation and other

associated subjects) studying in educational institutes/ Universities/

Colleges in India are eligible to be considered for the training under this

category. Participation certificate / merit certificate will be provided to

the eligible students.

Link for registering student participants of approved nodal center:

https://elearning.iirs.gov.in/edusatregistration/student

Subject: Pongal Celebration 2025 - Invitation
Body:
Dear VITians,

VIT has been organizing Pongal Celebrations every year through the Office

of Students’ Welfare in association with Tamil Literary Association,

Department of Physical Education, VAIAL & HOT School. It is time again to

celebrate the festival of harvest with gratitude in its full bloom. The

celebration will start with greeting and welcoming our Honourable Founder

and Chancellor, Dr. G. Viswanathan, by a traditional Tamil band lineup and

performance, followed by Parivattam and traditional Pongal celebrations.

Special traditional cultural events like Tanjavur Melam, Karagattam,

Bharathanatyam, Jikkaattam, Silambattam, Devarattam, Parayattam,

Thudumbattam and Periya Melam will be performed by invited professional

artists and VIT students.

As part of this, various sports and fun events like Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Sack

Race, Tyre Race, Three Leg Race, Kolam, Anthakshari, Slow Cycle Race, Tug

of War, Nondi Race, Kangaroo race, Karumbudaithal etc. have been organised

Guidelines for course registration and evaluation process

# Students are advised to check the curriculum and plan accordingly.

For the students of B. Tech Core Programmes, this project type course will

be considered under Programme Elective Category and for the students of

"Specialization Programmes", it will be considered under "Open Elective

Category". If the students of "Specialization Programmes" have already

earned sufficient credits under "Open Elective Category", then it is not

necessary to register for this project type course.

# Students are expected to form a team and identify a faculty guide

from any School to initiate the process.

# Project Team should comprise a minimum of two to a maximum of five

students only from any B. Tech Programme of any School / Five Year

Integrated Programme as applicable. (students of B. Tech Programme and Five

Year Integrated Programme can not be in the same team)

# Domain specific / Interdisciplinary / Multidisciplinary /

Cross-disciplinary projects are encouraged.

# Guide will finalize the tentative title / area of the work and

the team of students to work on each project. Course Registration is opened

on VTOP Login for the faculty members (Guide). (Preliminary discussion

between the guide and the student is essential)

# Students can work for one project type course at any point of

time.

# Course Registration will be done by the respective Guide only. The

Guide will fill in the necessary data (Project title and the Registration

Number of all the students proposed to work on each of the projects) on

VTOP Faculty Login.

# Subsequently the course will reflect on the list of registered

courses for that particular semester on VTOP Student Login. This three

credit course will not affect the upper limit of 27 credits allowed for a

regular semester.

# Minimum duration of the project period is six months and the

maximum duration is 12 months.

# Once the Project work is completed and a tangible

outcome (Research / Review Paper published / accepted in Scopus / WoS,

Journal / Conference Proceedings: Product Design / Patent Application) is

reached, the Guide will post the marks out of 100 for each student on VTOP

and submit.

# Absolute Grading System will be followed for the listed project

type courses as per VIT Grading Policy

# Even after 12 months, if the team fails to complete the project,

then the course will be de-registered for the students.

Faculty Members are requested to take note of the message and proceed

accordingly. Project Course Registration is enabled for all the faculty

members on "VTOP - Faculty Login"

Subject: Today's Special Event: Awareness Session on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (PoSH)-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

The Office of Students' welfare invites you for an awareness session on

PoSH.

As part of our commitment to fostering a safe and inclusive campus

environment, we are pleased to invite you to an "Awareness Session on

Prevention of Sexual Harassment (PoSH)" organized by the NSS Club and Red

Ribbon Club.

Date: Today, 07th January

Time: 03:00 PM - 05:00 PM

Venue: Shakespeare Gallery - TT

Dr. Ramya Nisal https://in.linkedin.com/in/ramyanisal?trk=public_post-text,

Director of the Rakshin Project by Sakshi. The Rakshin Project, a Youth Led

Movement, Pan India, to stop child sexual abuse started with a directive

received by Sakshi, from the Directorate of NSS, Ministry of Youth Affairs

& Sports, Government of India, for delivering workshops with NSS Volunteers

in order to strengthen ‘Youth as powerful enablers’ for creating a

Constitutional Rights Based Enabled Environment in the context of Gender

Equality, with a focus on building awareness about POCSOA 2012 (Amendment

2019) to #STOPCHILDSEXUALABUSE. Sakshi (Regd. NGO, 1992) recently signed an

MoU with the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, GOI and the Directorate

of NSS to continue the work. The Rakshin Project aims to address the

denial, stigma, shame, and silence associated with gender violence with a

focus on preventing child sexual abuse and building a culture of

accountability.

We encourage all students to attend this important session. Your

participation is crucial in creating a safe and respectful campus

environment for everyone.

We look forward to seeing you there.

Body:

We are excited to invite you to the Chapters and teams Exhibition at

Quanta '25, our annual showcase of student chapters and teams at VIT! This

is your chance to explore the diverse array of chapters and teams on

campus, discover new interests, and find out how you can become a part of

our vibrant community.

Time: 04:00 PM to 08:00 PM

Venue: SMV Portico

Join us on the 7th to meet chapter and team members, learn about their

initiatives, and see firsthand what they have to offer. This is an

incredible opportunity to connect with fellow students who share your

interests and passions. Whether you're into technology,

management,mechanical, automobile, manufacturing, space, civil, electrical,

electronics, chemical, biotechnology, agriculture, computer, IT, design,

architecture, automation, medical, entrepreneur, personality development,

energy, education, UI/UX, product design, etc. there’s one for everyone!

Mark your calendars, and don't miss out on the chance to become a part of

Body:
School of Computer Science and Engineering

Academic Regulations on Attendance Requirements

1. The attendance percentage will be calculated from the ‘date of

registration’ into a course to one day before the start of the exam

component. Computerized attendance monitoring system is adopted for posting

the attendance by the faculty.

2. A student is expected to maintain 100% attendance in all courses.

3. A student may need leave due to ill-health or to attend family

emergency is permitted to maintain a minimum of 75% (i.e. absent for 25% of

instructional hours) in each course, without producing any proof for the

absence.

· 25% absence includes medical, personnel, casual, official leave of

absence for organizing events/ seminars/ workshops/ technical/ cultural

festivals/competitions/ participation in co-curricular/ extra-curricular

events/ NSS & NCC camps, any other (valid or otherwise) reason.

4. Since no one is exempted from the minimum attendance requirements,

students who fail to maintain the minimum attendance criteria will not be

permitted to write the next evaluation component of the course (CAT/FAT

Exam component fixed by the course faculty in case of courses), and they

will be debarred from writing the exam.

5. Once the student fails to meet the minimum attendance requirement,

the attendance software will indicate the status of that exam component as

“Debarred” for the respective course.

6. Students having a CGPA of 9.00 and above (CGPA ≥ 9.00) and with no

current backlog courses are exempted from the minimum attendance

requirements.

· It is expected that these students will continue to attend all the

classes without absence and will not take this as an advantage to skip

classes.

· If such students’ CGPA falls below 9.00, they will be subjected to

the minimum attendance requirements again.

· The nine-pointers list will be dynamically generated and applied at

the time of preparation of the debarred list of each exam component

(CAT/FAT) of a course.

7. In case of emergency (Hospitalization/Death in the family)

· The first intimation must be given to the proctor.

· If he/she has been admitted to the hospital as an inpatient due to

medical reasons, they must submit their discharge summary, fitness

certificate, and hospital bills to the Head of the Department (

hod.ss@vit.ac.in) through the Proctor with a copy to the Programme

Secretary (secretary.ss@vit.ac.in) within three days after rejoining or

before the last working day whichever is early.

· Medical prescriptions are not considered under any circumstances.

· Based on the nature of the request, the school-level committee will

decide on Attendance Relaxation. Medical leaves will not be updated on

VTOP.

· After submitting the request, students are expected to attend all

the classes regularly and if absences are found at later stages, then

medical leave will not be considered.

8. During the exam period to avail permission for Re-CAT and Re-FAT due

to Hospitalization/ Death in the family, Students are required to follow

the circular from Dean Academics and CoE respectively (refer to the emails

from the respective office).

Best Regards,

Dr.K.S.Umadevi

Professor and Head

Dear Students

AICTE and MOE is calling student innovators including incubated startups

for IDE - Bootcamp -2025 between 17th Feb to 21st Feb. Interested students

can participate. For more information see the information in the mail

thread below

thanks and regards

C Ramesh Kumar

Director Innovations

The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and the Ministry of

Education's Innovation Cell (MIC) successfully organized the first edition

of the “Innovation, Design, and Entrepreneurship (IDE) Bootcamps.” This

initiative, envisioned by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, aims to

nurture the innovation, design, and entrepreneurial skills of student

innovators and innovation ambassadors from higher education institutions We

encourage all higher education institutions to motivate their students to

participate in the IDE Bootcamp and to spread this information within the

student community.

For glimpses about last year Edition 1 (Phase-I, Phase-II & Phase III) and

Edition 2 Phase I bootcamps, please go through the link below: -

https://bootcamp.mic.gov.in/ https://bootcamp.mic.gov.in/

Now, in the Second Edition of IDE Bootcamp Phase II, AICTE and MIC are

going to be organize 11 Bootcamps at following locations during the period

of 17th February 2025 to 21st February 2025 (Tentative).

12 cities are shortlisted (Tentative) for conducting the bootcamps as

follows: -

 students and early-stage incubated startups with ground breaking project

ideas to gain the skills and support needed to bring their innovations to

life.

Who Should Apply?

 - Students: If you have an innovative project idea and are enrolled in

 an undergraduate or postgraduate program at a recognized institution, this

 bootcamp is for you.

 - Incubated Start-ups in academic Institutions: Applications are

 welcome from early-stage companies that have a distinct innovation emphasis

 and have been nurtured at a local incubation facility. Preferably, a

 prototype or Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is being developed.

The bootcamp is a 5-day residential training program where student teams

from higher education institutions and startup teams will undergo intensive

experiential learning on design aspects of startups, design thinking,

business modeling, financial planning, and enterprise planning, followed by

mentoring and pitching rounds. Accommodation and meals will be provided to

participants during the IDE Bootcamps.

Application Process:

Please submit your application through the following link:

https://bootcamp.mic.gov.in/

Last Date to Apply:

15th January 2025, up to 2:30 PM

For any queries, feel free to contact us:

 - Email: idebootcamp@aicte-india.org, ankush.sharma@aicte-india.org,

 rc3.mic@aicte-india.org, aid_mic@aicte-india.org

 - Landline: 011-29581222, 011-29581223, 011-29581240

Don’t miss this chance to take your innovation journey to the next level!

Note: Prospective participants can give 2 location preferences for the

bootcamp. But allocation of the nodal center to the participants (if

selected) will be done as per availability to the nearest location.

Subject: Resubmit the Revaluation Comments in Codetantra
Body:
Dear Students,

This is regarding the revaluation comments entered in the codetantra. It

is found that many of the students' comments are not visible since the

students have not saved the revaluation comments. Hence we decided to get

the comments again from you for the revaluation process. I request you to

follow the below steps for giving the comments while applying for

revaluation. The details about the following procedure is attached for

your reference.

Procedure: 

Step 1. Login to codetantra using VTOP login credentials.

Step 2. Navigate to See Results button. Select the appropriate exam month

and date, then click on See Results

Step 3. Review the Answer Sheets and Provide Comments on Questions. Click

on the View Answer button for the question you want to comment on.

 A text box will appear where you can type your comments.

Step 4. Once you've added comments for all the necessary questions, click

on the Save Comments button at the top of the page

If you do not click the Save Comments button, your comments will not be

saved or submitted.

Note: All the students who have applied for revaluation should re-type

the comments and save the comments as per the above instructions.

Please complete this task before 7th Jan 2025(Tuesday) , 9.00 AM. For any

query, you can send an email to deputycoe@vit.ac.in <deputycoe@vit.ac.in>

 or asstcoe@vit.ac.in <asstcoe@vit.ac.in>. We will also ensure that the

revaluation process will start only after receiving comments from all the

students who applied for revaluation.

--

Subject: Announcing Yantra’25: A Week of Technical Innovation!
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are thrilled to announce the 5th edition of our much-anticipated annual

technical week, Yantra 2025! Events are scheduled to take place from

February 3 to February 9, 2025, and promises a week brimming with

innovation, learning, and groundbreaking ideas. This year, Yantra is set

to be bigger and better, bringing together innovation, collaboration, and

learning under the theme:“AI for SDG Goals”.

This is a great opportunity for students to showcase their technical skills

and talents through their active participation in a variety of technical

competitions. hackathons, workshops, technical talks- we have it all.

Join us for “A Week of Technical Innovation” as we merge the power of AI

with the vision of achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Whether you're a tech enthusiast, a budding innovator, or a seasoned

expert, Yantra’25 promises something exciting for everyone.

Stay tuned for updates on registrations, event schedules, and prize pool.

Let’s make Yantra’25 a memorable journey of learning and impact!

For more information: yantra.sw@vit.ac.in

Subject: New Year Celebration 2025 invite-reg
Body:
Dear Students, Staff, and Faculty,

As the clock strikes midnight and we bid farewell to 2024, the Office of

Students' Welfare invites you to a night of dazzling music, laughter, and

celebration to welcome the New Year! Join us for an unforgettable evening

at the Anna Auditorium on December 31st, 2024, starting at 8 PM sharp. Let

us gather as one for the symbolic cake cutting ceremony officiated by our

esteemed founder and chancellor, Dr. G Viswanathan, marking the start of a

prosperous new year.

Get ready for a vibrant blend of entertainment as we usher in 2025:

 - Movie Mania: A captivating film screening to set the mood for the

 evening.

 - Rhythm and Groove: Let loose and dance the night away with energetic

 music sets by our talented DJs.

 - Prize Bonanza: Win exciting gifts in fun games and raffles throughout

 the night.

 - Sweet Delights: Savor a delicious cake, a symbol of good luck and

 prosperity, making it the perfect choice for ringing in the New Year.

This is your chance to create lasting memories, connect with your fellow

VITians, and step into the New Year with joy and positivity. So, mark your

calendars, gather your VIT friends, and don your dancing shoes for a night

of unforgettable merriment!

Additional Details:

 - Date: December 31st, 2024

 - Venue: Anna Auditorium, VIT

 - Time: 8:00 PM onwards

 - Entry: Open to all VIT students, staff, and faculty

We look forward to celebrating with you!

Subject: Application Deadline : Live Project in Financial Markets (Equity Markets Analyst)
Body:
Hi ,

As today, 11.59 PM is the deadline to apply for the Finlatics Financial Markets Experience Program (FMEP), please note:

1. Due to the presence of training, mentoring and guidance, and live sessions, please note that no prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to be a part of this project.

2. If you have any upcoming assignment, examination, or personal commitment, you can pick a project start date after completing the same to help the project fit in with your schedule.

3. You will be allowed a break during the project tenure for any academic or personal commitment. You would also be allowed a Project Extension of an additional month in case you cannot complete it in the 2-month duration.

4. You can apply for the project using the link:

( https://www.finlatics.com/fm_application?src=vitv1d )

5. The time commitment required for the project is around 4 - 5 hours per week

6. You would also be engaged in an Artificial Intelligence-driven mock interview and get a detailed report to understand your areas of improvement.

If selected, the program has a minimal induction fee: Rs. 1999 + GST / Rs. 2999 + GST (based on student choice).

Fee Waiver: A fee waiver in the range of 15 - 25% shall be given to the Vellore Institute of Technology students on the abovementioned minimal induction fee.

To be eligible for the waiver, please apply before tonight's deadline.

The first email circulated at the campus is attached below.

Hi ,

We're pleased to open applications for the Finlatics Financial Markets Experience Program (FMEP), an online live project that helps students gain work experience in equity markets at Vellore Institute of Technology.

The project is running at leading campuses including IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIT Delhi and BITS Pilani among others, and was curated at the prestigious Atal Incubation Centre, supported by the Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog & Government of India.

STRUCTURE of the Live Project:

1. Equity trading, research, and analysis-based project

2. Create, manage, and maintain a real-time simulated portfolio on BSE 500 listed companies

3. The simulated portfolio will be assessed by linking it to the real-time BSE 500 INDEX, akin to an asset management company

4. Engage in sector-wise and company-specific research on the Indian Economy

5. Mentor-based guidance to each student by an Equity Advisor

6. Case studies covering valuation & stock analysis along with the live experience

7. Flexible start-date option, where the student can pick a start date for the project at their convenience

The project is doable on a standalone basis and also along with any other commitment due to its work from home, online structure.

BENEFITS to students :

1. Certificate of Work Experience in Financial Markets as an FMEP Equity Markets Analyst

2. Letter of Recommendation to top-performing students.

3. Engage in an Artificial Intelligence-driven mock interview and get a detailed report to understand your areas of improvement.

To apply, students can fill the form below and we will get in touch with them:

https://www.finlatics.com/fm_application?src=vitv1

All students must note that no prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to be a part of this project. Personalized guidance and mentoring, as well as live sessions, would be provided for financial markets to train students during the live project.

Project Duration: 2 months (3- 4 hours per week)

Project Start: Flexible on selected student choice. To balance the project along with any upcoming academic or personal commitments, selected students can choose to start it once they are completed

Project Break: Selected students will be eligible for a break during the project, in case they need it for any academic or personal commitments.

Incentives: Up to Rs. 6000 (to monthly top-performing students)

If selected, the program has a minimal induction fee: Rs. 1999 + GST / Rs. 2999 + GST (based on student choice).

Fee Waiver: A fee waiver of 15 - 25% shall be given to all Vellore Institute of Technology students on the abovementioned minimal induction fee.

To be eligible for the fee waiver, kindly apply through the above-mentioned link only.

We are looking forward to a fruitful engagement.

Subject: Fwd: Value Added Course on "Technical documentation with Latex" -VAC 2411 - Starts from 5th January
Body:
Dear Students and Research Scholars,

The value added course on “Technical documentation with LATEX using

Textstudio and Oveleaf” aims to introduce the more popularly used Latex

Software for translating the projects, research works into manuscripts in

the form of journal papers, conference papers and thesis. This course deals

with LATEX commands for page formatting, Mathematical equations, Lists,

Tables, Figures, References along with hands-on sessions using Textstudio

and Overleaf online latex document preparation platform.

Highlights of the course:

· 32 hours Course Duration

· Introduction to LATEX

· Practical training: : Documentation with LATEX using Texstudio

· Practical training: Online Documentation in Over leaf platform and

sharing it with collaborators.

· Manuscript preparation of student design/simulation project for a

journal/conference of choice

· E Certificate (Min of 75% attendance & 60% of marks)

Registration Fee: Rs 500 (Inclusive of GST) Registration Link : 

https://events.vit.ac.in/

Thanks and Regards,

Subject: Live Project in Financial Markets (Equity Markets Analyst)
Body:
Dear VIT students,

We're pleased to open applications for the Finlatics Financial Markets Experience Program (FMEP), an online live project that helps students gain work experience in equity markets at the Vellore Institute of Technology.

The project is running at leading campuses including IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIT Delhi and BITS Pilani among others, and was curated at the prestigious Atal Incubation Centre, supported by the Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog & Government of India.

STRUCTURE of the Live Project:

1. Equity trading, research, and analysis-based project

2. Create, manage, and maintain a real-time simulated portfolio on BSE 500 listed companies

3. The simulated portfolio will be assessed by linking it to the real-time BSE 500 INDEX, akin to an asset management company

4. Engage in sector-wise and company-specific research on the Indian Economy

5. Mentor-based guidance to each student by an Equity Advisor

6. Case studies covering valuation & stock analysis along with the live experience

Flexible start-date option, where the student can pick a start date for the project at their convenience

The project is doable on a standalone basis and also along with any other commitment due to its work from home, online structure.

BENEFITS to students :

1. Certificate of Work Experience in Financial Markets as an FMEP Equity Markets Analyst

2. Letter of Recommendation to top-performing students.

3. Engage in an Artificial Intelligence-driven mock interview and get a detailed report to understand your areas of improvement.

To apply, students can fill the form below and we will get in touch with them:

https://www.finlatics.com/fm_application?src=vitv1

No prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to be a part of this project. Personalized guidance and mentoring, as well as live sessions, would be provided for financial markets to train students during the live project.

Project Duration: 2 months (3- 4 hours per week)

Project Start: Flexible on selected student choice.

Project Break: Selected students will be eligible for a break during the project, in case they need it for any academic or personal commitments.

Incentives: up to Rs. 6000 (to monthly top-performing students)

If selected, the program has a minimal induction fee: Rs. 1999 + GST / Rs. 2999 + GST (based on student choice).

Fee Waiver: A fee waiver of 15 - 25% shall be given to all Vellore Institute of Technology students on the abovementioned minimal induction fee. This waiver will reduce the fee to Rs.1690 + GST / Rs. 2199 + GST.

To be eligible for the fee waiver, kindly apply through the above-mentioned link only.

We are looking forward to a fruitful engagement.

Body:
Office of the Controller of Examinations

Paper Seeing, Revaluation and Re-FAT Process for 

Fall Semester 2024-25 (Regular & Week End Intra Semester) FAT – Theory

 Paper Seeing and Revaluation:

· In the VTop student login, (“Examination → Marks → Fall

Semester 2024-25”) Marks for the Courses to which FAT was held during

Nov-Dec 2024 has been made available now.

· Actual Grades will be released on 01 January 2025 (Wednesday).

The Pass criteria and Grading Procedure are available in Academics →

Regulations

Tab in your login.

· If you want to know the question wise marks awarded to your

answers by the evaluator, you need to apply for it through V-Top. This is

referred as “Paper Seeing” process. It requires payment of Rs. 100 for each

paper. You can apply through: Examinations →Papersee/Rev → Fall

Semester 2024-25→Paper Seeing. You can choose course(s) you want to

apply for paper seeing. After Generating the Invoice, you need to make a

payment through “Online Payments” Tab in the same V-Top login.

· Once you have paid, within one or two working days, the

paper and question

wise marks awarded will be made available in CodeTantra login. You need

to use the same portal https://vit.codetantra.com for this process. After

seeing the paper, if you feel the mark awarded to a particular question is

not sufficient and the evaluator has missed something and there is a need

to recheck the mark, then you can apply for Revaluation of the Course. You

need to give suitable reason for the same in the comments section available

just below the mark awarded by the faculty.

· Please note that the Revaluation has to be applied only in V-Top

(in the same way as you have applied for paper seeing) and necessary

payments also needs to be paid through online payments tab. (Rs. 300 per

paper). Revaluation approval process in codetantra will be initiated only

after publishing the Grades, until then the status remains ‘approval

pending’ . Paper seeing and feedback / comments are mandatory for

re-evaluation and is in online mode only.

· Also note that “Paper seeing” and Revaluation is applicable only

for the Theory Courses to which FAT was conducted by CoE office . For other

components and Courses (like Laboratory / Project Courses IBL mode courses)

there is No Paper seeing and Revaluation Process.

· The students who were involved in Fall Semester 2024-25

examination malpractices are not eligible for paper seeing/ Re-valuation

process.

· After login, follow the instructions given in the platform for

giving comments to the questions which needs to be re-examined.

· Give your feedback with respect to the need for revaluation. If

no feedback is given for any question, your answer script will not be

considered for revaluation and No refund will be given for any approved

requests.

· Students should not approach or give any sort of request to any

faculty related to revaluation (increase of marks or grades). If we

receive any complaints from faculty, it will be treated as ‘Malpractice’

and revaluation request will summarily be rejected.

following reasons only:

by the ‘Re‐examinations Committee’. If needed the student may be asked to

followed for Re-FAT.

· Any student who fails to apply for Re‐FAT through VTop will NOT

be considered for further processing and has to repeat the course(s) by

· Please note that this process is only for getting approval for

grade will be published.

Dear Students,

 Round 2 application deadline for Johns Hopkins Carey Business School is

fast approaching on January 8, 2024.

This is to share that the GMAT/GRE is now optional for all full-time MS

programs. It’s entirely up to you whether you wish to include your scores

as part of your application.

As part of our partnership, students who have completed their undergraduate

program can be admitted to one of the MS programs at Carey Business School

and will be eligible for a 50% scholarship on the tuition fee.

Additionally, we strongly encourage the students to begin the course-by-course

evaluation of your transcripts as soon as possible. Evaluations can be

completed through any NACES-approved agencies, such as:

 - World Education Services (WES)

 - SpanTran

 - ECE

For more details about this process, please visit:

International Applicants Information

https://carey.jhu.edu/admissions/international-applicants.

If you have any questions or need assistance, feel free to reach out to

Shreyas Pardesi, Global Collaborations, Johns Hopkins Carey Business School

directly at +91 7875659000.

Additionally, you can join the official JHU Carey WhatsApp Group for

prospective students in India to connect with other applicants and stay

updated: Join Now https://chat.whatsapp.com/EfspUYZWeTSHPksFGCGIOT.

Wishing you the best as you complete your application!

Subject: Pongal Celebrations 2025: Participation in Kabaddi & Kho Kho Competitions-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

The Office of Students' Welfare will be organising Kabaddi & Kho Kho

Competitions as part of Pongal Celebrations 2025, in association with the

Department of Physical Education.

Keep your teams list ready in Excel or Word format. The list should have

the names, reg. no., phone no. & VIT email ID of all the team members.

 - Only 1 member per team needs to fill out the form.

 - Kabaddi: 10 members per team are allowed to register (7 Main

 Players + 3 Substitutes)

 - Kho-Kho: 12 members per team are allowed to register (9 Main

 Players + 3 Substitutes)

The application form will be shared by 06:00 AM on (26.12.2024)

Only the first 16 teams would get a chance to register and participate!!!

Subject: Student Webinar by the City University of London- UK - Topic: How Does a Society Embrace Technology- By Professor Nick Hine (15/12/25)
Body:
Dear Students,

I am writing to let you know that our next webinar will be delivered by

Professor Nick Hine on the topic of How does a society embrace

technology?: Exploring modelling and tools for enquiry, Wednesday 15th

January 2025 from 10am UK time.

Please register for the webinar using this link

https://city-ac-uk.zoom.us/meeting/register/tZcocuqurDkuEte8Y4q6rr8-pHTc6OuKSAfI.

An abstract for January’s topic is as follows:

Change alters society. If that change is associated with the introduction

of technology, it can be considered that technology has changed a society.

Society tends not to manage either the introduction of new technology nor

really understand how that introduction has influenced and changed the

society.

 As a consequence, understanding the changes and then managing the place

of technology tends to be a retrospective enterprise, often triggered by

evidence or a belief that harm has been caused. With seismic change in

society anticipated with the increasing adoption of technologies such as

AI, those associated with mitigating climate change and addressing health

epidemics such as obesity and diabetes, the ability to model and forecast

the consequences of change are essential.

In any design and development (engineering) endeavour, stakeholders with

different interests inevitably imagine roles and outcomes very differently.

Understanding societal change involves stakeholders with widely diverse

interests.

 Sociologists have a number of theoretical frameworks but few usable tools

to model a society and changes within it, and even fewer that can enable

them to explore these changes with stakeholders. Furthermore, modelling the

attributes of a society and the attributes of influence and change are

immensely difficult, not just because of the complexity of factors, but

also the accounting for the meaning, value and weighting of influence that

modulates change.

In this session we will explore this dilemma and explore an ongoing

conversation between a sociologist and a computer scientist who are

revisiting how bridging between stakeholders might be facilitated so that

useful and usable computing tools can be devised that support the inquiry.

More information about Nick can be found below:

Prof Nick Hine, drawing on his background in Electronic and Biomedical

Engineering and Applied Computing, has a fascination for looking for the

best fit between people and technology. This has been stimulated by his

research focussed on promoting social and economic integration of disabled

people in society, enabled by technology. 

This led to consideration of contexts that have included rehabilitation

technology, educational technology, smart home and smart cities and

home-based care. He currently co-leads the new User Experience Engineering

Masters programme at City St George’s University of London.

Register for the January webinar here:

https://city-ac-uk.zoom.us/meeting/register/tZcocuqurDkuEte8Y4q6rr8-pHTc6OuKSAf

(Please note that in the instance that recording was not possible for

confidentiality reasons a recording will not be provided). Details of the

upcoming 2025 webinars are also listed here and will be updated to provide

further information in due course. Each month will feature a new topic,

delivered by an expert within the field, and will showcase research and

teaching currently taking place within the School. Sessions will consist of

International Human Solidarity Day

International Human Solidarity Day is a day to celebrate our unity in

diversity; a day to remind governments to respect their commitments to

international agreements; a day to raise public awareness of the importance

of solidarity; a day to encourage debate on the ways to promote solidarity

for the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals including poverty

eradication; a day of action to encourage new initiatives for poverty

eradication.

IEEE Communications Society (IEEE ComSoc)

Event Name: Visionary Forces: Innovators vs Leaders

Time: 02:00 PM to 03:30 PM

Venue: MB210 (OFFLINE)

Event Description: IEEE COMSOC organizes "Visionary Forces", an engaging

and thought provoking event that brings that brings together the two

critical forces driving progress in today's world - technology innovation

and effective leadership. The event will be structured as a debate and

collaborative discussion, where participants explore the interplay between

cutting-edge tools and the strategic minds leading their implementation.

Registration: VTOP registration

Instagram link: https://www.instagram.com/vitieeecomsoc/

IEEE Communications Society (IEEE ComSoc)

Event Name: Out of the tank: Wild Ideas Edition

Time: 04:00 PM to 06:00 PM

Venue: MB210 (OFFLINE)

Event Description: IEEE COMSOC organizes "Out of the tank", a fun,

high-energy event inspired by the popular Shark Tank format, where

participants pitch their wildest, most creative, or even outright absurd

tech ideas to a panel of members. The goal is to encourage out-of-the-box

thinking, spark innovation, and celebrate creativity. The event is not

about the feasibility of the idea but rather the uniqueness of the concept

and the passion with which it is presented.

Registration: VTOP registration

hosted by the MUN Society! Dive into thought-provoking debates on pressing

global challenges aligned with the United Nations' Sustainable Development

Goals. Showcase your critical thinking, collaborate on innovative

solutions, and make your voice heard on issues that matter. Perfect for

aspiring change makers and future diplomats!

Registration: VTOP registration

American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME-VIT)

Event Name: Blog Fury 1.13

Time: 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM

Event Description: Smart materials have evolved from basic responsive

materials like shape memory alloys to advanced systems that self-heal and

adapt to their environment. These materials, which change properties in

response to stimuli like heat, pressure, or light, are now used in diverse

fields such as aerospace, healthcare, and robotics. Their development

continues to push the boundaries of innovation, enhancing efficiency and

performance in engineering.

Event Platform: CDMM 304 (Offline)

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/asme.vit/

Registration: VTOP

American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME-VIT)

Event Name: Mech Face-Off 1.14

Time: 3:45 PM to 4:45 PM

Event Description: Gear up for Mech Face Off 1.14, brought to you by ASME

VIT, where we debate the future of energy storage. The topic, "Graphene vs.

Carbon Nanotubes in Energy Storage," brings two groundbreaking materials

head-to-head. Explore their potential in revolutionizing batteries,

supercapacitors, and energy systems as participants dissect their unique

properties and applications. Dive into a clash of technical insights, bold

ideas, and visionary thinking that will illuminate the path.

Event Platform: CDMM 304 (Offline)

Time: 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM

Event Description: Empowering a Sustainable Future, Join us for an

immersive awareness and workshop event, where we'll explore innovative ways

to reduce our environmental footprint and create a more sustainable world.

Through engaging discussions, hands-on activities, and expert insights,

you'll gain the knowledge and tools to make a positive impact on the planet!

Event Description: In this event, we'll explore basic blockchain concepts

and the latest innovations in blockchain technology. The focus will be on

understanding new techniques and the emerging trends that are shaping the

future of blockchain. This session aims to provide participants with

in-depth knowledge of the topics, enhancing their understanding of how

blockchain is evolving and its potential impact on various sectors.

Registration: VTOP registration

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/adgvit?igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==

Event Name: ML Unboxed: A Beginner's Workshop

Time: 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM

Event Description: Join us for an engaging workshop on the fundamentals of

Machine Learning! This session will introduce you to the core concepts,

including types of ML like supervised and unsupervised learning, the

importance of data preprocessing, and foundational algorithms like Linear

Regression and Decision Trees. You’ll also learn essential model evaluation

metrics, such as accuracy and precision, to assess model performance. The

workshop will wrap up with a hands-on project using Python and

Scikit-Learn, where you’ll get to apply these concepts to build a simple ML

model. Perfect for beginners, this workshop offers a solid foundation to

Subject: Live Project in Data Science & Machine Learning with Python
Body:
Hi ,

As today, 11:59pm is the deadline to apply for the Finlatics Data Science & Machine Learning Experience Program, please note:

1. As Python would be taught in the program, please note that no prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to participate in the program.

2. Personalised guidance, mentoring, and live sessions would be provided to learn and help practice coding with Python.

3. If you have any upcoming assignment, examination, or personal commitment, you can pick a project start date after completing the same to help the project fit in with your schedule.

4. You will be allowed a break during the project tenure for any academic or personal commitment. You would also be allowed a Project Extension of an additional month in case you cannot complete it in the 2-month duration.

5. You can go over the project details using the copy of the mail below and apply for the project using the link :

https://www.finlatics.com/bads_application?utm_src=vitvd

6. The time commitment required for the project is around 3 - 4 hours per week.

If selected, the program has a minimal induction fee of Rs. 1999 + GST / Rs. 2999 + GST (on student choice)

Fee Waiver: A 20% fee waiver shall be given to all Vellore Institute of Technology students on the abovementioned minimal induction fee.

To be eligible for the waiver, kindly apply before tonight's deadline.

The first email circulated at the campus is attached below.

Hi ,

We're pleased to open applications for the Finlatics Data Science & Machine Learning Experience Program, an online live project that helps students gain experience in data science with Python and using machine learning algorithms at Vellore Institute of Technology.

This project runs at leading campuses, including IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIT Delhi, and BITS Pilani. Finlatics and was incubated at the Atal Incubation Centre, supported by Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog and Government of India.

STRUCTURE of the Live Project:

1. Learn the basics of Python and Machine Learning and how it can be used in data science.

2. Get hands-on learning and experience in writing various Python codes.

3. Dive into practical data manipulation and visualization using essential Python libraries.

4. Become proficient in using the Google Colab Notebook for machine learning

5. Gain an understanding of supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms using Python libraries

6. Explore statistical methods crucial for accurate data analysis, empowering learners with essential analytical skills.

7. Complete industry-specific case projects to understand the application of Python and Machine Learning in business scenarios

The project is doable along with any other commitment due to its work-from-home and online structure.

Student OUTCOMES:

1. Certificate of Work Experience in Data Science

2. Letter of Recommendation on performance

3. A Certificate of Proficiency i n Python and Machine Learning

To apply, students can fill out the form below, and we will get in touch with them:

https://www.finlatics.com/bads_application?utm_src=vitv

As Python would be taught in the program, all students must note that no prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to be a part of the program.

Personalized guidance & mentoring would also be provided to help students learn Python.

Live Sessions will be provided to help you practice coding with Python.

Project Duration: 2 months (3-4 Hours per week)

Project Start: Flexible on selected student choice.

Project Break & Extension: Selected students will be eligible for a break or extension during the project if needed for any exams, assignments, or personal commitments.

If selected, the program has a minimal induction fee of Rs. 1999 + GST / Rs. 2999 + GST (on student choice)

Fee Waiver: Vellore Institute of Technology students will be given a 20% fee waiver on the above mentioned minimal induction fee.

To be eligible for the waiver, kindly apply via the link above.

We are excited to have a fruitful engagement.
