Subject: Congratulations Team Orcus Robowars winners IIT Bomabay-reg
Body:
Dear VITians,

Greetings of the day,

We are thrilled to inform you that Team Orcus from the RoboVITics Club has

achieved outstanding success at the International Robowars event held at

Techfest,IIT Bombay held from the 17th to the 19th of December at IIT

Bombay, Mumbai.

Team Orcus from RoboVitics club emerged victorious in the 15kg and 60kg

categories.

 - 1st Place in the 60kg Category

 - 1st Place in the 15kg Category

Both the bots remained undefeated throughout the competition, eventually

securing the 1st place in their respective categories.

Techfest, IIT Bombay is the ultimate Robowars competition in India and by

winning it we have conquered the pinnacle of Indian Robowars.

Team members:-

Kommuru Karthikeya- 21MID0248

Abhinav Kumar-21BEE0150

Chaitanya Tejaswi - 22BCT0285

Riddhish Santosh Gupta- 22BME0405

Arnav Mishra- 23BIT0142

Vivaan Tarafdar- 23BEE0070

Archit Tiwari- 23BCT0011

The challenge was to design and build a robot capable of battling other

robots in a one-on-one tournament format, with the aim of causing maximum

damage or pushing the opponent's robot off the arena to score points. We

are immensely proud about this recognition to our college and extend our

gratitude for the support and encouragement we have received from the

management.

Congratulations to the team members and the faculty coordinator Dr. M.

SenthilKumar, (10347) Associate Professor Grade 2, SMEC.

We look forward to continuing our journey of innovation and excellence in

robotics.

Sender_Name: 'Director VIT Innovation' via B.Tech. - Comp  Sci Engg 2023 Group, Vellore Campus
Subject: Fwd: Participation in ISRO Robotic Challenge 2025-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

 See the email from ISRO regarding ISRO Robotic Challenge 2025 ( IRoC-U

2025 ). The IRoC-U 2025 challenges the students to develop ‘Autonomous

Navigation for an Aerial Vehicle (ANAV)’ without any external navigation

aid like GNSS, pseudolite or reflector arrays with a tagline ‘Fly me on

MARS’ . The last date for registration is 31st December 202. Interested

students can apply. The details of the event is below as a forwarded

message.

Thanks and regards

C Ramesh Kumar

Director Innovations

Greetings from Indian Space Research Organisation,

At ISRO we create unique opportunities for academia & industry to

participate in the technology developmental activities commensurate with

organisational objectives. In line with these objectives, U R Rao Satellite

Centre (URSC) solicits from the youth of India, innovative ideas and

designs of robotic rovers for future missions through the conduct of

IRoC-U. The objective here is to provide development opportunities in space

robotics to the participating entities and to leverage the creative

thinking among the youth of our Nation for ISRO interplanetary missions. It

is also expected to play an important role in augmenting ISRO’s activities

in space exploration.

The IRoC-U 2025 challenges the students to develop ‘Autonomous Navigation

for an Aerial Vehicle (ANAV)’ without any external navigation aid like

GNSS, pseudolite or reflector arrays with a tagline ‘Fly me on MARS’

All interested are encouraged to participate in this challenging

competition and join hands with ISRO, towards the advancement of space

science & technology in the country.

Please note that the date for registration is up to 31st December 2024 For

more information visit https://ursc.gov.in/IRoC-U2025

https://ursc.gov.in/IRoC-U2025

We look forward to your institution's enthusiastic participation!

Body:

Greetings!

The Office of Students' Welfare, invites you to "spring" to action on the

fourth day, as we gear up for an enthralling week of cultural

entertainment. As we revive ourselves from the hectic schedules and blues,

a much-needed breather from all the dreariness is serendipitous.

Presenting to you Prima Vera'24, a week of cultural entertainment housing

the various students and student teams of our university with interesting

competitions in dance, music, design, acting, animation, photography, art

and filmmaking with loads of exciting cash prizes to win.

Come join us for a scintillating experience!

Get ready to shine at the 5th edition of Prima Vera, VIT's annual cultural

Sender_Name: 'Dean SELECT' via B.Tech. - Comp  Sci Engg 2023 Group, Vellore Campus
Subject: Recruitment for Team Lambda
Body:
Dear Students,

Greetings of the day!!

We are excited to announce that Team Lambda, an official SELECT team, VIT

Vellore, is recruiting passionate and skilled individuals across various

departments to work on industrial projects, projects funded by Government

of India and international collaborative research.

Presently, our focus is on Autonomous Robot Development for various

industrial applications, including predictive solar panel maintenance,

smart buildings, digital twin and other cutting-edge projects. We are

currently offering a wide range of Winter Internship Opportunities, wherein

selected candidates will gain hands-on experience by working on projects

directly funded by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), India.

Skilled interns have the chance to secure a long-term position in the

team.

Why Join Us?

 - Gain experience in fully funded projects—No fee will be

 charged from the team members.

 - Build your skills and gain industry relevant experience.

 - Get Internship Completion Certificate.

Register Here: https://forms.gle/r13MkPPqfeuXpMAp6

https://www.google.com/url?q=https://forms.gle/r13MkPPqfeuXpMAp6&source=gmail-imap&ust=1735076736000000&usg=AOvVaw0pjyjvbDwHCVFiQiPGKY_Z

(Last Date : 19.12.2024 , 9:00 PM)

The domains open for recruitment are mentioned below: 

1.Computer Science Domain:

Frontend Developer

Requirements:

 - Proficiency in React.js, JavaScript, and HTML/CSS.

App Developer

Requirements:

 - Proficiency in React Native or Flutter

 - Experience with REST APls and backend integration.

Al and ML Developer

Requirements:

 - Proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow

 or PyTorch

 - Experience with CNNs, RNNs, and other ML/DL architectures

 - Familiarity with libraries like scikit-learn, NumPy, and Pandas,

 OpenCV and Flask is a plus.

2.EEE/EIE/ECE Domain:

Motor Drive Integration

Requirements:

 - Proficiency in working with BLDC motors and drivers (e.g., BLD-120A).

 - Knowledge of Pulse Width Modulation (PWM), I2C, and SPI protocols.

 - Experience with motor control algorithms (PID, feedback control).

 - Proficiency in any of this : MATLAB/Simulink (control

 systems),Proteus, Multisim, LTspice, PSpice

Power Supply and Power Source Management (BMS)

Requirements:

 - Proficiency in designing and managing Battery Management Systems

 (BMS).

 - Knowledge of DC-DC converters, voltage regulators, and power circuits.

 - Experience with energy optimization for solar panels and Li-ion

 battery systems.

 - Proficiency in any of this : Altium Designer, KiCad,

 Eagle,MATLAB/Simulink , Multisim, LTspice, PSpice

Sensor Integration and Electronics

Requirements:

 - Proficiency in integrating and calibrating sensors (IR, ultrasonic,

 gyroscope, etc.).

 - Hands-on experience with ADC/DAC conversions and sensor interfacing.

 - Knowledge of circuit design and signal conditioning.

Embedded Systems and Automation

Requirements:

 - Proficiency in Raspberry Pi and microcontrollers for

 hardware-software interfacing.

 - Programming skills in C/C++ and Python for hardware control.

 - Experience in Python programming for automation (RPi.GPIO, GPIO Zero).

 - Knowledge of real-time communication protocols like UART, SPI, and CAN

 bus.

 - Understanding IoT platforms and automation workflows.

3.Mechanical Domain CAD/CAM/CAE

Requirements:

 - Proficiency in SolidWorks or Fusion 360 for 3D modeling and

 assembly.

 - Experience in designing mechanical structures for robotics and

 automation systems.

Stress Analysis

Requirements:

 - Proficiency in ANSYS for static and dynamic stress analysis.

 - Experience in evaluating structural integrity under varying load

 conditions.

Vibration Analysis

Requirements:

 - Hands-on experience with DADiSP for vibration analysis.

 - Analyzing dynamic response and identifying vibration modes in

 mechanical parts.

Robotics/Kinematics

Body:
Hi ,

We're pleased to open applications for the Finlatics Data Science & Machine Learning Experience Program, an online live project that helps students gain experience in data science with Python and using machine learning algorithms at Vellore Institute of Technology.

This project runs at leading campuses, including IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIT Delhi, and BITS Pilani. Finlatics and was incubated at the Atal Incubation Centre, supported by Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog and Government of India.

STRUCTURE of the Live Project:

1. Learn the basics of Python and Machine Learning and how it can be used in data science.

2. Get hands-on learning and experience in writing various Python codes.

3. Dive into practical data manipulation and visualization using essential Python libraries.

4. Become proficient in using the Google Colab Notebook for machine learning

5. Gain an understanding of supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms using Python libraries

6. Explore statistical methods crucial for accurate data analysis, empowering learners with essential analytical skills.

7. Complete industry-specific case projects to understand the application of Python and Machine Learning in business scenarios

The project is doable along with any other commitment due to its work-from-home and online structure

Student OUTCOMES:

1. Certificate of Work Experience in Data Science

2. Letter of Recommendation on performance

3. A Certificate of Proficiency i n Python and Machine Learning

To apply, students can fill out the form below, and we will get in touch with them:

https://www.finlatics.com/bads_application?utm_src=vitv

As Python would be taught in the program, all students must note that no prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to be a part of the program.

Personalized guidance & mentoring would also be provided to help students learn Python.

Live Sessions will be provided to help you practice coding with Python.

Project Duration: 2 months (3-4 Hours per week)

Project Start: Flexible on selected student choice.

Project Break & Extension: Selected students will be eligible for a break or extension during the project if needed for any exams, assignments, or personal commitments.

If selected, the program has a minimal induction fee of Rs. 1999 + GST / Rs. 2999 + GST (on student choice)

Fee Waiver: Vellore Institute of Technology students will be given a 20% fee waiver on the above mentioned minimal induction fee.

To be eligible for the waiver, kindly apply via the link above.

Body:
Technology Information Forecasting and Assessment Council

(TIFAC CORE)

Invitation to VIT Students

Dear VIT Students,

We are pleased to invite you to collaborate with our esteemed Research

Center TIFAC CORE, dedicated to pioneering advancements in Sustainable

Transportation. Our center focuses on cutting-edge research in Sustainable

Mobility and is at the forefront of innovations that will shape the future

of energy, transport, and sustainability .

Research Domains at TIFAC CORE:

 1.

 Fuel Cell Technology

 2.

 Green Hydrogen Production

 3.

 Circular Economy for E-waste (Energy Storage in EV applications)

 4.

 Smart Wireless Charging Systems for EVs

 5.

 Power Converters for Sustainable Energy Systems

 6.

 Agrivoltaics and Photovoltaic Power Generation

Our mission is to drive innovation and create impactful solutions to

address global sustainability challenges. As a student, your involvement in

our ongoing projects and product development initiatives can be an

exceptional opportunity to enhance your academic and professional journey.

We also take this opportunity to thank all the students who have

contributed to our projects in the past and those who are currently

engaged. Your efforts have been instrumental in driving our vision forward.

Why Join Us?

 -

 Work directly on real-time projects and contribute to cutting-edge

 research and product development.

 -

 Collaborate with faculty and peers to publish your work in reputed

 journals, filing a joint patent and conferences, enhancing your academic

 profile.

 -

 Earn valuable project credits and fulfill academic requirements by

 engaging in meaningful research activities

 -

 Gain expertise in high-demand areas like renewable energy, power

 systems, and sustainable transportation

 -

 Build connections with industry experts, researchers, and innovators,

 opening doors to future career opportunities

Summer Internships: We also offer summer internships for students to

immerse themselves in research and development projects. This is a

fantastic opportunity for you to gain practical experience, sharpen your

skills, and work alongside professionals in the field of green energy and

mobility technologies.

We encourage students from diverse academic backgrounds to contribute to

the vibrant and multidisciplinary environment at our center. If you are

passionate about solving real-world problems, eager to innovate, and ready

to make a difference, this is your opportunity!

To express your interest, kindly fill out this Google Form:

https://forms.gle/zAvW8NBwudG5S8Hn6

Please visit our research center’s webpage at vit.ac.in/centers/tifac &

https://vit.ac.in/tifac-research-development to learn more about our

vision, projects, and achievements.

Join us in shaping a sustainable future through groundbreaking research and

innovation. Let’s work together to make a meaningful impact on society and

the environment.

Looking forward to welcoming you to our team!

Subject: Recruitment for Hyperloop Team Levitate -reg
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are thrilled to announce that Team Levitate Hyperloop, the Official

Hyperloop Team of VIT Vellore, is now recruiting passionate and talented

individuals across various domains. The team is working on cutting-edge

Hyperloop technology, and is dedicated to designing and building a fully

functional Hyperloop pod— a revolutionary transportation system that

combines speed, sustainability, and efficiency. If you are ready to

innovate and contribute to the future of transportation, this is your

opportunity!

Registration Link: https://forms.gle/pZfvDHNFr87hVfbp8

Domains Open for Recruitment:

 - Mechanical

 - Civil and Architecture

 - Electrical

 - Electronics

 - Computer Science

 - Physics

 - Chemicals

 - Marketing

 - Management

 - Design

 - Virtual Reality

Why Join Us?

 - Be part of a futuristic project shaping tomorrow's transportation.

 - Gain hands-on experience and work alongside like-minded innovators.

 - Represent VIT on national and international platforms.

Eligibility: Open to all VIT students with a passion for learning and

advancing technology.

Registration Link: https://forms.gle/pZfvDHNFr87hVfbp8

Deadline: 22nd December, 2025 11:59 pm

We look forward to dynamic individuals who want to make a difference.

Let’s levitate into the future together !

Subject: Research Opportunity in Automotive Research Centre (ARC)
Body:
Dear Student,

Greetings!

I am writing to you again regarding the research opportunity available in the Automotive Research Centre (ARC). ARC is an interdisciplinary centre that focuses its cutting-edge research that relates to the future direction of the global automotive industry. It is a unique centre that carries out research on Autonomous, Connected and Electric vehicle (ACE) technologies—electric vehicles, hybrid electric vehicles, autonomous vehicles, drones, battery management systems and fuel cells. The centre also focuses on the use of various gaseous fuels in IC engines, in particular, hydrogen as a fuel and new fuel formulations.

ARC has established state-of-the-art facilities to develop and test products in the field of self-driving vehicles. The centre has actively assisted automotive industries in niche areas and received grants from various agencies like DST, SERB, DRDO, ZF etc.,

ARC has research opportunities and is currently looking for students who are enthusiastic about learning and working on projects related to autonomous vehicles, drones, electric vehicles, battery management systems (BMS) and IC Engines. Our current projects often involve collaboration with an interdisciplinary team of faculty members across our institute and also from Binghamton University, USA.

Our research and development efforts are focused on the following domains:

1. Computer Science and Engineering

AI, ML, ROS developer. Sensor fusion, Perception, and mapping and Path planning.

2. Electrical & Electronics Engineering and Electronics and Communication Engineering

AI, ML, Control systems and Power electronics, Motor drives.

3. Mechanical Engineering

Application of AI, and ML in IC engines, Hydrogen and methanol engine development, and development of electronic control units for IC engines.

Eligibility:

 1. UG students from SMEC, SCOPE, SCORE, SENSE and SELECT can apply.

 2. PG students from Smart Mobility, Embedded Systems and Automotive Electronics programmes.

 3. Experienced students from other technical teams are preferred.

Research Outcomes:

 1. The opportunity to work in a cutting-edge research facility.

 2. Opportunity to work in a startup.

 3. Internship certificate on completion of the project.

 4. Letter of recommendation for higher studies.

 5. Research work leading to publications and patenting.

Interested students are requested to fill out the Google form given below before 19 December 2024.

https://forms.gle/fAyfMpQ2WLnUqDk5A

Subject: Recruitment drive for Team Sammard-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

We are thrilled to announce the recruitment drive for Team Sammard, where

innovation fuels aerospace excellence. Join our pioneering technical team,

contribute to groundbreaking missions, and elevate your skills in

engineering, management, and creativity.

What’s in it for you?

This is your chance to step out of the classroom and work on something

truly impactful. At Team Sammard, you'll develop real-world solutions and

witness firsthand how your contributions make a difference. You'll gain

practical experience that goes beyond theoretical knowledge, working on

challenging projects that push you to think creatively and innovate. It’s

an opportunity to grow, learn, and be part of a team building and

developing our newest rocket Airavata.

About Team Sammard

At Team Sammard, we design, build, and launch rockets while solving complex

challenges in rocketry and aerospace. From competing in prestigious events

like the Spaceport America Cup & CanSat to developing cutting-edge

machine-learning algorithms, flight software, propulsion systems, flight

computers, and rocket components, we offer unmatched opportunities to

innovate, learn, and excel. We are looking for new talent who will be

involved in developing our newest rocket - Airavata.

If you dream of pushing boundaries and leaving your mark on the aerospace

industry, Team Sammard is the place to be. 🚀

Available Domains

 -

 Computer Science: Work on software systems, machine learning algorithms,

 and embedded systems.

 -

 Management: Handle operations, coordinate logistics, attract sponsors,

 and craft impactful content, all while demonstrating expertise in editing,

 negotiation, and strategic planning.

How to Apply?

If you're ready to take on this exciting challenge and make a mark in

aerospace innovation, fill out the application form below:

https://forms.gle/ixvCGcbMmSa5cJz49 https://forms.gle/ixvCGcbMmSa5cJz49

Subject: Details on EIT Urban Mobility webinars
Body:
Dear Students,

Are you passionate about creating more liveable and sustainable cities? Do

you want to launch your own start-up working with the urban mobility

challenges or want to do rigorous research in the field? Then, you are in

the right place!

KTH Royal Institute of Technology, is a member in the EIT Urban Mobility

consortium which offers three double degree master’s programmes in the

field:

 - 🚴‍♂️ MSc Sustainable Urban Mobility Transitions (SUMT)

 Address climate challenges and lead transformative innovations in

 sustainable urban transport systems.

 - 📊 MSc Smart Mobility Data Science and Analytics (SMDSA)

 Leverage data science to design smarter, more efficient, and

 future-ready urban systems.

 - 🛠️ MSc Business Engineering in Urban Mobility (BEUM)

 Master the intersection of business, technology, and mobility solutions

 to create innovative urban projects.

⚡ FREE WEBINARS: 4–11 December 2024

Get the inside scoop directly from programme experts! Whether you’re

looking to clarify application details, explore career opportunities,

or learn about scholarships, these sessions are perfect for you.

Can't attend live? No worries! Register anyway to receive the recording.

This collaboration is set to enhance the exchange of students and faculty, initiate joint research and development programs, and establish joint twinning programs. Prominent figures from both institutions attended the MoU signing ceremony. Representing VIT were Chancellor Dr. G. Viswanathan, Vice President Mr. Sankar Viswanathan, Assistant Vice President Ms. Kadhambari S. Viswanathan, Vice Chancellor Dr. Kanchana Bhaaskaran, Pro-Vice-Chancellor Dr. Partha Sharathi Mallick, and Director of International Relations Dr. R. Seenivasan, along with other senior faculty members. From the University of Limerick, attendees included Prof. Syed Tofail, Chair of the UL India Committee and member of the Department of Physics; Mr. James Sergeant, UL Global Officer; Prof. Nanasaheb Thorat, member of the UL India Committee and Department of Physics; and Dr. Charlie O'Mahony, Researcher in the Department of Physics. 

This MoU represents a significant milestone in strengthening academic and research ties between the two esteemed institutions, fostering innovative educational and research opportunities.

Subject: Nominations for Masters Program at Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts, Switzerland
Body:
Dear Final Year Students,

Here is a brief overview of the study program at School of Computer

Science and Information Technology and nomination eligibility criteria

document attached.

 - Switzerland is one of World Highest Paid Country with Average Salaries

 (79,887 USD) globally and 1st Ranking country in Innovation and

 Technology.

 - HSLU Luzern is a Swiss public funded university with a practical

 focus.

 - Master of Science in IT, Digitalisation and Sustainability: Total

 study fees for 2 years: CHF 5800. Click here

 https://www.hslu.ch/en/lucerne-school-of-information-technology/degree-programs/master/information-technologies-digitalization-und-sustainability/

to

 access the study program website and download

 https://drive.switch.ch/index.php/s/1E52pl0BBDC7aPc more

 details(presentation copy, curriculum, fees, nomination criteria process

 and video).

 - Major’s options in Computer Science (Artificial Intelligence and

 Machine Learning, Robotics, Big Data, Data Science, Information and Cyber

 Security, Blockchain, Virtuality Reality or Augmented Reality, Software

 development etc ) or Digital Business.

 - International environment: 10+ countries with a class size of 25

 students

 - An option to pursue a Dual/Double degree program in the USA, Ireland,

 Austria, and Norway is possible

 - A housing assistance program is available to international students

 along with their admission offer.

 - Admissions are granted within two weeks.

All semester fees are included in this amount for the entire period of

study. Additionally, this amount includes fees for student ID cards,

examinations, libraries, exchange semester fees, copy and software

licenses, and lockers. Furthermore, university semester study fees are

expected to increase by CHF 500 per semester starting Fall 2025, and a

decision is expected by December 2024. Students admitted in December 2024

or before the decision is made will still pay the same fee in the Fall 2025

semester.

Interested students may fill the attached google form on or before the 5th

of December, 2024

https://forms.gle/fZAXeynnCs2EcUMA6

Subject: Johns Hopkins- USA-Whiting School of Engineering (WSE)-WSE Dean’s Master’s Fellowship for up to 50 admitted students
Body:
Dear Students,

Johns Hopkins Whiting School of Engineering (WSE) is pleased to invite

current seniors from Vellore Institute of Technology (all campuses) to

apply for admission into one of our more than 15 master’s programs this

fall, beginning August 2025. 

Furthermore, award the WSE Dean’s Master’s Fellowship for up to 50

admitted students across JHU partnership institutions in India. This

special, merit-based fellowship offers 50% off tuition for up to four

semesters of study and is tax-free. Applications must be submitted by the

program’s deadline to receive the fellowship.

We have also listed the deadlines below, and you can find additional

admissions details on our website. There is no application fee, and the GRE

is not required to submit your application. To apply, students should

provide two to three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, and

unofficial transcripts. We do accept waivers for English language

proficiency. Applicants can submit a waiver request directly in the

application and should select “Language of Instruction” as the reason for

the waiver.

On Thursday, December 12 at 8 a.m. ET/5:30 p.m. IST, we are hosting

special information sessions to coveradmissions requirements, student

resources, details about the Dean’s Master’s Fellowship, and more.

Applications must be submitted by the program’s deadline to receive the

fellowship.

MASTER’S APPLICATION DEADLINES

• Applied Mathematics and Statstics • December 15- 2024

• Biomedical Engineering • January 10- 2025

• Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering • February 15-2025

• Civil Engineering • March 1-2025

• Computer Science • February 15-2025

• Data Science • February 15-2025

• Electrical and Computer Engineering • February 15-2025

• Engineering Management • March 15-2025

• Environmental Health & Engineering • June 1-2025

• Global Innovation and Leadership through Engineering • March 15-2025

• Financial Mathematics • December 15-2025

• Materials Science • February 15-2025

• Mechanical Engineering • December 15-2025

• Occupational and Environmental Hygiene • June 1-2025

• Robotics • December 16-2024

• Security Informatics • March 1-2025

• Systems Engineering • March 1-2025

For more details:

Email:

wsegrad-admissions@jhu.edu

Thank you,

Best Wishes,

Dr.R.Seenivasan

Director -International Relations

Subject: Winter Research Internship Program 2024-25 for UG/PG Students at CFM, VIT Vellore: Apply by December 10, 2024
Body:
Dear Young Researchers,

Greetings from the Centre for Functional Materials!

CFM is thrilled to announce the call for applications to Winter Internship

Program!! Building out the program for the first time to start a unique

opportunity for the students registered under B.Tech./B.Sc./M.Tech./M.Sc. or

other equivalent programs at VIT Vellore, aspiring to carry out short

term (one

month) internship at Centre for Functional Materials (CFM), VIT Vellore.

The program offers research internship opportunities for early exposure to

Research and Development (R&D) in the Science, Technology, and Innovation

ecosystem at CFM. The winter internship program aims to provide

participants with rigorous training and preparation for engaging in

cutting-edge, multidisciplinary research focused on ‘Thin Film

Electronics and Crystallography, Neuromorphic Memory and Computing Devices,

Laser Material Processing, Organic & Flexible Electronics and Functional

Magnetic Materials (applications: energy, memory, health etc.)’.

We invite passionate and aspiring students to join us in exploring the

importance and complexities of the Functional Materials and contributing to

significant discoveries in this field.

Eligibility

1st and 2nd year students from B.Tech./B.Sc./Integrated M.Tech./M.Sc. and 1

st year students from M.Tech./M.Sc. would be eligible for this internship.

Salient features

ü During the program, interns will be required to adhere to CFM’s working

hours and other applicable norms. They will have the opportunity to

actively participate in CFM events such as materials research clubs and

research seminars.

ü Education and research: Paving way for new ideas and creativity of

products useful for societal needs.

ü Interns will be a co-author of the research publication or co-inventor

in a patent depending on his/her contribution.

ü Internship experience will go a long way in launching a research and

entrepreneurship career.

ü At the end of the program, the intern will be required to submit a

detailed report summarising the training and accomplishments.

ü On completion of the internship "Training Completion Certificate" will

be issued to the student.

Selection process

ü Faculty members from research centres float specified research areas

ü Applicants need to opt the interested research areas

ü Interviews are conducted for shortlist candidates during ‘13th to 14th

December 2024

ü Declaration of results will be on 15th December 2024

ü Winter Internship starts from 21st December 2024

Last date for submission of online application: 10th December 2024

 Registration

Link: https://forms.gle/dprXLHG1HaqBUQzj6

https://forms.gle/dprXLHG1HaqBUQzj6

Contact

More information on CFM’s research projects and other initiatives are

available at https://vit.ac.in/centers/cfm https://vit.ac.in/centers/cfm

Queries, if any, may be addressed to cfm@vit.ac.in mentioning "CFM Winter

Internship 2024-25" in the subject line

Other information: 

ü No grades will be awarded by CFM, VIT Vellore, for the work carried out

under this ambit.

ü There will be no financial support from CFM, VIT Vellore, for the

Internship Programme.

Note: Please find the Flyer which is attached.

Thank You

With my best regards,

Subject: Invitation for City University of London UK -Student Webinar: Maths for Machine Learning, Dr Neil Saunders (11/12/24)
Body:
Dear Students and Colleagues,

I am writing to let you know that our next webinar will be delivered by Dr

Neil Saunders on the topic of Maths for Machine Learning, Wednesday 11th

December 2024 from 15:30 IST (10:00 UK time). Please register for the

webinar using this link

https://city-ac-uk.zoom.us/meeting/register/tZEpd-qgrTwpG9WuyP8qQiG36C6Qzkf0Ysw-

.

An abstract for this month’s topic is as follows:

The field of Machine Learning (ML) has enjoyed an unprecedented wave of

enthusiasm in the last decade thanks to its applications in data science

and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Yet while these advances are impressive,

they are built quite fundamental mathematics which can often get lost to

view in this burgeoning field.

This can present challenges to anyone (individual or corporation) who

wishes to use ML & AI in their workflow, but doesn’t have the requisite

mathematical skills required to understand how they achieve their goals and

therefore, understand their limitations.

This talk will be a whistle-stop tour on some of the rudimentary

mathematics behind ML, data science and AI, demonstrating some

implementations in Python, and touching upon some of the ethical issues

around its applications in industry and society.

Register for the December webinar here:

https://city-ac-uk.zoom.us/meeting/register/tZEpd-qgrTwpG9WuyP8qQiG36C6Qzkf0Ysw-

https://city-ac-uk.zoom.us/meeting/register/tZEpd-qgrTwpG9WuyP8qQiG36C6Qzkf0Ysw-

I also wanted to make you aware that videos of previous webinars are

available here

https://connect.city.ac.uk/city/sst/city-student-webinar-for-partner-universities/_nocache

(apart from in the instance that recording was not possible for

confidentiality reasons).

Please note that Zoom is used for webinar delivery. Attendees will need an

existing Zoom account in order to register. If you need to register for a

free account, please visit Zoom https://zoom.us/signup#/signup for

details.

We will be releasing the details of the 2025 Webinars in due course. We are

due to start in January with a series of new topics and speakers and we are

excited to share this with you soon. Each month will feature a new topic,

delivered by an expert within the field, and will showcase research and

teaching currently taking place within the School. Sessions will consist of

an hour’s lecture followed by 30 minutes for audience questions. More

information about the webinars can be found here: City student webinar for

partner universities • City, University of London

Dear Students,

We are thrilled to announce the recruitment drive for Team Avatar and Team

Artemis, where innovation meets creativity in robotics. Here’s your chance

to join one of these pioneering technical teams, contribute to

groundbreaking projects, and enhance your technical expertise.

 About the Teams:

Team Avatar

Team Avatar is dedicated to creating a revolutionary humanoid robot capable

of performing human-like activities. By exploring the complexities of AI,

mechanics, and human-robot interaction, the team aims to break new ground

in robotics and technology.

Team Artemis

Subject: INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS APPEARING FOR FALL 2024-25 THEORY FAT
Body:
INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS APPEARING FOR FALL

 2024-25 THEORY FAT

Students appearing for FAT Exams, please READ INSTRUCTIONS CAREFULLY TILL

the END.

1. As per new regulations, the students must enter the examination hall

15-30 Minutes before the commencement of examination (between 9.00 - 9.15

AM for FN Session). Students are required to self-frisk by themselves

before collecting answer scripts. Students reporting beyond the specified

entry time will not be permitted to enter the examination hall. 

2. Possession of any Electronic Gadget (Mobile Phone, Smart Watch,

Bluetooth device, any device embedded with scanner /camera, etc.), holding

chit papers/ suspicious content in the examination hall is considered as

malpractice.

3. Students are not permitted to take the following materials inside the

exam halls: chit papers, mobile phones, ear buds, the lid of the

calculator, chit materials, a reference table that contains markings,

written content using pencil or pen, nano ear phones, electronic devices,

blue tooth devices/displays, mobile phones without SIM cards,

non-transparent pouches, microxeroxes, or any other irrelevant material to

the exams. Possession itself and/or its use of any of the above is

considered examination malpractice.

4. Malpractice rules are published in the student VTOP login; you are

required to go through them, and you are requested not to indulge in any

examination malpractices.

3. Based on the requirements, Frisking will be done prior to entering the

examination hall and during the examination. You may be required to do

self-frisking before entering into examination hall. Also two to five

minutes are permitted to do the same inside the exam hall before collecting

question paper and answer booklet.

4. If a student leaves the exam hall before 12.00 noon, he/she has to

submit the question paper along with answer sheet. 

5. On the day of exam, keep your bags in front of exam room, DONOT TAKE

NOTE BOOKS / BOOKS / BAGS TO EXAM DESKS

General Instructions

· You need to WEAR Student IDENTITY CARD during the ENTIRE EXAMINATION

PERIOD. If you don’t have a Proper ID Card contact Registrar Office and

apply for a new one and get it before coming to the Exam. The ID card

should be scratches free with proper tag. Exchange of ID cards or Tags will

be considered as Malpractice. If you have misplaced your ID card or forgot

to bring it to the Examination Hall, Report to the Control Room of your

test venue to get One Time Permit Slips. You need to pay Rs. 100 through

V-TOP online payment only.

· You will NOT be permitted to use toilet/washroom during the

examination, so be prepared for it.

· Exchange of Calculators, Stationaries, Code Books, pen, pencil etc.,

are not permitted. The code Books or standard tables should have been

signed by either by the faculty or School office. No markings of any kind

should be found in such booklets.

· As per VIT rules, even if you keep mobile phone/smart watch in a

switched off position inside the examination hall, it will be treated as

examination malpractice. Such malpractices will lead to confiscation of the

devices (including SIM card) for one semester and ’N’ grade (ALL PAPER

ZERO) in all the registered courses including lab & project components in

that semester. Hence, before entering the examination hall, students should

check their pockets thoroughly to avoid carrying mobile phone/smart watch

by mistake.

A. Pre-Exam Activities

1.

Note down your seating arrangement (Building, Room Number and Seat Number)

from the V-TOP students login. Seating arrangement will not be displayed

for courses in which a student has been debarred. Please report yourself

half an hour prior to exam. No student would be permitted to enter the hall

after 9.15 AM.

2.

Possession of un-authorised material, even if you do not intend to use it

will be considered as malpractice. Before starting the exam, check any

materials written on desks or walls, or found papers nearby/ around you in

the floor and inform the same to the invigilators.

B. During the exam

1.

Candidate has to sit in the allotted seat only. Listen to the invigilator

and follow their instructions at all times. Strict Silence should be

maintained in the examination hall. Discussions/ communications of any kind

inside exam hall are treated as examination malpractices.

2.

Check the class number in the Question paper with the Attendance sheet

Class Number. If you have not received the right question paper or

incomplete or badly printed, please contact the invigilator immediately. If

you have any doubt on class number, course name, course code, slot, and any

other details related to your question paper, please check while signing in

the attendance sheet.

3.

Read carefully and follow the instructions printed in the question paper

and in the answer booklet.

4.

Fill required details (Register No., course code, course title etc.) in the

answer booklet before you start writing the exam. After signing in the

attendance sheet, check the barcode sticker pasted on your answer booklet

for its correctness as your answer booklets will be scanned for valuation

using this barcode only.

5.

First clearly write the Question number in the space provided and then

start writing your answers. USE BLUE / BLACK PEN ONLY for writing the

Answers. Writings on any thin pens, / light colours may not be visible on

the scanned images used for evaluation. Remember to write the answers

within the space provided in the answer booklet. If you write anything

outside the margin, it will be cut during the scanning process. If you are

using extra sheets like graph sheets / templates given by faculty, write

your registration number alone on top left edge outside the margin and keep

it immediately after the first sheet. Do not fold it as it needs to be

scanned for valuation. Do your rough works in the last page of main answer

booklet itself. Before finishing the exam, strike out all the rough works.

6.

Don’t write anything in the question paper or in your hand or leg ot on

desk or on walls nearby you.

7.

Correcting pens, fluid or tape and erasable pens are not to be used for

corrections in the answer booklet.

8.

Do not discuss / borrow anything with other candidates during the

examination.

9.

Do not get involved in any unfair or dishonest practice during the exam. If

you try to cheat or break the rules in any way, it will invite appropriate

sanctions under malpractice.

10.

Students are not allowed to ask question of any kind during the

examination. Invigilators have been instructed not to answer any enquiry

whatsoever relating to the question papers, whether an explanation or

meaning or correction or typographical error

11.

On the day of the exam, if you feel that you are affected by ill health,

please contact the Chief Superintendent or Invigilator. You can write the

examination at the Health Centre.

12.

Do not leave the examination hall until told to do so by invigilator. You

cannot leave the examinations hall till 30 min from the start of the

examination.

13.

Do not take your answer booklets or unused one, from the examination hall.

It is a serious Malpractice.

14.

Answer booklet contains 42 pages and no additional sheets, no threads, will

be provided.

C. If booked under Malpractice

1.

Be calm and give a written response to the allegation and follow the

instructions from the exam squad / Invigilator / Asst. CS / CS.

2.

Do not indulge in any disrespectful activities such as shouting / creating

/ diverting attention of all other students, a scene in the examination

hall.

3.

Hand over the materials and get a receipt for electronic devices.

NON-COOPERATION WILL BE VIEWED AS AN ACT OF INDISCIPLINE WHICH MAY INVITE

SEPARATE DISCIPLINARY ACTION.

4.

Examination malpractice actions/punishments are very serious, may lead to

All paper ZERO or suspension of one semester. All are malpractice actions

are informed to the students / published in VTOP student Login. Please go

through it follow the examination rules appropriately

5.

OBEY ALL THE EXAMNATION RULES SERIOUSLY

Good Wishes

 Controller of Examinations

With Regards

Dr. T.B. SRIDHARAN. Ph.D., (DRDO)

Controller of Examinations,

Professor-Higher Academic Grade,

Vellore 632 014, TN, India.

Subject: Congratulations Team-VIT V at iGEM 2024 Grand Jamboree-reg
Body:
Dear VITian's,

We are delighted to inform you that our team VIT-V has represented VIT

Vellore and won a Silver Medal in the iGEM 2024 Grand Jamboree held at

Paris, France. VIT-V had the privilege of representing VIT in the 2024

International Genetically Engineered Machine (iGEM) competition. iGEM is a

renowned global synthetic biology competition that brings together students

to develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges through

bioengineering. The 2024 iGEM competition had over 4,500 participants. A

total of 400 teams from more than 50 countries competed this year,

fostering an environment of creativity, collaboration, and

interdisciplinary problem-solving.

Team VIT-V's Project

The project addresses high UV Index levels in Vellore, which contribute to

an increased risk of skin cancer. Under the guidance of our PI Dr. R. Siva

and Co-PI Dr. Kannan P, we engineered Escherichia coli to produce

carotenoids—natural pigments with antioxidant properties that can be used

for eco-friendly, broad-spectrum UV protection in skincare. This approach

supports both skin health and environmental sustainability.

Below is the list of the team members:

 1. D S Nishanth (21MSI0083)

 2. Pranjali Bhagat (21BBT0348)

 3. Naisarg Patel (22BBT0278)

 4. Ananya Pai (21BBT0093)

 5. Johan George (22BBT0245)

 6. Prakriti Shah (22BBT0083)

 7. ⁠Suchita Lathe (21BBT0369)

 8. Neha Sivakumar (21BBT0310)

 9. Tejaswini Deshmukh (21BBT0058)

 10. D K Harish Naaraayan (22BBT0218)

 11. Urvi Sinha (21BBT0223)

 12. ⁠Tanvi Duarah (21BBT0194)

 13. Utkarsh Srivastava (21BCB0199)

 14. Mohak Bhattacharyya (22BBT0174)

 15. Aadithya Hrudhay (22BCB0044)

 16. Swasti Tyagi (21BBT0326)

We are immensely proud to see Team VIT-V on such a global platform and hope

this accomplishment inspires further participation and innovation. Please

join us in congratulating the team members under the guidance of Dr. R Siva

(Dean-SBST) and Dr. Kannan P, (Asst. Professor Sr. Grade 1-SBST). This

recognition is a testament to our team's hard work, collaboration, and

innovative efforts in synthetic biology.

Subject: Fwd: Invitation to participate in ACEi - Hackathon '25 at Aravind Eye Hospital, Pondicherry
Body:
Dear Students and Research Scholars,

Greetings

Aravind Eye Care System (AECS) to extend an invitation to the students of

Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) to participate in our upcoming

event, ACEi

- Hackathon ‘25 which is scheduled to take place on January 3, 4 & 5,

2025, at Aravind Eye Hospital in Pondicherry.

At AECS, we are committed to fostering innovation in eye care through

collaborative problem-solving and the development of innovative solutions.

Our Aravind Centre for Eyecare Innovation (ACEi) has been instrumental in

promoting and practicing an innovative culture at AECS, and the annual

hackathon is a testament to our dedication to this cause.

During this event, doctors and staff from all branches of AECS will

collaboratively formulate problem statements and new project ideas aimed at

improving patient care. We have witnessed the valuable contributions of VIT

students in our previous hackathons, and we would be honoured to have your

institution's participation once again.

The hackathon provides a unique platform for students to engage with

real-world challenges in the field of eye care and transform their

innovative ideas into tangible solutions. At the end of the three-day

event, the top five teams, including students, will be recognized and

awarded certificates of appreciation as well as cash prize.

Additionally, some of the successful hackathon projects may require further

support, and we extend an invitation to VIT students to consider staying

longer for internship/capstone projects at one of our tertiary care

centers. AECS will cover lodging and food expenses during the project

period and also will support develop products and patenting of the same.

We are currently seeking candidates in the following domains (people from

other domains can also participate):

· Software Engineer: Proficient in web development, Android

development, and basic Python.

· Mechanical Engineer: Capable of CAD modeling and 3D printing.

· Electronics Engineer: Capable of creating circuits, sensors, and

working with microcontrollers.

· Industrial Designer: Proficient in research, conceptualization,

and ideation.

· Bio Medical Engineer: Knowledge in Bio-medical equipment and

instruments.

We believe that the diverse talents and skills of VIT students would

greatly contribute to the success of this ACEi - Hackathon ’25.

For those interested, please apply through the provided Application link

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdQtcmmCNvULuTvqoTfuKBtOP_7kYgX_q9dDBXftjBwsWx_aA/viewform.

(The deadline for submitting applications is 30th November, 2024).

Students will be selected after an interview by the expert team and the

nominated problem statements will be shared with the selected students

immediately upon their recruitment to ACEi – Hackathon ‘25.

If you or your students have any questions or require further information,

please feel free to contact us at udayakumar@aravind.org or

innovation@aravind.org.

We sincerely hope that VIT students will consider this invitation and join

us in making ACEi - Hackathon ‘25 a resounding success, as previous years.

Thank you for your attention and anticipated cooperation.

All the Best

Thanks and Regards

Yours Sincerely,

P.Arulmozhivarman

In recognition of the increasing impact television has on decision-making

by bringing world attention to conflicts and threats to peace and security

and its potential role in sharpening the focus on other major issues,

proclaimed 21 November as World Television Day.

World Television Day is not so much a celebration of the tool, but rather

recognition of the increasing impact television has on the process of

decision-making. Television was thus acknowledged as a major tool in

World Children’s Day

World Children’s Day was first established in 1954 as Universal Children's

Day and is celebrated on 20 November each year to promote international

togetherness, and awareness among children worldwide, and to improve

children's welfare. Mothers and fathers, teachers, nurses and doctors,

government leaders and civil society activists, religious and community

elders, corporate moguls and media professionals, as well as young people

and children themselves, can play an important part in making World

Children's Day relevant for their societies, communities, and nations.

World Children's Day offers each of us an inspirational entry point to

advocate, promote and celebrate children's rights, translating into

dialogues and actions that will build a better world for children.

The World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims

The World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims takes place on 20th

November every year as the appropriate acknowledgment of victims of road

traffic crashes and their families. It was started by the British road

crash victim charity, Road Peace, in 1993 and was adopted by the United

Nations General Assembly in 2005.

The objectives of the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims

 are to provide a platform for road traffic victims and their families to:

§ remember all people killed and seriously injured on the roads;

§ acknowledge the crucial work of the emergency services;

§ draw attention to the generally trivial legal response to culpable road

deaths and injuries;

§ advocate for better support for road traffic victims and victim families;

 § promote evidence-based actions to prevent and eventually stop

further road traffic deaths and injuries.

Sappers Day

The Corps of Engineers of the Indian Army, also called the Sappers,

celebrated their Corps Day on 18 November. The Indian Army Corps of

Engineers provides combat engineering support, develops infrastructure for

armed forces and other defense organizations, and maintains connectivity

along the borders, besides helping the civil authorities during natural

disasters. College of Military Engineering, Pune (CME) is the premier

technical and tactical training institution of the Indian Army Corps of

Engineers. The Corps consists of three groups of combat engineers, namely

the Madras Sappers, the Bengal Sappers, and the Bombay Sappers.

Sappers have a glorious history dating back to the mid-18th century. The

Corps officially recognizes its birth as 1780 when the seniormost group of

the Corps, the Madras Sappers, was raised. Subsequently, the Groups of

Bengal and Bombay Sappers were formed in their respective presidencies.

These Groups were later merged on 18 November 1932 to form the Corps of

Engineers. This day is celebrated as Corps of Engineers Day every year. The

Corps of Engineers provides combat engineering support and develops

infrastructure for the armed forces along our vast borders besides

providing succor to the populace during natural disasters. These tasks are

executed through four pillars of the Corps namely the Combat Engineers, the

Military Engineering Services, the Border Roads Organisation, and the

Military Survey of India.

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [16th November] 

 events.

Today's Events:

Scroll down for more details

YOGA CLUB

Event Name: Impact on Yoga in Mental Health

Event Timings: 8.00 AM to 9.00 PM

Event Platform: Gmail

Event Description: Join us to explore how yoga benefits mental health in a

1-2 page essay! Reflect on its impact on stress, focus, and emotional

resilience, incorporating personal insights or research. All students are

welcome to participate; prior yoga experience isn’t required. Submit your

essay to yoga@vit.ac.in between 15/11/2024 to 16/11/2024. Let's share how

yoga fosters a balanced mind!

Event Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/vit_yoga_club/?next=%2F

RoboVITics

Event Name: VITAA: Robotics x Space

Event Timings: 08:00 am to 10:00 am

Event Venue: TT312

Event Description: This speaker event, led by VIT alumna Raunika Anand as

she shares her experience working at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. In

this event, Raunika will provide insights into her journey in space

exploration, discussing the challenges and breakthroughs at JPL. Attendees

will gain a unique perspective on cutting-edge space missions and learn how

innovation and perseverance drive success in one of the most prestigious

research institutions in the world.

Event Registration: VTOP

IEEE VIT

Event Name: Alumni Talks: Rishiraj Chhabra

Event Timings: 11:00 AM - 12:30 PM

Event Venue: TT 727

Event Description: Rishiraj is a fullstack developer with over 2.5 yrs of

experience working with the industry developing innovative applications

that deliver value to end users. He holds a degree in ECE from VIT. In the

event he will talk about everything A to Z regarding campus to career.

Event Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/ieeevitvellore/

The Biotech Research Society India (BRSI)

Event Name: Wheels of Fortune

Event Timings: 11:00 am to 12:00 pm

Event Venue: SMVG21

Event Description: Get ready for Wheels of Fortune - the ultimate biology

showdown. Spin the virtual wheel and dive into exciting topics like

Anatomy, Marine life, insects, etc. Each spin reveals a question - answer

in 30 seconds to score points. Spin the second wheel to land on a Wildcard

to get perks or conditions like Call a Friend or Sing your answer. Compete

for the top spot on the leaderboard, and claim the top three spots.

Event Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/brsivitvellore/?hl=en

Facebook Link: https://www.facebook.com/brsivitvellore/

PB - Tamil Literary Association (TLA)

Event Name: Kavipezhai

Event Timings: 10 AM to 10 PM

Event Platorm: Gforms

Event Description: PB - TLA organizes "Kavipezhai" Where participants are

asked to write kavidhai based on The Beauty of the Tamil Language. This

topic encourages poets to express the elegance, depth, and emotional

richness of the Tamil language. Participants can explore themes like the

poetic flow of Tamil, its ancient literary heritage, the emotions it

conveys, or the pride in speaking and preserving this classical language

Top 3 Winners be choosed based on their creativity.

Event Registration: VTOP

ISA - VIT

Event Name: Pixel Perfect with TailwindCSS

Event Timings: 4 pm - 7 pm

Event Venue: Kamaraj Auditorium

Event Description: Join us for Pixel Perfect, an exciting hands-on workshop

where you'll master the essentials of TailwindCSS and put your skills to

the test! In this event, we'll kick off with a guided session on how to

quickly build sleek and responsive designs using Tailwind's utility-first

approach. Then, unleash your creativity in our mini design challenges as

you tackle unique briefs to create eye catching layouts, component designs

and more - all with TailwindCSS.

Event Registration: VTOP

IEEE - EMBS

Event Name: MicroMed Workshop- SDG event

Event Timings: 9 am to 1pm

Event Venue: TT 601

Event Description: Get a better understanding of MEMS and a practical

session to enhance your understanding of sustainable electronics. Join us

tomorrow at TT 601!

Event Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link:

https://www.instagram.com/p/DCY87M8vSFl/?igsh=YjRpcHRjeDBsb2o4

SIAM - VIT

Event Name: Graduate Guidance

Event Timings: 07:00 pm - 08:00 pm

Event Venue: TT 204

Event Description: SIAM invites Ms. Rohini Das, an alumni experience in ML,

AI and the math that powers them. It is a unique opportunity for

participants to learn how math integrates with Ai and expand their career

horizons, with an experienced professional working in these areas.

Event Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/siamvit/

IIChE - VIT

Event Name: Dynamics of Cement Industry

Event Timings: 11:30 am- 1:30 pm

Event Venue: SMV 101

Event Description: IIChE-VIT is hosting a guest lecture on November 16th,

from 11:30 AM to 1:30 PM at SMV 101. Mr. Parameshwaran Iyer, Head of Design

Manufacturing at Adani Cements, will lead an insightful session exploring

key aspects of process dynamics in the cement industry.

Event Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link:

https://www.instagram.com/p/DCY0kywzBg7/?igsh=MWZ0OXQybHU0a3B1MA==

CodeChef

Event Name: Alumni Connect

Event Timings: 10:00 AM - 12:00 PM

Event Venue: Shakespeare Gallery

Event Description: Alumni Connect is an interactive Q&A session featuring

accomplished co-founders and former CodeChef members. Gain valuable

insights into their entrepreneurial journeys, challenges, and successes.

This event offers a unique opportunity to interact, learn, and get inspired

by industry leaders who once walked the same path as you.

Event Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link:

https://www.instagram.com/codechefvit?igsh=MXNsN2F0Mzd3NXk1ag==

SAE - VIT

Event Name: SAE Podcast : Porsche : Holy Trinity

Event Timings: 7:30 pm

Event Platform: Youtube Live

Event Description: Welcome to yet another engaging and insightful SÆ

PODCAST. In this episode we talk all about the fan favourite- the Holy

Trinity of the automotive industry consisting of three marvels of

engineering from three manufacturers. Namely the elegant and beautiful

LaFerrari, a car way ahead of its time from the British manufacturer the

Mclaren P1 and the brutal German, the Porsche 918. Together these three

cars changed the automotive industry's standard for performance and created

a new league of their own. Join us as we uncover the stories and their

designs on the SÆ PODCAST on 16/11/24 on YouTube.

Event Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/sae_vit/?h

The Catalyst Club

Event Name: Echoes of Experience: Alumni Event

Event Timings: 2:00 pm to 3:30 pm

Event Platform: Google Meet

Event Description: Step into the world of alumni who once walked in your

shoes! Echoes of Experience is an inspiring seminar where accomplished VIT

alumni share their journeys, insights, and experiences from their

postdoctoral pursuits abroad. Gain valuable advice, discover new

perspectives, and envision the possibilities that lie ahead. Don’t miss

this unique opportunity to connect with those who have successfully

navigated paths you may aspire to follow.

Event Registration: VTOP

Hindi Literary Association (HLA)

Event Name: Shabd-vaash

Event Timings: 6:30 am to 8:30 pm

Event Platform: Google meet

Event Description: To guide the current members of the club, HLA has

reached out and invited their Club Alumni. In this workshop, you will learn

how the thinking process occurs behind writing. Various writing techniques

will also be discussed. Furthermore, their inspiration for writing will

also be talked about so young writers can enhance their thinking capability

and start to think outside the box.

Event Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/hla_vitu/

Zero Waste Management (ZWM)

Event Name: Planet Preservation: Painting Paths to Zero Waste

Event Timings: 10:00 AM - 12:00 PM

Event Platform: Google Forms

Event Description: In this 2-day event, participants form teams to tackle

assigned topics on waste management. On Day 1, teams research, brainstorm,

and prepare a PowerPoint and report outlining innovative solutions. Day 2

is for presentations, where teams showcase their ideas to a judging panel,

focusing on creativity, feasibility, and teamwork. This challenge

encourages critical thinking and collaboration, aiming to inspire

real-world sustainable solutions and build essential skills in research and

presentation.

Event Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link:

https://www.instagram.com/zwm_vit_vellore?utm_source=qr&igsh=MWk5cXoyMGMyYnQ0Yg==

Forms Link: https://forms.gle/qzC845FUM2G91UxE8

Vriksh

Event Name: International Day of Tolerance

Event Timings: 11 am to 11 pm

Event Platform: Google Drive

Event Description: In honor of the International Day of Tolerance, we

invite you all to participate in an inspiring essay writing competition.

This event aims to encourage awareness, understanding, and respect among

individuals from diverse backgrounds and cultures. Through this platform,

participants will reflect on the values of tolerance, empathy, and peaceful

coexistence in our increasingly interconnected world.Participants are

encouraged to explore what tolerance means in today’s society, the

importance of accepting different perspectives, and how individual actions

can contribute to a more inclusive world.

Event Registration: VTOP

Body:
Dear VITians,

Greetings!

In continuation of the VIT - BU webinar series, the third session- “Advancing Sustainability: Innovations in Li-ion Battery Recycling and Manufacturing” will be held on 15 November 2024 (Friday) at 7:00 pm (IST).

Dr. Xiaotu Ma, Ph.D, Assistant Professor - School of Systems Science and Industrial Engineering, Binghamton University will be delivering the talk.

Faculty members, research scholars and students can register using the following registration link. After registration, the registrants will receive a Zoom link to join the session.

Registration Link: https://forms.gle/KCUTDMvrWYvXmQVFAhttps://www.google.com/url?q=https://forms.gle/KCUTDMvrWYvXmQVFA&source=gmail-imap&ust=1732184399000000&usg=AOvVaw3djkY3I0SrMWtJSalj5tfs

(Zoom link provided after registration)

Abstract:

Lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries play a critical role in driving the shift toward more sustainable transportation and energy sectors, with their increasing use in electronics, electric vehicles, and energy storage systems. As demand rapidly rises, there is a growing number of spent batteries, raising concerns related to costs, health risks, and environmental impact. Consequently, recycling Li-ion batteries and developing sustainable manufacturing processes have become essential to address these challenges. However, significant obstacles remain, such as the reliance on toxic and costly organic solvents in conventional electrode production and the perception of recycled materials as inferior to their commercial counterparts. To overcome these hurdles, innovations such as dry-print electrode technology, alongside improved recycling and upcycling methods, are essential for ensuring that Li-ion batteries can contribute to a sustainable energy future. In response to these challenges, we have developed two advanced recycling processes: one based on a hydrometallurgical approach, which is widely favored in the industry, and the other based on direct recycling, which offers greater efficiency and advantages. Additionally, we have pioneered a roll-to-roll solvent-free electrode manufacturing process. This method not only eliminates the need for toxic and expensive organic solvents but also enhances fast-charging capabilities, providing a scalable, efficient, and cost-effective solution for battery manufacturing.

 Speaker Biography:

[cid:image001.png@01DB36AE.0FB04020]

Xiaotu Ma joined the School of Systems Science and Industrial Engineering at Binghamton University as an assistant professor in 2024. He earned his B.S. in Chemistry from Jilin University, China, in 2015, an M.S. in Materials Science and Engineering from Stevens Institute of Technology in 2017, and a Ph.D. in Materials Science and Engineering from Worcester Polytechnic Institute in 2021. His research focuses on developing advanced and sustainable electrodes and materials for energy storage, including lithium-ion batteries, battery manufacturing, safety, recycling, and fundamental electrochemistry.

Body:
Dear VITians,

Greetings !

The Office of Students Welfare, invites you to "spring" to action, as we

gear up for an enthralling week of cultural entertainment. As we revive

ourselves from the hectic schedules and blues, a much needed breather from

Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [12th November]

 - Mech Face-Off 1.11

 - Blog Fury 1.11 (Automated Robotic Arm)

 - Tech Elevate 1.18

 - Elemental Eye Spy

Scroll down for more information

IEEE Communications Society (IEEE ComSoc)

Event Name: Mind Meets Machine: Exploring BCI

Time: 09:30AM to 12:00PM

Venue: VOC Gallery, TT (OFFLINE)

Event Description: IEEE COMSOC Organizes "Mind Meets Machine: Exploring

BCI". Join us for an exciting session on Brain-Computer Interface (BCI)

technology, where we dive into the fascinating world of connecting the

human brain with digital systems. Discover how BCI enables direct

communication between neural activity and computers, opening up new

possibilities in fields like healthcare, assistive technology, and beyond.

Registration: VTOP registration

Instagram link: https://www.instagram.com/vitieeecomsoc/

American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME-VIT)

Event Name: Mech Face-Off 1.11

Event Description: Get ready for ASME-VIT's Mech Face Off 1.11! In this

intense debate, Direct Injection vs Port Injection take centre stage, each

competing for the title of the technology for fuel injection. Our debaters

will explore the mechanics, performance, and sustainability of each

approach, shedding light on the future of fuel injections techniques. Which

technology will shape the course for tomorrow’s future? Join us for an

insightful exploration into the future of innovation!

 

Event Venue: GDN G07 (offline)

Registration: VTOP

American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME-VIT)

Event Name: Blog Fury 1.11 (Automated Robotic Arm)

Time: 4:30 PM to 6:00 PM

Prepare for an exciting edition blog fury! This time, writers will explore

the cutting-edge world of automated robotic arms, highlighting the design,

versatility, and applications of this remarkable technology. From

revolutionizing manufacturing to enhancing precision in various fields,

robotic arms represent the forefront of industrial automation. Could these

mechanical innovations be the key to future technological breakthroughs?

Join us as our bloggers uncover the potential of robotic arms and share

insights that could transform the future of automation and industry!

Event Venue: GDN G07

Registration: VTOP

American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME-VIT)

Event Name: Tech Elevate 1.18

Time: 11:00 A.M. - 1:00 P.M.

Join us at Tech Elevate 1.18 for an engaging session on Automotive NVH

(Noise, Vibration, and Harshness) Engineering! This talk dives into the

science of reducing unwanted noise, vibrations, and discomfort in vehicles,

enhancing overall comfort. Our expert speaker will cover key aspects of NVH

analysis, including source identification, simulations, testing, and design

optimization. Discover how cutting-edge materials and engineering methods

are driving advancements in vehicle performance.

Event Venue: CDMM 304

Registration: VTOP

The Catalyst Club

Event Name : Elemental Eye Spy

Event Time :2:00 pm to 3:30 pm

Event Venue : TT 513

Event Description: The Catalyst Club will be hosting a game-show styled

event where students participate in pairs and attempt a quick and engaging

game of identifying chemistry visuals (elements, lab equipment,

scientists). Each picture will set a playful tone for an interactive and

visually engaging event.

Registration Link: Register on VTOP

Event Name: Energy Reimagined: Sustainable Future

Event Time: 11am to 12:30pm

Event Venue: GDN120

Description: Join us for an event focused on SDG Goal 7: Affordable and

Clean Energy, where our chapter members will share insights about the

future of renewable energy. The event aims to enlighten students about the

sustainable development goals and inspire them to contribute to a cleaner

and more sustainable energy future.

affect their IP’s value.

advanced IP strategies, focusing on different IP types, patent portfolio

lifecycle, global market strategies, and gain hands-on practice in IP

negotiation.

Subject: FLIP 2024 : Patent filing campaign for the UG and PG students
Body:
Dear Students,

Are you a budding innovator with a ground-breaking idea? IPR & TT Cell (in

collaboration with VITIST, IIC) invites you to explore the exciting world

of patent filing through the

 FLIP 2024 (Facilitating IP filing) campaign.

Why Patent Your Invention?

 - Protect Your Intellectual Property: Safeguard your innovative ideas

 and secure exclusive rights.

 - Commercialize Your Invention: Increase the potential for

 commercialization and licensing opportunities. You will earn a part of the

 revenue generated from licensing the IP.

We will facilitate money transfers to your bank account even after you

 graduate from the University if the filed IP is licensed to an industry. 

 - Enhance Your Academic Profile: Demonstrate your research capabilities

 and contribute to the university's intellectual property portfolio.

How to File a Patent:

· Identify Your Invention: The invention can be an outcome of a

short-term project/UGRE work/Capstone project/Project I/Project II/Set

conference projects etc. Clearly define the novelty and inventive step of

the work.

· Conduct a Prior art Search: Use online patent search software

available in our VIT library (request through IPR&TT Cell to assess the

patentability search software - Guidelines here:

https://vit.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Patent-search-software.pdf

https://vit.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Patent-search-software.pdf).

· Submit the Invention disclosure form (IDF): Submit the IDF in

VTOP through your faculty mentor.

The IPR &TT Cell is here to Help: 

 - Guidance and Support: Our team of experts can guide the patent filing

 process, including patent searching, drafting, and filing.

 - An exclusive Q/A session will be arranged for the registrants to help

 them through filling out the required forms and filing process

The timeline for FLIP 2024:

5.

Assessment by the External Experts (Lawyers’ team already associated with

Filing Complete Specification / Patents with the help of the associated

Sender_Name: 'Convenor Riviera' via B.Tech. - Comp  Sci Engg 2023 Group, Vellore Campus
Subject: Call for Students Organizers/Managers/Coordinators/Volunteers for Riviera'25- Reg
Body:
We at Vellore Institute of Technology-VIT Vellore believe that education is

not limited to the classroom but goes beyond. To facilitate this, VIT

conducts an Annual International Sports and Cultural Carnival Riviera that

strives to break every barrier, breach every limit, and

exceed every expectation year after year. With a footfall of more than

60,000 students from 70 different countries, it is with immense pleasure

and pride that we announce our next edition, RIVIERA 2025!

As we gear up for the next edition of RIVIERA, scheduled from 20th

February to 23rd February 2025, we are seeking enthusiastic individuals

who are eager to contribute their skills, creativity, and energy to create

an unforgettable experience for all participants.

We would like to invite applications from students for the post

of Student Organisers, Managers, Coordinators, and Volunteers for Riviera

‘25.

To apply, please fill out the form: https://forms.gle/VzZLaB9XvdquEuzY7

Deadline: 17th November 2025, Sunday 12:00 PM

The eligibility criteria are mentioned below:

1. Vellore Institute of Technology hosts two international

fests every year; those who have worked as Student Organizers in any one

fest, should not take part to give a fair chance to other students.

 2. Students’ Council members will not be considered for organizing

 positions. However, their services will be used appropriately.

 3. Academics requirements:

 Organizers should have at least 8.0 CGPA

 Managers should have at least 7.5 CGPA

 Coordinators should have at least 7.0 CGPA

 Volunteers should have at least 7.0 CGPA

 4. Physical attendance below 70% is not eligible for any of the posts.

 5. Students with standing arrears are not considered for any of the

 posts.

 6. Students who are involved in any disciplinary actions are not

 eligible. Even if he or she paid the fine, it is considered a disciplinary

 action.

 7. A student can be an Organizer/Manager if he/she has worked within

 the organizing committee of previous fests in the past year and has done

 considerable work. This needs to be acknowledged by the faculty coordinator

 of the concerned committee.

 Coordinators must have prominent contributions in clubs/chapters or in

 organizing any other event.

 Volunteers need not have prior experience.

 8. Students planning to do their project outside VIT are not eligible.

 9. If selected for the organizing team, the student should abide by the

 rules and regulations of the Riviera team.

 10. Only final-year students are eligible for the post

 of Student Organizer.

 Both final-year and pre-final-year students can apply for the post of

 Manager.

 Only pre-final year students can apply for the post of coordinator.

 Second-year students, the joining batch of 2023, are eligible only for

 the post of Volunteers.

 11. Only applicants who have completed the “Preferences for ProShow

 lineup” form sent by the Riviera’ 25 Convenor are eligible to apply for any

 post.

https://forms.gle/nbJV8WeZPGXzhzFL8

Join us in creating memories that will last a lifetime and fostering an

international community that celebrates diversity and unity. We look

forward to welcoming you to the RIVIERA family!

With warm regards

Dr K Gokul kumar

Professor-SMEC-VIT

Convenor-Riviera 25
