Body:
Dear Students, Research Scholars and Professors,

Greetings,

Chronic diseases are likely the leading cause of outpatient visits in your

hospital. It has become almost "normal" to suffer from at least one

condition—whether it’s cardiovascular disease (high blood pressure,

ischemic heart disease, heart attacks, strokes), diabetes, chronic

respiratory diseases, cancer, mental health disorders, or autoimmune

conditions. In India, deaths from chronic diseases have been steadily

rising by approximately 1% annually since 1990, when they accounted for 36%

of deaths. As of 2019, 65% of all deaths in the country are attributable to

chronic diseases (NCDs). This growing burden is not only causing immense

suffering but also creating unsustainable financial challenges for

individuals, families, society, and the nation.

 A significant portion of these chronic diseases is related to lifestyle

choices. Sometimes these habits stem from personal decisions; other times,

we find ourselves following societal trends or choosing convenience amidst

life’s many demands. Often, we may not even realize that making different

choices could have a profound impact on our health and quality of life.

The upcoming National Health Conclave (NHC), scheduled for October 15-16,

2024, offers a unique opportunity to explore the critical role of lifestyle

and Lifestyle Medicine (LM). The theme, "Lifestyle Medicine: Empowering

Communities, Transforming Lives," will bring together thought leaders,

healthcare professionals, academics, and policymakers to tackle urgent

healthcare challenges, share innovative practices, and foster collaborative

solutions. The event will feature five key sessions on Exercise,

Environment, Nutrition, Social Health, and Mental Health & Spirituality.

 For more details and registration, please visit https://www.nhc2024.org/

https://www.nhc2024.org/ 

Building on the success of the preceding 4 conclaves, this landmark event

aims to convene leaders and experts from various sectors to generate

implementable recommendations for enhancing healthy lifestyles across

India. With a history of impactful white papers influencing government

decisions, this conclave is a critical platform for collaborative action.

Kindly take part in this conclave discussion.

Thanks and Regards

Yours Sincerely,

P.Arulmozhivarman

Subject: Application Deadline : Live Project to Learn & Upskill in Machine Learning (ML)
Body:
Dear VIT students,

Please note that tonight, 11.59pm is the deadline to apply for the Finlatics Machine Learning program, an online live project that helps students learn and gain experience in using machine learning algorithms.

Along with the Vellore Institute of Technology, this project is running at leading campuses, including IIT Delhi, IIT Madras, IIM Bangalore and BITS Pilani, among others.

It was curated at the prestigious Atal Incubation Centre, supported by the Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog, and the Government of India.

STRUCTURE of the live project:

1. Learn the core concepts around Machine Learning algorithms

2. Become proficient in using the Google Colab Notebook for machine learning

3. Engage in data preprocessing - a critical activity to prepare data sets for building machine learning algorithms

4. Gain an understanding of supervised and unsupervisedmachine learning algorithms using Python libraries

5. Complete an industry-specific case project to understand the application of Machine Learning in business scenarios

The project is doable along with any other commitment due to its work-from-home and online structure.

Student OUTCOMES:

1. Certificate of Proficiency in Machine Learning

2. Letter of Recommendation on performance

To apply, students can fill out the form below, and we will get in touch with them:

https://82e6v.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/7nVU1aA2nfsTSlPYaV0LcO3ykXyRn8u/80Clc-zk7R3v

No prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to participate in the program. The program will impart all necessary training on Python and machine learning techniques.

Project Duration: 1 month /2 months (on student choice)

Project Start: Flexible start date option. Students can choose to start the project post-exams.

Project Break & Extension: Selected students will be eligible for a break during the project if needed for any exams, assignments, or personal commitments. They can also take an extension on the project.

If selected, the project has a minimal induction fee of Rs. 2999 + GST.

Fee Waiver: A 25% fee waiver shall be given to all Vellore Institute of Technology students on the abovementioned minimal induction fee. This waiver will reduce the fee to Rs. 2199 + GST.

To be eligible for the waiver, kindly apply before tonight's deadline.

The application process takes 2-3 minutes of your time and is free.

We are excited to have a fruitful engagement.

Subject: Live Project to Learn & Upskill in Machine Learning (ML)
Body:
Dear VIT students,

Finlatics is pleased to extend applications for the Finlatics Machine Learning program, an online live project that helps students learn and gain experience in using machine learning algorithms.

Along with the Vellore Institute of Technology, this project is running at leading campuses, including IIT Delhi, IIT Madras, IIM Bangalore and BITS Pilani, among others.

It was curated at the prestigious Atal Incubation Centre, supported by the Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog, and the Government of India.

STRUCTURE of the live project:

1. Learn the core concepts around Machine Learning algorithms

2. Become proficient in using the Google Colab Notebook for machine learning

3. Engage in data preprocessing - a critical activity to prepare data sets for building machine learning algorithms

4. Gain an understanding of supervised and unsupervisedmachine learning algorithms using Python libraries

5. Complete an industry-specific case project to understand the application of Machine Learning in business scenarios

The project is doable along with any other commitment due to its work-from-home and online structure.

Student OUTCOMES:

1. Certificate of Proficiency in Machine Learning

2. Letter of Recommendation on performance

To apply, students can fill out the form below, and we will get in touch with them:

https://82e6v.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/7nVU1aA2nfsTSlPYaV0LcO3ykXyRn8u/8TKaWGJVcCd5

No prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to participate in the program. The program will impart all necessary training on Python and machine learning techniques.

Project Duration: 1 month /2 months (on student choice)

Project Start: Flexible start date option. Students can choose to start the project post-exams.

Project Break & Extension: Selected students will be eligible for a break during the project if needed for any exams, assignments, or personal commitments. They can also take an extension on the project.

If selected, the project has a minimal induction fee of Rs. 2999 + GST.

Fee Waiver: A 25% fee waiver shall be given to all Vellore Institute of Technology students on the abovementioned minimal induction fee. This waiver will reduce the fee to Rs. 2199 + GST.

Dear All,

We would like to congratulate Mr. Aravinda Loshan Sankara Narayanan (Reg

No: 21BDS0228) for his outstanding accomplishments. His dedication, hard

work, and passion have not only brought great pride to himself but have

also brought laurels to VIT. We are incredibly proud to have him as part of

our academic community.

I would like to highlight three transformative experiences that have

significantly shaped his academic journey and personal growth:

2024, he had the distinct honor of representing India at the HCONF

Conference hosted by Harvard University out of over 25000+ applicants. This

experience provided him with the opportunity to interact with industry

leaders and inspiring personalities from around the world. During the

conference, he participated in the Impact Challenge, where they were tasked

with solving a real-world business problem for Patagonia. Competing against

seasoned professionals, including global consultants from McKinsey, Bain,

BCG, and KPMG, he proposed a solution that was well-received by Patagonia's

Asia-Pacific Director, leading to him being awarded the title of “Global

Winner of the HCONF Impact Challenge.”

of attending the “Innovation for Young Entrepreneurs” course at the

National University of Singapore. During this course, he actively

participated in all activities and led a team of five in the final

presentation, competing against 20 other teams. He isi honored to have

received a Letter of Commendation from NUS for my contribution to the

winning team.

AYIMUN, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia where he was allocated to the UNESCO Council

where he represented the Kingdom of Bhutan. During this MUN, collectively

as delegates from over 28 countries worked together to form a resolution

that emphasized the implementation of digital transformation in education.

He is excited to share that he was in the top-tier delegate in his council.

Mr Aravinda Loshan says, "These experiences have not only broadened my

horizons but have also allowed me to represent VIT on international

platforms, showcasing the quality of education and opportunities our

institution provides"

Mr. Aravinda Loshan Sankara Narayanan (Reg No: 21BDS0228), we look forward

excel in your endeavours.

Once again, Hearty congratulations on this remarkable achievement!

The idea of World Lung Day (WLD) was first conceived at the 2016 FIRS Kyoto

Assembly meeting. FIRS recognized the need for improved lung health to help

meet the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) given the

rapid pace of global industrialization disproportionately affecting the

most vulnerable as a result of age extremes, economic disadvantage, social

Body:
Dear Students, Research Scholars and Professors,

Greetings,

 VIT takes great effort in promoting the Deep Tech Research Program as an

initiative to foster cutting-edge research and innovation in transformative

technologies through Chancellor's Fellowship.

Our mission is to bridge the gap between academia and industry, driving

societal impact through scientific advancements.

Research Focus Areas

• Artificial Intelligence/Generative AI

(Healthcare/Climate/Environment/Energy/Finance)

• Machine Learning/Deep Learning

• Wireless Networks/IOT

• Image and Vision Computing

• Autonomous Robot

• Quantum Computing

• Cyber Security

• Space Technologies

• Blockchain Technologies

• Precision Agriculture

• Sustainable development

• Biotechnology (Genomics/Synthetic Biology/Food production/Fuel)

• Any other areas mentioned by NITI Ayog

(Problem Statement proposed by Research Scholar With the faculty guide

acting as mentorship) - Outcome Product Development –TRL 6

Eligibility:

Graduates must have an outstanding academic record in their Bachelor’s

Degree in Engineering / Technology are eligible to apply. A minimum of 75%

marks or a CGPA of 7.5 is mandatory on a 10- point scale or Master’s

degree in Engineering / Technology in the relevant discipline with a

minimum of 75% marks (of all the years /semesters) wherever marks are

awarded, or a CGPA 7.5 on a 10-point scale in cases where letter grades are

awarded or Equivalent qualifications like M.Sc. (Engineering) / M.S. [By

Research] / M.Tech. [By Research] in full-time or regular mode of

education is mandatory

Deep Tech Research Chancellor's Fellowship:

 First Year

• ₹ 40,000 (GATE Qualified (Above 60 Percentile)); 

• ₹ 35,000 (Others)

• 2nd- 3rd Years

• ₹50,000(GATE Qualified (Above 60 Percentile)); 

• ₹ 45,000 (Others)

Funding Extendable for 4th Year

 Periodic review of innovation, and patent attainment level will be

assessed.

Product Development upto TRL6 is mandatory for getting 4th Year funding

support.

Apply now and join our community of innovative researchers

innovators.

Dear Students,

 The second call for Student Startup Venture is open from June 2024. We are

about to close the call by the 25th of September 2024. Interested

candidates can apply. This is a reminder email.

KICK-START YOUR START-UP

For those interested in building Technology Products or aspiring to be

entrepreneurs, here is an opportunity to avail Student Startup Venture

(SSV) Grant from VIT!

SSV support has been extended to students since 2017, over 160 projects

have been supported and 19 startups have emerged…

Startups like https://vicara.co/ https://vicara.co/ ;

https://alfaleus.in/

https://alfaleus.in/ ; https://www.punar.in/ https://www.punar.in/;

kuppismart solutions pvt ltd/ have emerged with the support of SSV.

SSV comes with a grant of up to Rs. 2.00 lakhs for prototype development

activities. The duration of the project will be from October 2024 to July

2025. All students of UG, PG programs, and Research Scholars on the campus

are eligible to apply. A faculty mentor is mandatory for every team

of SSV (Maximum of 3 students + 1 faculty mentor). Only those who are

engaged in technology product development (hardware) can apply/ this is not

for app development/ pure software products /research activities.

This fund purely supports technology innovations leading to novel products,

prototypes, and venture creation.

Innovations in the following themes are encouraged.

1. Sustainability (including energy/ renewable energy

technologies)

2. Cleantech/ GreenTech Revolution

3. HealthTech Horizons

4. Smart Cities and Digital Realities

5. AgriTech – including post-harvest technologies

6. Clean Energy Breakthroughs

7. Smart devices based on AI/ML (including consumer &

enterprise AI solutions), IoT and IIoT

8. BioTech and Life Sciences

9. Robotics, Drones and Automation

10. Sports tech

To avail of this opportunity, please register on the below link on or

before the 25th of September 2024.

 Registration link for SSV: https://tinyurl.com/SSV2024-25

Kindly find attached the guidelines, which will help you with the

submission process. Kindly make sure that the outcomes are clearly met

during the completion of the project. Once the ideas have been

shortlisted, we will be contacting you on how to take further steps. The

projects completed through SSV will be given the opportunity to be

Pre-incubated/ Incubated at VIT-TBI.

disciplines

· EIL scholarships shall be awarded to meritorious and

other source whatsoever shall not stand eligible for the EIL scholarship

completion of the programme. The candidate shall send a progress report in

30 days of the announcement of the result and forwarded by the Head of the

Institution

based on the academic performance and good conduct of the student

· If a student has failed in any paper/ secured an aggregate of less

than 55% or equivalent in any semester/ year, he/she shall not be paid the

scholarship till he/she clears all the semesters

· The candidature of applicants with invalid caste/income

certificates and incomplete applications shall be rejected summarily.

The International Day of Sign Languages

The International Day of Sign Language is a unique opportunity to support

and protect the linguistic identity and cultural diversity of all deaf

people and other sign language users. This challenge aims to promote the

use of sign languages by local, national, and global leaders in partnership

with national associations of deaf people in each country, as well as other

deaf-led organizations. According to the World Federation of the Deaf,

there are approximately 72 million deaf people worldwide. More than 80% of

them live in developing countries. Collectively, they use more than 300

different sign languages.

Sign languages are fully-fledged natural languages, structurally distinct

from the spoken languages. There is also an international sign language,

which is used by deaf people in international meetings and informally when

traveling and socializing. It is considered a pidgin form of sign language

that is not as complex as natural sign languages and has a limited lexicon.

International Day of University Sport

The International Day of University Sport (IDUS) is celebrated annually on

September 20. Proposed by the International University Sports Federation

(FISU), it is officially endorsed by the United Nations Education, Science,

and Culture Organisation (UNESCO). The day aims at confirming the

importance of sport in universities and the role of universities in the

community as responsible actors for consolidating and developing quality

physical and sports education at the service of citizens.

This day is an opportunity to underline the social role played by

universities and their curricula, making sport available for everyone in

order to foster the regular practice of physical activity in the greatest

number of people. It also allows UNESCO to reaffirm its committed support

to personal and collective development through sport and education, for the

spread of a genuine sports culture, which we believe is inherent to a

culture of peace.

welcome for our freshers, offering memorable events and valuable mentoring

sessions.

including “Reaching the Moon: Chandrayaan 3,” where we had the privilege of

learning from ISRO experts. We also commemorated Kargil Vijay Diwas,

honoring our nation's heroes and reigniting patriotism within our student

body. The successful induction programs across our schools ensured a

seamless transition for new students into the VIT community.

July set a strong foundation for the year ahead. Be sure to check this

edition for more on upcoming events and opportunities to get involved.

For more details, please read the attached newsletter.

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [18th September]

World Bamboo Day

World Bamboo Day, observed annually on September 18, is a global initiative

that sheds light on the incredible significance of bamboo. This remarkable

plant, often referred to as “green gold,” holds immense potential in

sustainable development, poverty alleviation, environmental conservation,

and cultural preservation. World Bamboo Day serves as a platform to raise

awareness about the myriad benefits of bamboo and its role in addressing

pressing global challenges.

The potential of bamboo trees is highlighted on this day and is regarded to

be an alternative resource.

World Patient Safety Day

World Patient Safety Day calls for global solidarity and concerted action

by all countries and international partners to improve patient safety.

Furthermore, Day brings together patients, families, caregivers,

communities, health workers, health care leaders, and policy-makers to show

their commitment to patient safety. The theme of the very first World

Patient Safety Day was aimed at establishing the legacy of the day and

highlighting the importance of prioritizing and addressing patient safety

globally by all stakeholders.

For World Patient Safety Day, 17 September, WHO urges all stakeholders to “Act

now for safe and respectful childbirth!” with the theme “Safe maternal

and newborn care”. Approximately 810 women die every day from preventable

causes related to pregnancy and childbirth. In addition, around 6700

newborns die every day, amounting to 47% of all under-5 deaths. Moreover,

about 2 million babies are stillborn every year, with over 40% occurring

during labor. Considering the significant burden of risks and harm women

and newborns are exposed to due to unsafe care, compounded by the

disruption of essential health services caused by the COVID-19 pandemic,

the campaign is even more important this year. No one should be harmed in

health care. Yet thousands of patients across the world suffer avoidable

harm or are put at risk of injury while receiving health care every single

day.

Body:
Dear Students,

School of Electrical Engineering, Vellore Institute of Technology, Vellore

is excited to announce the upcoming 36-hour IEEE Region 10 sponsored

Hackathon dedicated to Affordable Medical Device Development! This is an

incredible opportunity to collaborate, innovate, and make a real impact

through technology. The event is planned during 3rd and 4th October, 2024.

The event is powered by All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS),

Technology Business Incubator (TBI-VIT), IEEE Power Electronics Society &

IEEE Madras Section.

What’s the Hackathon About?

In this event, students will work in teams to design and develop

innovative, cost-effective devices that have the potential to improve

accessibility and quality of life. Whether you are passionate about

healthcare, education, or everyday utilities, this hackathon is your chance

to bring your ideas to life and address pressing needs with affordable

solutions.

Purpose

v Region-10 Affordable Medical Device Development Hackathon (36 hours) has

been established aligning to IEEE tagline ‘Advancing technology for

Humanity’ to encourage all IEEE R10 council, section, subsection, student

branch, student branch society chapter and other affinity groups to join

hands and come together to design develop and prepare TRL 3/4 prototypes.

v It’s a medical device hackathon bringing together members of various

grades of various sections of IEEE Region 10 and inter-disciplinary teams

to explore medical device innovation.

v The outcome shall be TRL level 3/4 prototype of low-cost solution for

the medical problems.

v The hackathon leverages networking, team building, solutions to the

complex problems and bringing mechanical engineers, design engineers and

medical practitioners in the same platform.

Why Participate?

v Collaborate with Peers: Work alongside fellow students from diverse

backgrounds and skill sets

v Develop Skills: Gain hands-on experience in design, prototyping, and

problem-solving

v Win Prizes: Compete for exciting prizes and recognition for your

innovative solutions

v Networking Opportunities: Connect with industry professionals,

mentors, and potential future collaborators

v Certificates: To all mentors and participants

For registration:

v Every individual participant has to apply through the link to

participate in the hackathon

v Team size: 5 members including the mentor

v Each team shall have one YP (Young Professional preferably from industry

to see business side of the product), one senior member as mentor, one WIE

(women in engineering), one student member in a way that each team shall

have one mechanical/design Engineer, one Computer/ Electronics Engineering,

one Biomedical/ dental/ medical/ pharmacy/Physiotherapy student

v The selected students shall be shown the curated videos of problem

statements

v Based on the videos and expertise, the individuals shall opt for the

problem statement

v The organizers will summarize and based on the matching algorithm the

teams shall be formed à Groups will be formed by the organizers

v Four stages of the event: Team building, problem definition, concept and

prototyping, pitch to jury

Sign up https://tinyurl.com/Medical-device-Hackathon

Last date for registration: 20.09.2024

Additional Details:

· No Registration fees

· Resources Provided: Basic components will be provided

· Food and Refreshments: Food and refreshment will be provided

· We encourage all the students to participate, regardless of your

background or experience level. This is a fantastic chance to learn,

innovate, and make a difference.

For more information and to register, please see the event brochure

attached along with this mail. We look forward to seeing your creative

solutions and enthusiasm!

Coordinators: Dr S Albert Alexander & Dr A Chitra

Department of Energy & Power Electronics 

School of Electrical Engineering

Subject: Call for Student Research Forum- ATS 2024
Body:
Dear all,

Call for Student Research Forum (SRF):

A Student Research Forum (SRF) will be organized to promote and encourage

young researchers in Test Technology during the 2024 Asian Test Symposium

(ATS). This forum is a great opportunity for Bachelor and Masters students

who have completed their respective thesis within the last 12 months or who

are close to completing their thesis to present their work to a broad

audience. This forum will help students interact with pioneers in their

research domain and get valuable feedback on their work. The forum may also

help students to establish contacts for entering the job market. Entries

from eligible young researchers across India are invited for the Student

Research Forum.

About ATS-2024

The Asian Test Symposium started 1992 in Hiroshima, Japan, as an annual

symposium in the Asia Pacific region. Since then, the symposium has

continued its growth and development, visiting various historic cities in

Asia. This year, it is marking its 33rd anniversary to Ahmedabad, India.

The walled city of Ahmadabad was founded in 1411 AD on the eastern bank of

the Sabarmati River which is India’s first-ever UNESCO World Heritage City

and considered as epicenter of Indian Semiconductor activities in recent

era.

Conference Website: https://ec.nirmauni.ac.in/ats-2024/

History of ATS: http://www.ieee-ats.org/

Connect and follow ATS on https://www.linkedin.com/company/ats-2024

ATS-2024 technical program will include contributed papers and

contributions from invited speakers. ATS-2024 will have

pre-conference-tutorials, workshops, keynotes, plenary talks, technical

sessions, PhD forum, Student Research forum, Industry forum,

Women-In-Semiconductor forum and expert panels.

Several fellowships for students and academia will be available.

Eligibility

A student enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in any recognized

University or Institute on or before July 2023 and working on test-related

topics is eligible to participate in the contest.

An individual can only participate in the contest.

Submission Deadline: October 15, 2024

Notification of Qualification: October 31, 2024

Guideline for Submission

The extended abstract is to be submitted in PDF copy with a minimum font

size: of 10pt, Times New Roman font. Max three pages, including tables,

diagrams, and references (if any).

Documents to be Submitted

Proof of studentship: A copy of the valid identity cards or a letter from

the Head of the Department/Institute for the currently enrolled students. A

copy of the degree certificate (or the provisional certificate) is

sufficient for graduated students.

Submission

Contestants must submit the PDF version of the Extended abstract and

material by https://tinyurl.com/ATSsrf2024

Selection Procedure

There would be a two-tier selection process. The initial shortlisting would

be done by the Selection Committee based on the merits of the submission.

The shortlisted nominees will be invited to deliver a poster presentation

before the Selection Committee during the conference. The Selection

Committee would then recommend the nominee for conferment of the Award.

Awards

To be Announced Later.

Contact

Body:
Dear Students,

All are cordially invited for the below Guest Lecture.

Title: "PhD Chronicles: Navigating the Path of Research Excellence"

Speaker: Dr. Kirthika Senthil Kumar, Manager, Innovation & Enterprise

(MedTech), National Health Innovation Centre, Rochester Park, Singapore.

Date & Time: 13.09.2024 (Friday) & 03:30 pm.Venue: TT 312

Speaker Profile:

Dr. Kirthika Senthil Kumar

Kirthika Senthil Kumar is a pioneering figure in biomedical engineering,

clinical research, and entrepreneurship, whose work has significantly

impacted the healthcare sector. She earned her B. Tech. in Biomedical

Engineering from VIT, Vellore in 2016 and Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering

from the National University of Singapore (NUS) in 2021, where her

innovative research on flexible and stretchable sensors led to multiple

patents and over 700 citations, establishing her as a leader in the field.

During her tenure as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the N.1 Institute

for Health, she developed CURATE.AI http://curate.ai/, a digital health

innovation that secured more than SGD 150,000 in funding and advanced the

optimization of combinational drug treatments. As an entrepreneur, Kirthika

co-founded SkullBot and HiSEPOR, raising over S$100k through strategic

business pitches. Her achievements include winning the FuelAsia Innovation

Challenge and being named among Singapore's 100 Women in Tech. Kirthika has

also contributed to the IEEE community, serving as Treasurer for Women in

Engineering and chairing the Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society.

Currently, as Manager of Innovation and Enterprise (MedTech) at the

National Health Innovation Centre, she drives research commercialization,

collaborates with hospital clusters, negotiates licensing deals, and

fosters international partnerships, with a focus on transforming healthcare

through intellectual property.

The flyer is attached for your reference.

Body:
Dear Students,

Are you passionate about innovation, startups, and making a real impact?

Then the Institution's Innovation Council (IIC) at VIT is looking for YOU!

The IIC at VIT is a vibrant hub for students interested in all things

innovation and entrepreneurship. We offer a variety of exciting

opportunities through our different departments, and we're looking for

enthusiastic and talented individuals to join our team.

Here's a glimpse into the exciting roles we have available:

Events Department (10-15 members needed):

 - Be the backbone of our events, assisting in organization and execution.

 - Ensure smooth crowd management for a seamless experience.

 - Qualifications: 2nd or 3rd year students (exceptions for exceptional

 candidates). Adaptable, composed individuals with event management

 experience are preferred.

IPR Department (10 trainees needed):

 - Play a key role in organizing IPR events and workshops.

 - Promote IPR awareness and educate your peers.

 - Qualifications: 2nd or 3rd year students preferred. Prior knowledge

 of IPR is a plus.

Innovation Department (15 trainees needed):

 - Unleash your creativity! Help us organize events and activities that

 foster innovation and startups.

 - Be a mentor and guide, inspiring your peers to think outside the box.

 - Qualifications: 2nd year students (exceptions for exceptional

 candidates). Creative thinkers with strong leadership qualities. Experience

 in innovation or interdisciplinary projects is a plus. Diversity in

 experience is highly appreciated.

Startup Team (10 members needed):

 - Be a part of the startup ecosystem! Assist in event organization and

 contribute ideas to help build successful businesses.

 - Foster a collaborative and supportive community for aspiring

 entrepreneurs.

 - Qualifications: 2nd or 3rd year students (exceptions for exceptional

 candidates). Excellent communication and strategic thinking skills.

 Experience in building businesses or collaborating with people is preferred.

Social Media & Design Team (15 trainees needed):

 - Be the voice of the IIC! Craft compelling content for our social media

 platforms.

 - Edit videos, reels, and promos to capture the essence of our events.

 - Take stunning photos and videos to showcase our activities.

 - Qualifications: 2nd or 3rd year students preferred. Prior experience

 in video editing, photography, or videography is a must. Creativity and a

 knack for ideation are essential.

Editorial Team (10 members needed):

 - Document IIC events and create insightful reports.

 - Showcase your writing skills by crafting articles for our bi-annual

 newsletter (conducting interviews might be involved).

 - Contribute to the annual report with well-written event reports.

 - Write engaging captions and LinkedIn posts to keep our audience

 updated.

 - Qualifications: Students from any year (1st, 2nd, or 3rd). Excellent

 English proficiency is a must. Prior writing experience is beneficial but

 not mandatory.

Alumni Entrepreneurs and Industry Connect (4 members needed):

 - Bridge the gap! Facilitate communication with alumni entrepreneurs and

 industry professionals.

 - Build and maintain valuable connections to enhance our domain

 expertise.

 - Guide your peers in finding mentors for their entrepreneurial journeys.

 - Qualifications: Students from any year (1st, 2nd, or 3rd). Strong

 communication skills and English proficiency are essential. An interest in

 networking and building industry relationships is a must. Previous

 experience in event coordination or professional communication is a plus.

Ready to join the IIC family?

Fill out this form to express your interest and become a part of our

dynamic team: https://forms.gle/PrycuG7PFLC4Ttsa7

Last date for application- 15 Sep 2024

We can't wait to hear from you!

Body:
Dear VITians,

On the occasion of World Suicide Prevention Day, the Office of Students'

Welfare is pleased to invite you to a special speaker session aimed at

raising awareness about mental well-being and suicide prevention.

The session will be conducted by Dr. Shiva Prakash Srinivasan, a renowned

expert in the field, on 11th September 2024, from 10:00 AM at Channa Reddy

Auditorium. Dr. Srinivasan will share valuable insights on mental health,

offer coping strategies, and foster a deeper understanding of suicide

prevention.

We encourage all students and faculty to attend this important session as

we work together to promote mental well-being within our community.

Event Details:Date: 11th September 2024Time: 10:00 AMVenue: Channa Reddy

Auditorium

Your presence would be greatly appreciated. Let’s make mental health a

priority and come together to support one another.

Dear VITians,

World Suicide Prevention Day

World Suicide Prevention Day (WSPD), observed annually on 10th September,

is organized by the International Association for Suicide Prevention (IASP)

and endorsed by the World Health Organization (WHO). The theme of WSPD

2023, “Creating hope through action,” reflects the need for collective

action to address this urgent public health issue.

The main significance behind observing World Suicide Prevention Day is to

highlight the fact that suicides are preventable, and there are better

alternatives to suicide. The importance of the day is to reduce the stigma

associated with suicides and promote a culture where people don't hesitate

to seek help.

On the occasion of World Suicide Prevention Day, the Office of Students'

Welfare is pleased to invite you to a special speaker session aimed at

raising awareness about mental well-being and suicide prevention.

The session will be conducted by Dr. Shiva Prakash Srinivasan, a renowned

expert in the field, on 11th September 2024, from 10:00 AM at Channa Reddy

Auditorium. Dr. Srinivasan will share valuable insights on mental health,

offer coping strategies, and foster a deeper understanding of suicide

prevention.

We encourage all students and faculty to attend this important session as

we work together to promote mental well-being within our community.

Event Details:Date: 11th September 2024Time: 10:00 AMVenue: Channa Reddy

Auditorium

Your presence would be greatly appreciated. Let’s make mental health a

priority and come together to support one another.

Body:
Dear Student,

Greetings!

I am informing you that the Automotive Research Centre (ARC) is an interdisciplinary centre that focuses its cutting-edge research that relates to the future direction of the global automotive industry. It is a unique centre that carries out research on Autonomous, Connected and Electric vehicle (ACE) technologies—electric vehicles, hybrid electric vehicles, autonomous vehicles, drones, battery management systems and fuel cells. The centre also focuses on the use of various gaseous fuels in IC engines and new fuel formulations.

ARC has established state-of-the-art facilities to develop and test products in the field of self-driving vehicles. The centre has actively assisted automotive industries in niche areas and received grants from various agencies like DST, SERB, DRDO, etc.

ARC research group is currently seeking interns who are enthusiastic about learning and working on projects related to autonomous vehicles, drones, electric vehicles, battery management systems (BMS) and IC Engines. Our current projects often involve collaboration with an interdisciplinary team of faculty members.

Our research and development efforts are focused on the following domains:

1. Computer Science and Engineering: AI, ML, ROS developer. Sensor fusion, Perception, and Planning.

2. Electrical & Electronics Engineering and Electronics and Communication Engineering: AI, ML, Control Systems and Power Electronics.

3. Mechanical Engineering: Application of AI, ML and Vehicle Dynamics, Hydrogen and methanol engine development and Development of electronic control unit for IC engines.

Body:
Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [5th September]

events.

Teachers' Day

Teachers' Day is the perfect occasion to convey to your teachers the regard

and respect you have for them. In India, Teachers' Day is celebrated every

year on September 5 - the birth anniversary of the first Vice President of

India and exemplary teacher Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.

While Teachers' Day is usually celebrated in schools with a number of

events and activities. You can tell your teachers and professors how much

they mean to you with the help of these quotes. Send a quote to your

teachers and let them know how much you appreciate their hard work.

"Teaching is a very noble profession that shapes the character, caliber,

and future of an individual." - APJ Abdul Kalam

On the occasion of Teacher's Day, CC are organising one event.

Today's Events:

 - Bag of Thanks

 - CASA: Managing Relationships

 - EGG-CELLENT ENGINEERING

 -

A journey's end: Fogo-Agua combined Session 

Scroll down for more information

Nature Lovers Club 

Event Name : Bag of Thanks

Time: 11:00 am to 1:00 pm

Venue : VIT Campus (Offline)

Event Details : On the occasion of Teacher’s Day, Nature Lovers Club

presents "Bag of Thanks," an appreciation event designed to honor and

celebrate the contributions of our faculty. Faculties will receive

personalized paper bags containing seed balls and heartfelt cards as tokens

of gratitude. This event aims to foster a sense of community and

appreciation within the university while promoting environmental

sustainability through the seed ball initiative.

Registration : VTOP registration

Instagram link: https://instagram.com/natureclubvit?igshid=YmMyMTA2M2Y=

INSTITUTE OF INDUSTRIAL AND SYSTEMS ENGINEERS (IISE)

Event Name: CASA: Managing Relationships

Event Time: 11.00 am - 1.00 pm

Description: Join us for CASA: Managing Relationships, an engaging event

hosted by IISE at our college, featuring Clinton Joseph as the speaker.

This session is designed specifically for college students, focusing on the

essential skills needed to navigate and strengthen both personal and

professional relationships during your academic journey. Learn practical

tips on communication, conflict resolution, and building lasting

connections in a supportive environment.

Event Platform: MB210 (offline)

Registration: VTOP

Society of Manufacturing Engineers (SME)

Event Name : EGG-CELLENT ENGINEERING

Event Timings : 2pm to 5pm

Venue : FOODYS 3, Near SJT (Offline)

Event Description : An egg drop contest that challenges participants to

construct protective structures for an egg, which will be dropped from a

designated height. The goal is to prevent the egg from breaking upon

impact. Join us in this eggcellent event.

Venue: Foodys-3

Registration: VTOP

Toastmasters International 

Event Name: A journey's end: Fogo-Agua combined Session

Time: am 10 am - 2:00 pm

Venue : Rajaji Hall, MB

Join us for a special evening as we bid farewell to our fellow Toastmasters

who are embarking on new adventures. This event is not just a goodbye, but

a celebration of the growth, friendships, and memories we've shared

together.

We'll reflect on the remarkable speeches, the laughter, and the lessons

learned, all while recognising the contributions of those who have made our

club a vibrant community. Expect heartfelt speeches, tokens of

appreciation, and a warm atmosphere that embodies the spirit.

Registration: VTOP

National Nutrition Week

India marks National Nutrition Week annually in the first week of September

of Women and Child Development's Food and Nutrition Board in 1982 with the

objective to raise awareness of the importance of nutrition for the human

body. A well-balanced diet, with a combination of all the essential

nutrients, plays a pivotal role in the growth and development of our mind

Skyscraper Day

Skyscraper day is celebrated on September 3 each year, as this is the

anniversary of the birth of Louis H. Sullivan, the American architect who

was influential in the world of building tall buildings and was even called

the “father of skyscrapers”.

The construction of tall buildings has become so commonplace in cities

around the globe that the general public typically gives little thought to

the visionaries who are responsible for creating a city’s unique

skyline. Skyscraper Day is an opportunity to appreciate these architectural

Vellore Institute of Technology shared a post: Today marked the grand inauguration of the 7th edition of the two-day Agri Expo 2024, organized by the VIT Centre for Agricultural Innovations and Advanced Learning (VAIAL) and CSRD-RS. This remarkable event brought together over 5000 farmers from Vellore, Ranipet, Thirupattur, Thiruvannamalai, and other districts of Tamil Nadu.

The expo features an impressive exhibition with 130+ stalls, showcasing the latest advancements in agriculture, horticulture, agricultural engineering, animal husbandry, seed and organic certification, and more. State Government departments, agro-industries, farmer producer organizations, the banking sector, traditional food entrepreneurs, and VIT students and faculty are all participating in making this event a success.

Eminent speakers are conducting technical sessions to educate farmers on implementing advanced methods and technologies in agriculture. This is a fantastic opportunity for farmers to gain valuable insights and network with industry experts.

The event was graced by Chief Guest, Ms. V.R. Subbulaxmi, IAS, Vellore District Collector; Guest of Honour, Dr. T. Arumugam, Vice Chancellor - Thiruvalluvar University; Vice President, Dr. G.V. Selvam; Vice-Chancellor, Dr. V. S. Kanchana Bhaaskaran; Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Dr. Partha Sharathi Mallick; Registrar, Dr. T. Jayabarathi; Dean - VAIAL, Dr. S. Babu; faculty and students along with the farmers.

Subject: Australian National University (ANU) Guest Lecture Series on Science Technology Engineering Mathematics and Medicine (STEMM) from September to November 2024
Body:
Dear Students, Scholars, and Professors,

The Australian National University (ANU), a partner institution of VIT, is

organizing a series of Guest Lectures on Science Technology Engineering

Mathematics and Medicine (STEMM) from September to November 2024.

The 2024 ANU STEMM Guest Lecture series will feature a range of virtual

masterclasses / lectures delivered by ANU academic staff (including the

Nobel Prize winning astrophysicist Prof Brian Schmidt).

You may please register to attend the Lectures you are interested in

following the website: https://rb.gy/5es3r0 .

A flyer for the same is also attached herewith.

Each guest lecture will focus on a different discipline area and, as you

will notice from the abstracts, participants will be expected to have some

level of background knowledge (and ideally, would have completed some

university-level courses) in that subject area.

Subject: Be On Alert Against Being Conned Financially
Body:
Dear All,

It has been brought to our notice that some VITians have been conned into

parting with details like debit/credit card numbers, CVVs, Aadhaar numbers,

etc. that are used by tricksters to cheat the victims out of their money.

In some other cases, the victims (non-VITians) have been threatened that

FIRs have been registered against them for non-bailable offenses, and the

money is needed to be paid to hush up the case(s). The threat of illegal

items being found in the parcel sent by/addressed to the victim(s) has also

been used.

In their own interest, all VITians are hereby requested to be on utmost

alert against such frauds. Do not part with your confidential details, no

matter how convincing the person at the other end sounds.

Approach the cyber-crime branch of Vellore police, Office of the

Superintendent of Police (ground floor, left-wing, behind

Collectorate), Sathuvachari, Vellore, if you have already lost money in

such crimes, or have been contacted via such calls (voice, or WhatsApp) or

e-mail messages.

You can also report cyber crimes through the National Cyber Crime Reporting

Portal (NCRP) at https://cybercrime.gov.in/.

Also, you can report cyber crimes by calling the helpline number 1930.

Subject: NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program 2025-2026 (up to $60,000) – Opportunity Desk
Body:
Dear VITians,

NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program 2024 – 2025

The application deadline for the 2024-2025 academic year is Sept. 7, 2023

NVIDIA Since its founding in 1993, NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) has been a pioneer

in accelerated computing. The company’s invention of the GPU in 1999

sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined computer graphics,

ignited the era of modern AI and is fueling the creation of the metaverse.

NVIDIA is now a full-stack computing company with data-center-scale

offerings that are reshaping industry.

This is the twenty-third year that NVIDIA has invited PhD students to

submit their research projects for consideration. Recipients are selected

based on their academic achievements, professor nomination, and area of

research. We have found this program to be a great way to support academia

in its pursuit of cutting edge innovation, as well as an ideal avenue to

introduce NVIDIA to the future leaders of our industry.

It focuses on supporting students working in AI, machine learning,

autonomous vehicles, computer graphics, robotics, healthcare, high

performance computing and related fields. Awards are up to $60,000 per

student.

NVIDIA has long believed that investing in university talent is beneficial

to the industry and key to our continued growth and success. The NVIDIA

Graduate Fellowship Program provides funding in the amount of up to $60,000

per award to PhD students who are researching topics that will lead to

major advances in accelerated computing and its applications. NVIDIA

particularly invites submissions from students pushing the envelope in

artificial intelligence, robotics, autonomous vehicles, and related fields.

We select students each year who have the talent, aptitude and initiative

to work closely with us early in their careers. Recipients not only receive

crucial funding for their research, but are able to conduct groundbreaking

work with access to NVIDIA products, technology and some of the most

talented minds in the field. In addition, the Fellowship includes a summer

internship preceding the Fellowship year.

NVIDIA partners with industry leaders to tackle some of the most complex

computing challenges. We’re creating profound change in fields as diverse

as medicine, space exploration, automotive design and film production.

We’ve only scratched the surface of what we can accomplish when we apply

our technology to it. We need innovative and talented doctoral students,

who aren’t afraid of a challenge, to help us tackle these opportunities.

Applications for 2024 are now open

Application

Eligibility

Students must have already completed their first year of PhD level studies

(at the time of application)

Students must have majors in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, System

Architecture, Electrical Engineering, or a related area

Students must be engaged in active research as part of their PhD thesis

Students must be enrolled as a full time active PhD student during the

2024-2025 academic year (9 months) of the award – this means they should

not be expecting to graduate sooner than May/June 2025.

Students must be available to complete a summer internship (which due to

COVID-19 may be held remotely) prior to the start of their Fellowship year.

Students may not be immediate family of a current NVIDIA employee

Note: The award must be administered through the student’s university;

payment will be made to the university, not directly to the student

Evaluation criteria

Proposals Will be Evaluated for:

Student quality

Letters of recommendation

Academic performance (GPA) and achievements

Research quality

Research results to date

Research proposal for fellowship

Publication track record

Relevance to NVIDIA

How your work connects to NVIDIA’s primary research domains

How your research might influence the design, performance or use of future

GPUs

Application instructions

Graduate Fellowship Applications Must Include:

Research summary/thesis proposal – up to 2 pages, plus bibliography

(bibliography does not count toward 2 page maximum for proposal)

Resume/Curriculum Vitae (CV) including contact information

Professor nomination letters (2 letters minimum (must include one from

thesis advisor), up to 3 letters maximum — OK to have nomination letters

from non-professors, as long as you have one from your thesis

advisor/professor).

Confirmation of availability for summer internship

Submission Portal: It is the student’s responsibility to ensure that all of

these items are submitted prior to the deadline. We are using a Submission

Portal in which the student manages their own application. The student must:

Complete the student profile – start this now; you can go back to the

portal repeatedly until you submit the final application

Complete your application input including research summary thesis proposal

and resume (CV)

Add contacts for the letters of recommendation — an email will

automatically be sent on your behalf to each recommender you add — be sure

to add your professors/recommenders early in the process! Do not wait until

close to the deadline!

Monitor the status of your recommendation letters in the portal — do not

click on the final submission until the recommendation status shows

“recommendation uploaded” for each recommendation you are expecting — the

professor deadline has been set 1 day prior to the student deadline to

allow the student to ensure all documents are received before submitting —

the deadline for recommendation letters is 3pm Pacific September 6, 2023.

Communicate with the recommenders to complete their letter upload on time –

it is the student’s responsibility to ensure their letters are received

into the system.

Submit the final application when all items are complete, and prior to the

application deadline: 3pm Pacific September 7, 2023.

Submissions are currently OPEN. Please access the submission site here.

Notifications of final decisions will be emailed by the end of November

Terms and Conditions

The Graduate Fellowship Award must be used to further your research. The

breakdown of the award is between stipend, tuition and health insurance, in

that order. The award is an unrestricted gift to be used to further the

student’s research over the academic year. We ask that no overhead or

indirect costs are charged to the award. Awards are not transferable to

another student. Whether it is OK to combine the NVIDIA fellowship with

another fellowship depends on several factors — please contact the NVIDIA

Graduate Fellowship for details on this matter. Awards are issued to the

university for disbursement, not directly to the student. Amount of the

award cannot exceed stipend, tuition, and health insurance. There may also

be university-specific restrictions that pertain. Applications include

permission to use the student’s submission data for evaluation of a

potential fellowship award. Applicants may choose to opt-in for an

internship evaluation outside of the fellowship (in the event the applicant

is not chosen for an award.) If selected for an award, a completed

internship at NVIDIA is required before the Fellowship award year can

begin. Immediate family of NVIDIA employees cannot participate.

Helpful Hints for the Graduate Fellowship Submission: The Recommendation

Letter

A heavily-weighted component of the application evaluation is the

recommendation letter. It is therefore recommended that the candidate

afford it the proper attention and effort; here are a few tips that we

suggest:

Pick your recommenders wisely!

Your thesis advisor is required, but beyond that, you should select only

people who know you well enough to write a strong recommendation for you. A

recommendation from a high-profile researcher who barely knows you, or has

not worked with you, does not help your application.

Ask each of your recommenders in person/via email before you send the

request from the NVIDIA Grad Fellow portal. Ask them also if they have time

to write such a letter by the due date. If they are traveling or focused on

another deadline, their letter may be hastily composed and not help your

cause. It is also generally OK to ask them directly if they feel

comfortable writing a strong recommendation letter. If this is someone you

only took a class from a few semesters ago, they might not remember you

well enough to write you the kind of recommendation you are seeking – give

them a chance to tell you. If that is the case, then thank them and move on

to asking someone who knows you better.

If you are asking a recommender in industry, such as a former boss from a

summer internship, you may need to remind them what you’ve been working on

since they last worked with you. It always helps if you can stay in

somewhat regular touch with such contacts, so that a lot of time doesn’t

pass between updates.

Provide your recommenders with sufficient notice.

Your recommenders are busy people and cannot always pull off a last-minute

request. Give them at least a 2 week notice if possible.

Be sure to send the request from the submission portal early and

double-check with them that they received the email from the system –

sometimes the email goes into their spam folder, and it’s harder to find

when it’s the day before the deadline. Ask them to please confirm receipt

of the email within 24 hours of your sending it from the portal.

Send them a couple of polite reminders: if you’ve given them 2 weeks,

perhaps send a reminder at the one-week mark, and if they still haven’t

submitted the letter 3 days prior to the deadline (remember, you can check

their letter status on the submission portal), then send them one more

reminder.

Thank them for their recommendation as soon as you see their letter has

been submitted!

Graduate Fellowships FAQs

Do you have a specific research field requirement in EE, CE, or CS?

No. There are many ways that Engineering fields can touch NVIDIA, and we

are open to considering them.

 I am just starting my PhD this Fall. Am I eligible to apply?

You should have completed your first year of your PhD program at the time

of application. The requirement is not black and white, but the idea is

that after one year, there is a track record of research and experience.

With no Ph.D. experience, there is very little to judge the student’s

research on. So, it’s certainly fine to apply, but very unlikely to be

awarded. Of course, in special situations, there may be enough history to

make a compelling application. We suggest you look at the list of past

recipients and see whether your application is comparable. If so, then go

ahead and apply and see where your application falls in the review process

compared to all the other applications.

Do I need to have accepted publications?

Our prior fellowship recipients have had track records of multiple

publications in top-tier venues of their fields. To be competitive, you

should have at least one strong publication.

Is there a limit on how many Graduate Fellowship Awards one PhD student can

receive from NVIDIA?

No. At this time there is no limit on the number of times you can be

awarded the NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Award. Keep in mind you can only

receive one per year!

Is there a limit to the number of NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Awards granted

per University or per Research Team?

No. At this time, there is no limit per University nor is there a limit per

graduate team provided the research is different and interesting to NVIDIA.

I am a current Graduate Fellowship Recipient, can I apply again?

Yes. You can apply each year you are enrolled full-time until the year

before you complete your PhD. You can follow the same guidelines and

application process as any new applicant.

Are International PhD students eligible?

Yes. International students are eligible to apply. Keep in mind, the

Graduate Fellowship Award amount may vary by country, region or location.

Can I have more than one Professor Nomination Letter?

Yes, you can have up to three Professor Nomination Letters. It is OK to

have nomination letter(s) from non-professors, as long as you have one from

your thesis advisor/professor.

What if my professor/advisor doesn’t submit the Professor Nomination Letter?

We do require at least one Professor Nomination Letter from your thesis

advisor. Please be sure to add your recommendation contacts into the portal

early in the process so that your professor(s) have sufficient notice and

time to compose and upload their letter. Please remember it is the

student’s responsibility to ensure the professor nominations are turned in

on time, and following up with them prior to the deadline if they haven’t

uploaded their letter into the portal.

How are the Graduate Fellowship Recipients selected?

NVIDIA’s Graduate Fellowship Program has a committee of engineers headed by

our Chief Scientist, Bill Dally. The committee is comprised of over 60

senior technical staff and managers from research and development groups

across the company. This committee reviews all applicants competitively in

several review sessions. This is a very intensive process. The entire

review process usually takes about 8 weeks. Unfortunately, many qualified

candidates will not be selected due to the high quality of proposals and

limited number of awards available.

Can I work a part-time job during my Fellowship?

The goal of covering your stipend in full is to release you from the need

to work as a TA/RA or another outside job, and allow you to focus on your

research. However, we realize that sometimes part-time jobs provide a

benefit to the student other than money, and in those cases as long as the

work is beneficial to the progress of your PhD and a conflict of interest

does not exist between NVIDIA and the other entity, this would be

acceptable to NVIDIA. If there is any doubt on the conflict of interest,

please check with your NVIDIA Fellowship contact.

Subject: Flipkart GRiD Level 1 MCQ Test is live! | Flipkart GRiD 6.0 - Robotics Challenge
Body:
Flipkart GRiD 6.0 - Robotics Challenge

Hi Nayan Sharma,

We appreciate your participation in the Flipkart GRiD 6.0 - Robotics Challenge. As we approach the Level 1: MCQ Test, it's imperative to thoroughly review the essential instructions and guidelines provided below. 

To attempt the quiz:

  • Go to the Opportunity Page - Click Here
  • You will see a Verify/Play button in the Level 1: MCQ Test if you've registered to initiate the quiz.

Timelines & Instructions:

  • Online Assessment Window: 26th August 2024, 12:00 PM to 8:00 PM
  • Online Assessment Duration: 30 Minutes
  • Time Allotted per Question: 75 seconds
  • Total Questions to be answered: 24 multiple-choice questions based on E-Commerce trivia (Reference: https://stories.flipkart.com) and Tech (Technology Awareness + Techstack & Computer Science Fundamentals).
  • You can attempt the assessment anytime between the provided window.
  • Please ensure that you attempt the assessment in one sitting. Once you start, the timer will not stop. 
  • You will have to finish the assessment on or before 26 Aug 24, 08:00 PM IST. To get the complete assessment duration, you need to start the assessment latest by 26 Aug 24, 07:30 PM IST. Otherwise, you’ll get less time to complete the assessment.
  • Participants will be ranked on accuracy (score) and speed (time taken to answer the questions). This means that if two participants have the same score, then the one who answered their last question earlier will be ranked higher.
  • Each question will be timed and you are required to submit the answer to the questions before moving on to the next question. 
  • Your answers won't be auto-saved and you will have to submit answers individually. 
  • Please note that all team members must take the quiz and the average scores of all the members will be considered for shortlisting.
  • Your answers won't be auto-saved and you will have to submit answers individually. 
  • Please ensure that you have a stable internet connection of a minimum of 2 MBPS.
  • The preferred browser to take the quiz is Google Chrome.

Proctoring Related:

  • You can attempt the assessment only on a desktop/laptop with webcam access.
  • The assessment will be hosted in full-screen mode.
  • Anything that disturbs the full-screen mode of the assessment is treated as a violation. It may be due to any of the following reasons but not limited to:
    • Tab Switching
    • Screen Sharing with anyone
    • Clicking on the escape button
    • Computer going on Sleep (Adjust your power or sleep mode settings)
    • Windows or Browser or any Application specific notifications (Put them on DND Mode or switch them off while the assessment is on)
    • Anything else that may result in disturbing the full-screen mode
  • The assessment does not get terminated on the first such instance. Only repeated violations will result in disqualification and termination of the assessment immediately.
  • Your face will be verified before the start of the assessment from the photo that was captured during registration. 
  • Your face may be verified again during the assessment.
  • Your face will be constantly detected and violations will be tracked and reported while the assessment is on. Eg: Two faces in front of the camera, No one in front of the camera, etc.
  • You’ll have to share your screen during the assessment. 

Key Instructions:

  • You can access the assessment from the opportunity page. 
  • You will see a Verify/Play button in the MCQ Assessment round to initiate the assessment.
  • While you are taking the assessment, your answers and the time of their submission are also tracked by the system question-wise.
  • You will not be able to browse through the questions.
  • There is no negative marking for this assessment.
  • Any participant resorting to unfair practices will be directly disqualified from Flipkart GRiD 6.0
  • All decisions in the matter of eligibility, authenticity & final judgment will be with Unstop and Flipkart.

Reporting unfair practices

Please note, that any participant resorting to unfair practices will be directly disqualified from the challenge. In case any participant sees any unfair means, please email us the screenshot (maybe of social media groups) at support@unstop.com. Team ID and Email ID are displayed on the screen while taking the test. Any screenshot circulation of such a team will result in disqualification. 

All the Best!

Regards,
Flipkart Team

technology and management, showcasing how they shape our world for the

better.

only celebrate our engineering community's innovative spirit but also

provide a unique platform for learning and networking. Whether you are

seeking to expand your knowledge or connect with researchers and fellow

students in your field, Engineers Day promises to be an opportunity you

wouldn't want to miss!

We wholeheartedly encourage everyone to participate actively in the event.

Let’s come together as a community and celebrate the vital role that

International Day for the Remembrance of the Slave Trade and its Abolition

The International Day for the Remembrance of the Slave Trade and its

Abolition is observed on August 23 every year to memorialize the deplorable

practice of the transatlantic slave trade. The day, designated by UNESCO,

was first observed on August 23, 1998. The Slave trade was a common

practice during the imperialist regimes of European nations. People from

Africa and Asia were traded under this practice as slaves and transported

to colonial settlements such as Haiti, the Caribbean, and other parts of

the world. The international slave trade was abolished on March 25, 1807.

The theme for this year is “Fighting slavery's legacy of racism through

transformative education” The enslavement of over 13 million Africans

during the Transatlantic Slave Trade was driven by the racist ideology that

these women, men and children were inferior because of the colour of their

skin. Countless families were torn apart

liturgical language. The day was first celebrated in 1969 and comprises

various events that talk about the impact and importance of Sanskrit.

This Indo-Aryan language has been declared as a classical language that’s

identified for its scientific construction and is in excessive demand

languages in the world. Also, many languages find their roots in Sanskrit

Subject: VIT - Deakin University Australia : 2025 Research Internship Program
Body:
Dear Students,

We are delighted to announce that applications for the 2025 Research

Internship Program at Deakin University's Faculty of Science, Engineering,

and Built Environment (SEBE) are now open! This program offers an

exceptional opportunity for high-performing students from our esteemed

partner institutions to engage in cutting-edge research projects under the

guidance of experienced Deakin academic supervisors from January – June of

each year.

Program Highlights

 - Immersive Research Experience: In place of student’s final year

 research projects at VIT, students will join ongoing Deakin research

 projects across a range of disciplines, including Information Technology,

 Engineering, Life and Environmental Sciences, and Architecture and

 Construction Management.

 - Professional Growth: Participants will gain invaluable insights,

 develop essential professional skills, and experience life as an

 international student in Australia.

 - Collaborative Environment: Students will work alongside Deakin’s

 academic staff and peers, fostering intercultural collaboration and

 knowledge exchange.

 - Co-supervision: Selected students from your esteemed institution are

 required to nominate a co-supervisor from VIT who will ensure the alignment

 of the research project at Deakin to the academic needs of the VIT program.

 Co-supervision also allows us to connect researchers from our institutions

 for future peer-to-peer research collaborations.

 - No tuition fees: There are no tuition fees payable to Deakin as part

 of this program, however students are expected to cover all costs

 associated with travelling to Australia (flights, visa, insurance,

 accommodation, and meals etc.)

Application Process/Eligibility and Selection Criteria/Staff and Student

Expectations:

Please see information in the attached flyer.

The direct link to apply here:

https://deakindigital.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_bNQ8bn99a5qw01E

Key Dates:

 - Application Deadline: 25 August 2024 (Midnight AEST)

 - Interviews: September 2024

 - Outcomes and Offer Letters: late September/October

 - Internship Start: January 2025

For more details, please refer to the attached flyer, which includes

detailed information on the program, application deadlines,

student/co-supervisor expectations and accommodation information.

We are excited to welcome a new cohort of talented students to Deakin and

look forward to another successful year of the Research Internship Program.

Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us at

sebe-international@deakin.edu.au.

Dear Students,

The Office of Students' Welfare is committed to your overall well-being and

success. We understand that student life can be demanding, and you may face

challenges that can impact your academic performance, mental health or

personal life. We encourage you to reach out for help if you are facing any

difficulties. You don't have to go through these challenges alone.

We offer counselling services through our dedicated team of counsellors.

These services are designed to provide you with a safe and supportive space

to discuss any concerns you may have, including:

 -

Academic Stress 

 - Relationship Issues

 - Anxiety and Depression

 - Social Difficulties

 - Family Problems

 - Coping with Personal Loss

 - Adapting to University Life

Our counsellors are trained professionals who will listen to you without

judgment and offer guidance and support to help you navigate these

challenges. All counselling sessions are strictly confidential.

This service is also available to all Faculty and Staff.

Subject: Smart India Hackathon '24 (SIH'24)-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

We are happy to announce the conduct of Prelims for Smart India Hackathon

'24.

The Smart India Hackathon (SIH) is a nationwide initiative that provides

students with a platform to solve problems in daily life. The initiative is

led by the Government of India and aims to promote innovation and

out-of-the-box thinking among young minds. The SIH also aims to harness the

creativity and technical expertise of Indian students to benefit the

nation.

The SIH provides students with the opportunity to solve problems for

government departments, industries, and other organizations. The

participating teams tackle problem statements posted by departments of

Union Ministers and State governments. Themes for SIH'24 include:

 - Agriculture, FoodTech & Rural Development

 - Blockchain & Cybersecurity

 - Clean & Green Technology

 - Fitness & Sports

 - Heritage & Culture

 - MedTech/BioTech / Health Tech

 - Miscellaneous

 - Renewable / Sustainable Energy

 - Robotics and Drones

 - Smart Automation

 - Smart Vehicles

 - Travel & Tourism

 - Transportation & Logistics

 - Disaster Management

 - Smart Education

 - Toys & Games

 - Space Technology

 - Smart Resource Conservation

The SIH also aims to inculcate a culture of product innovation and a

mindset of problem solving.

The teams that are interested may fill out the form on or before 23/08/2024,

05:00 pm. Shortlisted teams will be called in for a presentation and

mentoring. We will be hosting prelim SIH internally to nominate the student

teams for SIH 24.

https://tinyurl.com/VIT-prelimSIH-24

Internal Hackathon:

To nominate the teams for Hackathon, we will have to conduct an Internal

Hackathon. So this form is created to collect your willingness to

participate.

Instructions:

https://policies.google.com/privacy?hl=en-IN

1.Team size should be 6 members with at least one female student included

mandatorily, else the team will be disqualified.

2. Adhere to the tracks/problem statement suggested by the organizers of

SIH, mentioned in the reference excel.

3. Internal Hackathon will be conducted and the winners will be nominated

to participate in SIH '24. Further details will be communicated to the

shortlisted teams.

4. All the members should be from VIT, Vellore.

5. Students from different branches are encouraged to form diverse teams.

6. This form will stop collecting the responses on 23/08/2024 (05:00 pm).

For More information: Dr. Naiju CD, SPOC, SIH '24

https://sih.gov.in/

#SmartIndiaHackathon#InnovationSeAtmanirbharBharat

Dear Students,

We are excited to invite you to World Entrepreneurship Day 2024, a

celebration of innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurial spirit!

Date: 21st August 2024Time: 9:30 AM - 6:30 PMVenue: Dr. M. Channa Reddy

Auditorium and Foodys 

This year's event promises to be an unforgettable experience, with:

- Inspiring keynote speakers and panel discussions

- Networking opportunities with fellow entrepreneurs and industry experts

- Showcase of innovative startups and projects

- Alumni entrepreneurs sharing their ventures and experiences

- Interactions with current students, faculties, and industry leaders

STUDENT STARTUPS | FACULTY STARTUPS | ALUMNI STARTUPS |

Join us to:

- Learn from successful entrepreneurs and industry leaders

- Connect with like-minded individuals and potential collaborators

- Get inspired to turn your ideas into reality

- Be part of a global movement celebrating entrepreneurship

- Be inspired by our successful and esteemed alumni as they return to their

alma mater to share their journeys and reflect on how the world has

transformed since they first stepped foot outside these hallowed halls.

We are honoured to announce that our Chief Guest for the event is Vish

Sahasranamam, Founder and CEO of Forge Innovation & Ventures, a renowned

entrepreneur and innovator, and our Guests of Honor are Nikunj Dang,

Founder and CEO of Yagnum, a leading expert in AI and machine learning, and

Ezhilmaran Arumugam, Director at Axis Global Automation, a seasoned

industry leader and innovator.

Mark your calendars for 21st August 2024 and get ready to be inspired!

Register for the Event: https://forms.gle/p9jjVCbUut3RbV3M9

Please contact our student coordinator, Sudarshan JR +91 9629010200, for

further details.

We look forward to seeing you there!

World Photo Day originates from the invention of the Daguerreotype, a

photographic process developed by Frenchmen Louis Daguerre and Joseph

Nicephore Niepce in 1837. On January 9, 1839, the French Academy of

Sciences announced the Daguerreotype process. On August 19, the French

government purchased the patent and announced the invention as a gift “free

to the world”.

The Daguerreotype wasn’t the first permanent photographic image. In 1826,

Niepce captured the earliest known permanent photograph known as “View from

the Window at Le Gras” using a process called heliography.

Subject: Avoiding any unpleasant interactions on campus - Reg.
Body:
Dear Students,

As we embark on another academic year, let us remember about our commitment

to creating a safe, inclusive, and respectful environment on campus. Ragging,

in any form, is strictly prohibited on our campus. It is a practice that

not only undermines the dignity of individuals but also disrupts the

harmony and camaraderie that we strive to foster. As you know, our

institution has a zero-tolerance policy towards ragging, and we ensure that

every student feels secure and respected.

Ragging includes any act of physical or mental abuse, bullying, harassment,

or any conduct by one student towards another that causes harm, fear, or

humiliation. Engaging in ragging can result in severe disciplinary action,

including suspension, expulsion, and legal consequences as per the law. We

have established a dedicated anti-ragging committee and helpline to support

and protect students.

If you or your friend is experiencing or witnessing ragging, please do not

hesitate to report it immediately. All reports will be handled with

confidentiality and sensitivity. Your cooperation and active participation

are essential in upholding our values and maintaining a safe and nurturing

atmosphere. Let us stand united against ragging and support each other in

creating a community where everyone can thrive without fear or intimidation.

Students from the Freshers Batch of 2024 are requested to inform/report any

unpleasant interactions/incidents that they face in campus, hostels or

outside the campus. Also, you are cautioned not to join any unofficial

whatsapp/telegram groups.

Seniors are also requested to not get involved in any such acts which may

invite severe disciplinary actions against them.

URGENT: Mandatory Psychometric Test (LitQ) for all 2026 Batch & 2027

Batch - Virtually

As part of understanding every student’s aspiration toward their student

progression, the CDC office will be conducting a

MANDATORY Psychometric Test for all students (All fall semester).

All the students might have received the mail from Litq. All are asked to

take the test on or before 15th August 2024 without fail. 

Please watch the below video before taking the test.

https://youtube.com/live/qhFKKivKt-w?feature=share

https://youtube.com/live/qhFKKivKt-w?feature=share

Please find the attached test not taken students list as on 14th August

2024. If you have already taken, please ignore.

Note: Now this test is conducted for the Academic year 2024-25.

The outcome of the Test: 

Effective work performance results from the right combination of knowledge

and skills, cognitive abilities, emotional intelligence, workplace

behavioural style (rooted in personality), alignment to work culture and

key work competencies. Knowing these personal success drivers will equip

you with the understanding of what makes you unique, what your strengths

are, and what areas of development will help you in launching a successful

and rewarding career. The litq.io smart assessment The litq.io smart

assessment is

a scientifically designed immersive game that takes roughly 30 minutes to

complete. Designed by experts with over 50 years of experience in assessing

and aligning human potential, the Litq assessment stitches together a

series of game-based work simulations with situational judgment scenarios

and cognitive games to provide useful insights into work potential.

Instructions:

 - To get started, open an incognito mode in the Chrome browser

 - Sign up at: https://litq.io/signup

 - Input the promo code exactly as given, including the hyphen, with no

 spaces

 - Refer to the instructions beside the password icon to set the password

 in the right format

 - Input the first and last name without gaps. If a middle name exists,

 it can be included with the first or last name without spaces.

 - Email address used for signing up should also remain unchanged.

 - College name is pre-filled and should remain unchanged.

 - Provide accurate details, including official email ID, roll number,

 and current educational information (e.g., Masters, M.Sc. Chemistry).

Partition Horror Remembrance Day

Partition Horrors Remembrance Day remembers the sufferings of many Indians

during the partition. Several families were displaced and many lost their

lives in the partition. It aims to remind Indians the need to remove social

divisions, disharmony and to further strengthen the spirit of oneness,

social harmony and human empowerment. The partition had left 10 to 20

million people displaced and left 2 hundred thousand to 2 million dead.
