Subject: Discover Design Thinking - Call for Design Contest
Body:
Dear VITians,

We're thrilled to announce a Design contest sponsored by Microchip as a

part of VDAT-2024 hosted by Vellore Institute of Technology, Vellore.

The objective of this contest is to provide a platform for students and

research scholars to showcase innovative hardware and software solutions to

real-world problems. Whether it's enhancing efficiency, promoting

sustainability, improving accessibility, or addressing societal challenges,

we want to see your creative ideas come to life.

We are calling all talented designers to participate and showcase their

creativity and skills. The winner of the contest will have the opportunity

to work with us on a special project and will receive a cash prize.

We believe that this contest is a great opportunity for designers to

showcase their talents and gain recognition for their work. We hope that

you will consider participating in the contest and look forward to

receiving your submissions.

Idea Submission

 - Your idea submission should cover a description of the idea along with

 a block diagram of your idea

 - Benefits and value addition of your solution, example application

 scenarios.

 - Your team description along with your contact information with mailing

 address.

 - Faculty can be part, but lead author should be student. Presenter in

 the conference has to be student.

Steps for submission

 - 1. Use the design contest submission template provided. TEMPLATE

 https://vit.ac.in/vdat2024/Design-Contest-Submission-Template.docx

 - 2. Fill in all required details with a minimum font size: 10 pt, Times

 New Roman font. Max two pages including tables, diagrams, and references

 (if any).

 - 3. Submit a PDF version using the CMT portal. SUBMIT HERE

 https://cmt3.research.microsoft.com/User/Login?ReturnUrl=%2FVDAT2024

Eligibility

 - Participants should be full-time undergraduate/postgraduate/Phd.

 students from a reputed institute.

For more details, please visit the conference website:

https://vit.ac.in/vdat2024/design-contest.html

Body:
Dear VIT Students,

Finlatics is pleased to extend applications for the Finlatics Machine Learning program, an online live project that helps students learn and gain experience in using machine learning algorithms.

Along with the Vellore Institute of Technology, this project is running at leading campuses, including IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIT Delhi, and BITS Pilani, among others.

It was curated at the prestigious Atal Incubation Centre, supported by the Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog, and the Government of India.

STRUCTURE of the live project:

1. Learn the core concepts around Machine Learning algorithms

2. Become proficient in using the Google Collab Notebook for machine learning

3. Engage in data preprocessing - a critical activity to prepare data sets for building machine learning algorithms

4. Gain an understanding of supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms using Python libraries

5. Complete an industry-specific case project to understand the application of Machine Learning in business scenarios

The project is doable along with any other commitment due to its work-from-home and online structure.

Student OUTCOMES:

1. Certificate of Proficiency in Machine Learning

2. Letter of Recommendation on performance

To apply, students can fill out the form below, and we will get in touch with them:

https://www.finlatics.com/ml_application?src=vitv

Please note that no prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to participate in the program. The program will impart all necessary training on Python and machine learning techniques.

Project Duration: 1 month / 2 months (on student choice)

Project Start: Flexible on selected student choice. Students can choose to start the project post-exams to balance the project along with any upcoming exams, assignments, or personal commitments.

Project Break & Extension: Selected students will be eligible for a break during the project if needed for any exams, assignments, or personal commitments. They can also take an extension in duration if they cannot complete it in the given time.

If selected, the program has a minimal induction fee of Rs. 1999 + GST.

Fee Waiver: A 15% fee waiver shall be given to all Vellore Institute of Technology students on the abovementioned minimal induction fee. This waiver will reduce the fee to Rs. 1690 + GST.

To be eligible for the waiver, kindly apply through the link above.

We are excited to have a fruitful engagement.

Subject: Live Project in Equity Markets, Futures & Options
Body:
Dear VIT students,

We're pleased to open applications for the Finlatics Equity & Derivative Markets Experience Program, an online Live Project that helps students gain work experience in equity markets and futures & options at the Vellore Institute of Technology.

The project is running at leading campuses, including IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Madras and BITS Pilani among others, and was curated at the prestigious Atal Incubation Centre, supported by the Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog & Government of India.

STRUCTURE :

Equity Markets

1. Equity trading, research, and analysis based project.

2. Create, manage and maintain a real-time simulated portfolio on BSE 500 listed companies.

3. The simulated portfolio will be assessed by linking it to the real-time BSE 500 INDEX, akin to an asset management company.

4. Engage in sector-wise and company-specific research on the Indian Economy.

5. Learn and apply Fundamental & Technical Analysis to companies.

Futures & Options (Derivative Markets)

1. Learn and understand derivatives and instruments like forwards, futures, and options

2. Understand how derivative instruments like futures & options are traded

3. Gain insights into the valuation models of futures & options

4. Develop an understanding of various option trading strategies

The project is doable along with any other commitment due to its work from home, and online structure.

Student OUTCOMES:

1. Certificate of Work Experience in:

a. Equity Markets as an Equity Markets Analyst

b. Futures & Options as a Derivative Markets Analyst

2. Letter of Recommendation on performance

To apply, students can fill out the form below and we will get in touch with them:

https://forms.gle/qwFUpvfjYEe73K7v8

All students must note that no prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to be a part of this project. Personalized guidance and mentoring and live sessions would be provided on equity markets and futures & options to train students during the project .

Project Duration: 2 months

Project Start: Flexible on selected student choice. To balance the project along with any upcoming exams, assignments, or personal commitments, selected students can choose to start it once they are completed.

Project Break & Extension: Selected students will be eligible for a break during the project if they need it for any exams, assignments, or personal commitments. They can also take an extension in duration if they cannot complete it.

Incentives: up to Rs. 6000 (to monthly top-performing students)

If selected, the project has a minimal induction fee: Rs. 2999 + GST / Rs. 3999 + GST (on student choice)

Fee Waiver: A fee waiver of 25% shall be given to all Vellore Institute of Technology students on the abovementioned minimal induction fee. This will reduce the fee to Rs. 2199 + GST / Rs. 3049 + GST.

To be eligible for the waiver, kindly apply via the above-mentioned link only.

We are looking forward to a fruitful engagement.

Dear VIT Student,

Congratulations on being shortlisted for the Internship Program!

As mentioned above, Teachnook in collaboration with IBM & IIT ROORKEE is

organizing a 2 Month Training + Internship program designed by IBM.

Interested students fill out the form, if you get shortlisted you will get

a call from our HR Team;

APPLY HERE: https://forms.gle/dd9UA7bGq4orjCut6

https://forms.gle/dd9UA7bGq4orjCut6

Join Our Official WhatsApp Group For More Information;

https://chat.whatsapp.com/LREQ7ZCB1MNJSpaUAYci6m

https://chat.whatsapp.com/LREQ7ZCB1MNJSpaUAYci6m

Top Preferred Courses: 

✅

Artificial Intelligence.✅ Data Science.✅ Data Analytics.✅ Cyber Security.

✅ Full Stack Web Development.

Here is an outline of the program's structure.

First month: During the program's first month, IBM training will be

conducted in the form of live lectures, and you will have live mentorship

from industry professionals. You will have access to the IBM Portal, where

you can interact with the trainers and fellow students. Login credentials

will be provided to registered students.

Second month: Internship with live mentorship for projects from

professionals. The LIVE INDUSTRY PROJECT will give students an experience

in solving real-world problems.

10+ Minor Project: The minor project is an individual project,

Where students will be doing projects on each topic they will be learning.

Major Project (CAPSTONE): The major project is a group project, and you

will work in a group of 3-4 interns, with specific responsibilities

assigned to each intern. The company will provide you with all the required

data and materials for the project.

Third month: Based on your performance during the program's first two

months, we will conduct a technical interview in the same company during

the third month. You will be offered a stipend-based Internship if you

perform well in the interview.

After Completion of the program, the student shall receive a :

✅

Program completion certificate issued by IBM.✅ Co-Branded Internship

certificate.

✅ Letter of Recommendation from IBM.

✅ Access to a growth community.

Body:
Greetings from Kuppismart Solutions Pvt Ltd

Dear Students,

Are you looking to gain hands-on industry experience and enhance your

skills this summer? KuppiSmart Solutions Pvt Ltd is excited to announce

internship opportunities tailored for students pursuing bachelor's degrees

in various disciplines. Whether you're passionate about hardware

engineering, website development, app development, market research, machine

learning, design, 3D designing, Printing, or content writing, we have roles

suited to your interests and expertise.

Internship Roles:

1. Hardware Engineer Internship: Suitable for EEE and EC students

proficient in soldering, PCB designing, microcontroller programming,

embedded programming, MATLAB, circuit designing, and industrial wiring.

2. Website Development Internship: Ideal for students with skills in

React J.S., software development, frontend, and backend development.

3. App Development Internship: Perfect for those interested in mobile app

development.

4. Market Research, Survey, and Strategy Planning Internship: Open to MBA

students with a knack for market analysis and strategic planning.

5. ML and AI Development Internship: Suited for students passionate about

machine learning and artificial intelligence.

6. Designer Internship: Requires proficiency in design software like

Canva for creating posters and other visual content.

7. Content Writing Internship: For students with strong writing skills

and a passion for creating engaging content, particularly in the form of

blogs.

8. 3D designing and Printing: Requires proficiency in 3D printing &

design, CAD

Duration: Starts from June 1st. The internship will span 45 days with

no stipend provided during the probation period. If performance is

exceptional, the opportunity for an internship role with a stipend will be

considered

Perks:

- Certificate of Completion

- Hands-On Experience

- Development of Industry-Level Skills with the guidance of industrial

experts

- Enhancement of Your Resume

- Letter of Recommendation (for selected candidates)

- Flexible Work Hours

- Industrial Internship Academic Credits (Only for VIT students)

Location: The internship will be available both online and offline in

Hyderabad. Preference will be given to students willing to work offline.

Apply here:- https://forms.gle/uWVU5QGcAnMHWMdq9

If you're ready to dive into the world of industry and gain valuable

experience that will propel your career forward, we encourage you to apply

for our summer industrial internships at KuppiSmart Solutions Pvt Ltd.

We look forward to welcoming motivated and enthusiastic students to our

team for an enriching and rewarding internship experience.

Best regards,Akhil Reddy K.CEO.KuppiSmart Solutions Pvt Ltd.8688484493

Subject: IET India Scholarship Award 2024 - Reg.
Body:
Dear Students,

The Institution of Engineering and Technology (The IET) is one of the

world’s largest professional societies for engineers, headquartered in the

UK, with over 154,000 members in 148 countries. The India chapter of the

IET started operations in India in 2006, from Bengaluru and works closely

with industry, academia, and government towards its global mission, and

conducts wide-ranging activities that focus on areas such as Future

technologies, the Future of Mobility, and Transport, as well as the Future

of Work.

The IET India Scholarship Award recognises and nurtures future engineering

leaders of India. The 8th edition of the IET India Scholarship Award is

accepting applications now.

IET India Scholarship past winners have secured positions at top firms

like Google,

Apple, and NASA!

Eligibility Guidelines:

 - Any first, second, third and fourth year full time regular UG

 Engineering student from an AICTE/UGC approved institution. (Open to

 students across all engineering branches as recognised by the AICTE/UGC.)

 - All regular credit courses must have been cleared in a single attempt

 by the applicant.

 - UG marks should be at least 60% in aggregate for the semesters cleared

 so far or corresponding to CGPA of at least 6.0 in a 10 point scale

 - There is no age limit for the applicant.

 - Application is open to IET members, as well as non-members.

 - Students from AICTE/UGC approved Institutions and national institutes

 are eligible to apply for scholarships.

 - If you are a student member of the IET, you get a 15% additional

 weightage boost in your application.

For more Information, visit IET scholarship website

https://email.ietinfo.org/c/1ahhXcUSYBokJ3dldbhmEpmQePq.

Last Date for Application: 31st May 2024.

Body:
Dear Students,

Greetings!

Are you a leader who wants to make a change?

The Office of Students' Welfare is currently seeking nominations for the

2024-2025 academic year.

The Student Council is a diverse group of students from across all

departments, working to represent the needs and aspirations of the entire

student body. If you're passionate about making VIT an even better place,

we encourage you to nominate yourself!

For more information on the nomination process and the role of the Student

Council, please visit the following links.

Google Form Links:

Executive & Member Secretary: https://forms.gle/PYkToeGdRDhT7QNc7

Secretary (Cultural & Technical): https://forms.gle/GME7hxTswz2kLdR57

Digital Support Team: https://forms.gle/Pc683RoM7NVvezET9

The link will be available only till 18.05.2024 (Saturday), 5:00 PM and

deactivated afterwards.

The applications received only through the google form will be scrutinized

and called for an interview.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA:

1. Only Final and Pre Final Year Students shall apply for the post of Executive

and Member Secretary.

2. Final Year Students to act as Executive Member and Pre Final Year

Students to act as Member Secretary.

3.

Executive & Member Secretary:

 - For all 5 Year Programmes (B. Arch. and Integrated Programmes), only

 2020 and 2021 Year Students to be considered eligible for the posts of

 Executive Member & Member Secretary respectively.

 - For all 4 Year Programmes (B. Tech., B. Des. & B. Sc. Hons.), only

 2021and 2022 Year Students to be considered eligible for the posts of

 Executive Member & Member Secretary respectively.

 - For all 3 Year Programmes (B.B.A., B.Com. & B.Sc.), only 2022 and 2023

 Year Students to be considered eligible for the posts of Executive

 Member & Member Secretary respectively.

 - For all 2 Year Programmes (M. Tech. & M.Sc.), only 2023 Year Students

 to be considered eligible for the posts of Executive Member.

4. Students from all years are eligible to apply for the post of Secretary

(Cultural & Technical) and Digital Support Team Member.

5. Minimum of 9 CGPA required for a student to be eligible for the post of

Student Council Member.

6. Minimum of 8.5 CGPA required for a student to be eligible for the post

of Secretary (Cultural & Technical).

7. Minimum of 7.5 CGPA required for a student to be eligible for the post

of Digital Support Team Member.

8. Students involved in any disciplinary issues, currently or in the past,

are not eligible for holding any post.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF STUDENT COUNCIL MEMBERS:

· To officially represent all the students in the school / institute.

· To identify and help solve problems encountered by students in the

school / institute.

· To communicate its opinion to the school / institute administration on

any subject that concerns students.

· To promote and encourage the involvement of students in organizing

school / institute level activities.

· To inform students about any subject that concerns them.

· To consult students on any issue of importance and bring it to the

notice of the Students' Welfare office.

· To support and contribute to achieve better / higher accreditation for

the institute.

· To participate in the development of the school activities.

· To propose activities to the school/institute administration that would

improve the quality of student life in the school/institute.

We look forward to receiving your nominations!

Body:
28th International Symposium on VLSI Design and Test (VDAT) 2024

September 1-3, 2024

Vellore, Tamil Nadu, India

https://vit.ac.in/vdat2024/ https://vit.ac.in/vdat2024/

Paper submission Deadline

15th May 2024

Tutorial proposal submission

Conference Dates

1st to 3rd September 2024

Dear VITians,

Greetings!

We are excited to present our upcoming flagship event from the VLSI Society

of India, the 28th International Symposium on VLSI Design and Test

(VDAT-2024), scheduled to be held from 1st to 3rd September 2024 at Vellore

Institute of Technology (VIT), Vellore, Tamil Nadu, India.

VDAT-2024 is one of the flagship annual events of the VLSI Society of

India. VDAT 2024 is technically co-sponsored by the IEEE Madras Section,

IEEE Circuits and Systems Madras Section, and IEEE Computer Society Madras

Section.

This event features Keynotes, invited talks, Tutorials, Hands-on workshops,

Panel Discussions, a Design Contest, Technical paper presentations, a VLSI

Career guidance forum, Exhibits from industries etc.

 Call for Papers

Authors are invited to submit original, unpublished research manuscripts on

the following tracks. Papers should be submitted in PDF format (Portable

Document Format) as per the IEEE Conference paper format.

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1PV9pB7lXrIEEt7eofo68WP66b4Tqk0Yb/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104323223968587299792&rtpof=true&sd=true

 The detailed guidelines for paper submissions can be found on the

conference website.

TRACKS

· Emerging Devices and Material Technologies

· VLSI Circuit and System Design

· CAD for VLSI

· Testing and Verification

· Embedded Systems Design

· Emerging Processors for System Design

 All the full-length papers presented at the conference will be submitted

to IEEE Xplore Digital Library (awaiting for approval) subject to meeting

the quality requirement of IEEE.

Paper submission Link: https://cmt3.research.microsoft.com/VDAT2024

Design Contest

Objective of this Design contest to provide a platform for the UG/PG/Ph.D

students to showcase innovative hardware and software solutions to

real-world problems.

Track 1: Hardware Platform: Smart, Connected, and Secure Systems for a

Sustainable Society

Track 2: Optimized AI Face Detection on SAMA5D27 WLSOM1-EK

Track 3: FocusFlow: A Wearable to Manage Student Stress and Attention

Track -4: Smart, Connected, and Secure Systems for a Sustainable Society.

· Last Date for submission of Idea: 15th May 2024

· Experts from the Microchip team will guide and mentor during the

time of implementation.

· Following the first round of screening, shortlisted teams will

convert their ideas into applications/solutions.

· Hardware kits will be shipped to the selected teams by Microchip.

PhD Thesis forum

To promote and encourage young researchers in the domain of VLSI Design and

Embedded Systems, a PhD Thesis Forum will be organized during the

conference. This forum is a great opportunity for PhD students who have

completed their respective thesis within the last 12 months or who are

close to completing their thesis to present their work to a broad audience.

This forum will help students interact with pioneers in their research

domain and get valuable feedback on their work. The forum may also help

students to establish contacts for entering the job market. Entries from

eligible young researchers across India are invited for the PhD Research

Forum.

Tutorials

Tutorials are an integral and important part of all the editions of VDAT,

where instructors have the opportunity to share their expertise on a

specific field/research with fellow researchers and those who wish to

discover said field/research. We are soliciting proposals for topics of

academic and industrial applications interests. These topics may be

established or it may be emerging – and with profound and/or new insights

thereto, that is best articulated by means of an oral presentation.

Please note this year we will have the tutorial session in offline mode

which includes short tutorials, half-day tutorials, full day tutorials, and

Hands-on Tutorials.

We look forward to your active participation and presence at VIT, Vellore

for VDAT-2024 in September 2024.

Body:
Dear VITians,

“March is like a mischievous child. It startles, delights and vexes—all in

the same day—then, suddenly, with a sunny smile, it declares total

innocence.” - Peggy Toney Horton, Sunshine Hollow

March was a month packed with exciting events and opportunities for

learning, celebration, and community engagement like Quality Week Events,

Blood Donation Camp, Holi Celebrations, International Women's Day,

International Happiness Day and the much awaited, YANTRA'24!

International Women's Day was celebrated to acknowledge the invaluable

contributions of women across diverse fields. The Chief Guest for the

event, Ms. Pallavi Shastri, Vice President & Head HR, Bosch Limited, Bosch

India, passionately advocated for empowering women in entrepreneurial and

leadership roles, emphasizing their pivotal role in driving progress and

fostering inclusivity in society and the workplace.

As part of Viksit Bharat, Prime Minister, Mr. Narendra Modi's live address,

from the 'India’s Techade: Chips for Viksit Bharat' event, electrified VIT

Vellore's campus with anticipation and fervor with a participation of over

120 students.

The Youth Red Cross Association organised a Blood Donation Camp on 14th

March, 2024, fostering a culture of social responsibility and voluntarism,

the event stood as a beacon of hope and solidarity within the community.

Drawing an overwhelming response from donors and volunteers alike, the camp

epitomized the spirit of altruism and collective action.

International Women's Day was celebrated with various activities like the

Happiness Wall, Speaker Session and fun activities like tic-tac-toe,

balloon bursting, and limbo, emphasizing on the importance of happiness in

daily life.

University Day and Annual Sports Day 2024, held on March 27 at the Anna

Auditorium, celebrated student achievements in academics, sports, and

extracurricular activities. Prof. T G Sitharam, Chairman of AICTE, was the

Chief Guest. Our Honourable Chancellor, Dr. G Viswanathan highlighted VIT's

success as a top-ranking engineering institute, emphasizing its commitment

to excellence and innovation. Prof. Sitharam encouraged students to

cultivate ambition through effective upskilling and continuous learning.

Quality Week at VIT was a celebration of talent, creativity, and

intellectual exploration. Various clubs came together to host a series of

engaging events, each leaving a distinct impression on participants and

attendees.

Yantra hosted various events which kept the students active throughout the

week. Renowned external speakers graced our campus, delivering talks and

workshops that delve into cutting-edge technologies, industry trends, and

the transformative power of innovation. This year’s Yantra was focusing on

Sustainable Development Goals. From robotics showcases to AI workshops,

Yantra offered a diverse array of activities that cater to every tech

enthusiast's curiosity and passion.

To read about more such events and activities, check out our newsletter!

Coal Miners’ Day

Coal Miners’ Day is celebrated on May 4 to recognize the hard work of some

of the great unsung heroes of the Industrial Revolution. Coal miners spend

most of their days digging, tunneling, and extracting coal from the mines.

They dig deep into the Earth to bring out the riches that help to sustain

our life. Coal mining is one of the toughest professions. The day is

celebrated to show appreciation for the coal miners and honour their

accomplishments.

The coal miners have been working for centuries, however, they became

significantly important during the Industrial revolution between 1760 and

1840 when coal was used on a large scale to fuel stationary and locomotive

engines and heat buildings. Coal is a natural resource that accelerates

both economic and social development. In India, coal mining began in the

year 1774 when John Summer and Suetonius Grant Heatly of the East India

Company started commercial exploration in the Raniganj Coalfield along the

western banks of the Damodar river.

Subject: INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS APPEARING FOR WINTER 2023-24 THEORY FAT
Body:
Dear Students 

Please read the following instructions carefully:

INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS APPEARING FOR WINTER

 2023-24 THEORY FAT

Students appearing for FAT Exams, please READ INSTRUCTIONS CAREFULLY TILL

the END.

1. As per new regulations, the students must enter the examination hall

15-30 Minutes before the commencement of examination (between 9.00 - 9.15

AM for FN Session). Students reporting beyond the specified entry time will

not be permitted to enter the examination hall. 

2. Possession of any Electronic Gadget (Mobile Phone, Smart Watch,

Bluetooth device, any device embedded with scanner /camera, etc.), holding

chit papers/ suspicious content in the examination hall is considered as

malpractice.

3. Students are not permitted to take the following materials inside the

exam halls: chit papers, mobile phones, ear buds, the lid of the

calculator, chit materials, a reference table that contains markings,

written content using pencil or pen, nano ear phones, electronic devices,

blue tooth devices/displays, mobile phones without SIM cards,

non-transparent pouches, microxeroxes, or any other irrelevant material to

the exams. Possession itself and/or its use of any of the above is

considered examination malpractice.

4. Malpractice rules are published in the student VTOP login; you are

required to go through them, and you are requested not to indulge in any

examination malpractices.

3. Based on the requirements, Frisking will be done prior to entering the

examination hall and during the examination. You may be required to do

self-frisking before entering into examination hall. Also two to five

minutes are permitted to do the same inside the exam hall before collecting

question paper and answer booklet.

4. If a student leaves the exam hall before 12.00 noon, he/she has to

submit the question paper along with answer sheet. 

5. On the day of exam, keep your bags in front of exam room, DONOT TAKE

NOTE BOOKS / BOOKS / BAGS TO EXAM DESKS

General Instructions

· You need to WEAR Student IDENTITY CARD during the ENTIRE EXAMINATION

PERIOD. If you don’t have a Proper ID Card contact Registrar Office and

apply for a new one and get it before coming to the Exam. The ID card

should be scratches free with proper tag. Exchange of ID cards or Tags will

be considered as Malpractice. If you have misplaced your ID card or forgot

to bring it to the Examination Hall, Report to the Control Room of your

test venue to get One Time Permit Slips. You need to pay Rs. 100 through

V-TOP online payment only.

· You will NOT be permitted to use toilet/washroom during the

examination, so be prepared for it.

· Exchange of Calculators, Stationaries, Code Books, pen, pencil etc.,

are not permitted. The code Books or standard tables should have been

signed by either by the faculty or School office. No markings of any kind

should be found in such booklets.

· As per VIT rules, even if you keep mobile phone/smart watch in a

switched off position inside the examination hall, it will be treated as

examination malpractice. Such malpractices will lead to confiscation of the

devices (including SIM card) for one semester and ’N’ grade (ALL PAPER

ZERO) in all the registered courses including lab & project components in

that semester. Hence, before entering the examination hall, students should

check their pockets thoroughly to avoid carrying mobile phone/smart watch

by mistake.

A. Pre-Exam Activities

1.

Note down your seating arrangement (Building, Room Number and Seat Number)

from the V-TOP students login. Seating arrangement will not be displayed

for courses in which a student has been debarred. Please report yourself

half an hour prior to exam. No student would be permitted to enter the hall

after 9.15 AM.

2.

Possession of un-authorised material, even if you do not intend to use it

will be considered as malpractice. Before starting the exam, check any

materials written on desks or walls, or found papers nearby/ around you in

the floor and inform the same to the invigilators.

B. During the exam

1.

Candidate has to sit in the allotted seat only. Listen to the invigilator

and follow their instructions at all times. Strict Silence should be

maintained in the examination hall. Discussions/ communications of any kind

inside exam hall are treated as examination malpractices.

2.

Check the class number in the Question paper with the Attendance sheet

Class Number. If you have not received the right question paper or

incomplete or badly printed, please contact the invigilator immediately. If

you have any doubt on class number, course name, course code, slot, and any

other details related to your question paper, please check while signing in

the attendance sheet.

3.

Read carefully and follow the instructions printed in the question paper

and in the answer booklet.

4.

Fill required details (Register No., course code, course title etc.) in the

answer booklet before you start writing the exam. After signing in the

Dear VITian's,

With immense pleasure, we extend our heartfelt congratulations to all the

winners of Yantra 2024.

The fourth edition Yantra-the weeklong technical innovation, which took

place from 18th to 24th March, 2024 and Central hack in the Month of April.

This year's Yantra featured an unprecedented lineup of 60 diverse events

designed and aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals of UN to

inspire, educate, and challenge participants from all walks of life with;

 - 20 exciting hackathons

 - 18 dynamic workshops

 - 14 exciting tech competitions

 - 8 tech talks

We are thrilled to announce the outstanding achievers across our 60 events,

including hackathons, workshops, tech competitions, and tech talks, after

a week full of intense competition, innovation, and teamwork. The

participants' talent, creative thinking, and problem-solving skills were

truly impressive. Every winner has exhibited remarkable abilities,

imagination, and dedication, genuinely capturing the essence of Yantra.

As we celebrate the winners of Yantra 2024, we also celebrate the spirit of

innovation, collaboration, and lifelong learning that defines our

community. We look forward to witnessing your continued growth and success

in the exciting journey ahead.

Central Hack Attracted 750+ Students.

123 teams participated in Rounds 1 and 2.

The competition heated up as only 25 teams advanced to Round 3.

In a final push, 15 teams made it to the final pitching round.

This high participation with 750+ students highlights the thriving Central

Hack community. The sizable prize money of Rs. 5 lakh promised a rewarding

experience for the winners.

getting an Overall Prize money Rs. 1014000/-

(Ten Lakh Fourteen Thousand only)

Yantra 2024 provided a one-of-a-kind platform for learning, networking, and

exploring cutting-edge technology.

Once again, congratulations to all the winners! Your triumphs inspire us

all and reaffirm the limitless possibilities that technology offers.

Dear VITian's,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [26th April]

events.

World Intellectual Property Day

World Intellectual Property Day is observed annually on 26 April. The event

was established by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) in

2000 to "raise awareness of how patents, copyright, trademarks and designs

impact on daily life" and "to celebrate creativity, and the contribution

made by creators and innovators to the development of societies across the

globe". 26 April was chosen as the date for World Intellectual Property Day

because it coincides with the date on which the Convention Establishing the

World Intellectual Property Organization entered into force in 1970. World

Intellectual Property Day 2021 shines a light on the critical role of

small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the economy and how they can

use intellectual property (IP) rights to build stronger, more competitive,

and resilient businesses.

International Chernobyl Disaster Remembrance Day

The United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution designating 26

April as International Chernobyl Disaster Remembrance Day. In its

resolution, the General Assembly recognized that three decades after the

disaster there remain persistent serious long-term consequences and that

the affected communities and territories are experiencing continuing

related needs.

Based on the official reports, nearly 8,400,000 people in Belarus, Russia,

and Ukraine were exposed to radiation, which is more than the population of

Austria. About 155,000 sq. km of territories in the three countries were

contaminated, which is almost half of the total territory of Italy.

Agricultural areas covering nearly 52,000 sq. km, which is more than the

size of Denmark, were contaminated with cesium-137 and strontium-90, with

30-year and 28-year half-lives respectively. Nearly 404,000 people were

resettled, but millions continued to live in an environment where continued

residual exposure created a range of adverse effects.

Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [24th April

] events.

International Day of Multilateralism and Diplomacy for PeaceWorld peace

has been a topic of conversation and concern ever since the end of the

First World War in 1918. A need to foster peace on a global level became a

priority for every nation, and establishing an organization that would

cater to that responsibility was the first plan of action.

The League of Nations was the first intergovernmental organization tasked

with the mission of world peace. It was founded after World War I by the

Paris Peace Conference. After 26 years, the league was dissolved due to it

not being able to hold off aggressions from the Axis Powers during World

War II. Multilateralism is the concept in which the U.N. was established.

Simply put, multilateralism is the union or alliance of multiple countries

toward a common goal. It is anti-unilateralism, meaning even the smallest

powers are given a voice in global matters. The U.N. has become the most

visible symbol for multilateralism, and the foundation for the creation of

other multilateralism efforts such as the World Health Organization, the

World Bank, the World Trade Organization, and even the North Atlantic

Treaty Organization (NATO).

National Panchayati Raj Day

The Panchayati Raj Day, recognized annually by the Ministry of Panchayati

Raj on 24th April, commemorates the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 of the

Constitution coming into effect in the year 1993. This day celebrates the

national local self-governance and democratic decentralization. The

Ministry of Panchayati Raj, the nodal ministry, works on the mission of

empowerment, enablement and accountability of Panchayati Raj Institutions

to ensure inclusive development with social justice and efficient delivery

of services.

A strengthened local self-government would strengthen the commitment of

rural India towards self- reliance promoting social, economic and cultural

change transforming the lives of our rural population. This year, 2022, the

Subject: Reliance Foundation Undergraduate Scholarships - Reg.
Body:
Dear Students,

The Reliance Foundation Undergraduate Scholarships aim to support up to

5,000 meritorious students based on a merit-cum-means criteria for their

undergraduate college education, empowering them to continue their studies

without financial burden. The Scholarships aim to enable students to become

successful professionals and realize their dreams, unlocking their

potential to lift themselves and their communities up and contributing

towards India’s future socio-economic development.

Students with a household income of under Rs. 15 lakh who are enrolled in

the first year of their undergraduate studies pursuing any subject stream

can apply. The programme will also aim to encourage applications by girls

and specially-abled students. Selected scholars will receive a scholarship

of up to 2 lakhs over the duration of their degree programme. In addition

to the scholarship grant, the Reliance Foundation Undergraduate

Scholarships will provide scholars an opportunity to be part of a vibrant

alumni network and an enabling support system that will create long-term

impact on their lives and career trajectories.

Scholarships Features:

 - Support meritorious students from all corners of the country with an

 undergraduate college education

 - For first year students studying any stream of their choice

 - Awarded on a merit-cum-means basis to meritorious students

 - Up to 5,000 undergraduate scholars will be selected

 - The total amount of scholarship available over the duration of the

 degree programme, will be up to Rs/INR 2 Lakhs

 - Scholarship will go beyond financial support, with students

 automatically gaining networking opportunities through a strong alumni

 network

Eligibility Criteria: You must fulfil the following eligibility criteria

in order to apply.

 - Be a resident Indian citizen

 - Passed Standard 12th with minimum 60%

 - Currently enrolled in 1st year regular full-time degree course in any

 stream

 - Students having HouseHold income < Rs. 15 Lakhs (preference given to <

 Rs. 2.5 Lakhs)

 - Aptitude Test is mandatory

Following students are not eligible:

 - Students who are in the 2nd year or higher

 - Students pursuing their degree through online, remote, distance or any

 other non-regular modes

 - Students who have passed diploma after std. 10th

 - Students pursuing 2 year undergraduate degree courses

 - Students who do not answer the mandatory aptitude test or are found

 cheating during the test

To Apply, click on: https://shorturl.at/crxN5 https://shorturl.at/crxN5

For any additional questions, please text “hi” on WhatsApp to 7977 100 100

Subject: Hearty Congratulations to our Honorable Chancellor Sir from all VITians
Body:
Dear VITians,

I am greatly pleased to extend our warmest congratulations to our beloved

and Honorable Chancellor who will receive the State University of New York

(SUNY) honorary Doctor of Laws degree on May 10 during Binghamton

University’s Commencement ceremony for the Thomas J. Watson College of

Engineering and Applied Science.

Receiving this honorary doctorate is a well-deserved acknowledgment of our

Honorable Chancellor’s outstanding contributions and it is a testament to

his relentless pursuit of excellence, our founder’s exceptional dedication

to educational administration, for the cause of higher education in India,

his thriving visionary leadership in international higher education, and his

humanitarian efforts and entrepreneurship. This will be the second Honorary

Doctorate conferred on our Chancellor Sir, after the previous honor from

West Virginia University in 2009. As he receives this well-deserved honor,

it also signifies the immense potential for future endeavors with his

passion and vision continuing to shape the landscape of higher education.

Binghamton University's President, Prof. Harvey Stenger, commended

Chancellor Sir for his remarkable accomplishments and highlighted the

university's strong partnership with VIT. He emphasized the significance of

ongoing collaborations between the two institutions through research and

student exchanges. The successful 15-year partnership between Watson

College, Binghamton University, and VIT has resulted in joint academic

programmes, faculty exchanges, and collaborative research, strengthening

academic connections and facilitating knowledge sharing. For more details,

please refer to the link given below.

Thirukkural says thus:

அஞ்சாமை ஈகை அறிவூக்கம் இந்நான்கும்

எஞ்சாமை வேந்தர்க் கியல்பு.

Translation: Courage, generosity, knowledge (wisdom), motivation (Zeal)

are the four essential elements of a successful leader (King). 

His dedication to excellence in the path of the above four serves as a

beacon light of inspiration for all of us to follow him. Hearty

Congratulations from all of us, to our Honorable Chancellor Sir on this

remarkable achievement. We pray for his continued success, fulfillment, and

boundless opportunities in all his future endeavors.

Binghamton University News Link

https://www.binghamton.edu/news/story/4875/vellore-institute-of-technology-chancellor-to-receive-honorary-degree-at-watson-college-commencement

International Mother Earth Day

International Mother Earth Day was established in 2009, by the United

Nations, and It was decided to designate April 22 as International Mother

Earth Day. It recognizes that "the Earth and its ecosystems are our home"

and that "it is necessary to promote harmony with nature and the Earth."

The term Mother Earth is used because it "reflects the interdependence that

exists among human beings, other living species and the planet we all

inhabit".

International Mother Earth Day provides an opportunity to raise global

public awareness of the challenges to the well-being of the planet and all

the life it supports. Mother Earth is clearly urging a call to action.

Nature is suffering. Oceans filling with plastic and turning more acidic.

Subject: Safety precautions for Heat Waves.
Body:
Safety precautions for Heat Waves. 

Heat Wave

A Heat Wave is a period of abnormally high temperatures, more than the

normal maximum temperature that occurs during the summer season in the

North-Western parts of India. Heat Waves typically occur between March and

June, and in some rare cases even extend till July. The extreme

temperatures and resultant atmospheric conditions adversely affect people

living in these regions as they cause physiological stress, sometimes

resulting in death.

Health Impacts of Heat Waves

The health impacts of Heat Waves typically involve dehydration, heat

cramps, heat exhaustion and/or heat stroke. The signs and symptoms are as

follows:

Heat Cramps: Ederna (swelling) and Syncope (Fainting) generally accompanied

by fever below 39C i.e.102F. Heat Exhaustion: Fatigue, weakness,

dizziness, headache, nausea, vomiting, muscle cramps and sweating. Heat

Stoke: Body temperatures of 40C i.e. 104F or more along with delirium,

seizures or coma. This is a potential fatal condition

DO"S AND DONT"S

Heat Wave conditions can result in physiological strain, which could even

result in death.

To minimise the impact during the heat wave and to prevent serious ailment

or death because of heat stroke, you can take the following measures:

Avoid going out in the sun, especially between 12.00 <1200> noon and 3.00

p.m.

Drink sufficient water and as often as possible, even if not thirsty Wear

lightweight, light-coloured, loose, and porous cotton clothes.

Use protective goggles, umbrella/hat, shoes or chappals while going out in

sun.

Avoid strenuous activities when the outside temperature is high. Avoid

working outside between 12 noon and 3 p.m.

While travelling, carry water with you.

Avoid alcohol, tea, coffee and carbonated soft drinks, which dehydrates the

body.

Avoid high-protein food and do not eat stale food.

If you work outside, use a hat or an umbrella and also use a damp cloth on

your head, neck, face and limbs

Do not leave children or pets in parked vehicles If you feel faint or ill,

see a doctor immediately.

Use ORS, homemade drinks like lassi, torani (rice water), lemon water,

buttermilk, etc. which helps to re-hydrate the body.

Keep animals in shade and give them plenty of water to drink. Keep your

home cool, use curtains, shutters or sunshade and open windows at night.

Use fans, damp clothing and take bath in cold water frequently.

TIPS FOR TREATMENT OF A PERSON AFFECTED BY A SUNSTROKE:

Lay the person in a cool place, under a shade. Wipe her/him with a wet

cloth/wash the body frequently. Pour normal temperature water on the head.

The main thing is to bring down the body temperature. Give the person ORS

to drink or lemon sarbat/ whatever is useful to rehydrate the body. Take

the person immediately to the nearest health centre. The patient needs

immediate hospitalisation, as heat strokes could be fatal.

Source : National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)

Dear Students,

Greetings!

Are you a leader who wants to make a change?

The Office of Students' Welfare is currently seeking nominations for the

2024-2025 academic year.

The Student Council is a diverse group of students from across all

departments, working to represent the needs and aspirations of the entire

student body. If you're passionate about making VIT an even better place,

we encourage you to nominate yourself!

For more information on the nomination process and the role of the Student

Council, please visit the following links.

Google Form Links:

Executive & Member Secretary: https://forms.gle/PYkToeGdRDhT7QNc7

Secretary (Cultural & Technical): https://forms.gle/GME7hxTswz2kLdR57

The link will be available only till 18.05.2024 (Saturday), 5:00 PM and

deactivated afterwards.

The applications received only through the google form will be scrutinized

and called for an interview.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: 

1. Only Final and Pre Final Year Students shall apply for the post of Executive

and Member Secretary.

2. Final Year Students to act as Executive Member and Pre Final Year

Students to act as Member Secretary.

3.

Executive & Member Secretary: 

 - For all 5 Year Programmes (B. Arch. and Integrated Programmes), only

 2020 and 2021 Year Students to be considered eligible for the posts of

 Executive Member & Member Secretary respectively.

 - For all 4 Year Programmes (B. Tech., B. Des. & B. Sc. Hons.), only

 2021and 2022 Year Students to be considered eligible for the posts of

 Executive Member & Member Secretary respectively.

 - For all 3 Year Programmes (B.B.A., B.Com. & B.Sc.), only 2022 and 2023

 Year Students to be considered eligible for the posts of Executive

 Member & Member Secretary respectively.

 - For all 2 Year Programmes (M. Tech. & M.Sc.), only 2023 Year Students

 to be considered eligible for the posts of Executive Member.

4. Students from all years are eligible to apply for the post of Secretary

(Cultural & Technical) and Digital Support Team Member.

5. Minimum of 9 CGPA required for a student to be eligible for the post of

Student Council Member.

6. Minimum of 8.5 CGPA required for a student to be eligible for the post

of Secretary (Cultural & Technical).

7. Minimum of 7.5 CGPA required for a student to be eligible for the post

of Digital Support Team Member.

8. Students involved in any disciplinary issues, currently or in the past,

are not eligible for holding any post.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF STUDENT COUNCIL MEMBERS: 

· To officially represent all the students in the school / institute.

· To identify and help solve problems encountered by students in the

school / institute.

· To communicate its opinion to the school / institute administration on

any subject that concerns students.

· To promote and encourage the involvement of students in organizing

school / institute level activities.

· To inform students about any subject that concerns them.

· To consult students on any issue of importance and bring it to the

notice of the Students' Welfare office.

· To support and contribute to achieve better / higher accreditation for

the institute.

· To participate in the development of the school activities.

· To propose activities to the school/institute administration that would

improve the quality of student life in the school/institute.

We look forward to receiving your nominations!

Subject: Lecture series: Nanomanufacturing (Lecture-1), BU-VIT-AP Research Webinar - Dr. Jia Deng @ Thu Apr 18, 2024 7:30-8:30 PM
Body:
> Dear Professors, Research Scholars, and Students,

>

> Greetings from the International Relations Office!

>

> You are cordially invited to an online Lecture-1 titled 'Atomic Force

> Microscope-Based High-Resolution Nanopatterning,' scheduled for Thursday,

> April 18, 2024, from 7:30 pm to 8:30 pm (India Standard Time - Kolkata),

> Please find the attached poster for the same.

>

> Registration Link: https://forms.gle/wGM59ACSz4cyaHEX8 (Please use our

> University email ID for registration. The Zoom link will be provided upon

> registration)

>

> Abstract: Nanomanufacturing of sub-100 nanometer patterns is crucial

> for various fundamental research fields, from physics to biology, and

> commercial applications ranging from semiconductor devices to biomedical

> sensors. Atomic force microscope (AFM)-based nanomanufacturing, as an

> emerging low-cost and easy-to-set-up technique, has the potential to

> achieve comparable resolution to that of electron beam lithography, a

> commonly used technique for fabricating photolithography masks and

> arbitrary nanopatterns. Various AFM-based nanomanufacturing approaches have

> been developed, including mechanical direct scratching, dynamic plowing,

> thermal-mechanical material removal, electrostatic nanolithography, and

> dip-pen nanolithography. However, in most existing AFM-based material

> removal approaches, the dimensions of nanopatterns are limited by the tip

> sizes, which restricts the nanomanufacturing resolution and efficiency.

> Relatively large forces in material removal processes lead to quick tip

> wear and degraded fidelity of nanopatterns. To address this issue, we have

> innovated multiple energy-assisted AFM-based nanopatterning processes,

> integrating mechanical vibration, Joule heating, and electric fields to

> enable high-resolution nanopatterning. Our results demonstrate the

> effectiveness of external fields in enhancing AFM-based nanomanufacturing

> capabilities.

>

> Industrial Engineering at Binghamton University as an assistant professor

> in 2017. He earned a B.S. degree in Process Equipment and Control

> Engineering in 2010 from Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan, China. In

> 2013, he received an M.S. degree in Mechatronics Engineering from Huazhong

> University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China. In 2017, he earned his

> Ph.D. in Industrial Engineering from North Carolina State University,

> Raleigh, North Carolina. His research interests include process innovations

> and applications of AFM-based nanomanufacturing and additive manufacturing.

>

Dear Students, Research Scholars and Professors,

Greetings,

As professors of VIT, Vellore, we would greatly appreciate your input on

the concept of intelligent plates. This is a test to assess the concept and

gather the respondents' expectations on the product, pricing, channels, and

promotions. The purpose of this survey is to investigate the viewpoints of

respondents regarding the utility, user-friendliness, affordability,

effectiveness, health awareness, and inclination to use the intelligent

plate. Anyone with a concern regarding their health can complete this form.

Please allocate a duration of 10-15 minutes to complete the subsequent

form. All replies are intended for scholarly purposes and will be kept

confidential. To gain a clear idea of what an Intelligent Plate is,

we kindly encourage you to click on the provided link and view the

accompanying video.

https://forms.gle/hLmHUEZJn9ZzDvqw5

Eat What you Need

Eat What You Need for a Healthy and Happy Life. The concept of "Eat What

You Need" promotes mindful and healthy eating habits by integrating

Technology, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML).

The aim is to assist individuals in making informed decisions about their

food intake based on their body's actual needs rather than impulsive

desires. It revolves around balancing caloric intake, nutrients, proteins,

and carbohydrates based on an individual's body mass and activity levels.

This approach is expected to lead to a healthier and happier life by

preventing overeating, promoting weight management, and ensuring

nutritional balance.

Concept:

The i-Plate is a technologically advanced device that takes the form of a

food plate and provides detailed information about the food placed on it.

The device will be capable of providing information on a host of parameters

such as:

· Weight of the food placed on it.

· The number of calories provided by the food

· The nutritional elements present in the food

The “i-Plate" aims to personalize eating habits, ensuring that the user

consumes the right amount of food with the necessary nutrients for their

body. This approach is expected to lead to a healthier and happier life by

preventing overeating, promoting weight management, and ensuring

nutritional balance.

Thanks for your active participation and happy healthier life

Thanks and regards

Yours Sincerely,

P.Arulmozhivarman

Subject: Release of XIX Edition of SMEC's MechnoVIT Newsletter- reg,
Body:
Dear Colleagues, Scholars, and Students

Festive Greetings!

We are delighted to bring you the XIX Edition of the SMEC Newsletter

"MechnoVIT". The "MechnoVIT" team is delighted to share the outstanding

achievements of our students, researchers, and faculty members from January

to March 2024. During this quarter, the school organised the

"Industry-Academia Networking Conclave" in association with the Career

Development Centre. Our Founder & Honourable Chancellor Dr. G. Viswanathan

inaugurated the event in the presence of our esteemed industrial

dignitaries. The conclave has attracted the participation of 63

organizations, and we signed 11 MoUs during the Conclave. Thanks to all our

valuable industry partners.

The most noteworthy accomplishment for the school is the receipt of 20

patents and several national/international projects. It is a great fortune

that many adjunct professors visited us during this time. We take great

pride in the many national and international accolades bestowed on our

students and faculty for their extraordinary achievements. The school is

making consistent strides forward, according to data on patents and

publications. Ideation and Design Thinking— the school has equipped a new

lab during this time.

We also signed the MoU with VOLVO in the presence of our Honorable Founder

& Chancellor. The Managing Director of VOLVO, Shri. Kamal Bali was present

at the MoU ceremony. We have the opportunity to develop a brand new

postgraduate programme on smart mobility thanks to our partnership with

VOLVO. The program's courses will be co-designed and co-taught by

professionals from VOLVO and VIT. In addition, the MoU makes it possible to

provide students with internships and job placements.

The School, as is customary, has organised several training programmes,

expert talks, and industry visits for our students, colleagues, and staff.

I'd appreciate it if you could forward this E-newsletter to your friends,

colleagues, and others.

We will meet you in the XX edition of MechnoVIT, which will include a

slew of new developments and intriguing topics.

Happy Reading!

Thank you

World Art Day

Each year, on 15 April, World Art Day celebrations help reinforce the links

between artistic creations and society, encourage greater awareness of the

diversity of artistic expressions and highlight the contribution of artists

to sustainable development. It is also an occasion to shine a light on arts

education in schools, as culture can pave the way for inclusive and

equitable education.

Art nurtures creativity, innovation and cultural diversity for all peoples

across the globe and plays an important role in sharing knowledge and

encouraging curiosity and dialogue. These are qualities that art has always

had, and will always have if we continue to support environments where

artists and artistic freedom are promoted and protected. In this way,

furthering the development of art also furthers our means to achieve a free

and peaceful world. There is much to learn, share and celebrate on World

first day of the traditional Tamil new year. The new year begins with the

first month of the Tamil solar calendar, Chittirai.

While Tamilians across the world celebrate Puthandu, many other

communities across India celebrate their traditional new year on the same

day or (14th or 15th April) - it is Vishu for people in Kerala, Bihu for

Jallianwala Bagh Massacre Day

The Jallianwala Bagh massacre, also known as the Amritsar massacre, took

place on 13 April 1919, when Acting Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered

troops of the British Indian Army to fire their rifles into a crowd of

unarmed Indian civilians in Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, Punjab, killing at

least 379 people and injuring over 1,200 other people.

On Sunday, 13 April 1919, Dyer, convinced a major insurrection could take

place, banned all meetings. This notice was not widely disseminated, and

many villagers gathered in the Bagh to celebrate the important Hindu and

Sikh festival of Baisakhi, and peacefully protest the arrest and

deportation of two national leaders, Satyapal and Saifuddin Kitchlew. Dyer

and his troops entered the garden, blocking the main entrance behind them,

took up position on a raised bank, and with no warning opened fire on the

crowd for about ten minutes, directing their bullets largely towards the

few open gates through which people were trying to flee until the

ammunition supply was almost exhausted. The following day Dyer stated in a

report that "I have heard that between 200 and 300 of the crowd were

killed. My party fired 1,650 rounds.

Dear VITians,

The Office of Students' Welfare invites you for today's special event: A

Session on "A Conflict Mind Interference on Social Media".

Social Media, once a platform for connection, has become a battleground for

conflicting ideas. This constant exposure to opposing viewpoints, often

presented in a sensationalized way, can create a state of conflict-mind

interference – a mental tug-of-war that disrupts our ability to think

clearly and form our own informed opinions. By being mindful of conflict

mind interference and adopting these strategies, we can reclaim control of

our online experience and engage with social media in a way that fosters

understanding and critical thought.

Subject: FAQ related to Yantra'24 Central Hackathon-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

Greeting from Team Yantra'24!

Some of the frequently asked question for Yantra Central Hackathons:

1) Team Structure: The Central Hackathon encourages all students of VIT

Vellore to participate, emphasizing an open team structure. There are no

restrictions on team composition, meaning any student from VIT Vellore can

join forces with others, fostering collaboration and the pooling of diverse

skill sets.

2) Screening Round: To progress to Round 1 of the hackathon, participants

must submit an idea aligned with the tracks provided on the official

website. This submission serves as the gateway to the main event, ensuring

that teams are prepared with a well-thought-out concept.

3) Venue Details: Information regarding the venue for the Central Hackathon

will be disseminated to each team that successfully qualifies for Round 1.

This comprehensive venue information, encompassing location and other

essential details, will be made available on the official hackathon

website. It is essential for qualifying teams to stay updated by regularly

checking the website for the latest updates and specific instructions

regarding the venue.

4) Problem Statements: At the onset of the hackathon event, the problem

statements will be revealed on-site, introducing an element of real-time

challenge and excitement for participating teams. Teams will have the

opportunity to select their preferred tracks and problem statements during

this phase, allowing for flexibility and the chance to tailor their focus

based on the challenges presented. This flexibility empowers teams to make

adjustments and pivot to different problem statements within the designated

timeframe before the first review.

5) OD will be provided for the whole duration of the hackathon to all the

participants.

6) Registration: All the members of the team have to register on the portal

and join their respective team.

7) Last Date to Register and Idea Submission: Last date to register for

Central Hackathon is 12 April 1:00 pm.

Register Now at https://yantra.vit.ac.in

practical knowledge directly from professionals at the forefront of their

fields.

<admissions@inspiredstudy.com> , +91 74188 80288

Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you to today’s [5th April] 

event.

International Day of Conscience

The International Day of Conscience marks the value of the human

conscience. It came into existence on July 25, 2019, by the UN General

Assembly, under UN resolution 73/329. Building a culture of peace needs

extensive educational, cultural, social, and civic effort in which everyone

has something to contribute and learn. It is an open-minded worldwide

approach with a specific goal, namely to establish a culture of peace

inseparable from culture as a whole and take root in people's hearts and

minds. The theme for this year is “Promoting the Culture of Peace with

Love and Conscience.”

Essay Writing

People, especially teenagers, have a strong desire to belong and feel

accepted by their peers. This can make it hard to resist pressure from

friends, even if you know what they're asking you to do isn't a good idea.

Also, as digital technology has woven itself into the fabric of our

existence, influencing everything from how we communicate to how we learn

and work, the impact is undeniable, offering a potent mix of benefits and

drawbacks.

Share your ideas through the essay writing competition on the importance of

conscience in this age!

Topic: "Overcoming Groupthink: How Can We Follow Our Conscience When the

Pressure to Conform is High?"

practical knowledge directly from professionals at the forefront of their

fields.

For more information about InspirED & the university please visit -

https://youtu.be/2BiCM1f7tWg | https://www.smu.edu.sg |

SMU equips you for a dynamic exposure in these fields, fostering leadership

for their selected subjects. It includes on-campus training and corporate

enclosed.

https://meet.google.com/dom-hntk-bjc to join the video meeting)

regarding course enrollment.

4. For programme-related queries, reach out to

admissions@inspiredstudy.com , +91

74188 80288

Dear Students,

I am writing to you to inform you about the Deakin Vice Chancellor's 100%

Scholarship 2024. The Deakin Vice Chancellor's Meritorious 100% Scholarship

program is designed to attract top-tier international students to pursue

undergraduate or postgraduate courses at Deakin University. This

prestigious scholarship opportunity aims to recognize and support students

with outstanding academic achievements and co-curricular involvement.

This scholarship covers the entire duration of the program and is open to

both bachelor's students seeking to transfer to Deakin and accelerated

master's students.

https://www.deakin.edu.au/study/fees-and-scholarships/scholarships/find-a-scholarship/deakin-vice-chancellors-international-scholarship

To be eligible for consideration, prospective international students must

meet the following criteria:

· Be applying for a course at Deakin University

· Meet the eligibility requirements for studying at Deakin University

· Have attained a minimum of an 80% average (or equivalent) in their

previous studies

Applicants are required to submit the following supporting documents along

with their application:

1. Completed Deakin International Scholarship Program application form

2. Personal statement (300 words)

3. Two references who can provide insight into the applicant's

community engagement and/or leadership capacity

4. Completed application to study at Deakin, including academic

transcripts

The personal statement should be written by the applicant and reflect their

personal views. It should include:

· Reasons for choosing Deakin University for their studies

· Overview of extracurricular activities and work experience (paid or

voluntary)

· Why they believe they would be an outstanding ambassador for Deakin

University

· Any additional information that would support their application

Selected applicants may also be invited to attend an interview as part of

the selection process.

Subject: SW Newsletter_February 2024 - Reg.
Body:
Dear VITians,

“Though February is short, it is filled with lots of love and sweet

surprises.” - Charmaine J. Forde

February is an interesting month. It might not be the most glamorous month

in the calendar but February has its charms.

The month kicked off with the Annual NSS Special Camp in Vandranthangal

village, Katpadi. Various programmes like surveying, training the self help

group, teaching the school kids which included awareness and motivational

talks, tree plantation, medical camp, etc were conducted. The Camp was

inaugurated by the VIT Chancellor, Vice Presidents, Pro-VC, Registrar, VAO

& other village leaders.

An orientation programme was organized by the VIT Standards Club on 6th

February 2024 that aimed to educate the members about the crucial standards

landscape, with a focus on the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Dr. Baskar

A., Technical Consultant, Butterfly Gandhimathi Appliances Limited was the

Chief Guest for the session.

The Installation Ceremony of the Rotaract Club saw the new leadership

outline their vision for 2024. Mr. Hemant Sahal, Founder and CEO of Digii

(formely CollPoll) was invited to provide insights on Viksit Bharat 2047.

The month also witnessed the much awaited cultural extravaganza,

Riviera'24, with various cultural and sports events. Pre-Riviera events

like Agaaz, Kalaa etc. offered wonderful experience and entertainment to

the students. The Proshows saw some of the maestros like Shankar Mahadevan,

Vijay Prakash, G V Prakash, Saindhavi, Sathyprakash and Band Agam perform

their hit numbers.

To read about more such events and activities, check out our newsletter!

International Day of Solidarity with Detained and Missing Staff Members

Since the founding of the United Nations in 1945, hundreds of brave men and

women have lost their lives in its service. During the 1990s, the growing

number and scale of UN peacekeeping missions put many more at risk. More

lives were lost during the 1990s than in the previous four decades

combined. The International Day of Solidarity with Detained and Missing

Staff Members is marked each year on the anniversary of the abduction of

Alec Collett, a former journalist who was working for the United Nations

Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA)

when he was abducted by armed gunman in 1985. His body was finally found

in Lebanon’s Bekaa Valley in 2009.

This is a day to mobilize action, demand justice and strengthen our resolve

to protect UN staff and peacekeepers, as well as our colleagues in the

non-governmental community and the press.

Holi

Known as the festival of colors, Holi is celebrated on the last full moon in

the lunar month of Phalguna. This ancient tradition marks the end of winter

and honors the triumph of good over evil. Celebrants light bonfires, throw

colorful powder called gulal, eat sweets, and dance to traditional folk

music.

Holi celebrations take different forms in various parts of India and can

last between 40 days in some regions and just two days in others. The most

common ritual https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/ritual is perhaps the

lighting of a bonfire that represents the burning of Holika, or Holika

Dahan, in North India. In South India the ritual is known as Kama Dahanam

and is associated with the legend of Shiva and Kama.

World Tuberculosis Day

World TB Day is celebrated on March 24 each year to raise public awareness

and understanding about the world’s deadliest infectious killer

tuberculosis and its devastating health, social and economic impact on

people around the world. March 24 marks the day in 1882 when Dr Robert Koch

announced that he had discovered the bacterium that causes TB, which opened

the way towards diagnosing and curing this disease. However, TB still

claims 4 100 people lives each day and close to 27 000 people fall ill with

this preventable and curable disease. World TB Day is an opportunity to

focus on the people affected by this disease and to call for accelerated

action to end TB suffering and deaths.

The theme of World TB Day 2024 - ‘Yes! We can end TB!’ – conveys a message

of hope that getting back-on-track to turn the tide against the TB epidemic

is possible through high level leadership, increased investments and faster

uptake of new WHO recommendations.

World Forest Day

The United Nations General Assembly recognizes March 21 as the

International Day of Forests and utilizes this day to raise awareness about

the importance of forest restoration. Trees were once treated as sacred

entities but are now being destroyed in the name of urbanization. There's

no limit to how much humans take from nature without giving back. To truly

value nature and understand the significance of forests, it is important to

learn about the history and power this day holds.

slipping away and march forward together to create a movement. It's time to

Subject: Mykolas Romeris University - State scholarships available for academic year 2024-2025
Body:
Dear Students,

The Calls for Lithuanian State scholarships are already announced for

2024-2025 academic year Below we are outlining both calls: 1. State

scholarships for short-term studies and 2. State scholarships for Full-time

 Master degree studies:

1) Lithuanian state scholarships for short-term (1-2 semesters) mobility.

The Call for next academic year (2024/2025) is already launched by the

Educational exchanges support foundation

https://studyin.lt/scholarships/short-term-studies/

https://studyin.lt/scholarships/short-term-studies/ and it is a

possibility to our bilateral partners to encourage their students to APPLY

for state scholarhip for short-term mobility and come to Mykolas Romeris

University for either autumn or spring semester or for both semesters.

 There are 35 scholarships available in total. Candidates of the first

and second study cycle, approved for the short–term studies, will receive a

monthly scholarship of 550 EUR. Candidates of the third study cycle

(doctoral students) approved for the short–term studies will receive a

monthly scholarship of 1100 EUR. Deadline for the online application

submission is 15th of April 2024 . Citizens of the following countries,

who are Your University Students are eligible to apply:

• Azerbaijan, Armenia, Australia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Brunei,

Cambodia, Canada, China (N.B. from MRU: it is meant for Taiwanese

applicants only) , Georgia, India, Indonesia, Israel, Japan, Kazakhstan,

Laos, Malaysia, Moldova, Mongolia, Myanmar, New Zealand, Pakistan, the

Philippines, Republic of South Africa, Singapore, South Korea, Thailand,

Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, the USA, Vietnam.

 • Foreigners of Lithuanian origin (from all foreign countries).

Students must physically study in Lithuania in order to receive the State

scholarship. Remote studies are not eligible for financing. Students will

be paid scholarship for the period they will study and be present

physically at the receiving university..

Those students who are interested in applying for short-term state

scholarship will be considered as nominated by your University (as your

university will be signing the conditional agreement, a template of which

is attached to this message) and will have to complete two application

forms:

 1. application form of MRU (at https://incoming.mruni.eu) for exchange

 under bilateral agreement

AND if he wants to receive a financial support for his exchange period –

also

(2) an application for short-term state scholarship with all required

documents through the NEW online application system of funding :

https://sistema.smpf.lt/

Candidates will be informed about the selection results by e-mail no later

than 1 July 2024.

Please share this information with your University students and encourage

them to take part in international exchanges between your University and

Mykolas Romeris University. All information (including List of courses)

about exchange studies at Mykolas Romeris University are on our web-site

Subject: Deadline to Apply for Live Project in Data Science and as a Business Analyst
Body:
Hi ,

Please note that tonight, 11.59pm is the deadline at the Vellore Institute of Technology to apply for the Finlatics Business Analyst & Data Science Experience Program, an online live project that helps students learn & gain work experience in data-driven decision-making and data science with Python.

This project runs at leading campuses, including IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIM Bangalore, IIM Ahmedabad, and BITS Pilani.

STRUCTURE of the live project:

1. Understand types of data analytics, their usage, and their benefits across industry segments like Consumer Goods, Tourism, and e-commerce, among others, through a case study-driven approach.

2. Solve business problems of technology-oriented businesses that impact their profitability

3. Learn the basics of Python and how it can be used as a tool in data science

4. Get hands-on learning and experience in writing various Python functions.

5. Learn Power BI, a pan-industry business intelligence tool used to analyze data

6. Apply Power BI to sales data to gain insights into marketing campaigns

7. Learn how various statistical methods can be used in Python to generate insights.

8. Complete industry-specific case projects to understand the application of Python-based data science in business scenarios.

The project is doable along with any other commitment due to its work-from-home and online structure.

Student OUTCOMES:

1. Certificate of Work Experience as a Business Analyst and in Data Science

2. Letter of Recommendation on performance

3. A Certificate of Proficiency in Python & Power BI will be issued at the end of the program

To apply, students can fill out the form below, and we will get in touch with them:

https://82e6v.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/7nVU1aA2nfsTSlPYaV0LcO3ykXyRn8u/8ScPoOlGy4nC

As Python would be taught in the program, all students must note that no prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to be a part of the program.

Personalized guidance & mentoring would also be provided to help students learn Python & understand the usage of Power BI.

Live Sessions would be provided to help students learn Python & for discussions on Business Strategies.

Project Duration: 2 months

Project Start: Flexible on selected student choice. Students can choose to start the project post-exams to balance the project along with any upcoming exams, assignments, or personal commitments.

Project Break & Extension: Selected students will be eligible for a break during the project if needed for any exams, assignments, or personal commitments. They can also take an extension in duration if they cannot complete it in the given time.

Time Commitment: 4 - 5 hours per week

If selected, the program has a minimal induction fee of Rs. 2999 + GST / Rs. 3999 + GST (on student choice)

Fee Waiver: A 25% fee waiver shall be given to all Vellore Institute of Technology students on the abovementioned minimal induction fee. This waiver will reduce the fee to Rs. 2199 + GST / Rs. 3049 + GST.

To be eligible for the waiver, kindly apply before tonight's deadline. Applying for the project takes 2-3 mins of your time and is free of all charges.

We are excited to have a fruitful engagement.
