Subject: Live Project in Data Science and as a Business Analyst
Body:
Hi ,

We're pleased to open applications for the Finlatics Business Analyst & Data Science Experience Program, an online live project that helps students learn & gain work experience in data-driven decision-making and data science with Python at the Vellore Institute of Technology.

Finlatics is recognized for Skill Development & Assessment by the Department for Promotion of Industry & Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce & Industry, and was incubated at the Atal Incubation Centre - NMIMS, supported by Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog and Government of India.

This project runs at leading campuses, including IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIM Bangalore, IIM Ahmedabad, and BITS Pilani.

STRUCTURE of the live project:

1. Understand types of data analytics, their usage, and their benefits across industry segments like Consumer Goods, Tourism, and e-commerce, among others, through a case study-driven approach.

2. Solve business problems of technology-oriented businesses that impact their profitability

3. Learn the basics of Python and how it can be used as a tool in data science

4. Get hands-on learning and experience in writing various Python functions.

5. Learn Power BI, a pan-industry business intelligence tool used to analyze data

6. Apply Power BI to sales data to gain insights into marketing campaigns

7. Learn how various statistical methods can be used in Python to generate insights.

8. Complete industry-specific case projects to understand the application of Python-based data science in business scenarios.

The project is doable along with any other commitment due to its work-from-home and online structure.

Student OUTCOMES:

1. Certificate of Work Experience as a Business Analyst and in Data Science

2. Letter of Recommendation on performance

3. A Certificate of Proficiency in Python & Power BI will be issued at the end of the program

To apply, students can fill out the form below, and we will get in touch with them:

https://82e6v.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/7nVU1aA2nfsTSlPYaV0LcO3ykXyRn8u/y2zGMt-ToDP0

As Python would be taught in the program, all students must note that no prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to be a part of the program.

Personalized guidance & mentoring would also be provided to help students learn Python & understand the usage of Power BI.

Live Sessions would be provided to help students learn Python & for discussions on Business Strategies.

Project Duration: 2 months

Project Start: Flexible on selected student choice. Students can choose to start the project post-exams to balance the project along with any upcoming exams, assignments, or personal commitments.

Project Break & Extension: Selected students will be eligible for a break during the project if needed for any exams, assignments, or personal commitments. They can also take an extension in duration if they cannot complete it in the given time.

Time Commitment: 4 - 5 hours per week

If selected, the program has a minimal induction fee of Rs. 2999 + GST / Rs. 3999 + GST (on student choice)

Fee Waiver: A 25% fee waiver shall be given to all Vellore Institute of Technology students on the abovementioned minimal induction fee. This waiver will reduce the fee to Rs. 2199 + GST / Rs. 3049 + GST.

To be eligible for the waiver, kindly apply via the link above. We are excited to have a fruitful engagement.

Dear VITians,

India is known as an IT hub and now it aims to take lead in Artificial

intelligence, Semicon design and production, quantum computing etc. India's

Techade signifies India's dedication to embracing the digital age to ensure

sustainable development, create new job opportunities, enhance quality of

life, and establish a strong presence in the global technology landscape.

India Semiconductor Mission has been set up by the Government of India to

create an end-to-end semiconductor ecosystem to enable the nation to become

a significant player in the global semiconductor industry. Aligning with

India’s Semi-Conductor Mission and with an aim to strengthen the

semiconductor facilities in India, Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra

Modi will lay down the foundation stone of the three Semiconductor

facilities on 13th March 2024. The three semiconductor facilities are:

 - India’s First Fab Facility in Dholera, Gujarat

 - OSAT facility in Sanand, Gujarat

 - OSAT facility in Morigaon, Assam

In this regard, Live Streaming of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi

following schedule:

The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) Raising Day is celebrated

every year on March 10 to commemorate the establishment of the CISF in

1969. The CISF is a premier central armed police force under the Ministry

of Home Affairs, which is responsible for providing security cover to

various public sector undertakings, airports, seaports, power plants, and

other important infrastructure projects across the country.

situations, including terrorist attacks, hijackings, bomb threats, and

hostage situations. The force is equipped with state-of-the-art weapons,

specialized vehicles, and other modern security equipment. The CISF also

has a dedicated canine unit, which is trained to sniff out explosives and

other illicit materials.

Body:
Dear Students,

Greetings from the U.S. Consulate General Chennai! We are excited to share

information on the Quad Fellowship

http://r100313.usief.org.in/c/l?u=10D2C9CD&e=17BAEB9&c=187D9&t=0&l=11D8ED8F&email=YX%2F4q%2FrpJvFz32HJmqDUw%2FEtUpur2Ctu&seq=1

- an exciting opportunity open to exceptional master's and doctoral

students in science and technology who demonstrate academic excellence,

exceptional results in their field, and a desire to use their talents to

promote collective good. The fellowship, initiated by the Quad countries

of Australia, India, Japan, and the United States, and administered by the

Institute of International Education (IIE), sponsors exceptional STEM

master's and doctoral students to study in the United States.

The Quad Fellowship is a first-of-its-kind fellowship designed to build

ties among the next generation of scientists and technologists. It offers

an unparalleled blend of financial support, cross-cultural exchange, and

networking:

 - A one-time stipend of US $40,000 for academic expenses.

 - Networking opportunities with accomplished minds in STEM, government,

 and society.

 - Multicultural alumni network dedicated to advancing innovation and

 research for positive social impact.

For more information including eligibility and application process, please

visit this link: exchange programs

http://r100313.usief.org.in/c/l?u=10D2C9CE&e=17BAEB9&c=187D9&t=0&l=11D8ED8F&email=YX%2F4q%2FrpJvFz32HJmqDUw%2FEtUpur2Ctu&seq=1

Application Deadline: April 1, 2024, at 5 pm ET (April 2, 2024, at 3:30

am IST) 

Thank you.

U.S. Consulate General Chennai

Subject: Input Requested: Acquisition of Fuel Cell and MEA Fabrication Facilities
Body:
Dear Sir / Madam,

TIFAC CORE is committed to advancing sustainable transportation, and we are

actively involved in the development of a fuel cell vehicle.

Our center has submitted a proposal for the acquisition of state-of-the-art

facilities to initiate the in-house development of a robust and efficient

fuel cell stack for transportation applications. These facilities will

provide the essential infrastructure and equipment to support our in-house

fuel cell stack development efforts.

The proposed acquisition encompasses two key facilities:

Fuel Cell Analytical Facility: This facility will be meticulously

designed to house a comprehensive suite of essential components and

equipment. This includes FC electronic loads, mass flow controllers,

humidifiers, PEMFC/DMFC single cell assemblies, PEMFC stacks, peristaltic

pumps, controllers, and dedicated hydrogen and oxygen gas lines. These

instruments will enable us to conduct rigorous and in-depth performance

evaluations of our fuel cell designs, providing invaluable data for

optimization and refinement.

MEA Fabrication Facility: This facility will empower us to achieve

complete in-house fabrication of Membrane Electrode Assemblies (MEAs), a

core component of fuel cells. The facility will be equipped with advanced

tools such as hot presses, ultrasonic bath sonicators, hot plates with

stirrers, vacuum ovens, and dedicated vacuum benches. This comprehensive

setup will allow for the precise control and optimization of MEA

manufacturing processes, ensuring consistent quality and performance

characteristics for our fuel cell stacks.

We're confident that by tapping into the collective knowledge of our

research community and utilizing the capabilities of the proposed

facilities, we can achieve substantial progress in developing highly

efficient and locally produced fuel cells for various applications.

To guarantee that these facilities adequately meet the diverse needs of our

VIT research community, we kindly ask for your valuable input.

Specifically, we are keen to hear your opinions on the proposed facilities

and any suggestions you may have for additional features that would improve

their utilization and functionality

To facilitate your feedback, we have created a Google Form (

https://forms.gle/1G9T5NH2CjxFyZP1A). Please submit your responses by March

15, 2024.

CodeCraft: Unveiling Javascript & DOM 

Mozilla Firefox Club is organising a comprehensive Technical Workshop

designed for individuals with basic knowledge of HTML and CSS where

participants will delve into the fundamentals of JavaScript, covering

Outsmart the Dilemma: Mastering Strategy with Game Theory.

workshop organised by our student chapter of International Society of

Automation. Analyze choices, anticipate reactions, and make data-driven

decisions every time. We'll unlock the secrets of strategic automation,

showing you how to conquer dilemmas in business, negotiations, and even

friendly competition. It's not about luck, it's about mastering the system.

Join us and become the player everyone wants on their team.

Body:
Dear Colleagues, Scholars, and Students

We are delighted to inform you that the School of Mechanical Engineering in

association with the Career Development Centre is organizing a

three-day Industry

Academic Networking Conclave (IANC) 2024 on March 07-09, 2024. The

inaugural Ceremony of IANC 2024 is scheduled to be held on 07/03/2024

(Thursday) at 10:00 am in Anna Auditorium.

The theme of this year’s conclave is “Sustainable Technologies for a

Better Future”. As shared with you all in our earlier mail, the IANC 2024

events cover a wide range of areas that include:

 - Carbon Neutrality

 - Circular Economy

 - Digital Transformation towards Industry 5.0

 - Future Materials & Manufacturing

 - Green Energy Technologies

 - Smart Mobility

 - Sustainable Healthcare System

This conclave brings together representatives from over 60 industries and

organisations. Renowned industry experts will offer plenary talks on the

issues. This conclave includes 28 plenary sessions and 6 Technical

Challenges spread over several days. We strongly believe that the plenary

sessions foster innovative thinking and multidisciplinary collaboration

among students and professors. Please find attached a full agenda for the

plenary sessions.

Highlights of the Conclave:

 - Exchange of MoU

 - Technical Challenge | Hack-a-Thon | Design-a-thon contests

 - Poster Presentation

 - Job Fair

In addition, 21 industries are participating on 07/03/2024 to provide job

opportunities to the Diploma students, in this Job Fair arranged by our

Career Development Centre.

The inaugural invitation and brochure of IANC 2024 are attached for your

kind information.

We, the team of SMEC and CDC cordially invite you all to join us at the

inaugural ceremony of IANC 2024.

Thank you

Texas Instruments India invites applications for WiSH – Women in

Semiconductors and Hardware, which is aimed at encouraging women

engineering students to pursue careers in the semiconductor industry. WiSH

is an all-access month-long mentorship program leading to an opportunity to

intern with Texas Instruments!

We have added Embedded Software track this year. Students can indicate

their domain preference (Hardware/Embedded Software) while registering.

 streams

 3. Having a minimum CGPA of 7/10 or 70% in their current degree

 4. Curious about the world of semiconductors and enthusiastic to learn

 more

Selection Process:

 1. Profile based shortlisting

 2. Online aptitude test (+ Basic software test for students choosing

 embedded software track)

 3. Shortlisting based on the candidate’s application and Test

 performance

 4. Discussion with a TI engineer

Program Format:

When? 

Summer 2024, in the semester break between the 4th and 5th semesters for

bachelors and 2nd and 3rd semesters for masters students.

Mode?

Hybrid mode with students participating virtually for the first three weeks

and coming to the TI site at Bangalore for the final fourth week

Subject: Procedure to be followed for Medical/Emergency Leave - Reg.
Body:
Dear Students,

Greetings !!!

 1. For any kind of leave including medical reasons students are advised

 to use the permitted 25% relaxation in attendance and a minimum of 75%

 is mandatory to appear for the exams.

 2. In case of emergency (Medical reasons / Hospitalization / Death in

 the family), the first intimation must be given to the proctor.

 3. If he/she has been admitted to the hospital as an inpatient due to

 medical reasons, they have to submit his/her discharge summary, fitness

 certificate, and hospital bills must be sent to the Head of the

 Department (hod.ss@vit.ac.in <hod.ss@vit.ac.in>) through the Proctor with

 a copy to the Programme Secretary (secretary.ss@vit.ac.in) within three

 days after rejoining or before the last working day whichever is early.

 4. Medical prescriptions are not considered under any circumstances.

 5. In addition, During the exam period to avail permission for Re-CAT

 and Re-FAT due to Medical reasons/ Hospitalization/ Death in the

 family Students are advised to follow the circular from Dean Academics

 and CoE respectively (refer to the emails from the respective office).

 6. Based on the nature of the request, the school-level committee will

 decide whether to permit or reject the request for Attendance Relaxation

 for appearing on the Exam. Medical leaves will not be updated on VTOP.

 7. After a medical leave request, students are expected to attend all

 the classes regularly and if absences are found at later stages, then

 medical leave will not be considered.

Ref:

VIT/Regr./2024/039

28 February 2024

CIRCULAR

Sub: Riviera 2024 Pro-Shows – Guidelines to be followed

The Riviera 2024 Pro-Show events will be held from 29.02.24 to 03.03.24 at

the SJT Ground from 6:00 p.m. onwards. The students are requested to abide

by the following guidelines for the same.

1. Students who have purchased tickets ONLY are permitted to enter the

venue from 5:00 p.m. onwards.

2. No students will be permitted after 7:00 p.m. to enter the venue.

3. Students are requested to swipe their ID cards at the entry counter

at the venue.

4. Pro-Shows tickets are not transferable under any circumstance

to other students.

5. Students have to undergo frisking before they reach the entry

counter.

6. Outside food, beverages, water bottles, backpacks, bags, and

all other takeaway items are strictly prohibited inside the venue.

7. Separate zones for standing and sitting have been arranged at the

venue. Zones B1 to B4 are for standing and Zones B5 to B8 are for sitting

on the boy’s side and similarly G1 and G2 are for standing and G3 and

G4 are for sitting on the girl’s side (Layout of the venue is attached

herewith).

8. A restricted number of students will be allowed in each zone and

they will be filled on first-cum-first-serve basis.

9. Students wanting to leave the venue in between the show will not be

permitted to re-enter.

10. Any act of indiscipline by the student will be viewed seriously and

subject to severe actions as per the student code of conduct.

11. The Pro-Show venue is under CCTV surveillance.

12. Food stalls, drinking water, restrooms, and ambulance facilities are

available inside the venue. For any emergency, the student can contact the

faculty coordinators in the respective zones.

13. Eating places are provided near the food stalls. Taking food and

beverages inside the Zones is strictly prohibited.

14. Men's Hostel students are requested to enter the venue ONLY through

the Railway Underground Bridge (RUB) between SJT and PRP buildings. Entry

is not permitted through any other subway.

15. Day scholar boys will be permitted to enter the venue near RUB

adjacent to PRP (VAIAL entrance) through Gate 11 only.

16. Ladies Hostel students and day scholar girl students are requested to

enter the Pro-Show venue through the F-Block Ladies' Hostel gate. Day

scholar girls are allowed into the campus only through the Main Gate.

17. Students who are not attending the Pro-Shows are requested to leave

the campus before 7:00 p.m. from 29.02.24 to 03.03.24. The hostel-in-time

is 7:00 p.m. for students who are not attending the Pro-Shows.

18. Students are requested to collect their online deliveries before 5:00

p.m. from 29.02.24 to 03.03.24.

Your cooperation in this regard is highly solicited.

Enjoy the events and make Riviera 2024 a grand success!!!

National Science Day

National Science Day is celebrated every year on February 28 across the

nation to mark and recognize the contributions of scientists towards the

development of the country. National Science Day is held to commemorate the

discovery of the Raman Effect. On February 28, 1928, Sir CV Raman

discovered the Raman Effect for which the Physicist was awarded the Nobel

Prize in 1930.

To mark the anniversary of India's greatest discovery- 'Raman effect', the

government of India felicitates scientists whose contributions played an

eminent role in the field of science. National Science Day is celebrated to

raise awareness of the importance of science in daily life. Colleges and

institutions across the country also celebrate National Science Day by

organizing public speeches, radio, TV, science movies, science exhibitions

appeared and failed to clear ['F' & 'N' grades]

Eligible.

Scheduled from 28th May 2024 onwards. (Tentatively)

been given should be registered and should adhere to the schedule given for

Re-FAT / Regular Arrear. Please note that there will not be any second

chance what so ever be the reason for not appearing in Re-FAT. There is no

Fee for Re-FAT Process.

For Regular Arrear, Students should register for ALL the Components of a

selected course. Component wise registration is NOT permitted. For

example, if a course has both theory and laboratory components, the student

should register for both theory and laboratory components to clear the

backlog, even though the student would have cleared either the theory or

laboratory component of that particular course earlier. If a course has a

‘J’ component, the student should appear for the final review again. It

will be considered equivalent to FAT for the project component of the

course.

If a student fails to clear in the arrear examination, the student can once

again register for the subsequent arrear examination or for re-registration

in subsequent semester again as a complete course (all components).

No individual component of a course is permitted once someone registers

for an arrear for that course.

Matribhasha Diwas or International Mother Language Day

International Mother Language Day is celebrated every year on 21st February.

The main purpose of celebrating this day is to promote the awareness of

language and cultural diversity all across the world. It was first

announced by UNESCO on November 17, 1999. Since then it is being celebrated

every year. The date represents the day 21st February 1952 when four young

students were killed in Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh who campaigned to

officially use their mother language, Bengali, in Bangladesh.

On International Mother Language Day the UN's Educational, Scientific, and

Cultural Organization (UNESCO) and UN agencies participate in events that

promote linguistic and cultural diversity. They also encourage people to

maintain their knowledge of their mother language while learning and using

more than one language. Governments and non-governmental organizations may

use the day to announce policies to encourage language learning and support.

Subject: Calling Innovative Minds! VIT's Hyperloop Team-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

Greetings from VIT Students' Welfare !

Hyperloop, the “fifth mode of transport”, is a high-speed rail system which

essentially aims to eliminate friction and air drag. Moreover, it

incorporates the use of magnetic levitation of a “pod” moving within a

partially evacuated “tube”, thereby achieving a considerably high speed

which can potentially reach the speed of sound. This mode of transport will

be marked by its immunity to weather, collision-free commute, which can

move at twice the speed of a plane, with low power consumption and energy

storage for 24-hour operations.

Challenge yourself and revolutionize transportation! The Hyperloop VIT

Team, supported by SW, offers a unique opportunity to design and build

magnetically levitated Pods on a global stage. Join a diverse team, develop

your skills, and be inspired by Hyperloop's transformative potential.

Submit your proposal here: https://forms.gle/1jobXznK1K3z92hH7

https://forms.gle/1jobXznK1K3z92hH7

Last Date to Submit the Proposals: 20th March, 2024.

Sample Proposal PPT has been attached for your reference.

There are five distinguished Hyperloop teams from India. These teams, which

have consistently demonstrated India's excellence in various international

competitions, aim to acquaint a diverse Indian audience with the mechanics

of the Hyperloop. Moreover, they seek to provide students and student-led

teams with a blueprint to establish their own Hyperloop ventures. VIT

intends to follow suit by establishing its own Hyperloop team, focused on

similar objectives, dedicated to advancing the technology for competing on

the international stage.

Below are descriptions of the critical technological aspect essential to

the operation of the Hyperloop.

Propulsion: The movement of the pod within the evacuated tube, taking

into account the various factors of magnetic levitation and resistive

forces, is propulsion.

Mechanical Subsystem: This is the subsystem that represents the overall

structure of the pod, right from the chassis to the innards and their

placements, to bring out the max efficiency of the structure.

Control System: It is essentially the brain of the Hyperloop which will

control the overall functioning of the structure by passing essential

commands that navigate the pod.

Power System: This subsystem is essentially responsible for executing the

commands by the Control System of the pod and is vital for the holistic

functioning of the pod as well as the interaction between the pod and the

tube.

Infrastructure: A pivotal addition to the series of subsystems, the

Infrastructure subsystem deals with the development of the tube.

For more information about Hyperloop teams:

National Deworming Day

National Deworming Day is observed all over the nation every year on

February 10 aiming towards eradicating intestinal worms which are also

known as Soil-Transmitted Helminths (STH). It is an initiative of the

Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India to make every

child in the age group of 1-19 years, (enrolled and unenrolled) worm-free.

 

The overarching theme of National Deworming Day 2024 is "Eliminate STH:

Invest in a Healthier Future for Children” and revolves around public

health, with a specific focus on preventing and controlling parasitic worm

infections, particularly in children. The campaign seeks to create

awareness about the impact of parasitic infections on health, education,

and overall socio-economic development.

World Pulses Day

World Pulses Day is celebrated on 10 February every year. According to the

United Nations, this day is dedicated to highlighting the importance of

pulses and their nutritional benefits. This day was established to

emphasise the importance of pulses in mitigating global food challenges,

improving human health, and improving soil health.

This year, the theme for World Pulses Day is "Pulses: Nourishing Soils and

People". The theme emphasises the importance of pulses in improving soil

health and nutrient cycling, which can lead to increased crop productivity

and food security. The theme also highlights the role of pulses in

addressing climate change and promoting environmental sustainability.

Body:
Dear Students,

Applicants must contact the French laboratory or institution on their own.

Call for Applications 2024

The French Institute in India, Embassy of France is accepting applications

for the below scholarship programmes for the academic year 2024

CHARPAK LAB SCHOLARSHIP : Deadline: 13 February, 2024 (23:59 IST)

The students enrolled in an Indian institution at Bachelor’s or Master’s

degree level, planning to undertake a training/research project at a French

higher education institution or laboratory during their academic break

(between May and July) are eligible to apply.

Scholarship inclusions

- monthly stipend of 700 euros

- student visa fee waiver

Applicants must contact the French laboratory or institution on their own

as per their research interests, before applying for the scholarship. For

more information, visit https://www.inde.campusfrance.org/charpak-lab

-scholarship.

CHARPAK MASTER'S SCHOLARSHIP : Deadline: 20 March, 2024 (23:59 IST)

Students or professionals who wish to pursue a master's degree program in

France for one or two years in any discipline are eligible to apply for

this scholarship.

Scholarship inclusions

- Monthly allowance of 860 euros

- Student visa and Etudes en France fee waiver

- Assistance to find affordable student accommodation (priority access to

CROUS residencies, subject to availability)

- Social security

The interested candidates must submit their application on the online

scholarship portal along with the documents listed on the Campus France

India website. For more information, visit

https://www.inde.campusfrance.org/charpak-master-s-scholarship

Note:

- applicants must have applied for admission to a French higher education

institution (study period beginning between September and December 2024)

before starting the scholarship application procedure

- those who have not received the acceptance letter from the French

university before the scholarship deadline, can attach an email

communication or other proof to show that they will receive it later.

For queries, write to scholarship.france@ifindia.in

World Cancer Day

World Cancer Day aims to prevent millions of deaths each year by raising

awareness about cancer, and pressing governments and individuals across the

world to take action against the disease. Between 2022 and 2024, the focus

of World Cancer Day is to help “Close the cancer gap.”

This year marks the third and final year of the campaign. The theme for

this year is “Together, we challenge those in power”. This theme

encompasses the global demand for leaders to prioritize and invest in

cancer prevention and care and to do more to achieve a just and cancer-free

world.

55th Death Anniversary of Dr. C. N. Annadurai

Conjeevaram Natarajan Annadurai (15 September 1909 – 3 February 1969),

popularly known as Anna, also known as Arignar Anna or Perarignar

Anna (Anna, the scholar or Elder Brother), was an

Indian Tamil politician who served as the fourth and last Chief Minister of

Madras State from 1967 until 1969 and first Chief Minister of Tamil

Nadu for 20 days (after Madras State was renamed Tamil Nadu) before his

death.

Annadurai was known as one of the best Tamil orators during his time. He

developed a style in Tamil public speaking using metaphors and pleasing

alliterations, both in spoken and written language. Anna was also best

known for his extempore speaking ability being very well affluent on

rhetoric skills.

World Wetlands Day

2nd February each year is World Wetlands Day to raise global awareness

about the vital role of wetlands for people and our planet. This day also

marks the date of the adoption of the Convention on Wetlands on 2 February

1971, in the Iranian city of Ramsar on the shores of the Caspian Sea.

We are facing a growing freshwater crisis that threatens people and our

planet. We use more freshwater than nature can replenish, and we are

destroying the ecosystem that water and all life depend on most – Wetlands.

The campaign highlights the contribution of wetlands to the quantity and

quality of freshwater on our planet. Water and wetlands are connected in an

inseparable co-existence that is vital to life, our well-being, and the

health of our planet. Wetlands are land areas that are saturated or flooded

with water either permanently or seasonally. Inland wetlands include

marshes, ponds, lakes, fens, rivers, floodplains, and swamps. Coastal

wetlands include saltwater marshes, estuaries, mangroves, lagoons, and even

coral reefs. Fishponds, rice paddies, and saltpans are human-made wetlands

Martyrs' Day

January 30 is observed as the Martyrs' Day every year across the country to

mark the death anniversary of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, popularly known

as Mahatma Gandhi or Bapu. Martyrs' Day or 'Shaheed Diwas' also aims at

paying respect to the freedom fighters who gave up their lives in the fight

for India's independence.

Gandhi died at the spot on January 30, 1948, some five months after India

gained independence from the British. Ever since then, India observes that

day as Shaheed Diwas to mourn the loss of its greatest freedom fighter.

This year, the Central government has directed all state governments and

union ministries to observe two minutes of silence on January 30 in the

memory of martyred freedom fighters.

Subject: GENERAL NOTICE: VIT Students Code of Conduct-reg
Body:
Dear Students/Parents/Guardians,

Greetings from VIT!

GENERAL NOTICE

As we have begun the new semester, I want to take a moment to remind

everyone of the importance of adhering to the student code of conduct. This

code outlines the expectations for student behavior both on and off campus,

and it is essential that we all work together to create a safe and

respectful learning environment.

The student code of conduct covers a wide range of topics, including

academic integrity, misuse of ID card, bullying and harassment,

discrimination, organizing events, social media abuse, making malicious

statements, drug and alcohol use, etc. It is important that you

familiarize yourself with the code so that you understand your

responsibilities as a student.

I encourage you to review the student code of conduct carefully. You can

find it on the VIT website or by clicking here.

https://vit.ac.in/sites/default/files/Student-Code-of-Conduct.pdf

As you know, hostel students are allowed outings for 2 hours on weekdays

and 4 hours on weekends and holidays. Kindly remind the students to avoid

any inappropriate behavior during these outings. Engaging in such behavior

could result in disciplinary action as outlined in the Student Code of

Conduct.

If you have any questions about the student code of conduct, please do not

hesitate to contact me or your proctor.

Thank you for your cooperation.

Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you to today’s [26th January] 

special events.

Republic Day

Republic Day is celebrated on 26 January to commemorate the day the

Constitution of India came into effect. Even though we had gained

independence on 15 August 1947, nascent India did not have its laws which

were drafted and finally adopted in the year 1950. After working for 2

years, 11 months, and 18 days, the draft constitution was prepared by a

committee. The Constituent Assembly then formally adopted it on 26 November

1949. However, the day it came into effect was pushed back two months to 26

January 1950 as it marked the anniversary of the Purna Swaraj Diwas which

was on 26 January 1930. On this day, a resolution demanding “complete

freedom” from the British was drawn.

Every year, a Republic Day parade is held at the Rajpath in New Delhi. The

day begins with the prime minister paying tribute to the soldiers who

sacrificed their lives for the country at the Amar Jawan Jyoti in India

Gate. Colorful tableaus, tank shows, air shows, and bike pyramids are some

of the most famous attractions of the parade.

Happy Republic Day!

LIVE Streaming of VIT Republic Day Celebrations

on our official YouTube Channel.

Subject: Welcome to NPTEL Online Course : Forests and their Management
Body:
Dear Learner
Welcome to SWAYAM-NPTEL Online Courses and Certification!
Thank you for signing up for our online course "
Forests and their Management
"
. We wish you an enjoyable and informative learning experience.
Details regarding the course: 
Name of the course:
 
Forests and their Management
 
Course url:
 
https://onlinecourses.nptel.ac.in/noc24_bt23/preview
Course duration :
 
12 weeks
 
 
 The course will begin on 
22 January 2024
 When content is released on the portal, you will get an email alerting you.
CONTENT AND ASSIGNMENTS
Every week, about 2.5 to 4 hours of videos containing content by the Course instructor will be released along with an assignment based on this. Please watch the lectures, follow the course regularly and submit all assessments and assignments before the due date. Your regular participation is vital for learning and doing well in the course. This will be done week on week through the duration of the course.
Please do the assignments yourself and even if you take help, kindly try to learn from it. These assignment will help you prepare for the final exams. Plagiarism and violating the Honor code will be taken very seriously if detected during the submission of assignments. 
ANNOUNCEMENT AND DISCUSSION GROUPS TO CLEAR DOUBTS:
The announcement group - will only have messages from course instructors and teaching assistants - regarding the lessons, assignments, exam registration, hall tickets etc. 
The discussion forum (Ask a question tab on the portal) - is for everyone to ask questions and interact.Anyone who knows the answers can reply to anyone's post and the course instructor/TA will also respond to your queries. Please make maximum use of this feature as this will help you learn much better.
If you have any questions regarding the exam, registration, hall tickets, results, queries related to the technical content in the lectures, any doubts in the assignments, etc can be posted in the forum section
TO GET A CERTIFICATE - PROCESS AND CRITERIA:
The course is free to enroll and learn from. But if you want a certificate, you have to register and write the proctored exam conducted by us in person at any of the designated exam centres.
The exam is optional for a fee of Rs 1000/- (Rupees one thousand only).
Date and Time of Exams: 
27 April 2024
 Morning session 9am to 12 noon; Afternoon Session 2pm to 5pm.
Registration url: Announcements will be made when the registration form is open for registrations.
The online registration form has to be filled and the certification exam fee needs to be paid. More details will be made available when the exam registration form is published. If there are any changes, it will be mentioned then.
Please check the form for more details on the cities where the exams will be held, the conditions you agree to when you fill the form etc.
CRITERIA TO GET A CERTIFICATE
Average assignment score = 25% of average of best 8 assignments out of the total 12 assignments given in the course. 
Exam score = 75% of the proctored certification exam score out of 100
Final score = Average assignment score + Exam score
YOU WILL BE ELIGIBLE FOR A CERTIFICATE ONLY IF AVERAGE ASSIGNMENT SCORE >=10/25 AND EXAM SCORE >= 30/75. If one of the 2 criteria is not met, you will not get the certificate even if the Final score >= 40/100.
Certificate will have your name, photograph and the score in the final exam with the breakup.It will have the logos of NPTEL and IIT Kanpur .It will be e-verifiable at 
nptel.ac.in/noc
.
Only the e-certificate will be made available. Hard copies will not be dispatched.
Once again, thanks for your interest in our online courses and certification. Happy learning. 
- NPTEL team

Every year, January 25 is celebrated as the National Tourism Day in India.

This day has been marked by the government in order to promote tourism in

role of tourism in the country and how it plays a crucial role in the

Indian economy. India is a diverse country and is filled with the alluring

beauty of culture and history. Every state has its own different cultures

and diversification.

National Tourism Day is a glorious day in India’s history. Our country has

a special place all over the world because of its beautiful tourist

destinations. The terrain, language, and the way of living changes here

every few kilometres. National Tourism Day is celebrated every year to

acknowledge this beautiful diversity.

National Voters' Day

National Girl Child Day

National Girl Child Day was first initiated in 2008 by the Ministry of

Women and Child Development. The purpose of this day is to spread awareness

about the gender-based discrimination that girls face in our society and to

bring change in the attitude towards girls. The objective behind

celebrating the National Girl Child Day is to provide support and

opportunities to the girls of India. It also aims towards promoting

awareness about the rights of the girl child and to increase awareness on

the importance of girl education, and their health and nutrition.

The Indian government has taken several steps over the years to change this

and improve the conditions of girls. Several campaigns and programs such as

Save the Girl Child, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, free or subsidized education

for the girl children, reservations for women in colleges and universities

have been initiated to reduce this discrimination. Starting from female

infanticide to gender inequality to sexual abuse, there is no dearth of

issues. The main objective behind this is to highlight the inequalities

faced by girls, to promote awareness including the rights of a girl child,

the importance of education, health, and nutrition. Nowadays also gender

Dear VITians,

and secured the 3rd position at the Tata Technologies Innovent Hackathon

on 18th January 2024 in Pune. They won a cash prize of Rs. 50,000/- and a

paid internship, including a Full-Time Employment offer from Tata

facilitating expedited charging. Leveraging VRFB technology not only

benefits, enhancing the novelty of the solution.

Subject: Student Achievement by Team Future Fits in the Smart India Hackathon - Reg.
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are happy to share that our student Team Future Fits participated in the

Smart India Hackathon and emerged winners in the Problem Statement SIH1451

at the grand finale held at Noida Institute of Engineering and Technology.

The problem statement required the team to develop an AI/ML tool capable of

detecting compromises in various networking devices, such as firewalls,

routers, and servers with a specific emphasis on moving beyond the

traditional reliance on Indicators of Compromise (IoCs). The team proposed

a Comprehensive Threat Detection Framework. This innovative solution

leverages eBPF technology for real-time data monitoring across the

aforementioned devices and incorporates six specialized agents, each

equipped with machine learning models. These agents focus on monitoring

system calls, network flows, IP addresses, DNS queries, ransomware

behaviors, and correlated anomalies. The framework also integrates a

whitelisting feature for continuous improvement, allowing administrators to

refine threat detection models. This comprehensive approach, along with a

user-friendly web application, establishes an effective and adaptive system

to ensure the security of networks.

Team Members:

Parakram Diwas

Parakram Diwas (Bravery Day) is celebrated in India on 23 January. It was

introduced by the Government of India in 2021 to celebrate Netaji Subhas

Chandra Bose's 125th birth anniversary. Parakram Diwas will be celebrated

'in order to honor and remember Netaji's indomitable spirit and selfless

service to the nation'. Parakram Diwas is celebrated to inspire people of

this country, especially the youth, to act with fortitude in the face of

adversity as Netaji did, and to infuse in them a spirit of patriotic fervor.

Of the many freedom fighters who laid their lives for the country's cause,

Subhash Chandra Bose is one of those that is fondly remembered by the

Indians. Popularly known as 'Netaji', he was born on January 23, 1897. His

aim was simple: to get India the much-needed independence. Despite his

differences, it was the ultimate goal of freedom that did not deter him

from that path.

Essay Writing Competition (Tamil)

Topic: Thiruvalluvarin Tamizh (திருவள்ளூவரின் தமிழ்)

Thiruvalluvar was a renowned Tamil poet-philosopher who is best known for

his work, the Thirukkural. He is considered one of the greatest Tamil poets

and his work is highly respected in Tamil culture. Thiruvalluvar's life and

times are not well-known, and there are many different accounts of his

life. However, it is generally believed that he lived sometime between the

3rd century BCE and the 5th century CE. He is said to have been born in

Mylapore, a suburb of present-day Chennai, India.

The Thirukkural is a collection of 1330 couplets that are divided into

three parts: Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth), and Inbam (love). The text

covers a wide range of topics, including ethics, politics, economics, and

love. The Thirukkural is known for its wisdom and its insights into human

nature. It has been translated into many languages and is considered one of

the most important works of Tamil literature.

Despite Tiruvalluvar’s reasonable tone, many of his ideas were

revolutionary. He dismissed the caste system: “One is not great because of

one’s birth in a noble family; one is not low because of one’s low birth.”

The poet maintained that goodness is its own reward and should not be

regarded as a mere means to a comfortable afterlife.

Thiruvalluvar says that the only indestructible wealth is education. He

says a person who shuns learning is akin to an animal. Comparing those who

read with those who do not is not an appropriate comparison, for how can

one compare man and beast?

Calling all writers! Share your insights on "Thiruvalluvarin Tamizh" in a

regarded as a mere means to a comfortable afterlife.

Subject: Academic Regulations on Attendance Requirements - Reg.
Body:
Dear Students,

Greetings.

 - A student is expected to maintain 100% attendance in all courses.

 - A student may need leave due to ill health or to attend some family

 emergency, a student is permitted to maintain an attendance of 75% (i.e.

 absent for 25% of instructional hours) in each course, without producing

 any proof for the absence.

 - This 25% absence includes medical, personnel, casual, official leave

 of absence for organizing events/ seminars/ workshops/ technical/ cultural

 festivals/competitions/ participation in co-curricular/ extra-curricular

 events/ NSS & NCC camps and any other (valid or otherwise) reason. 

 - A computerized attendance monitoring system is adopted for posting the

 attendance by the faculty.

 - Since no one is exempted from the minimum attendance conditions

 stipulated below, students who fail to maintain the minimum attendance

 criteria will not be permitted to write the next evaluation component of

 the course (CAT/FAT Exam component fixed by the course faculty in case of

 courses) and they will be considered as ‘debarred from writing the exam’.

 - The attendance software shall indicate the student status of that exam

 component as ‘Debarred’ once the student crosses below the minimum

 attendance requirement.

 - Students who are ‘debarred’ from writing the FAT component of a course

 shall be awarded an “N2” grade and they have to re-register the course

 again and clear with a performance grade.

 - The attendance percentage will be calculated from the ‘date of

 registration’ into a course to one day before the start of the exam

 component.

 - To encourage students to attend seminars, conferences, workshops,

 training programmes, short-duration courses offered by specialized

 institutions, etc. who otherwise shy off availing of such benefits due to

 losing attendance in various courses, students having a CGPA of 9.00

 and above (CGPA ≥ 9.00) and with no current backlog courses are exempted

 from the minimum attendance requirements. 

 - It is expected that these students will continue to attend all the

 classes without absence and will not take this as an advantage to skip

 classes.

 - If such students’ CGPA falls below 9.00, they will be subjected to the

 minimum attendance requirements again.

 - For this purpose, the nine-pointer list will be dynamically generated

 and applied at the time of preparation of the debarred list of each exam

 component (CAT/FAT) of a course.

Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you to today’s Special Event.

Thiruvalluvar Day: Essay Writing Competition (Tamil)

Topic: Thiruvalluvarin Tamizh (திருவள்ளூவரின் தமிழ்)

Thiruvalluvar was a renowned Tamil poet-philosopher who is best known for

his work, the Thirukkural. He is considered one of the greatest Tamil poets

and his work is highly respected in Tamil culture. Thiruvalluvar's life and

times are not well-known, and there are many different accounts of his

life. However, it is generally believed that he lived sometime between the

3rd century BCE and the 5th century CE. He is said to have been born in

Mylapore, a suburb of present-day Chennai, India.

The Thirukkural is a collection of 1330 couplets that are divided into

three parts: Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth), and Inbam (love). The text

covers a wide range of topics, including ethics, politics, economics, and

love. The Thirukkural is known for its wisdom and its insights into human

nature. It has been translated into many languages and is considered one of

the most important works of Tamil literature.

Despite Tiruvalluvar’s reasonable tone, many of his ideas were

revolutionary. He dismissed the caste system: “One is not great because of

one’s birth in a noble family; one is not low because of one’s low birth.”

The poet maintained that goodness is its own reward and should not be

regarded as a mere means to a comfortable afterlife.

Thiruvalluvar says that the only indestructible wealth is education. He

says a person who shuns learning is akin to an animal. Comparing those who

read with those who do not is not an appropriate comparison, for how can

one compare man and beast?

Calling all writers! Share your insights on "Thiruvalluvarin Tamizh" in a

500-word essay.

Subject: Wishing you all a happy Lohri, Pongal, Makar Sankranti, and Bihu!
Body:
Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare wishes you all a Happy Lohri, Pongal, Makar

Sankranti, and Bihu!

Lohri, Pongal, Makar Sankranti and Bihu are festivals that represent

different cultures but unite under one country – India. All the festivals

are loosely related to one single premise – crops, but vary depending on

the part of the country it is celebrated in. Let’s look at each of these

four festivals that people celebrate together.

Pongal, the four-day harvest festival celebrated in South India, especially

Tamil Nadu, will be celebrated with great enthusiasm from January 15-18

this year. Celebrated in mid-January every year, it also marks the

beginning of Uttarayan- the sun's journey towards the north and the end of

the winter season.

A large bonfire with people dancing, singing, and having a good time is

what contains the essence of this festival. Lohri is celebrated a day

before Makar Sankranti and is primarily celebrated in North India,

especially in the agricultural state of Punjab. It marks the end of the

sowing season. Delicacies and snacks, for example, Rewri, Peanuts, Sarson

Ka Saag, Makke Ki Roti, etc., are enjoyed with full vigor.

Makar Sankranti follows Lohri by a day and is a popular festival in most

parts of the country, but the festivity is at its prime, mainly in North

India. The festival marks the advent of the harvest season and also

signifies the end of Winter as the days start getting longer. Many people

dip in the sacred waters of the Ganga and offer their prayers to the Sun.

In many parts of North India, kites take over the skies, and delicious

sweets such as Til Ke Laddoo are enjoyed.

The same spirit and the same premise, when it travels all the way to North

East India, takes the shape of Magh Bihu. The end of the harvest season is

what the festival represents. Traditional dance, traditional games, and

activities such as Cooking in Meji (Bamboo Huts) define the festival in the

state of Assam.

Body:
Dear Student,

Best Wishes !!! The procedure to be followed for Medical/Emergency Leave.

 1. For any kind of leave, students are advised to use the permitted 25%

 relaxation in attendance, including medical reasons, and a minimum of 75%

 is mandatory to appear for the exams.

 2. In case of emergency (Medical reasons / Hospitalization / Death in

 the family), the first intimation must be given to the proctor. Then,

 the request must be sent to the Head of the Department (hod.ss@vit.ac.in

 <hod.ss@vit.ac.in>) recommended by Proctor with a copy to the

 Programme Secretary (secretary.ss@vit.ac.in).

 3. If he/she has been admitted to the hospital as an inpatient due to

 medical reasons, they have to submit their discharge summary, fitness

 certificate, and hospital bills along with a request letter signed by the

 Proctor and HoD to the Programme Secretary in SJT322 within three days

 after rejoining or before the last working day whichever is early.

 4. For Re-CAT, the documents shall be submitted to the Programme

 Secretary and signed by the Proctor. Medical prescriptions are not

 considered under any circumstances. The reFAT is permitted based on CoE

 norms (refer to reFAT norms mail sent by CoE).

 5. Medical leaves will not be updated on VTOP. Instead, based on the

 nature of the request, the school-level committee will decide whether to

 permit or reject the request for Attendance Relaxation for appearing on the

 Exam.

 6. After a medical leave request, a student is expected to attend all

 the classes regularly and if absences are found at later stages, then

 medical leave will not be considered.

He saw hope for the future in every child and believed that “muscles of

Subject: Today's Special Event by SW Office : Pravasi Bharatiya Divas'24 Celebration - Reg.
Body:
Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare is celebrating the 18th Pravasi Bharatiya

Divas today. Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD) has been celebrated on 9th

January every year since 2003 to mark the contribution of the Overseas

Indian community in the development of India. January 9 was chosen as the

day to celebrate this occasion since it was on this day in 1915 that

Mahatma Gandhi, the greatest Pravasi, returned to India from South Africa,

led India’s freedom struggle and changed the lives of Indians forever. The

Embassy of India in Oslo commemorated the 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas in

Lier on January 6, 2024, celebrating the stories of the first-generation

Pravasis in Drammen and Lier. Over 150 people attended, engaging in

interactive panel discussions and enjoying bhangra dance.

Wishing you a joyous Pravasi Bharatiya Divas 2024! May this celebration

bring you closer to your roots and fill your heart with happiness. Cheers

to the global Indian community! May the bonds that connect us across

borders grow stronger, and may your journey be filled with success and

prosperity. Join us in the celebration!

Date: 09 Jan, 2024

Time: 06:00 PM onwards

Venue: Greenos

All are invited!

Subject: Student Achievement at Shaastra, IIT Madras - Reg.
Body:
Dear VITians,

We are pleased to inform you that 2 Student Teams from VIT Team Veloce,

under the ASME Projects procured First and Second Runner-Up positions

in the Airbus Flight Challenge 2024, held at Shaastra, IIT Madras.

Airbus Flight Challenge focused on formulating a mathematical model for

aircraft parked on an incline, as observed in certain airports like

Courchevel Altiport, among others. In the event that the pilot neglects to

apply brakes and the plane begins to roll downhill, the objective is to

determine its critical velocity and center of gravity just before it

initiates an upward pitch.

Team 1: First Position with Cash award of Rs 25,000/-

Solution: The team's approach involved addressing the scenario of an

aircraft on an incline without brakes or wheel chocks. They focussed on

determining the minimum velocity required for rear-wheel braking to prompt

the aircraft to pitch up. To achieve this, the team meticulously gathered

aircraft-specific data for an A350-900 (weight, CG position, braking

performance). They formulated dynamic equations that account for

gravitational forces and braking effects and translated these into MATLAB

for computational analysis.

Team Members:

 1. Ramanesh S - 20BME0271

 2. Sudarshan G - 21BME0151

 3. Daksh Oli - 22BME0123

Team 2: Second Runner Up Position with Cash award of Rs 10,000/-

Solution: They developed a mathematical model with an integrated real

time physics solver (Body Dynamics) and computer vision into on board

control systems. The model is capable of determining instantaneous critical

velocity, slope angle of runway and also predicts future critical

velocities and slopes down the runway. The Hough Transform & Canny edge

detection system was used in the model.

Team Members:

 1. Aditya Kothari - 21BME0578

 2. Aditya Kunte - 21BME0055

 3. Souvik Mukherjee - 21BEC0345

Congratulations and Best Wishes to the teams!

Body:
Dear Students

A gentle reminder...

TODAY IS THE LAST DATE FOR PAPER SEEING (FRESHERS). THIS DATE CANNOT BE

EXTENDED UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES.

 Office of the Controller of Examinations

 Ref.No. : VIT/CoE/2024/24002

 Date: 04-January-2024

Paper Seeing, Revaluation and Re-FAT Process for 

Fall 2023-24 Freshers (except Freshers 3Yr Programme / B.Sc – Agri /

B.Des) FAT – Theory 

 Paper Seeing and Revaluation:

· In the VTop student login, (“Examination → Marks → Fall

Semester 2023-24”) Marks for the Courses to which FAT was held during Dec

2023 has been made available now.

· Actual Grades will be released on 10 January 2024 (Wednesday).

The Pass criteria and Grading Procedure are available in Academics →

Regulations

Tab in your login.

· If you want to know the question wise marks awarded to your

answers by the evaluator, you need to apply for it through V-Top. This is

referred as “Paper Seeing” process. It requires payment of Rs. 100 for each

paper. You can apply through: Examinations →Papersee/Rev → Fall

Semester 2023-24→Paper Seeing. You can choose course(s) you want to

apply for paper seeing. After Generating the Invoice, you need to make a

payment through “Online Payments” Tab in the same V-Top login.

· Once you have paid, within one or two working days, the

paper and question

wise marks awarded will be made available in CodeTantra login. You need

to use the same portal https://vit.codetantra.com for this process. After

seeing the paper, if you feel the mark awarded to a particular question is

not sufficient and the evaluator has missed something and there is a need

to recheck the mark, then you can apply for Revaluation of the Course. You

need to give suitable reason for the same in the comments section available

just below the mark awarded by the faculty.

· Please note that the Revaluation has to be applied only in V-Top

(in the same way as you have applied for paper seeing) and necessary

payments also needs to be paid through online payments tab. (Rs. 300 per

paper).

· Also note that “Paper seeing” and Revaluation is applicable only

for the Theory Courses to which FAT was conducted by CoE office . For other

components and Courses (like Laboratory / Project Courses IBL mode courses)

there is No Paper seeing and Revaluation Process.

· Actual Grades will be released after the completion of

“Paper-Seeing” and Revaluation Registration Processes. The links for Paper

seeing and Revaluation payments have been enabled in VTop Students login.

Paper seeing and feedback / comments are mandatory for re-evaluation and

is in online mode only.

Particulars

Dates

Paper seeing registration link / payment [per paper Rs. 100]

 04- Jan -2024 to 08- Jan -2024

Revaluation registration link / payment [per paper Rs. 300]

05- Jan -2024 to 09- Jan -2024

Paper Seeing in https://vit.codetantra.com/

https://vit.codetantra.com/

05- Jan -2024 to 09- Jan -2024

 Once the Paper seeing request is approved, the evaluated copy of answer

sheets would be made available in CodeTantra as per the above

schedule. Use your VTop login credentials for login.

· After login, follow the instructions given in the platform for

giving comments to the questions which needs to be re-examined.

· Give your feedback with respect to the need for revaluation. If

no feedback is given for any question, your answer script will not be

considered for revaluation and No refund will be given for any approved

requests.

· Students should not approach or give any sort of request to any

faculty related to revaluation (increase of marks or grades). If we

receive any complaints from faculty, it will be treated as ‘Malpractice’

and revaluation request will summarily be rejected.

Re-FAT:

As per VIT Academic regulations (Page 22) Re-FAT will be permitted for the

following reasons only:

S. No.

Description

Supporting Evidence(s) Required

1.

Calamity in the family [Death of father / mother / own brother / sister]

Death certificate or Prior communication to the Proctors

2.

Hospitalization of the student

(for in-patient treatment only)

Medical Certificate, Investigation Report, Bills and Discharge Summary.

· Eligible students should apply in VTop student login (

Examination > Re-Exam Application) between 11th January 2024 and 25th

January 2024 and upload the necessary evidences.

· Re-FAT requests will be scrutinized by the School Dean and then

by the ‘Re‐examinations Committee’. If needed the student may be asked to

appear before the Committee for presenting the case.

· For the ReFAT approved courses the Grade assigned will be

converted to “---“ by February end. ReFAT will be scheduled along with

the Winter 2023-24 Regular Arrear and the Winter/Regular Arrear Process

will be followed for Re-FAT.

· Any student who fails to apply for Re‐FAT through VTop will NOT

be considered for further processing and has to repeat the course(s) by

registering again in subsequent semesters. 

· Please note that this process is only for getting approval for

Re-FAT. After it is approved, students need to register in Arrear / Re-FAT

Tab for registering the course when it is permitted. The schedule will be

available only in Arrear/ Tab. If someone misses the approved Re-FAT, no

second chance will be given and it will be treated as absent accordingly

grade will be published.

Guidelines for course registration and evaluation process

# Students are advised to check the curriculum and plan accordingly.

For the students of B. Tech Core Programmes, this project type course will

be considered under Programme Elective Category and for the students of

"Specialization Programmes", it will be considered under "Open Elective

Category". If the students of "Specialization Programmes" have already

earned sufficient credits under "Open Elective Category", then it is not

necessary to register for this project type course.

# Students are expected to form a team and identify a faculty guide

from any School to initiate the process.

# Project Team should comprise a minimum of two to a maximum of five

students only from any B. Tech Programme of any School / Five Year

Integrated Programme as applicable. (students of B. Tech Programme and Five

Year Integrated Programme can not be in the same team)

# Domain specific / Interdisciplinary / Multidisciplinary /

Cross-disciplinary projects are encouraged.

# Guide will finalize the tentative title / area of the work and

the team of students to work on each project. Course Registration is opened

on VTOP Login for the faculty members (Guide). (Preliminary discussion

between the guide and the student is essential)

# Students can work for one project type course at any point of

time.

# Course Registration will be done by the respective Guide only. The

Guide will fill in the necessary data (Project title and the Registration

Number of all the students proposed to work on each of the projects) on

VTOP Faculty Login.

# Subsequently the course will reflect on the list of registered

courses for that particular semester on VTOP Student Login. This three

credit course will not affect the upper limit of 27 credits allowed for a

regular semester.

# Minimum duration of the project period is six months and the

maximum duration is 12 months.

# Once the Project work is completed and a tangible

outcome (Research / Review Paper published / accepted in Scopus / WoS,

Journal / Conference Proceedings: Product Design / Patent Application) is

reached, the Guide will post the marks out of 100 for each student on VTOP

and submit.

# Absolute Grading System will be followed for the listed project

type courses as per VIT Grading Policy

# Even after 12 months, if the team fails to complete the project,

then the course will be de-registered for the students.

strategic prowess by presenting innovative marketing strategies for

existing products and brands. The competition challenged participants to

redefine these products while preserving their core essence. Participants

engaged in a formal presentation format, addressing a judge panel that

Subject: Additional Learning Concept _ reopened from Winter 2023 - 24 onwards
Body:
Dear All,

The provision for awarding marks to the students under “Additional

Learning” component will be enabled on “VTOP Faculty Login” from the

forthcoming Winter 2023 -24 onwards. The required details are provided

below:

In order to make student learning capabilities more meaningful and activity

oriented, programmes like Hack-a-thons, Make-a-thons and other similar

activities

can be conducted on campus. In order to integrate this in academics,

additional marks can be awarded to the student by the faculty after due

assessment of the performance of the student. The student can get benefitted

by such additional marks, to a maximum of 20, which can be added to the CAM

score for one course per semester. Allotment of such additional marks is

subject to conditions that (1) the activity should have been scheduled for at

least 24 continuous hours, (2) monitored by the faculty who is offering the

course related to the activity, (3) the team size should not be more than

three and (4) the assessment done in one semester cannot be used / forwarded

to the subsequent semesters. The allotment of the marks may vary from 5

(just participation) – 20 (prize winner) depending on the involvement and

output of the student in the event as per the details given below. The

faculty handling the course will award the marks based on the performance

of the student. If a student wishes to do a project in courses and results

with tangible output can also be considered for additional marks.

Participation throughout the event and active involvement

5 Marks

Tangible output/result producers

10 Marks

Considerable amount of creative input in the outcome

15 Marks

Prize/award winners of the event

20 Marks

In any case, prior approval from the faculty handling the course and the

School Dean is essential for the inclusion of additional marks for such

categories. This additional learning is course specific. It is the

responsibility of the School to make sure that additional marks are

allotted to only one course for a specified activity. The total internal

marks (including the additional marks) is given an upper limit of 60 (40

being the marks given to the final assessment test).

Mere performance of routine experiments should not be considered for

additional marks.

Attending “online Courses”, “Workshops / Seminars” organized by any

institute are not to be considered for additional marks.

Since the award of marks is a sensitive matter, any violation of the

academic regulations will be viewed seriously. Moreover, the faculty

members may also note that the “Additional Learning” is only an option and

it is at the discretion of the respective faculty members to use this

component for awarding marks.

with regards

M. Anthony Xavior PhD

Body:
Office of the Controller of Examinations

Paper Seeing, Revaluation and Re-FAT Process for 

Fall 2023-24 (Seniors & Freshers 3Yr Programme / B.Sc – Agri / B.Des)

FAT – Theory 

 Paper Seeing and Revaluation:

· In the VTop student login, (“Examination → Marks → Fall

Semester 2023-24”) Marks for the Courses to which FAT was held during Nov-Dec

2023 has been made available now.

· Actual Grades will be released on 03 January 2024 (Wednesday).

The Pass criteria and Grading Procedure are available in Academics →

Regulations

Tab in your login.

· If you want to know the question wise marks awarded to your

answers by the evaluator, you need to apply for it through V-Top. This is

referred as “Paper Seeing” process. It requires payment of Rs. 100 for each

paper. You can apply through: Examinations →Papersee/Rev → Fall

Semester 2023-24→Paper Seeing. You can choose course(s) you want to

apply for paper seeing. After Generating the Invoice, you need to make a

payment through “Online Payments” Tab in the same V-Top login.

· Once you have paid, within one or two working days, the

paper and question

wise marks awarded will be made available in CodeTantra login. You need

to use the same portal https://vit.codetantra.com for this process. After

seeing the paper, if you feel the mark awarded to a particular question is

not sufficient and the evaluator has missed something and there is a need

to recheck the mark, then you can apply for Revaluation of the Course. You

need to give suitable reason for the same in the comments section available

just below the mark awarded by the faculty.

· Please note that the Revaluation has to be applied only in V-Top

(in the same way as you have applied for paper seeing) and necessary

payments also needs to be paid through online payments tab. (Rs. 300 per

paper).

· Also note that “Paper seeing” and Revaluation is applicable only

for the Theory Courses to which FAT was conducted by CoE office . For other

components and Courses (like Laboratory / Project Courses IBL mode courses)

there is No Paper seeing and Revaluation Process.

· Actual Grades will be released after the completion of

“Paper-Seeing” and Revaluation Registration Processes. The links for Paper

seeing and Revaluation payments have been enabled in VTop Students login.

Paper seeing and feedback / comments are mandatory for re-evaluation and

is in online mode only.

Particulars

Dates

Paper seeing registration link / payment [per paper Rs. 100]

 29- Dec-2023 to 01- Jan -2024

Revaluation registration link / payment [per paper Rs. 300]

29- Dec -2023 to 02- Jan -2024

Paper Seeing in https://vit.codetantra.com/

https://vit.codetantra.com/

29- Dec -2023 to 02- Jan -2024

 Once the Paper seeing request is approved, the evaluated copy of answer

sheets would be made available in CodeTantra as per the above

schedule. Use your VTop login credentials for login.

· After login, follow the instructions given in the platform for

giving comments to the questions which needs to be re-examined.

· Give your feedback with respect to the need for revaluation. If

no feedback is given for any question, your answer script will not be

considered for revaluation and No refund will be given for any approved

requests.

· Students should not approach or give any sort of request to any

faculty related to revaluation (increase of marks or grades). If we

receive any complaints from faculty, it will be treated as ‘Malpractice’

and revaluation request will summarily be rejected.

Re-FAT:

As per VIT Academic regulations (Page 22) Re-FAT will be permitted for the

following reasons only:

S. No.

Description

Supporting Evidence(s) Required

1.

Calamity in the family [Death of father / mother / own brother / sister]

Death certificate or Prior communication to the Proctors

2.

Hospitalization of the student

Medical Certificate, Investigation Report, Bills and Discharge Summary.

· Eligible students should apply in VTop student login (

Examination > Re-Exam Application) between 8th January 2024 and 19th

January 2024 and upload the necessary evidences.

· Re-FAT requests will be scrutinized by the School Dean and then

by the ‘Re‐examinations Committee’. If needed the student may be asked to

appear before the Committee for presenting the case.

· For the ReFAT approved courses the Grade assigned will be

converted to “---“ by February end. ReFAT will be scheduled along with

the Winter 2023-24 Regular Arrear and the Winter/Regular Arrear Process

will be followed for Re-FAT.

· Any student who fails to apply for Re‐FAT through VTop will NOT

be considered for further processing and has to repeat the course(s) by

registering again in subsequent semesters. 

· Please note that this process is only for getting approval for

Re-FAT. After it is approved, students need to register in Arrear / Re-FAT

Tab for registering the course when it is permitted. The schedule will be

available only in Arrear/ Tab. If someone misses the approved Re-FAT, no

second chance will be given and it will be treated as absent accordingly

grade will be published.

International Day of Epidemic Preparedness

The International Day of Epidemic Preparedness, celebrated on December

27th, raises awareness about staying ready for disease outbreaks and

working together to keep people safe. The first-ever International Day of

Epidemic Preparedness, held on 27 December 2020, was called for by the UN

General Assembly to advocate the importance of preventing, preparedness for

and partnering against epidemics.

As exemplified by the ongoing coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic major

infectious diseases and epidemics have devastating impacts on human lives,

wreaking havoc on long-term social and economic development. Global health

crises threaten to overwhelm already overstretched health systems, disrupt

global supply chains and cause disproportionate devastation of the

livelihoods of people, including women and children, and the economies of

the poorest and most vulnerable countries.

National Consumer Rights Day

Understanding consumer rights remains pivotal in today's market landscape.

While marketplaces ideally operate on ethical principles, consumers may

face exploitation without adequate awareness of their rights. Every year,

National Consumer Rights Day is observed on December 24.

In 1986, the Consumer Protection Act was passed and received the assent of

the President on December 24. Since then, National Consumer Rights Day has

been celebrated on this day to commemorate the occasion. The Consumer

Protection Act acts to protect consumers from defective goods, negligent

services, and unfair trade practices.

National Farmers' Day

Kisan Diwas or National Farmers' Day is observed on December 23, the birth

anniversary of Chaudhary Charan Singh, the fifth prime minister of India.

Born into a farmer's family, Chaudhary Charan Singh was known for his

farmer-friendly policies. He was the prime minister between July 1979 and

January 1980. During his short time as prime minister, Chaudhary Charan

Singh worked hard for the welfare of Indian farmers. He introduced several

welfare schemes for the farmers. The government, in 2001, decided to mark

Charan Singh's birth anniversary as Kisan Diwas.

Kisan Diwas is a day to remember the role of Indian farmers in the economy.

Chaudhary Charan Singh played a key role in bringing the issues of small

and marginal farmers to the forefront. He always fought and stood for

farmers' rights.

Body:
Dear VITians,

“Peering from some high window, at the gold of November sunset and feeling

that if day has to become night, this is a beautiful way.” — E. E. Cummings

November is the season of gratitude, stirring a reflective energy that

inspires us to cherish each moment of dwindling daylight and the soothing

cool breeze.

The Student Council was formally inaugurated on the 8th of November, 2023.

Shri. Abash Kumar, DGP/Director, Fire and Rescue Services TamilNadu, the

Chief Guest of the event, shared his experiences as a student leader and

his further journey in professional development. The Student Council

members took the oath affirming their commitment to serve with diligence

and integrity.

A heritage visit was organised for the international students, offering a

deeper glimpse into the city's rich history and vibrant culture. The

students visited the famous Golden Temple, Vellore Fort and Natarajan

Temple and thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

Quanta 2023, the Annual Expo of the Clubs and Chapters saw a huge

attendance of students who had gathered to know more about the various

Clubs & Chapters in VIT. The CC members also pitched in about their

respective team activities with great enthusiasm.

Cricket is not just a game, it's a religion in India. VIT witnessed the

same on the 19th of November, as we organised a LIVE screening of the ICC

Men's Cricket World Cup Finals. The atmosphere was electric as supporters

of both teams filled the auditorium with cheers and chants. Though India's

loss was a bit disappointing, the event saw new friendships blossom.

In commemoration of the late Smt. Rajeswari Viswanathan's death

anniversary, the NSS Cell and Red Ribbon Club of VIT Vellore organized a

blood donation drive on November 21st, 2023. The event drew an impressive

turnout, with 561 registered donors, and 443 individuals generously donated

their blood.

The Fourth Edition of PRIMAVERA was organised in the month of November. The

event showcased the budding talents of VIT in dance, music, poetry,

painting and photography. The Finale was graced by chief guest Ms. Lalasa

Rachpudi of the Telugu Indian Idol fame, who performed some popular movie

songs.

To read about more such events and activities, check out our newsletter!

National Mathematics Day

National Mathematics Day is celebrated every year on December 22, honoring

the birth anniversary of mathematical genius Srinivasa Ramanujan. Before he

died at the age of just 32 from tuberculosis, he had already given the

world around 3500 mathematical formulae that scientists have still not been

able to completely prove. The main objective behind celebrating the day is

to raise awareness among people about the importance of mathematics for the

development of humanity.

The legendary mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan made extraordinary

contributions to mathematical analysis, number theory, infinite series &

continued fractions. From compiling over 3900 mathematical results and

equations to getting discoveries named after him, his numerous assertions

in mathematics opened up new vistas of mathematical research. He was a

self-taught mathematician who made extraordinary contributions to the world

of mathematics, S Ramanujan was one of the most influential mathematicians

of his time.

Subject: Google | Solution Challenge 2024 | Are you ready?
Body:
Hello,

2024 Solution Challenge

https://developers.google.com/community/gdsc-solution-challenge is a

global annual competition for university students to solve for one or more

of the United Nations 17 Sustainable Development Goals

https://developers.google.com/community/gdsc-solution-challenge/UN-goals

using Google Technology. We would like to invite student developers to

participate in the same. We encourage you to spread the word ahead in your

network of student developers.

Here are few steps to participate in the challenge :

December 1st, 2023 - January 20, 2024

After registration

January 04, 2023 - January 20, 2024

January 21, 2024 to February 22, 2024

Step 1 : Register

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSftGdrvD-r-X2QcyeYt82EP_7xPxZ_TwmMWItyrGc-7l_7PtQ/viewform

and showcase your interests.

Remember to join a GDSC Club as a member https://gdsc.community.dev/ to

International Migrants Day

The United Nations General Assembly in the year 1999 created the

International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant

Workers and Members of their Families. But on December 04, 2000, keeping

account of the large and increasing number of migrants across the globe,

December 18 was decided as International Migrants' Day.

International Migrants Day was created to commemorate the importance of

strengthening international cooperation and migration bilaterally,

regionally, and globally. The day plays a significant role in determining

the movement of people due to voluntary or forced movements for

environmental issues like disaster and poverty. The various factors that

result in the characteristics and scale of migration in the present and the

future have created the issue of migration.
