Subject: Viksit Bharat@2047: Voice of Youth
Body:
Dear VITians,

Viksit Bharat@2047 is the vision of the Government of India to make India a

developed nation by 2047, the 100th year of its independence. The vision

encompasses various aspects of development, including economic growth,

social progress, environmental sustainability and good governance.

Therefore, it is important to channelise the innovative ideas of the youth

into nation-building by inviting them to ideate and contribute to the

vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047. It is important that every youth takes

part in this important nation building exercise. As part of the Viksit

Bharat@204, the Govt. of India invites ideas/feedback for Viksit Bharat.

Please follow the following steps while submitting your feedback:

 - Visit the Viksit Bharat section in the MyGov Portal.

Link:

https://innovateindia.mygov.in/viksitbharat2047/

 https://innovateindia.mygov.in/viksitbharat2047/ Or Scan the

 Following

QR Code: 

 - Answer the following questions sequentially on the Portal:

- How should a Viksit Bharat look like in 2047 in different aspects? -

 What do we need to do to reach this goal? - What can you do to make

 ViksitBharat@2047 possible? 

 - Provide the idea for the Viksit Bharat @ 2047 and mention about your

 role/ contribution towards making India a developed nation.

 - Submit the form along with your email ID and download the Certificate

 from your email.

 - Share your experience and your thoughts, pictures with certificates on

 Social Media with #Ideas4ViksitBharat

 - Students can upload the Selfie with the specific background/

 ViksitBharat @ 2047 banner (digital banner available in SW Office) showing

 participation in the initiative on Facebook or Instagram account tagging

 #Ideas4ViksitBharat

 - The image may also be used as DP on social media platforms.

Students are requested to follow the Students' Welfare Whatsapp Channel using

the following link for receiving further updates on the same:

https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va7h2MyHFxP3rg3n191Y

https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va7h2MyHFxP3rg3n191Y

#Ideas4ViksitBharat

National Energy Conservation Day

National Energy Conservation Day is observed every year on December 14. The

day focuses on making people aware of global warming and climate change and

promotes efforts toward saving energy resources. Energy conservation is an

effort made to reduce the consumption of energy and to use at least energy

so that energy sources can be saved for future uses. However, energy

conservation is achievable either by using energy more efficiently or by

reducing the amount of service usage.

Most of the energy sources we use in our daily lives are 'non-renewable'

they cannot be reused and renewed. It is said that our energy resources may

last only for another 40 years or so. Therefore, every individual must

include energy conservation in their behavior and make energy conservation

plans more effective.

Subject: MH Circular: Online Room reservation counseling for 2021 admitted B. Tech students (2023-24) - Reg
Body:
Office of the Men’s Hostel, VIT, Vellore

 13, December, 2023

CIRCULAR

Online Room reservation counseling for 2021 admitted B. Tech students

(2023-24)

 - This is to inform all 2021 admitted B. Tech Indian, NRI, and

Foreign students

 of the Men’s Hostel that the online room reservation counselling for the

 winter semester-2023-24 will be held on December 18, 2023, from 10:30

 AM to 8:00 PM.

 - Students will be checked into the allotted rooms only if the fee

 payment procedure is complete.

 - Fee payment through VTop will be enabled from Dec 21st, 2023, 3.00 PM

 onward. Room and mess type details can be viewed immediately on payment.

 Caterer details will be made available from 31st Dec 2023 onward.

 - Students will be permitted to check inside their allotted rooms and

 dine in their respective messes from Jan 1st 2024 onward. Due to

 genuine reasons if a student happens to report on 31st Dec 2023, He will be

 permitted to stay in the dormitory without mess.

NCGPA Based Ranking: Priority will be given based on students’ academic

performance as well as the Code of Conduct. Normalized CGPA of the

students’ will be calculated as stated below:

NCGPA = CGPA X (GROUP TOPPER CGPA / BRANCH TOPPER CGPA)

Counselling Process: 

 1. NCGPA rank of the students taking part in the counselling process

 will be displayed in their respective student login ONE day in advance

 before Mock room counselling.

 2. Students can select their room partners as per their preferences.

 Indians can choose NRI & Foreign students as their roommates as well.

 3. Student having a higher rank is allowed to group students with lower

 NCGPA and apply for a shared accommodation (1, 2, 3, 4, 6 & 8 bedded rooms).

Application Flow

 1. Login to the Hostel Counselling Portal (Link will be made available

 in the VTOP spotlight)

 2. Please note your Rank. Read the instructions available as FAQ

 thoroughly.

 3. Click on ‘Create Basket’. Create the basket for the room type you

 prefer to stay in (as many as possible, especially when the rank goes

 beyond 500 to secure a bed). Also check the room type availability during

 counseling to judiciously create baskets.

 4. Add group members (friends) you wish to include as in-mates of that

 respective bed type. Now the system will trigger OTP to your friend’s

 registered VIT email ID.

 5. Your friend can share her consent for joining with you by sharing her

 OTP.

 6. You may enter the OTP and finalize the request.

 7. Repeat Step 03 to Step 06 for each basket and friends included in the

 basket

 8. After finalizing all the baskets, click on ‘Block Selection’ which

 is mandatory without which bed cannot be allotted.

 9. Select the basket you have created, followed by the respective

 selection, the system will list the blocks where the respective

 room-bed type is available. Click ‘Add’ to include the block as one of

 your preferences.

 10. A minimum of 2 baskets per block should be added to complete

 the process. Students can prioritize the block and subsequently save

 the respective choice. Blocks that are not preferred by the students can be

 given the least priority.

 11. Repeat Step 09 and 10 for providing the list of block preferences.

 12. You can edit the priority.

 13. Now you can log out from the application.

 Note:

 1. OTP will be triggered while adding a friend under various bed types.

 2. Deletion of block choice is not possible. However, you can least

 prioritize the same.

Greetings !!

The one day webinar on “Sustainability Horizons: A De-carbonization India

Alliance (DIA) Tribute to India National Energy Conservation Day" is

organized by the VIT Vellore and Society of energy engineers and managers,

IEEE power and energy society in association with School of Electrical

Engineering and School of Mechanical Engineering.

The path to a Green Future is shown by this massive one-day thought

leadership event.

Date : 14-12-2023

Time : 9 am to 9 pm

Meeting link: 

https://youtube.com/live/nywTLAcN1D4

We cordially invite everyone to participate in the event and get the

benefits. A detailed schedule with the speakers is given in the

brochure that is attached for your kind reference.

My special appreciation to Dr. Palanisamy & Dr. Balaji who are organising

the webinar.

Thank you.

Viksit Bharat@2047 is the vision of the Government of India to make India a

developed nation by 2047, the 100th year of its independence. The vision

encompasses various aspects of development, including economic growth,

social progress, environmental sustainability and good governance.

Therefore, it is important to channelise the innovative ideas of the youth

into nation-building by inviting them to ideate and contribute to the

vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047. It is important that every youth takes

part in this important nation building exercise. As part of the Viksit

Subject: VIKSIT BHARAT @ 2047 – IDEATHON COMPETITION
Body:
Dear Students and Research Scholars,

Greetings,

Viksit Bharat@2047 is the vision of the Government of India to make India a

developed nation by 2047, the 100th year of its independence. The vision

encompasses various aspects of development, including economic growth,

social progress, environmental sustainability, and good governance. As

India stands at this crucial juncture, poised to take off on its growth

trajectory, it is important to realise that tremendous dedication and

belief in India’s destiny, immense desire, potential, talent, and

capabilities of the Indians, especially the youth, coupled with steadfast

leadership, is necessary to realise this potential. There is enormous work

that needs to be undertaken in a mission mode to make India Viksit Bharat

by 2047. For this to happen, there is a need to chalk out a bold,

ambitious, and transformative agenda, and its communication to all

stakeholders. The role of the youth, who constitute our largest population

group, has a huge role here as they will lead India to Viksit Bharat by

2047. Therefore, it is important to channelise the innovative ideas of the

youth into nation building by inviting them to ideate and contribute to the

vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047. It is important that every youth, more so

the youth in colleges/ institutes and Universities take part in this

important nation building exercise.

In support of the inspiring vision of "Viksit Bharat @ 2047," VIT Vellore

is thrilled to announce an Ideathon organized by the Office of Academic

Research and Institution's Innovation Council (IIC). This is a unique

opportunity for students to contribute to the development of our nation by

showcasing their creativity and innovative thinking.

We invite students from all schools at VIT Vellore to participate in this

exciting competition. The Ideathon will focus on finding solutions to

real-world problems and developing innovative ideas that can help us

achieve the vision of a developed India by 2047.

Here are some key details about the Ideathon:

· Theme: Viksit Bharat @ 2047

· Open to: All students from VIT Vellore

· Rewards: The best ideas from each school will be rewarded

Guidelines:

Þ Individual student participants can submit one page write up to

propose “Ideas for the Vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047”. 

Þ Last date to submit ideas: 17 Dec 2023

World Kindness Day

World Kindness Day was first commemorated in 1998 by an organization called

The World Kindness Movement, formed at a 1997 Tokyo conference of

like-minded kindness organizations from around the world. In the United

Kingdom, Kindness Day UK is organized by Kindness UK, a not-for-profit

organization. World Kindness Day is here to remind us that simple acts like

appreciating someone’s effort can go a long way. Being kind is a win-win

situation for both the receiver as well as for the person who does the

action. There are several ways one can project kindness and inspire others

to follow the same.

World Kindness Day is to highlight good deeds in the community focusing on

the positive power and the common thread of kindness for good that binds

us. Kindness is a fundamental part of the human condition which bridges the

divides of race, religion, politics, gender, and location. Kindness Cards

are also an ongoing activity that can either be passed on to recognize an

act of kindness or ask that an act of kindness be done. Approaches are

being made to the United Nations by the peak global body, the World

Kindness Movement, to have World Kindness Day officially recognized and its

members unanimously sign a Declaration of Support for World Kindness.

International Human Rights Day

The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was ratified by the UN General

Assembly on this day in 1948, known as Human Rights Day. This year marks

the 75th anniversary of one of the world's most groundbreaking global

pledges: the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR). This landmark

document enshrines the inalienable rights that everyone is entitled to as a

human being - regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, language,

political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or

other status.

The Day serves as a powerful reminder of the fundamental rights and

freedoms that belong to every individual, regardless of background, and

underscores the collective responsibility to uphold and protect these

rights.The theme for Human Rights Day 2023 is "Freedom, Equality and

Justice for All".

Subject: MH Circular: Procedures for organizing hostel rooms before moving out for the winter holidays-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

During the winter semester of 2023–24, 3rd year students will be

accommodated in the vacant beds. Therefore, everyone is hereby advised to

adhere to the procedures listed below,

 - Make sure that everyone keeps your valuable things in your Cupboard

 duly locked.

 - Keep no high-value cash, valuables, or articles in the room. Carry all

 of your unpacked loose belongings, and make sure nothing is left out in the

 open or straggling.

 - Make sure your room is left open and inform your block supervisor

 before leaving for winter vacation. The supervisor will carry out the

 inspection.

 - The block supervisor will lock the room and hand over the room when

 you come back after winter vacation.

Solicit your cooperation in this regard.

Thanks and Regards,

Body:
Dear Students,

Greetings!

We trust this message finds you and your loved ones in good health and

happiness.

As a member of the VIT family, your role in the growth and success of the

institution has been invaluable. Under the visionary guidance of our

Founder and Chancellor, Dr. G. Viswanathan, VIT has surpassed its

commitment to providing world-class education. In the academic year

2021-2022, we established the fully residential "Vellore International

School (VIS)" in Chennai, under the aegis of the VIT Group of Institutions.

We thank you for your support and wishes in this initiative.

Situated in 35 acres of greenery near Kelambakkam, Chennai, VIS provides an

ideal setting for comprehensive learning rooted in Indian values and global

pedagogy. The school imparts holistic education, shaping students into

well-rounded individuals with professional ethics and an appreciation for

multicultural environments.

VIS has achieved remarkable milestones in a short span, earning accolades

such as the "Best Emerging International School" and "Best Residential

School" at the Times Education Awards by Times of India. Distinguished

visitors have appreciated the school's philosophy, holistic student

development culture, impressive infrastructure, innovative teaching

methods, and lush green eco-system.

We are glad to announce that admissions for the third batch, from grade 5

onwards, in both ICSE and Cambridge (CAIE) curricula, commenced on October

20th, 2023.

The attached brochure offers an overview of the school's offerings.

Please share this information with your friends and relatives who might be

interested in admitting their children in international residential

schools.

We value your active participation in nurturing the spirit of the VIS

family.

Please take a look at the walkthrough video -

https://youtu.be/-0JCeUoxmFs?si=3iH662jswghv1VqT

Your continued engagement is essential in propelling VIS to newer heights.

Thanking you,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [6th December

Today's Events:

 - Road to Recovery

Fifth Pillar

Event Name: CASA: Substance Abuse A Global Concern

Time: 09:00 PM – 10:00 PM

Event Description: Join us for an informative discussion on the topic

“Substance Abuse a Global Concern” with our esteemed guest Dr. B.

Radhakrishnan, Medical Research Scientist at Maryland Department of Health

USA. This event will focus on critical aspects of substance abuse at global

level and provide perceptions to overcome the challenges.

it's clutches in a quiz, with questions carefully created to understand

your ability. Embark on a journey of holistic development and healing

yourself.

World Soil Day

World Soil Day (WSD) is held annually on 5th December as a means to focus

attention on the importance of healthy soil and to advocate for the

sustainable management of soil resources. This year, by addressing the

increasing challenges of soil management, the Food and Agriculture

Organization (FAO) campaign "Keep soil alive, protect soil biodiversity"

aims to raise awareness of the importance of sustaining healthy ecosystems

and human well-being.

By encouraging people around the world to engage in proactively improving

soil health, the campaign also aims to fight soil biodiversity loss. If we

do not act soon, the fertility of the soil will continue to be adversely

affected at an alarming rate, threatening global food supplies and food

safety.

Subject: Fwd: Expression of Interest and Support for Hackathon 5.0 and Internship/Capstone Opportunities at Aravind Eye Care System
Body:
Dear Students and Research Scholars,

Greetings,

I am writing on behalf of Aravind Eye Care System (AECS) to extend an

invitation to the students of Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) to

participate in our upcoming event, Hackathon 5.0 which is scheduled to

take place on January 5, 6, and 7, 2024, at Aravind Eye Hospital in

Pondicherry.

At AECS, we are committed to fostering innovation in eye care through

collaborative problem-solving and the development of innovative solutions.

Our Aravind Centre for Eyecare Innovation (ACEi) has been instrumental in

promoting and practicing an innovative culture at AECS, and the annual

hackathon is a testament to our dedication to this cause.

During this event, doctors and staff from all branches of AECS will

collaboratively formulate problem statements and new project ideas aimed at

improving patient care. We have witnessed the valuable contributions of VIT

students in our previous hackathons, and we would be honoured to have your

institution's participation once again.

The hackathon provides a unique platform for students to engage with

real-world challenges in the field of eye care and transform their

innovative ideas into tangible solutions. At the end of the three-day

event, the top three teams, including students, will be recognized and

awarded certificates of appreciation.

Additionally, some of the successful hackathon projects may require further

support, and we extend an invitation to VIT students to consider staying

longer for internship/capstone projects at one of our tertiary care

centers. AECS will cover lodging and food expenses during the project

period.

We are currently seeking candidates in the following domains (people from

other domains can also participate):

· Software Engineer: Proficient in web development, Android

development, and basic Python.

· Mechanical Engineer: Capable of CAD modeling and 3D printing.

· Electronics Engineer: Capable of creating circuits, sensors, and

working with microcontrollers.

· Industrial Designer: Proficient in research, conceptualization,

and ideation.

We believe that the diverse talents and skills of VIT students would

greatly contribute to the success of this Hackathon 5.0.

For those interested, please apply through the provided Application link

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfH_TDaIRqDYqdhi7e2XtJO0Jat3orkO6mV4L33UH-beETksw/viewform.

(The deadline for applications is December 9th, 2023).

Students will be selected after an interview by the expert team and the

nominated problem statements will be shared with the selected students

immediately upon their recruitment to hackathon 5.0.

If you or your students have any questions or require further information,

please feel free to contact us at udayakumar@aravind.org or

kunal.a@aravind.org.

We sincerely hope that VIT students will consider this invitation and join

us in making Hackathon 5.0 a resounding success.

Thank you for your attention and cooperation.

Thanks and Regards

Yours Sincerely,

P.Arulmozhivarman

Subject: Medical/Emergency Leave Procedure - reg.
Body:
Dear Student,

Best Wishes !!!

The procedure to be followed for Medical/Emergency Leave.

 1. For any kind of leave, students are advised to use the permitted 25%

 relaxation in attendance, including medical reasons, and a minimum of 75%

 is mandatory to appear for the exams.

 2. In case of emergency (Medical reasons / Hospitalization / Death in

 family), the first intimation must be given to the proctor. Then, the

 request must be sent to the Head of the Department (hod.ss@vit.ac.in

 <hod.ss@vit.ac.in>) recommended by Proctor with a copy to the

 Programme Secretary (secretary.ss@vit.ac.in).

 3. If he/she has been admitted to the hospital as an inpatient due to

 medical reasons, they have to submit their discharge summary, fitness

 certificate, and hospital bills along with a request letter signed by the

 Proctor and HoD to the Programme Secretary in SJT322 within three days

 after rejoining or before the last working day whichever is early.

 4. For Re-CAT, the documents shall be submitted to the Programme

 Secretary and signed by the Proctor. Medical prescriptions are not

 considered under any circumstances. The reFAT is permitted based on CoE

 norms (refer to reFAT norms mail sent by CoE).

 5. After a medical leave request, a student is expected to attend all

 the classes regularly and if absences are found at later stages, then

 medical leave will not be considered.

 6. Medical leaves will not be updated on VTOP. Instead, based on the

 nature of the request, the school-level committee will decide whether to

 permit or reject the request for Attendance Relaxation for appearing on the

 Exam.

Subject: Safety precautions during these challenging weather conditions-reg
Body:
Dear Students,

"Who doesn’t love the sound of rain, the smell of earth, and the sight of

bright green trees paired with blooming flowers?"

India Meteorological Department (IMD) has predicted heavy rains in several

districts of the Tamil Nadu state including Vellore in the coming days. We

want to remind you of the importance of taking safety precautions during

these challenging weather conditions. With exams currently underway, it is

crucial to ensure your safety and well-being while commuting to and from

the home/hostel to campus.

We urge you to follow these essential guidelines to stay safe during heavy

rains:

 - Plan your commute: Check the weather forecast before leaving

 home/hostel to anticipate weather conditions. Plan your route carefully,

 avoiding low-lying areas, flooded streets/pathways, and overflowing

 streams.

 - Wear appropriate clothing: Dress appropriately for the weather, opting

 for waterproof outerwear, such as a raincoat or rain poncho, and sturdy

 footwear.

 - Carry an umbrella: An umbrella will provide essential protection from

 heavy rainfall and keep you dry.

 - Be mindful of surroundings: Stay alert and aware of your surroundings,

 especially when walking or cycling in rainy conditions. Watch out for

 potholes, debris, and slippery surfaces.

 - Follow a healthy diet: During the rains, your body is prone to

 infections. Most diseases in the rainy season are waterborne and drinking

 filtered or boiled water is essential. Avoiding raw foods like salads is

 also beneficial to stay healthy in this season. Avoid eating street foods,

 which is one of the biggest causes of various diseases. Outside foods are

 prepared in unhygienic conditions and are prone to various infestations. It

 is recommended you consume hot home/hostel-prepared food to stay healthy.

 - One of the most important safety tips for the rainy season is to stay

 away from electric wires⁠-especially the ones that have either fallen from

 heavy rain or are dangling precariously from the pole, about to fall off.

Special instructions to Day Scholars and Day Boarders:

 - Allow ample travel time: Heavy rains can significantly impact traffic

 conditions. Allow extra time for your commute to account for slower traffic

 speeds and potential road closures.

 - Seek shelter indoors: If caught in unexpected heavy rain, seek shelter

 immediately. Avoid staying under trees, and power lines. Look for a sturdy

 building or public shelter.

 - Do not attempt to cross flooded areas: Whether on foot or by vehicle.

 - Follow instructions from authorities: Pay attention to instructions

 and warnings from local authorities regarding road closures, or other

 emergency measures.

Remember, your safety is our top priority. Please prioritize your

well-being during heavy rains and take necessary precautions to ensure a

safe and successful exam season.

The Office of Students' Welfare wishes you all safe and successful exams.

National Pollution Control Day

National Pollution Control Day is observed on December 2nd. This day would

mark the 38th anniversary of the Bhopal Gas Tragedy. Being considered as

one of the world's worst industrial disaster, the day was later marked as

the National Pollution Control Day since then. The day also remembers the

innocent people who lost their lives due to the horrifying Gas tragedy

incident. Apart from raising awareness about the rising pollution of air,

water, and soil, this day also shifts the attention of people with regards

to the pollution control acts. It tells us how industrial accidents could

be prevented by abiding by the rules and regulations listed out in the

pollution control acts.

World AIDS Day

World AIDS Day, designated on 1 December every year since 1988, is an

international day dedicated to raising awareness of the AIDS pandemic

caused by the spread of HIV infection and mourning those who have died of

the disease. Government and health officials, non-governmental

organizations, and individuals around the world observe the day, often with

education on AIDS prevention and control. World AIDS Day is one of the

eleven official global public health campaigns marked by the World Health

Organization (WHO).

On 1 December WHO joined partners in paying tribute to all those working to

provide HIV services, and in calling on global leaders and citizens to

rally for “global solidarity” to maintain essential HIV services.

Office of the Men’s Hostel, VIT, Vellore

29th November, 2023

CIRCULAR

Online Room reservation counseling for 2021 admitted B. Tech students

(2023-24)

 - This is to inform all 2021 admitted B. Tech Indian, NRI and

Foreign students

 of the Men’s Hostel that the online room reservation counselling for the

 winter semester-2023-24 will be held on December 18, 2023, from 10:30

 AM to 8:00 PM.

 - Mock room counselling will be conducted on 4th December 2023 from

 10:30 AM to 8:00 PM.

 - Students will be checked into the allotted rooms only if the fee

 payment procedure is complete.

 - Fee payment through VTop will be enabled from Dec 21st, 2023, 3.00 PM

 onward. Room and mess type details can be viewed immediately on payment.

 Caterer details will be made available from 31st Dec 2023 onward.

NCGPA Based Ranking: Priority will be given based on students’ academic

performance as well as the Code of Conduct. Normalized CGPA of the

students’ will be calculated as stated below:

NCGPA = CGPA X (GROUP TOPPER CGPA / BRANCH TOPPER CGPA)

Counselling Process: 

 1. NCGPA rank of the students taking part in the counselling process

 will be displayed in their respective student login ONE day in advance

 before Mock room counselling.

 2. Students can select their room partners as per their preferences.

 Indians can choose NRI & Foreign students as their roommates as well.

 3. Student having a higher rank is allowed to group students with lower

 NCGPA and apply for a shared accommodation (1, 2, 3, 4, 6 & 8 bedded rooms).

Application Flow

 1. Login to the Hostel Counselling Portal (Link will be made available

 in the VTOP spotlight)

 2. Please note your Rank. Read the instructions available as FAQ

 thoroughly.

 3. Click on ‘Create Basket’. Create the basket for the room type you

 prefer to stay.

 4. Add group members (friends) you wish to include as in-mates of that

 respective bed type. Now the system will trigger OTP to your friend’s

 registered VIT email ID.

 5. Your friend can share his consent for joining with you by sharing his

 OTP.

 6. You may enter the OTP and finalize the request.

 7. Repeat Step 03 to Step 06 for each basket and friends included in the

 basket

 8. After finalizing all the baskets, click on ‘Block Selection’.

 9. Select the basket you have created, followed by this the system will

 list the blocks where the respective room-bed type is available.

 10. Click ‘Add’ to include this block as one of your preference.

 11. Repeat Step 09 and 10 for providing the list of block preferences.

 12. You can edit the priority.

 13. Now you can log out from the application.

 Note:

 1. OTP will be triggered while adding a friend under various bed types.

 2. Deletion of block choice is not possible. However, you can least

 prioritize the same.

Subject: Final Call for Papers - International Conference on Recent Advances in Industrial and Systems Engineering (RAISE) 2023 - reg.
Body:
Dear Colleagues, Scholars and Students

Greetings!

The School of Mechanical Engineering, Vellore Institute of Technology,

Vellore is hosting the International Conference on Recent Advances in

Industrial and Systems Engineering (RAISE 2023) in collaboration with

the Institute

of Industrial and Systems Engineers (USA), Royal Academy of Engineering

(UK), Oklahoma State University (USA), Northern Illinois University (USA),

Cranfield University (UK), University of Sussex (UK), and University of

Derby (UK) from 20 to 22 December 2023.

The conference will provide an excellent platform for knowledge exchange

between researchers working in the areas of Digitalization and

Sustainability Challenges in Resilient Manufacturing and Service

Operations. Prospective authors are invited to submit a full paper (not

exceeding 10 pages).

Call for Papers:Authors are invited to submit original, unpublished

papers. Topics include but are not limited to:

· Resilient manufacturing and service operations.

· Digitalization and resilient in manufacturing operations.

· Digitalization and resilient service operations.

· Sustainable manufacturing and service systems.

(For a complete list of topics please refer to the conference website)

Conference Proceedings

Springer Proceedings:

Accepted papers of RAISE 2023 will be published as a book volume in the

Lecture Notes in Multidisciplinary Industrial Engineering series by

Springer Nature (https://www.springer.com/series/15734).

Proceedings with ISBN:

We would like to inform the authors that the approval of your manuscript

for publication in Springer Proceedings will depend on the selection

process by Springer. Kindly note that Springer may exercise additional

quality control of the manuscript as it may decide at its sole discretion. If

your paper is not considered by Springer to publish in Lecture Notes on

Multidisciplinary Industrial Engineering, it will be published in a

Proceeding with ISBN number with no additional cost.

Special Issues in the Scopus/SCIE/ESCI indexed Journals

Quality manuscripts presented at the conference will be short-listed for

consideration for publication in the Special Issues of International

Journals. This is a post-conference activity, and the short-listed authors

will be invited to submit the extended and revised version of their

manuscript. The manuscripts are handled by guest editors from the

initiation of the review process until the final decision. The details

about the level of revision expected and the timeline for the Special Issue

publication will be provided in the invitation letter. The list of Journals

for which the special issue approvals are obtained is made available in the

‘Publication’ sub-menu under the ‘Submission’ menu of the conference

webpage.

Conference Website :

https://vit.ac.in/RAISE2023/

Paper submission link :

https://easychair.org/my/conference?conf=raise20230

Contact us at email : raise@vit.ac.in

Important Dates:Full Paper submission Due : 30

November 2023

Paper acceptance notification : 07 December 2023

Final paper submission due : 10 December 2023

Registration due : 10 December 2023

Kindly circulate the mail to your peers as well.

Thank you

its prominent treasures is the Vellore Fort, a 16th-century marvel blending

historical events during British rule. Adding to its allure, the

Jalakandeswarar Temple stands as a symbol of architectural brilliance and

spiritual devotion. The Christian Medical College, a modern landmark,

harmoniously blends education, healthcare, and heritage. Through these

sites, visitors immerse themselves in Vellore's diverse culture, history,

and the remarkable legacy left behind by its people, making it a

captivating destination for heritage enthusiasts.

Constitution Day of India

Constitution Day also known as 'Samvidhan Divas', is celebrated in India on

26th November every year to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of

India. On 26th November 1949, the Constituent Assembly of India adopted the

Constitution of India, which came into effect on 26th January 1950.

The Government of India declared 26 November as Constitution Day on 19

November 2015 by a gazette notification.

Constitution Day of India

On November 26 every year, India celebrates National Milk Day to

commemorate the efforts of Dr Verghese Kurien, the brain behind the White

Revolution. Dr Kurien played an instrumental role in the development of the

dairy industry. His efforts also made India self-sufficient as far as its

dairy needs were concerned.

Earlier, in 1970, the NDDB embarked on Operation Flood, a national

development project to establish a milk grid countrywide. White Revolution

is one of the largest programmes, called Operation Flood, which made India

one of the largest milk and its derivative providers on a global scale.

Body:
INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS APPEARING FOR FALL 2023-24 THEORY FAT

Students appearing for FAT Exams, please READ INSTRUCTIONS CAREFULLY TILL

the END.

1. The students must enter the examination hall 15 Minutes before the

commencement of examination (9.15 AM for FN Session). Students reporting

beyond the specified entry time will not be permitted to enter the

examination hall. 

2. Possession of any Electronic Gadget (Mobile Phone, Smart Watch,

Bluetooth device, any device embedded with scanner /camera, etc.), holding

chit papers/ suspicious content in the examination hall is considered as

malpractice.

3. Based on the requirements, Frisking will be done prior to entering the

examination hall and during the examination.

4. If a student leaves the exam hall before 12.00 noon, he/she has to

submit the question paper along with answer sheet. 

5. On the day of exam, keep your bags in front of exam room, DONOT TAKE

NOTE BOOKS / BOOKS / BAGS TO EXAM DESKS

General Instructions

· You need to WEAR Student IDENTITY CARD during the ENTIRE

EXAMINATION PERIOD. If you don’t have a Proper ID Card contact Registrar

Office and apply for a new one and get it before coming to the Exam. The ID

card should be with complete with proper tag. Exchange of ID cards or Tags

will be considered as Malpractice. If you have misplaced your ID card or

forgot to bring it to the Examination Hall, Report to the Control Room of

your test venue (SJT810) to get One Time Permit Slips. You need to pay Rs.

100 through V-TOP online payment only.

· You will NOT be permitted to use toilet/washroom during the

examination, so be prepared for it.

· Exchange of Calculators, Stationaries, Code Books, pen, pencil

etc., are not Permitted. The code Books or standard tables should have been

signed by either by the faculty or School office. No markings of any kind

should be found in such booklets.

· As per VIT rules, even if you keep mobile phone/smart watch in a

switched off position inside the examination hall, it will be treated as

examination malpractice. Such malpractices will lead to confiscation of the

devices (including SIM card) for one semester and ’N’ grade in all the

registered courses including lab & project components in that semester.

Hence before entering the examination hall, students should check their

pockets thoroughly to avoid carrying mobile phone/smart watch by mistake.

A. Pre-Exam Activities

1.

Note down your seating arrangement (Building, Room Number and Seat Number)

from the V-TOP students login. Seating arrangement will not be displayed

for courses in which a student has been debarred. Please report yourself

half an hour prior to exam. No student would be permitted to enter the hall

after 15 min from the scheduled start time of the exam.

2.

Bring proper ID card and necessary stationery items.

3.

Possession of un-authorised material, even if you do not intend to use it

will be considered as malpractice.

B. During the exam

1.

Candidate has to sit in the allotted seat only. Listen to the invigilator

and follow their instructions at all times. Strict Silence should be

maintained in the examination hall. This rule is applicable to both

invigilators as well as students.

2.

Check the class number in the Question paper with the Attendance sheet

Class Number. If you have not received the right question paper or

incomplete or badly printed, please contact the invigilator.

3.

Read carefully and follow the instructions printed in the question paper

and in the answer booklet.

4.

Fill required details (Register No., course code, course title etc.) in the

answer booklet before you start writing the exam. After signing in the

attendance sheet, check the barcode sticker pasted on your answer booklet

for its correctness as your answer booklets will be scanned for valuation

using this barcode only.

5.

First clearly write the Question number in the space provided and then

start writing your answers. USE BLUE / BLACK PEN ONLY for writing the

Answers. Writings on any light colours may not be visible on the scanned

images used for evaluation. Remember to write the answers within the space

provided in the answer booklet. If you write anything outside the margin,

it will be cut during the scanning process. If you are using extra sheets

like graph sheets / templates given by faculty, write your registration

number alone on top left edge outside the margin and keep it immediately

after the first sheet. Do not fold it as it needs to be scanned for

valuation. Do your rough works in the last page of main answer booklet

itself. Before finishing the exam, strike out all the rough works.

6.

Don’t write anything in the question paper or in your hand or leg.

7.

Correcting pens, fluid or tape and erasable pens are not to be used for

corrections in the answer booklet.

8.

Do not discuss / borrow anything with other candidates during the

examination.

9.

Do not get involved in any unfair or dishonest practice during the exam. If

you try to cheat or break the rules in any way, it will invite appropriate

sanctions under malpractice.

10.

Students are not allowed to ask question of any kind during the

examination. Invigilators have been instructed not to answer any enquiry

whatsoever relating to the question papers, whether an explanation or

meaning or correction or typographical error

11.

On the day of the exam, if you feel that you are affected by ill health,

please contact the Chief Superintendent or Invigilator. You can write the

examination at the Health Centre.

12.

Do not leave the examination hall until told to do so by invigilator. You

cannot leave the examinations hall till 30 min from the start of the

examination.

13.

Do not take your answer booklets or unused one, from the examination hall.

It is a serious Malpractice.

14.

Answer booklet contains 42 pages and no additional sheets will be

provided. 

C. If booked under Malpractice

1.

Be calm and give a written response to the allegation and follow the

instructions from the Invigilator/ Asst. CS/CS.

2.

Do not indulge in any disrespectful activities such as shouting / creating

a scene in the examination hall.

3.

Hand over the materials and get a receipt for electronic devices.

NON-COOPERATION WILL BE VIEWED AS AN ACT OF INDISCIPLINE WHICH MAY INVITE

SEPARATE DISCIPLINARY ACTION.

Good wishes

With Regards

Dr. T.B. SRIDHARAN. Ph.D., (DRDO)

Controller of Examinations,

Subject: Opportunity for Science students to participate in National Space Science Symposium (NSSS) 2024
Body:
Kind Attn: PG and Final year UG Science students

Dear Student,

Kindly refer to the information about the student session of National Space

Science Symposium (NSSS) 2024.

The next NSSS will be held in Goa University during 26th February to

1st March 2024. The student session of NSSS - 2024 would include a

workshop, tailored for the PG and final year UG level science

students, as well as presentations by students on novel ideas related

to space science and technology, consistent with the theme "Space

Exploration Vision & Ideas till 2047". In addition to this, the

symposium will enable the students to interact with scientists, attend

Plenary sessions, Interdisciplinary lectures, as well as the Public

lectures.

The last date for registering (shortlisting through an online test)

for PAN India students is 30th November 2023.

For details of Student Session and Registration for online test, visit

https://jigyasa.iirs.gov.in/workshop-detail

To know about other sessions of NSSS please visit

https://nsss2024.unigoa.ac.in/

Subject: Achievers and Special Achievers 2024 - Reg.
Body:
Dear Students,

Student Achievements (National/International) will be honoured as Achievers

for National accomplishments and Special Achievers for International

accomplishments during the 'University Day' every year. Students can submit

their accomplishments for the same through the student login under Services

(Menu) Special Achievers (Tab). We have enabled the Achievers & Special

Achievers Data Upload Option on VTOP for the students who have represented

VIT in various National & International Events for the Achievement Period

Jan 2023 to Nov 2023.

As the Achievers & Special Achiever, after approval from the respective

Deans, will be awarded during the University Day 2024, please select the

year "2024" for updating the achievements.

Please note that securing ranks/qualifying in competitive exams for your

Higher Education is not considered an achievement under this category.

Body:
Office of the Controller of Examinations

Ref.No. : VIT/CoE/2023/23030

Fall Semester 2023-24 Regular Arrear Paper Seeing and Revaluation

· The links for Paper seeing and Revaluation have been enabled in

VTop Students login. Paper seeing and feedback / comments are mandatory for

re-evaluation and is in online mode only.

· If you want to know the question wise marks awarded to your

answers by the evaluator, you need to apply for it through V-Top. We call

this as the Paper Seeing Process. It requires payment of Rs.100 for each

paper. You can apply through: ExaminationsàRegular Arrear/Re-FATà

Papersee/RevàFall Semester 2023-24àPaper Seeing. You can choose course(s)

you want to apply for paper seeing. After Generating the Invoice, you need

to make a payment through “Online Payments” Tab in the same V-Top login.

· Once you have paid, within one to two working days, the

paper and question

wise marks awarded and total marks out of 100 will be made available in

CodeTantra login. You need to use the same portal

https://vit.codetantra.com for this process. After seeing the paper, if you

feel the mark awarded to a particular question is not sufficient and the

evaluator has missed something and there is a need to recheck the mark,

then you can apply for Revaluation of the Course. You need to give suitable

reason for the same in the comments section available just below the mark

awarded by the faculty.

· Please note that the Revaluation has to be applied only in V-Top

(in the same way as you have applied for paper seeing) and necessary

payments also needs to be paid through online payments tab. (Rs. 300 per

paper).

· There might be a tab in CodeTantra platform also for Revaluation

which is NOT for our use. It is their default settings. Kindly IGNORE it.

·

Particulars

Dates

Paper seeing registration link / payment [per paper Rs. 100]

23-Nov-2023 to 25-Nov-2023

Revaluation registration link / payment [per paper Rs. 300]

24-Nov-2023 to 26-Nov-2023

Paper Seeing in https://vit.codetantra.com/

24-Nov-2023 to 26-Nov-2023

Once the Paper seeing request is approved, the evaluated copy of answer

sheets would be made available in CodeTantra after 1 or 2 working days. Use

your VTop login credentials for login.

· After login, follow the instructions given in the platform for

giving comments to the questions which needs to be re-examined.

· Give your feedback with respect to the need for revaluation. If

no feedback is given for any question, your answer script will not be

considered for revaluation and No refund will be given for any approved

requests.

· Students should not approach or give any sort of request to any

faculty related to revaluation (increase of marks or grades). If we receive

any complaints from faculty, it will be treated as ‘Malpractice’ and

revaluation request will summarily be rejected.

Fibonacci Day 2023

It is observed on November 23 annually to honor one of the most influential

mathematicians of the Middle Ages namely Leonardo Bonacci. Let us read in

detail about the day. It honors the sequence and Leonardo Bonacci who

brought this series. He is one of the most leading mathematicians of the

Middle Ages. The day recognises the significance and cost of Fibonacci's

contributions to mathematics.

It is observed on November 23 because the digits of this date form a

Fibonacci sequence. Or we can say that when the date is written in mm/dd

format (11/23) it forms a Fibonacci sequence; 1,1,2,3.

Subject: SW Newsletter_October 2023 - Reg.
Body:
Dear VITians,

“In the entire circle of the year, there are no days so delightful as

those of a fine October.” - Alexander Smith

VIT embraced the enchanting hues of autumn and the thrills of October! As

the month unfolded, the campus witnessed an unforgettable season filled

with laughter, warmth, and a touch of enchantment.

The Office of Students' Welfare organised Newbie Festa 2023 for the

Freshers batch of 2023. The First Years rocked the stage with some

spectacular music and dance performances. As a welcome gesture, the seniors

also performed and motivated the first years.

Onam Celebration has been a custom in VIT for many years now. This year was

no different. "Thanima'23" was conducted on the 1st of October, 2023. Mr.

Gopi Sundar, Music Director and a National Award Winner was the Chief Guest

for the event. Our Honourable Chancellor, Vice Presidents, Pro-Vice

Chancellor and Registrar graced the occasion and wished the Malayalee

Community in VIT. The event saw the traditional and regional art forms like

Thiruvathirakali, Kalari Abhyasam, Mohiniyattam, Oppana, Vanjipaatu, Margam

Kali etc, followed by the traditional Onasadhya. The special performance by

the Chief Guest was thoroughly enjoyed by the audience.

Farewells are always emotional and difficult. The UG Farewell and

Chancellor's Dinner for the Class of 2024 was organised from 30th October

to 01st November, 2023. A photo session, cultural evening and Chancellor's

Dinner was arranged as part of it. Students had a great time as they

re-lived all their sweet memories on campus, took pictures and bid adieu to

their friends, juniors and faculty members.

The celebration of Ayudha Pooja fostered a sense of community and

encouraged everyone to appreciate each others' efforts to create a

harmonious and productive environment. The unity felt by the participants

of this celebration was a testament to the shared values of diligence and

craftsmanship.

"Meri Maati Mera Desh" programme is an initiative aimed at commemorating

the sacrifices of our courageous 'Veers' who have dedicated themselves to

serving our nation selflessly. This programme is envisioned as a

culminating event of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, a celebration of our

independence and the spirit of patriotism. The Nature Lover's Club

organised the event as a remembrance to the Five eminent brave-hearts Rani

Velu Nachiyar, Veerapandiya Kattabomman, Tirupur Kumaran, Subramani

Bharathi and Kumaraswami Kamaraj.

Find this and a lot more in the October edition of our Newsletter!

World Television Day

In recognition of the increasing impact television has on decision-making

by bringing world attention to conflicts and threats to peace and security

and its potential role in sharpening the focus on other major issues,

including economic and social issues, the United Nations General Assembly

proclaimed 21 November as World Television Day.

World Television Day is not so much a celebration of the tool, but rather

the philosophy which it represents. Television represents a symbol of

communication and globalization in the contemporary world. This was done in

recognition of the increasing impact television has on the process of

decision-making. Television was thus acknowledged as a major tool in

informing, channeling, and affecting public opinion.

As part of World Television Day, CC are doing Two events.

Television in Democracy.' Discover how television plays a pivotal role in

shaping political discourse, educating citizens, and holding governments

accountable. Learn about its impact on democracy and its ability to

influence public opinion. Don't miss this insightful presentation that

sheds light on the crucial interplay between television and democratic

societies.

World Children’s Day

World Children’s Day was first established in 1954 as Universal Children's

Day and is celebrated on 20 November each year to promote international

togetherness, and awareness among children worldwide, and to improve

children's welfare. Mothers and fathers, teachers, nurses and doctors,

government leaders and civil society activists, religious and community

elders, corporate moguls and media professionals, as well as young people

and children themselves, can play an important part in making World

Children's Day relevant for their societies, communities, and nations.

World Children's Day offers each of us an inspirational entry point to

advocate, promote and celebrate children's rights, translating into

dialogues and actions that will build a better world for children.

The World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims

The World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims takes place on 20th

November every year as the appropriate acknowledgment of victims of road

traffic crashes and their families. It was started by the British road

crash victim charity, Road Peace, in 1993 and was adopted by the United

Nations General Assembly in 2005.

The objectives of the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims

 are to provide a platform for road traffic victims and their families to:

§ remember all people killed and seriously injured on the roads;

§ acknowledge the crucial work of the emergency services;

§ draw attention to the generally trivial legal response to culpable road

deaths and injuries;

§ advocate for better support for road traffic victims and victim families;

 § promote evidence-based actions to prevent and eventually stop

further road traffic deaths and injuries.

Sappers Day

The Corps of Engineers of the Indian Army, also called the Sappers,

celebrated their Corps Day on 18 November. The Indian Army Corps of

Engineers provides combat engineering support, develops infrastructure for

armed forces and other defense organizations, and maintains connectivity

along the borders, besides helping the civil authorities during natural

disasters. College of Military Engineering, Pune (CME) is the premier

technical and tactical training institution of the Indian Army Corps of

Engineers. The Corps consists of three groups of combat engineers, namely

the Madras Sappers, the Bengal Sappers, and the Bombay Sappers.

Sappers have a glorious history dating back to the mid-18th century. The

Corps officially recognizes its birth as 1780 when the seniormost group of

the Corps, the Madras Sappers, was raised. Subsequently, the Groups of

Bengal and Bombay Sappers were formed in their respective presidencies.

These Groups were later merged on 18 November 1932 to form the Corps of

Engineers. This day is celebrated as Corps of Engineers Day every year. The

Corps of Engineers provides combat engineering support and develops

infrastructure for the armed forces along our vast borders besides

providing succor to the populace during natural disasters. These tasks are

executed through four pillars of the Corps namely the Combat Engineers, the

Military Engineering Services, the Border Roads Organisation, and the

Military Survey of India.

Subject: Hackathon on Cost-effective affordable Cloth bag- “The Bag-It Challenge” -Meendum Manjappai
Body:
Dear All,

Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board has launched a

Hackathon on Cost-effective affordable Cloth bag- “The Bag-It Challenge”

Tamil Nadu Government banned the use of one-time use and throwaway plastics

irrespective of thickness as per vide GO. 84 dated 25.06.2018 effective

from 1st January 2019. Despite the rigorous implementation of these

regulations, including inspection raids and awareness campaigns throughout

the state, the use of single-use plastic carry bags continues to persist in

contravention of the bans. This persistence can be attributed to several

factors, including the cost-effectiveness and functional advantages of

plastic. Many alternatives such as paper or reusable bags, while more

environmentally friendly, tend to be more expensive and may not offer the

same level of durability and convenience as plastic."

The government of Tamil Nadu launched a people's campaign namely “Meendum

Manjappai” in December 2021. Meendum in Tamil means once again and

Manjappai means the yellow bag. The campaign has brought focus on the

age-old eco-friendly tradition of always carrying a yellow cloth bag. The

Meendum Manjappai campaign is a call for back-to-basics in the future.

To address this challenge, the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board has

planned a Hackathon with the primary objective to generate creative ideas

and develop cost-effective cloth bags that are appealing to a wide range of

people. By making eco-friendly options more attractive and accessible, the

hope is to eradicate the use of single-use carry bags. The hackathon will

be a valuable platform for entrepreneurs, innovators, and designers to

collaborate and create practical, appealing, and cost-effective cloth bags.

These bags can then be introduced into the market as alternatives to

single-use plastics. The hackathon may also involve identifying sustainable

materials and manufacturing methods, as well as strategies for promoting

the adoption of these eco-friendly bags among consumers.

National Epilepsy Day

In India, November 17 is observed every year as National Epilepsy Day to

create awareness about epilepsy. Epilepsy is a chronic disorder of the

brain characterized by recurrent ‘seizures’ or ‘fits’. The seizures are

caused as a result of sudden, excessive electrical discharges in the

neurons (brain cells). The condition can affect people at any age and

each age group has unique concerns and problems.

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), about 50 million people

have epilepsy across the world, out of which 80 percent of people are

living in developing countries. Although epilepsy is treatable,

three-fourths of affected people in developing countries do not receive the

required treatment. In India, about 10 million people suffer from seizures

associated with epilepsy. For more info:

https://www.nhp.gov.in/National-Epilepsy-Day_pg

Event Description: Yes-No-Maybe is a classic literary event where

participants participate in teams, where one of the members is tasked with

making the other members of their team guess the prompt given by asking

yes-no-maybe and guess the prompt under a given time limit. Its an

World Kindness Day

World Kindness Day 2023 is a global observance dedicated to promoting and

celebrating acts of kindness. This day serves as a reminder of the positive

impact that kindness can have on individuals, communities, and the world at

large. It encourages people to perform intentional acts of kindness and

foster a culture of compassion and generosity.

The theme for the year 2023 is a powerful reminder – “Be Kind Wherever

Possible.” The theme for this year underscores the importance of kindness

as a universal principle that should be practiced in every corner of the

globe and in every aspect of our lives.

As part of World Kindness Day, CCs are doing 1 Event.

Time: 09:00 AM - 05:00 PM

Event Platform: Instagram

Event Description: World Kindness Day is celebrated every year on November

13th. This day was first introduced in a conference in Tokyo by the World

Kindness Movement, a coalition of NGOs from various countries across the

globe. This day serves as a global reminder to promote and celebrate acts

of kindness and encourage goodwill among individuals and communities, and

to demonstrate that even the smallest acts of kindness and empathy can

create far-reaching ripple effects of positivity out into the world. It's a

day when we unite across all borders to promote compassion, empathy, and

understanding. To celebrate this day, VIT Leo Club presents you with

"Kindness Quest", a quizzing event. In this quiz, we'll explore the

history, stories, and significance of kindness in our lives.

World Pneumonia Day

World Pneumonia Day was established in 2009 to raise awareness about

pneumonia, promoting interventions to guard against, prevent, and treat

pneumonia, and generating action to combat the disease. While pneumonia can

strike anyone, the elderly and young children under two years old are

particularly vulnerable.

Pneumonia is the leading cause of infectious mortality in both adults and

children globally, accounting for the majority of deaths in children under

five. The day also focuses on encouraging global action, especially in low-

and middle-income countries, and offering many opportunities to lower the

number of deaths from respiratory illnesses like pneumonia.

National Education Day

National Education Day is observed on 11 November in India to honour

Maulana Abul Kalam's birthday. He was born on 11 November, 1888 in Mecca

now in Saudi Arabia, and died on 22 February 1958 in New Delhi.

Maulana Abul Kalam Azad’s contributions in the field of education,

nation-building, and institution-building are exemplary. He is the key

architect of education in India. He was India's first Vice President and

also the first education minister of independent India from 1947 to 1958.

As part of National Education Day, CCs are organising 2 Events.

or creed, and he evoked the minds of countless with his vision of secular

and united India. Azad’s contributions to educational reforms continue to

inspire us. Inspired by his legacy, VIT LEO Club is conducting an engaging

quiz- “Ignite the Intellect” to test your knowledge, raise awareness about

World Science Day for Peace and Development

World Science Day for Peace and Development is an international day that

highlights the important role that science has in society and is celebrated

each year on November 10. It also highlights the need to engage the wider

public in debates on emerging scientific issues. By linking science more

closely with society, World Science Day aims to ensure that citizens are

kept informed of developments in science. It also underscores the role

scientists play in broadening our understanding of the planet we call home

and in making our societies more sustainable.

The objectives of World Science Day for Peace and Development are to:

Strengthen public awareness on the role of science in peaceful and

sustainable societies; Promote national and international solidarity for

shared science between countries; Renew national and international

commitment for the use of science for the benefit of societies; Draw

attention to the challenges faced by science and raising support for the

scientific endeavor. Individuals and institutions around the world are

encouraged to organize an event or activity on World Science Day, including

government officials, students, the media, and school pupils.

National Legal Services Day

National Legal Services Day was first observed in the country in the year

1995. The day was started by the Supreme Court of India 25 years ago.

National Legal Services Day date also holds a special meaning as the Indian

Legal Services Authorities Act 1987 came into effect on November 9, 1995.

Since then National Legal Services Day date is November 9 and the day is

observed every year.

The primary aim of this day is to spread awareness among the people. The

day also aims at providing free legal aid and legal advice to the needy,

poor and weaker sections in the society to ensure justice for all the

people of the country. As the day is being celebrated all over India today,

a lot of people have been wondering about the National Legal Services Day

history and significance. For all the people who are curious about the

National Legal Services Day history and its significance, here is

everything you need to know about it.

National Cancer Awareness Day

National Cancer Awareness Day is observed every year on November 7 in

India. The main objective of the day is to highlight the significance of

increased awareness about cancer prevention and early detection for the

general public. The National Cancer Control Programme was initiated in 1975

to provide cancer treatment facilities in the country. The program was

modified almost ten years later to provide a boost to prevention and early

detection.

National Cancer Awareness Day was first announced in September 2014.

November 7 was chosen as the date of observance to generate awareness about

early detection and causing-causing lifestyles. November 7 coincides with

the birth anniversary of Nobel-prize winning scientist Madame Curie, who is

remembered for her discovery of radium and polonium and her massive

contribution to the fight against cancer. Curie's work also led to the

development of nuclear energy and radiotherapy for the treatment of cancer.

for registration.

Registration Steps:

Step 1: Click on Login/Register

This is the first step for both new as well as registered users. You will

find the button on the top-right of the home page.

Step 2: Click on Register

Please note that once you complete your registration process, you will be

able to log into the application using the Sign In option.

Step 3: Select Region as India

Step 4: Fill in your user details.

Please fill in your First Name, Last Name, Email Id and Username (Email ID

without @email service provider, No special characters should be mentioned

in the username)

Step 5: Accept T&C and Consent Statement

Under Terms and Conditions document via the hyperlink on ‘here’ and click

Accept to select the second checkbox.

A QR code will be displayed in the window.

Step 6: Install Microsoft Authenticator from Play Store/App Store

Click on the "+" icon. Choose Personal account in the Add Personal

account and click on Scan QR code.

Step 7: Scan the QR code.

Scan the QR Code which is displayed after the Step 5.

Please enter the One-time code which is generated in the system. And click

on Submit.

Step 8: You will be redirected to the profile page to fill out and save

the required details.

Verify your mobile number with OTP. Fill the other necessary information’s

like

Body:
Dear VITians,

"Nuakhai, a harvest's gift, with golden grains, 

Nature's bounty and the farmer's sweat sustains. 

With joy and love, the village unites, 

dancing to rhythms on festive nights. 

In the heart of Odisha, a treasure so rare, 

Nuakhai's beauty, beyond compare."

The Office of Student's Welfare presents "BARNALI", an evening as colourful

as its name. The event is organised by the students of the Odisha Literary

Association to celebrate the Nuakhai Festival. Nuakhai is observed in the

state of Odisha to welcome the new rice of the season. The festival is seen

as a new ray of hope, held the day after the Ganesh Chaturthi festival. It

has a big significance for farmers and the agricultural community.

Join us as we celebrate the Odia culture, rich in traditions and vibrant

heritage, art, music, dance, and spirituality that weaves the fabric of

Odisha's identity!

Dear VITians,

"Nuakhai, a harvest's gift, with golden grains, 

Nature's bounty and the farmer's sweat sustains. 

With joy and love, the village unites, 

dancing to rhythms on festive nights. 

In the heart of Odisha, a treasure so rare, 

Nuakhai's beauty, beyond compare."

The Office of Student's Welfare presents "BARNALI", an evening as colourful

as it's name. The event is organised by the students of the Odisha Literary

Association to celebrate the Nuakhai Festival. Nuakhai is observed in the

state of Odisha to welcome the new rice of the season. The festival is seen

as a new ray of hope, held the day after the Ganesh Chaturthi festival. It

has a big significance for farmers and the agricultural community.

Effective work performance results from the right combination of knowledge

and skills, cognitive abilities, emotional intelligence, workplace

behavioural style (rooted in personality), alignment to work culture and

key work competencies. Knowing these personal success drivers will equip

you with the understanding of what makes you unique, what your strengths

are, and what areas of development will help you in launching a successful

and rewarding career. The litq.io smart assessment. The litq.io smart

assessment is

a scientifically designed immersive game that takes roughly 30 minutes to

complete. Designed by experts with over 50 years of experience

in assessing and aligning human potential, the Litq assessment stitches

together a series of game-based work simulations with situational judgment

scenarios and cognitive games to provide useful insights into work

potential.

Please find the attached student list with the venue and test time. These

students must attend the test. It is mandatory for all candidates.

Greetings!

We at Vellore Institute of Technology-VIT Vellore believe that education is

not limited to the classroom but goes beyond. To facilitate this, VIT

conducts an Annual International Sports and Cultural Carnival Riviera that

strives to break every barrier, breach every limit, and exceed every

expectation year after year. With a footfall of more than 60,000 students

from 70 different countries, it is with immense pleasure and pride that we

announce our next edition, RIVIERA 2024!

As we gear up for the next edition of RIVIERA, scheduled from 29th

February to 3rd March 2024, we are seeking enthusiastic individuals who

are eager to contribute their skills, creativity, and energy to create an

unforgettable experience for all participants.

We would like to invite applications from students for the post of Student

Organisers, Managers, Coordinators, and Volunteers for Riviera ‘24.

To apply, please fill out the form: https://forms.gle/v8dAzrezY5SzFgu49

Deadline: 9th November 2024, Thursday by 12:00 PM

The eligibility criteria are mentioned below:

 1. VIT University hosts two international fests every year; those

who have worked as Student Organizers in any one fest should not take

part in giving a fair chance to other students.

 1. Students’ Council members will not be considered for organizing

 positions. However, their services will be used appropriately.

 2. Academics requirements:

 Organizers should have at least 8.0 CGPA

 Managers should have at least 7.5 CGPA

 Coordinators should have at least 7.0 CGPA

 Volunteers should have at least 7.0 CGPA

 3. Physical attendance below 70% is not eligible for any of the posts.

 4. Students with standing arrears are not considered for any of the

 posts.

 5. Students who are involved in any disciplinary actions are not

 eligible. Even if he or she paid the fine, it is considered a disciplinary

 action.

 6. A student can be an Organizer/Manager if he/she has worked within

 the organizing committee of previous fests in the past year and has done

 considerable work. This needs to be acknowledged by the faculty coordinator

 of the concerned committee.

 Coordinators must have prominent contributions in clubs/chapters or in

 organizing any other event.

 Volunteers need not have prior experience.

 7. Students planning to do their project outside VIT are not eligible.

 8. If selected for the organizing team, the student should abide by the

 rules and regulations of the Riviera team.

 9. Only final-year students are eligible for the post of Student

 Organizer.

 Both final-year and pre-final-year students can apply for the post of

 Manager.

 Only pre-final year students can apply for the post of coordinator.

 Second-year students, the joining batch of 2022, are eligible only for

 the post of Volunteers.

Join us in creating memories that will last a lifetime and fostering an

international community that celebrates diversity and unity. We look

forward to welcoming you to the RIVIERA family!

Dr K Gokul kumar PhD

Convenor Riviera' 24

International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists

The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed 2 November as the

‘International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists. The date

was chosen in commemoration of the assassination of two French journalists

in Mali on 2 November 2013. This landmark resolution condemns all attacks

and violence against journalists and media workers.

In the past fourteen years (2006-2019), close to 1,200 journalists have

been killed for reporting the news and bringing information to the public.

In nine out of ten cases the killers go unpunished. Impunity leads to more

killings and is often a symptom of worsening conflict and the breakdown of

law and judicial systems. This day calls upon States to promote a safe and

enabling environment for journalists to perform their work independently

and without undue interference.

National Unity Day

National Unity Day is celebrated in India on 31st October. It was

introduced by the Government of India in 2014. The day is celebrated to

mark the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel. This year marks

the 145th birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The official

statement for National Unity Day by the Home Ministry of India cites that

the National Unity Day "will provide an opportunity to re-affirm the

inherent strength and resilience of our nation to withstand the actual and

potential threats to the unity, integrity, and security of our country."

C&C are organizing three events as part of National Unity Day.

World Thrift Day

World Thrift Day is celebrated every year on 31 October. In India, due to

the death of the late Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on the same day in 1984,

this day is being celebrated on 30th October. The day aims to promote the

savings and financial security of individuals and nations as a whole. The

aim of the day is to change the behavior of people towards saving and

constantly remind them of the importance of wealth. Saving wealth helps to

start a business, get a good education, and avail good healthcare

treatment.

The day was established to create awareness among the people about the idea

of saving their money in a bank rather than keeping it at home. The saving

habit of people will give independence to both people as well as the

Country.

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [28th

International Animation Day

October 28, International Animation Day was an international observance

proclaimed in 2002 by the ASIFA as the main global event to celebrate the

art of animation. Honoring the birth of animation, recognized as the first

public performance of projected moving images: Emile Reynaud’s Theatre

Optique in Paris, on the 28th of October 1892. ASIFA coordinates and helps

promote IAD celebrations all over the world, putting the art of animation

in the limelight in a global worldwide celebration of animation. In recent

years, this unique event has been commemorated in more than 50 countries,

on every continent of the world.

Every day we witness the importance and beauty of animation in a variety of

media. It spreads in commercial theatres – featuring 3D animation and

special effects, on TV, publicity, the music industry, cross-media,

internet, but, most especially, it develops and grows as an art form,

through shorts, multimedia, and feature films, created by independent

authors, artists, students, and children from all over the world. Animation

includes an impressive range of approaches, techniques, and goals. Created

by drawing, painting, and animating puppets and objects, using clay, sand,

paper, and computer, working with multiple narratives and non-narratives,

reflecting a diversity of themes and performances, presented on a variety

of platforms. All of this confirms that ANIMATION is an extraordinary and

powerful medium of art, cultural expression, and communication. And, as a

visual storytelling medium, animation can communicate across cultures

without verbal language. It truly is a means of cultural connection.

Body:
Dear Students,

As you are already aware that Yuva Sangam is Yuva Sangam is a flagship

program of the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB) initiative, launched by

the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India. This initiative focuses on conducting

exposure tours of the youths comprising mainly students studying in Higher

Educational institutions (HEIs) & some off-campus youths from one state to

other states & vice versa. It provides an immersive experience of various

facets of life, development landmarks, recent achievements and a youth

connect in the host state. The program aims to promote national integration

and understanding by connecting youth from different parts of the country

through educational and cultural exchanges.

In addition to the cultural exchange, Yuva Sangam also includes a number of

other activities that are designed to help students develop their

leadership, sports and soft skills. For example, students may get an

opportunity not only to participate in workshops on leadership,

communication, and teamwork but also sports events that may be organised by

SAI. They will also have the opportunity to meet and interact with VVIPs,

celebrities or important personalities of the host state.

IIM Tiruchirappalli serves as Tamil Nadu’s nodal centre and has partnered

with IIIT Kota in Rajasthan to facilitate this initiative. Through Yuva

Sangam’s cultural and educational tours, participants will not only gain

exposure to different cultures and traditions but also explore aspects of

development, technology and build lifelong connections with fellow students

from across India.

All interested students can register online at https://ebsb.aicte-india.org/

the Code VITa Contest. It will come under Dream offer and the selected

students will be eligible for Super Dream offers. It will be an added

advantage (if you get shortlisted in TCS Digital Process) when you attend

Super Dream companies Selection process.

The last date for registration is on or before 5th November 2023. Please

note your CT NO. after the registration. The details are appended below:

Students from all the year (Engineering & Arts ) are eligible for the

contest. Request your help to increase the students registration.

Please find the below attached link to get brief about the contest and link

for registration.

Registration Link: https://codevita.tcsapps.com/

Registrations are open for students from all the YOP.

Registration Steps:

Step 1: Click on Login/Register

This is the first step for both new as well as registered users. You will

find the button on the top-right of the home page.

Step 2: Click on Register

Please note that once you complete your registration process, you will be

able to log into the application using the Sign In option.

Step 3: Select Region as India

Step 4: Fill in your user details.

Please fill in your First Name, Last Name, Email Id and Username (Email ID

without @email service provider, No special characters should be mentioned

in the username)

Step 5: Accept T&C and Consent Statement

Under Terms and Conditions document via the hyperlink on ‘here’ and click

Accept to select the second checkbox.

A QR code will be displayed in the window.

Step 6: Install Microsoft Authenticator from Play Store/App Store

Click on the "+" icon. Choose Personal account in the Add Personal

account and click on Scan QR code.

Step 7: Scan the QR code.

Scan the QR Code which is displayed after the Step 5.

Please enter the One-time code which is generated in the system. And click

on Submit.

Step 8: You will be redirected to the profile page to fill out and save

the required details.

Verify your mobile number with OTP. Fill the other necessary information’s

like

 - Academic Year of Completion

 - Nearest TCS Location

 - Institute name

 - Your Reference Number

Laptop as the QR Code needs to be scanned via cell phone.

The World Day for Audiovisual Heritage

The World Day for Audiovisual Heritage takes place on the 27th of October

every year. This day is celebrated to raise awareness of the significance

and preservation risks of recorded sound and audiovisual documents (films,

sound, video recordings, radio, and television programs).

[image:

95042177-world-day-for-audiovisual-heritage-on-october-27-background.jpg]

The main objectives of raising public awareness of the need for

preservation; providing opportunities to celebrate specific local,

national, or international aspects of the heritage; highlighting the

accessibility of archives; attracting media attention to heritage issues;

raising the cultural status of audiovisual heritage; highlighting

audiovisual heritage in danger.
